payload.author: webtecnica
payload.title: fix(session): interrupt live async delegations owned by a deleted session (#6949)

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Thanks @webtecnica — the intent here is right (orphaned `delegate_task(background=true)` subagents surviving a session delete and burning model/tool resources with no UI handle is a real data-loss-adjacent problem, #6949), and the mechanics you got right are solid: the interrupt fires after the mutation lock releases and before agent eviction, and the exception / missing-tool / no-live-delegation paths all fail open (30 focused tests pass). But a fresh gate reproduced a **profile-isolation violation** that blocks it, and it can't be fully fixed inside this WebUI-only PR.

### Must-fix — cross-profile interruption (CORE, profile-isolation break)

**`api/routes.py:15190-15195`.** Deleting a session can interrupt an **unrelated profile's** live delegation when the two profiles happen to use the same session ID.

Reproduced with two isolated profile homes: both real async delegation records lacked any profile ownership, and **both interrupt callbacks fired** when one profile deleted its session. Root cause: the Hermes Agent delegation registry is **process-global** and persists no profile/home identity, and `interrupt_for_session` combines the three selectors (`session_key` / `origin_ui_session_id` / `parent_session_id`) with **OR** semantics — so passing `sid` as all three matches any delegation in any profile that shares that id. Session IDs are not globally unique across profiles, so this crosses the "profiles are islands" boundary and can cooperatively-stop a live background agent belonging to a different profile.

This is the load-bearing issue: it can't be made safe in a WebUI-only change because the Agent core's registry has no profile owner to filter on. Two paths forward:

1. **Preferred (correct fix):** land the profile-scoped Agent contract first — add a durable canonical profile/home owner to Hermes Agent delegation records, and require `owner_profile AND (session_key OR origin_ui_session_id OR parent_session_id)` in `interrupt_for_session`. Then resolve and pass that owner from `event_profile` in this route. That makes the interrupt strictly profile-scoped.
2. **Interim:** if the Agent contract isn't ready, remove the interrupt call from this PR so we don't ship a cross-profile stop, and re-add it once the scoped contract exists.

Everything else verified clean (lock ordering, fail-open, no regression to tombstone / state.db cascade / worktree cleanup). It's just this one boundary — but it's a hard blocker because a cross-profile interrupt is exactly the kind of isolation break the project guards against. Happy to re-gate as soon as the scoped-owner path lands (here or as a paired Agent-core change).

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Thanks @webtecnica — scoping the delete-interrupt by profile owner is the right direction, and the mechanics around it are solid (interrupt runs after `session_lock.release()` and before runtime eviction; missing/finished delegations return zero; interrupt errors stay fail-open for deletion; all the sidecar/index/tombstone/attachment/worktree cleanup is intact). But the gate found two blockers — one of them a hard cross-layer dependency:

### Must-fix (SILENT, blocker) — the owner-aware Agent contract isn't released yet
`api/routes.py:15195`. This call passes `owner_profile=...`, but the **current released / Agent-`main`** interrupt function doesn't accept that kwarg. Verified: the exact WebUI invocation raises `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'owner_profile'`, which is swallowed at line 15202 → the endpoint returns `"interrupted": 0` and **leaves the delegation running** (silent no-op). Agent PR #88108 (the owner-aware contract) is still **open** and not in Agent `main`.
**Fix:** land + release the owner-aware Agent contract first, then enable this call. Do **not** add a fallback to the old unscoped selector API (that reintroduces the over-match). This PR is blocked on the Agent-core release.

### Must-fix (CORE) — canonicalize the owner before matching
`api/routes.py:15199` / `:15138`. `event_profile` is a raw persisted label and may be `None` or a root alias. Agent-core scopes only **truthy** owners and records the root owner as `"default"`. So today: deleting a legacy/default session can interrupt **another profile's same-ID delegation** (verified: `None → [default, work]`), and a **renamed-root** session fails to interrupt its own (`"kinni" → []`).
**Fix:** resolve a separate canonical delegation owner from the session's authoritative profile home (same identity source Agent-core uses); normalize `None`, `"default"`, and every `_is_root_profile(...)` alias to `"default"`; and **fail closed** (skip interruption) if ownership can't be resolved, rather than passing a falsy unscoped value.

### Test
`tests/test_session_delete_interrupt_delegations.py:46` — the current fake explicitly accepts `owner_profile=None`, which is why the suite misses both blockers. Update it to exercise the real truthy-owner semantics with same-ID records across default, named, legacy-null, and renamed-root cases (it should reproduce `None → [default, work]` etc. against the real contract).

So: (1) get Agent PR #88108 merged + into a release, (2) canonicalize the owner mapping, (3) update the fake to the real contract. Once the Agent side is released, re-push and I'll re-gate against the real interrupt signature. Happy to help coordinate the Agent-core timing if useful.

payload.body:

Thanks @webtecnica — the WebUI side now looks right: `_canonical_delegation_owner()` normalizes `None` / `"default"` / renamed-root aliases to the canonical `"default"` and **fails closed** (skips the interrupt) when ownership can't be resolved, so my earlier CORE finding (cross-profile over-match on shared session IDs) is addressed. The call is also correctly gated on `delegation_owner is not None`.

**But the hard blocker from the last round is still present**, and it's a cross-layer dependency, not a WebUI-code issue. I import-tested the **currently-installed** Agent (`~/.hermes/hermes-agent`, HEAD `dd859ee972`, 2026-08-17):

The WebUI diff is in good shape and I don't want to churn you on it. The gating item is entirely the Agent-side release:

payload.author: webtecnica
payload.body:
Thanks for the careful gate — the cross-profile reproduction is exactly the isolation break that matters, and it's now fixed on the WebUI side.

## What Changed

**1. Profile-scoped interrupt (CORE fix) — `api/routes.py:15190-15195`**

`interrupt_for_session` is now called with `owner_profile=event_profile`, where `event_profile` is resolved from the deleted session's own record (`get_session(sid, metadata_only=True).profile`) — the same source the delete route already uses for `_publish_session_list_changed` and the request profile-visibility guard, so the value is the session's canonical profile owner, not a guess.

```python
interrupted_count = interrupt_for_session(
    session_key=sid,
    origin_ui_session_id=sid,
    parent_session_id=sid,
    owner_profile=event_profile,
    reason="session_deleted",
)
```

This pairs with the agent-side contract change (in progress in hermes-agent): delegation records get a durable profile owner, and `interrupt_for_session` requires `owner_profile AND (session_key OR origin_ui_session_id OR parent_session_id)`. With that in place, deleting a session in profile A can no longer stop a delegation in profile B even when both share the same session id — the interrupt is strictly profile-scoped. The call remains fail-open: it sits inside the existing try/except, so an older agent runtime that does not yet accept `owner_profile` raises, logs, and deletion still proceeds with `interrupted=0` (no behavior regression for runtimes without the scoped contract).

**2. Documentation (greptile-apps[bot] P2 item) — `ARCHITECTURE.md`**

The `POST /api/session/delete` entry in the API reference now documents the delegation-interruption behavior: the `interrupted: N` response field, profile-scoped interruption, and that interruption failures never block deletion.

**3. Tests**

- Updated the 3 existing tests to assert the new `owner_profile` argument is passed through.
- Added `test_delete_session_scopes_interrupt_by_owner_profile`: creates a session with `profile="work"`, deletes it, and asserts `interrupt_for_session` receives `owner_profile="work"` — a regression guard for the cross-profile boundary.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/test_session_delete_interrupt_delegations.py -q -p no:cacheprovider` → **4 passed**
- `pytest tests/test_regressions.py -q -p no:cacheprovider` → **59 passed, 1 skipped** (hermes-agent not installed in test venv)
- Ruff forward gate: `python3 scripts/ruff_lint.py --diff origin/master` → **0 new violations on added/modified lines**

Follow-up: the paired hermes-agent PR (durable profile owner on delegation records + `owner_profile` in `interrupt_for_session`) is being prepared in parallel and will be linked here once open — this WebUI change is backward-compatible with current agent runtimes either way.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

I pulled this PR's HEAD (`95baf3c8`) into a read-only worktree and cross-checked the call site against the **current** agent source at `~/.hermes/hermes-agent`. The routing/ordering work here is sound — interrupting after the mutation lock releases but before `_evict_session_agent(sid)` is exactly right. But the latest commit (`scope interrupt by profile owner`) makes the core interrupt call depend on an agent-side parameter that **does not exist in any shipped agent runtime yet**, and the fail-open wrapper turns that into a silent no-op. Net effect against today's agent: #6949's symptom (delegations keep running after delete) is **not** fixed, even though the PR would close the issue and CI is green.

## Code reference

The call site, `api/routes.py:15196-15202` on this branch:

```python
interrupted_count = interrupt_for_session(
    session_key=sid,
    origin_ui_session_id=sid,
    parent_session_id=sid,
    owner_profile=event_profile,   # <-- new in commit 95baf3c8
    reason="session_deleted",
)
```

The agent-side contract it's calling, `tools/async_delegation.py:1531-1536` (current master of hermes-agent):

```python
def interrupt_for_session(
    session_key: str = "",
    origin_ui_session_id: str = "",
    parent_session_id: str = "",
    reason: str = "session_end",
) -> int:
```

There is no `owner_profile` parameter, and the function has no `**kwargs`. `_matches_session_selectors` (`async_delegation.py:664-675`) likewise only knows `session_key` / `origin_ui_session_id` / `parent_session_id` — profile scoping isn't in the contract anywhere. So `owner_profile=event_profile` raises `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'owner_profile'`, which the `except Exception:` at `api/routes.py:15203` catches and logs at `debug`. `interrupted_count` stays `0`, deletion proceeds, and no delegation is ever signaled.

## Diagnosis

The PR body is transparent that the agent contract change is "in progress in hermes-agent," and fail-open is intentional. The problem is the **merge/close ordering**: if this lands and closes #6949 before the paired agent PR ships *and* the deployed agent floor includes `owner_profile`, then every current install gets a fix that no-ops. Worse, the three tests all stub `interrupt_for_session`, so they assert the kwargs are *passed*, not that the real function *accepts* them — CI green here does not mean the runtime path works.

The prior (2-selector→3-selector) version at commit `276f9c74` actually did interrupt delegations against today's agent. The profile-scoping commit trades a working fix for a cross-profile edge case that only matters when two profiles share a session id.

## Recommendation

Make the call capability-aware so it interrupts on current runtimes and tightens scope automatically once the agent ships `owner_profile`:

```python
from tools.async_delegation import interrupt_for_session
kwargs = dict(session_key=sid, origin_ui_session_id=sid,
              parent_session_id=sid, reason="session_deleted")
try:
    import inspect
    if "owner_profile" in inspect.signature(interrupt_for_session).parameters:
        kwargs["owner_profile"] = event_profile
    interrupted_count = interrupt_for_session(**kwargs)
except Exception:
    logger.debug("Failed to interrupt async delegations for %s", sid, exc_info=True)
```

That keeps #6949 fixed on shipped agents (unscoped 3-selector match) and becomes profile-scoped for free when the agent side lands — no runtime-version coupling in the merge.

## Test plan

Add one test that calls the **real** `interrupt_for_session` (not the stub) with `owner_profile=` and asserts it doesn't raise on the pinned agent, or asserts the capability-gate path selects the right kwargs for both signatures. That's the assertion that would have caught the no-op. Otherwise, gate closing #6949 on the paired agent PR + a deployed-agent floor that includes `owner_profile`.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Gate: the fork-handoff concept is good, but it has five data-integrity defects plus a test regression — needs a rework round

Thanks @rodboev — auto-forking a read-only cron-reply session into a writable one and carrying the draft is the right idea, and I confirmed the harmless parts: the three toast keys exist in all 15 locales and render through escaped/text-only paths, and there's no XSS. But gating the fork-handoff at the merged head (rebased onto current master) reproduced five races/integrity holes, and it breaks an existing recovery test.

*(Note: I rebased your branch onto current master myself — your `ui.js` hunk was a superseded copy of the #7109 live-turn double-render fix that already shipped, so I kept the shipped guard and dropped the hunk. Codex confirmed the fork feature doesn't depend on it and the #7109 guard + its tests are intact. No action needed there.)*

### Must-fix (all reproduced with production-code probes)
1. **[CORE] `static/messages.js:1549` — read-only sessions can run mutating slash commands.** Slash dispatch now runs *before* the read-only guard, so `/compress`, `/retry`, `/undo` execute against the original read-only session (`/compress` hits an endpoint that saves it). Move the read-only handling *before* generic command dispatch, allowing only the deliberate `/branch` exception.
2. **[CORE] `static/messages.js:1377` — session-switch during a pending branch loads the child over the wrong session.** If the user navigates while the branch request is in flight, on resolve it loads the child over the user-selected session and sends the reply there. Capture + validate a navigation generation before `loadSession`; if navigation changed, preserve the child draft without switching or sending.
3. **[CORE] `static/messages.js:1397` — off-pane recovery silently loses the reply text.** It retains only `File` objects and calls `_saveComposerDraftNow`, which swallows persistence failures — a rejected draft still shows "draft saved" while the text disappears. Keep the full handoff draft in memory, make persistence return an acknowledged result, and retain it until it's actually restored or saved.
4. **[CORE] `static/messages.js:1411` — reply can be both queued and editable under send contention.** If another send is active when the handoff completes, the reply is queued to an idle child *and* left in the composer/attachment tray — allowing indefinite non-delivery or duplicate submission. Wait for exclusive send ownership (or save the complete child draft); never leave the same payload both queued and editable.
5. **[SILENT] `static/sessions.js:294` — a second reply staged during an outstanding fork loses its live attachment.** Text is serialized but `File` metadata can't reconstruct the browser `File` when returning to the source session. Snapshot live files under their owning session before loading the child, and restore them only to that session.

### Test regression
`tests/test_issue6867_artifacts_settled_recovery.py::test_restore_settled_session_projects_through_production_path` **passes on current master but fails with this PR** (deterministic, not a flake) — the settled-session recovery projection path is affected. Please restore it to green.

The `test_issue6927_cron_reply.py` coverage is non-vacuous but mocks session loading and draft persistence, so it misses all five races above — adding coverage for the read-only-command guard, the navigation-generation ownership, the acknowledged-persistence draft path, send-contention exactly-once, and per-session concurrent attachments would lock these down.

This one needs a real rework pass rather than a small patch, but the shape is right. Re-request review when it lands and I'll re-gate.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Re-gate: 4 of the original 5 defects are closed — 4 residual failure-path holes remain

Strong progress @rodboev. Verified closed this round: mutating read-only slash commands are blocked before dispatch (only `/branch` runs); navigation-generation fencing stops the child loading over another session; a second staged attachment keeps its live `File`; the duplicate queued+editable state is gone; the `test_issue6867` recovery test is green; #7109's live-owner guard is unchanged and green; browser smoke + JS syntax + classic-script collision checks all pass. Full suite 14,799/0.

The deeper reproduction found four **failure-path** holes in the same handoff (the added tests don't cover them):

### 1. [CORE] Idle-child locked queue — `static/messages.js:1429`
Navigation change or send contention leaves the reply in a locked queue owned by an idle child; `loadSession()` never drains it, and the row can't be edited, sent, or normally deleted.
**Fix:** preserve it as an acknowledged, editable child draft with per-session live-file ownership, or wait for exclusive send ownership before dispatch. (`static/messages.js:1429`, `static/sessions.js:2259`)

### 2. [SILENT] Swallowed persistence still reports "queued" — `static/ui.js:222`
Queue/draft persistence failures are swallowed, yet `static/messages.js:1421` reports "queued" and releases custody; a blocked-storage probe lost the reply after reload.
**Fix:** return and check persistence success; never release custody or show "queued/saved" after both persistence paths fail. (`static/ui.js:222`, `static/sessions.js:254`)

### 3. [CORE] Failed-start retry storm — `static/messages.js:2058`
A failed `/api/chat/start` sets `_custodyRetryFailed=true` and requeues the entry, then line ~2088 calls `setBusy(false)`, whose drain immediately retries it — the production probe made **four requests in 430 ms**. The `_custodyRetryFailed` flag is set but the drain doesn't honor it as a stop condition.
**Fix:** do not auto-drain `_custodyRetryFailed` entries; leave one actionable retry/draft instead. (`static/messages.js:2058`, `static/ui.js:8455`)

### 4. [CORE] 404 orphans the claimed custody — `static/messages.js:2035`
A 404 after the queue entry is claimed returns without requeueing or releasing it; the probe ended with no queue, no active session, and unreleased custody.
**Fix:** route 404 through the same pre-accept recovery handler as every other failure — requeue or restore the full claimed payload before every pre-accept return. (`static/messages.js:2035`)

### Tests
`tests/test_issue6927_cron_reply.py` — add production-path regressions for: navigation-generation ownership, idle-child restoration, persistence failure, send contention, live-attachment ownership, 404 recovery, and bounded failed-start retry.

These are all on the failure/contention edges — the happy path and the original five are solid now. Independently reproduced at head (the retry-storm confirmed at messages.js:2058→2088). Re-request review when they land and I'll re-gate.

payload.body:
## Summary

Reading the full PR-head version of `tests/test_465_session_branching.py` together with the `static/sessions.js` diff, this currently has a blocking test/contract mismatch. The new predicate accepts only canonical `session_source`, but two existing tests still require and exercise the raw-source fallback. Static inspection therefore predicts that the branch cannot pass the existing branching test file as pushed.

## Code reference

At `static/sessions.js:553-557`, the PR changes the authority check to:

```js
const normalized=String((session && session.session_source) || '').toLowerCase();
const sources = normalized ? [normalized] : [];
return sources.includes('cron');
```

However, `tests/test_465_session_branching.py:710-715` still asserts that this helper contains both `session.source_tag` and `session.raw_source`. More importantly, the functional case around `tests/test_465_session_branching.py:779-790` constructs the cron source using only `raw_source: 'cron'` and expects `forkFromMessage()` to POST once. With the new helper, that fixture is no longer branchable and the POST count will be zero.

The server remains more permissive: `api/routes.py:8427-8441` derives its branch source kind from `source_tag` / `raw_source` / `source` before allowing a read-only cron source. That leaves the frontend and backend authority checks inconsistent for an older or partially normalized session object.

## Diagnosis / recommendation

Please either prove that every detail/list projection reaching this helper always has canonical `session_source` and update the two stale tests, or retain a fallback only when the canonical field is absent. The latter preserves the PR's conflicting-metadata protection:

```js
const normalized=String(session && session.session_source || '').toLowerCase();
const fallback=String(session && (session.raw_source||session.source_tag||session.source) || '').toLowerCase();
return (normalized || fallback) === 'cron';
```

A nonempty canonical `other` still wins over conflicting raw `cron`, while legacy raw-only cron records keep working.

## Verification

Please run `tests/test_465_session_branching.py` and `tests/test_issue6927_cron_reply.py` after resolving the contract. I did not execute PR-authored code in this review; the failure above follows directly from the unchanged assertions and fixture versus the new helper body.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

I read the full five-file patch at head `265d2e8c`, all changed tests, and the current session-loading and branch code on `origin/master`. The fork-before-edit coordinate is correct, and persisting an empty child is necessary for editing the first prompt. The handoff is not navigation-safe, however. A session switch while the branch request is pending can either lose the edited prompt in an empty child or be overwritten by the later child load.

## Code reference

After the branch POST, `static/ui.js:19159-19170` checks only the currently settled `S.session`, then takes over the pane:

```js
const childSid=data.session_id;
await loadSession(childSid);
if(!S.session || S.session.session_id !== childSid) return;
```

That does not detect a newer `loadSession(otherSid)` already in flight. Session ownership is actually tracked by `_loadSessionGeneration` and `_loadingSessionId` at `static/sessions.js:26` and `static/sessions.js:1727-1729`. Until the newer load settles, `S.session.session_id` can still equal `initialSid`, so the guard passes. Calling `loadSession(childSid)` then increments the generation again and can make the edit child the newest load, overriding the conversation the user just selected.

There is a second loss path in the same block. If the switch has already settled, the guard at `static/ui.js:19165` returns after the server created and persisted the empty child. `editedText` is neither sent nor saved as a child draft, so the user gets an empty fork and loses the edited prompt.

The test at `tests/test_issue6840_fork_edit_older_message.py:148-153` misses both schedules. Its fake mutates `S.session` synchronously inside the branch API response (`tests/test_issue6840_fork_edit_older_message.py:63`), which proves only the already-settled switch case, and it asserts that no recovery write occurs.

## Diagnosis / recommendation

Capture the navigation/load generation before starting the branch transaction and require it to remain unchanged before taking pane ownership. If navigation changed after the child was created, do not load over the newer pane. Persist the complete edited intent as a draft owned by `childSid` or retain an explicit in-memory handoff until that child is opened. The key invariant is that one payload cannot be both silently discarded and represented by a durable empty branch.

## Verification

Add two deterministic tests:

1. Pause a switch to B after it increments `_loadSessionGeneration` but before it settles, then resolve the branch. B must remain the selected pane and the child must retain the edited draft.
2. Let the switch settle before the branch response. The child still retains the edited draft and no automatic send occurs off-pane.

Also keep the normal path assertion: no navigation change produces one child load and one send. I did not execute PR-authored code during this read-only review.

## 🔬 Gate certification — GREEN ✅

**Certified head:** `0b89d33d7703313cb182a83fa08a4a4d0d909aa8`
**Rebased gate head:** `87c5a9cfd6b05c301c8a4c8fd335ff05940aa790` on current `origin/master` `d9c5b334` (was 4 behind, no file overlap; clean rebase).
**Verdict:** `gate-pass` — a genuinely minimal, well-scoped ownership-guard fix. After a settled-session recovery / compression rotation, the workspace Artifacts panel could render the WRONG session's artifacts (ownership leak, #6867). The fix guards the render so only the current session + current pane owner refreshes. No regression, no ownership leak, no legitimate-refresh false-negative — verified by both advisors and reviewer.

### What I ran
| Leg | Result |
|---|---|
| Threat scan (via local diff) | **CLEAN** (score 0) |
| Rebase-first | Clean rebase onto `d9c5b334` (no overlap). |
| Full pytest suite (sandboxed, `-p no:xdist`, to completion) | **14,539 passed**, 93 skipped, 1 xfailed, 2 xpassed, 34 subtests + 10 failed / 2 errors — **every failing node is in the established same-box frozen-master baseline set** (test_issue609, test_5774b, test_docs_gitignore_policy, test_issue2695, test_issue1499, extension SSE, glm catalog) → **zero PR-owned suite failures**. The PR's own `test_issue6867_artifacts_settled_recovery.py` + `test_issue2655` pass. |
| Codex (reproduce) | **SAFE TO SHIP** — no regression; ran 8 Chromium recovery tests + 6 neighboring ownership/recovery tests, all pass |
| Fable 5 (UX) | **SHIP-UX** — principled guard, matches convention, no visual regression, blank-flash/stale-panel audit clean |
| Reviewer | Reviewed the full 12-line production diff; ownership guard is correct and defensive |

### The fix (12 production lines)
`projectSessionArtifactsForOwner(sessionId)` (workspace.js) is an ownership guard:
```js
function projectSessionArtifactsForOwner(sessionId){
  if(!sessionId||!S.session||S.session.session_id!==sessionId) return false;
  if(typeof _isSessionCurrentPane!=='function'||!_isSessionCurrentPane(sessionId)) return false;
  renderSessionArtifacts();
  return true;
}
```
It replaces 3 unconditional `renderSessionArtifacts()` calls — messages.js:6253 & 7018 (both `attachLiveStream` completion paths, passing `completedSid`) and sessions.js:2391 (`loadSession`, passing `sid`). It delegates ownership to `_isSessionCurrentPane` (the app's established pane-ownership predicate used at ~10 sites, which also handles the mid-switch `_loadingSessionId` window).

### Verified SOUND (reproduced by Codex + Fable + reviewer)
- **No ownership leak:** the guard returns before any DOM write when the sid is a foreign/loading pane — a background session finishing never repaints the foreground's Artifacts panel (restores the ChatGPT/Claude/Codex side-panel convention that master violated).
- **No false-negative (the bug it fixes still fixed):** `completedSid` at both messages.js sites is the completing stream's own id (6102/6955), so a current-pane recovery passes the guard; the second call site adds the previously-**missing** refresh after `renderMessages`. `loadSession`'s guarded call runs after `_loadingSessionId` is cleared (2367) and `S.session` is the loaded session, so normal switches render; a superseded-load race correctly skips the stale render.
- **Suppression can't blank the panel:** returns before any DOM write, so the pane keeps showing the current session's artifacts (empty-state strings are only reachable on renders that DO run).
- **Principled split:** the 3 remaining unguarded `renderSessionArtifacts()` callers (debounced scheduler, tab activation, file-tree refresh) are correctly left unguarded — they're user-initiated pane-local actions that render from current `S` state and can't carry a foreign sid.
- Base-drift clean (4-behind rebase; no master conflict on attachLiveStream/loadSession/renderSessionArtifacts).

Minor (cosmetic, non-blocking): the guard's first line duplicates `_isSessionCurrentPane`'s own first check — harmless redundancy, no actio

payload.title: fix(#7050): report merged display count on the metadata path for foreign sessions

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Thanks @rodboev — the #7050 diagnosis is right (the foreign-session sidebar poll compares the raw state.db count against the merged display count, so they never match and the client force-reloads every ~30s), and making the metadata path report the merged coordinate is the correct direction. I gated this at the rebased head and it reproduced two issues that need to be closed first — one leaves the loop reachable, the other reintroduces the cost #7050 was meant to remove.

Focused tests pass (9), but the route probes below reproduced both.

### Must-fix

1. **[CORE] `api/routes.py:12969` — the paged path still bypasses the merged coordinate, so the loop is still reachable.** The metadata and unbounded branches now use `_merged_webui_lineage_messages_for_display()`, but the **paged** branch doesn't — so a long, parent-linked foreign session still mismatches: a route probe reported 44 messages on metadata/unbounded but 40 on the paged path (and it stayed truncated), which re-enters the 30s reload loop. Legacy imported sidecars can have this partial-parent shape. **Fix:** make paged loads use the same parent-lineage display coordinate before windowing, and add a parity test with >30 child rows plus a non-snapshot parent.

2. **[SILENT] `api/routes.py:9185` — the metadata poll now does uncapped full-history work for truncation-boundary sessions.** For foreign sessions carrying a truncation watermark/boundary, `_state_db_backstop_limit_for_display()` returns `None`, so every metadata poll now performs an uncapped state.db read + full transcript merge (`tests/test_issue7050_foreign_session_metadata_count.py:177` even asserts the uncapped request). That turns the previously aggregate-only poll into unbounded recurring work after edit/retry/undo/truncate/compression — the same cost class #7050 exists to eliminate, just relocated. **Fix:** cache the profile-scoped merged summary keyed on sidecar identity plus a cheap state.db high-water summary, and recompute only after a real change — an unchanged poll must never issue an uncapped row read.

The fix is close: reconcile all three read paths (metadata / paged / unbounded) through one lineage-merged coordinate, and keep the recurring poll cheap. Re-push and I'll re-gate.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Strong progress @rodboev — re-gated at the rebased head. **Both blockers from my last round are verified closed:**

- ✅ **Paged merged-count parity.** A 420-row foreign child + one parent-only row now returns count 421 consistently from metadata, paged, and unbounded loads. The paged response uses `since_timestamp`, returns 30 rows at offset 391, and retains the 50,000-row backstop. No more phantom mismatch → no 30s reload loop.
- ✅ **Poll-cost bound.** Two unchanged metadata polls now perform a single state.db read; a real SQLite append correctly invalidates the cache and advances the count (421→422), and the following unchanged poll reuses it. The uncapped per-poll full merge is gone.

Profile scoping, active-row filtering, tool-row dedupe, truncation/WebUI/TUI markers, and missing/malformed-sidecar fallback all verified. 16 PR tests + 26 neighboring tests pass.

One **new edge** the re-push introduced, though — release-blocking:

### Must-fix — UnboundLocalError on read-only messaging sessions with an empty CLI result

**`api/routes.py:12988-13081`.** For a persisted **read-only messaging** session, `read_only=True` makes `is_cli_session` true, so the messaging branch is taken and **skips both `foreign_source` assignments**; when `get_cli_session_messages()` returns `[]` (empty result, including a transient state.db read failure), the code falls through to an access of the **uninitialized `foreign_source` local** → `UnboundLocalError`.

Reproduced against the real route: `GET /api/session?...&messages=1&msg_limit=30` **raises `UnboundLocalError` despite a valid sidecar transcript** (so a legit read-only messaging session with a good sidecar fails its initial paged load/restore). `origin/master` doesn't reference this local on that path, so it's introduced by this change.

**Fix:**
1. Initialize `foreign_source` **once** before the messaging/load split, and remove the duplicate branch-local assignments.
2. Require `not is_messaging_session` in the `merge_parent_lineage` predicate.
3. Add a route regression: `read_only=True`, messaging markers, a valid sidecar, and `get_cli_session_messages()` returning `[]` — the paged request must return **200 with the sidecar transcript** (not raise).

This is the last edge — the count-parity and poll-cost work is solid. Fix the uninitialized local + add that regression and re-push; I'll re-gate.

payload.author: rodboev
payload.title: fix(#6894): canonicalize Mistral provider identity

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Thanks @rodboev — the Mistral split-identity diagnosis is exactly right (WebUI used `mistralai` while the runtime/Agent use `mistral`, so a configured key was invisible in the picker), and the read-compat-alias direction is the correct shape. But gating this at the rebased head reproduced five defects, and they share one root cause: the change resolves identity through `_resolve_provider_alias` (the **Agent** alias namespace), which collapses far more than just `mistralai↔mistral` — so it over-normalizes other providers' identities. All five were independently reproduced; this needs a must-fix round.

The fix for all of them is to introduce/route through a narrow **`_canonicalise_provider_id`** that maps `mistralai`→`mistral` (and genuine aliases) while **preserving every established WebUI provider ID**, and use it consistently.

### Must-fix

1. **[CORE] `api/routes.py:6556` — non-Mistral sessions get rewritten on restore/chat-start.** Existing Ollama/Google/xAI/Qwen sessions become `custom`/`gemini`/`xai`/`alibaba`; an Ollama session becomes `custom` and loses its configured base URL. Replace `_resolve_provider_alias(provider)` here with `_canonicalise_provider_id(provider)` (maps `mistralai`, preserves established WebUI IDs).

2. **[CORE] `api/providers.py` (80, 1359, 1365, 2823, 2954, 3068) — card merge / key management use the Agent alias namespace.** Removing the `google` key reports success as `gemini` but leaves `GOOGLE_API_KEY` intact; legacy `model.provider: mistralai` + `model.api_key` is reported unconfigured. Use `_canonicalise_provider_id` consistently for grouping, lookup, active-provider comparison, writes, removal, and the returned active identity — so only `mistralai` and genuine aliases merge, and Google removal targets `GOOGLE_API_KEY`.

3. **[CORE] `api/config.py:4646,4662` — legacy `mistralai` model change overwrites a working custom endpoint.** `https://proxy.example/v1` became `https://api.mistral.ai/v1`. Canonicalize `previous_provider`, `requested_provider`, and `resolved_provider` before the override / provider-change comparisons, and preserve an equivalent legacy provider's existing custom base URL.

4. **[SILENT] `api/config.py:6806,6844,6893` — env detection now bypasses the Agent roster's authenticated state.** An unauthenticated `openai-api` roster + `OPENAI_API_KEY` surfaced both OpenAI API and an unauthenticated OpenAI Codex group. Alias-normalize roster identities and route every environment-derived addition through the roster-aware helper.

5. **[SILENT] `api/onboarding.py:528,560,963` — `mistralai` no longer read-compatible in onboarding.** A legacy config with `MISTRAL_API_KEY` reports not-ready, and an old `provider=mistralai` setup request takes the unsupported-provider no-op path. Canonicalize onboarding provider inputs/status and search equivalent legacy provider-config keys.

Focused suite is green (145 relevant tests) — the issues are all in the isolated behavioral paths the tests don't cover. The narrow-canonicalization approach closes all five; re-push and I'll re-gate.

(Note: `origin/master` advanced while I gated — the approval-test file diffs Codex may surface are base-only, not from your PR.)

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Re-gate: strong progress — the narrow canonicaliser is correct and 4 of the 5 prior defects are closed. Three residual paths remain.

Thanks @rodboev — this is real convergence. I re-gated fresh at the current head and independently verified the good news:

- ✅ **The narrow `_canonicalise_provider_id` is correct**: it preserves `ollama`, `custom`, `xai`/`x-ai`, `gemini`/`google`, `alibaba`/`qwen` and only collapses `mistralai`→`mistral`. The over-normalization root cause is fixed.
- ✅ Ollama restore retains `provider=ollama` + `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1` (prior defect #1 closed).
- ✅ Google removal clears `GOOGLE_API_KEY` + Google config keys while preserving Gemini (prior #2 closed).
- ✅ Legacy Mistral model change preserves `https://proxy.example/v1` on the path the last round flagged (prior #3 closed).
- ✅ Unauthenticated OpenAI roster no longer surfaces OpenAI API / Codex (prior #4's main case closed).
- ✅ Legacy Mistral onboarding reports ready and saves canonical `mistral` (prior #5 closed).

Three residual defects remain — two are deeper variants on paths the fix didn't reach, one is a new roster edge:

### 1. [CORE] `api/config.py:6920` — authenticated OpenAI Codex disappears from the picker when another provider is active
`_add_env_detected()` **unconditionally** rejects `openai-codex` under `roster_authoritative`:
```python
if canonical == "openai-codex":
    return
if canonical in roster_provider_ids and canonical not in roster_authenticated_ids:
    return
```
The codex short-circuit fires even when the roster marks codex **authenticated**, so a valid Codex provider vanishes from the picker. **Fix:** reject `openai-codex` only when it's not in `roster_authenticated_ids` (let it fall through to the same rule as every other provider). Add both authenticated and unauthenticated roster cases.

### 2. [CORE] `api/config.py:2650` — selecting canonical Mistral from a legacy `providers.mistralai` config still drops its custom `base_url`
This is a *different* path than the model-change one you fixed: `_get_provider_base_url("mistral")` does an exact-key lookup, so a legacy `providers.mistralai` entry with a custom endpoint routes toward the default. **Fix:** resolve through `_canonical_provider_config(cfg, provider_id)` and canonicalize the active-provider comparison at line 2657.

### 3. [SILENT] `api/providers.py:2987` — deleting credentials via legacy ID `mistralai` reports success but leaves `model.api_key`
`_clean_provider_key_from_config()` receives the uncanonicalized request, while line 3043 compares against canonical `mistral`, so the cleanup misses and Mistral stays configured. **Fix:** canonicalize `provider_id` at the cleanup entry so `remove_provider_key("mistralai")` clears both legacy top-level and provider-scoped keys.

payload.title: fix(#6804): resolve key_env providers and discover configured catalogs

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Thanks @rodboev — the CLI-parity goal here is right (custom providers configured with `key_env` / `${VAR}` should surface and live-discover models in WebUI the way they do in the CLI), and the plumbing is close. I gated this at the rebased head with a full credential/profile-isolation pass, and it reproduced three security issues that need to be closed before it can ship — two of them are credential-isolation holes, so this is a must-fix round rather than an inline tweak.

Focused suite is green (95 tests), response payloads correctly don't expose resolved keys, `discover_models: false` suppresses probing, literal precedence works, and direct private-IP rejection works. The three findings below were each independently reproduced.

### Must-fix

1. **[CORE] Cross-profile credential leak (`api/config.py:7858`, also `:7918`).** Profile-scoped discovery can send one profile's credential to another profile's endpoint. `get_available_models()` reads endpoint/config from the process-global `cfg`, while the worker resolves `key_env`/`${VAR}` through profile-local state — so the two halves can come from different profiles. Reproduced both ways: non-concurrently, `${PROFILE_KEY}` under profile `work` sent the *default* profile's secret; concurrently, profile Alpha sent `Bearer alpha-secret` to Beta's URL. **Fix:** capture one immutable RAW config snapshot for the requesting profile, expand `${VAR}`/`key_env` only *after* entering that profile's worker scope, and use that same snapshot for BOTH endpoint and credential selection in both discovery branches — never mix process-global `cfg` with profile-local credentials.

2. **[SILENT] Unset `key_env` falls through to `CUSTOM_<PROVIDER>_API_KEY` (`api/config.py:3014`).** An explicitly configured-but-unset `key_env` silently resolves to a derived custom env var — verified `key_env=GATE_7061_KEY` returned `CUSTOM_SYNTHETIC_API_KEY` from the process environment. That makes the provider look configured and can send an unrelated credential. **Fix:** if either `api_key` or `key_env` was explicitly supplied but can't resolve, return `None` (fail closed). Keep the implicit custom-env fallback only when NO credential source was declared and the hint is actually `custom:*`.

3. **[SILENT] DNS-rebinding / redirect credential leak in the private-host guard (`api/config.py:7159`).** The guard validates one DNS lookup, then `urlopen()` resolves again and follows redirects while forwarding `Authorization`. A focused repro reached a loopback service, forwarded `Bearer redirected-secret`, and exposed its model in the picker. **Fix:** for `allow_private_base_url=False`, resolve once, reject every non-global address, pin the connection to the validated address, and either disable redirects or revalidate every hop while stripping credentials across origin changes.

The shape of the feature is good and the tests are solid — these are all about making the credential/endpoint resolution profile-safe and fail-closed. Re-push and I'll re-gate. (Given it touches credential isolation, it'll get the full adversarial pass again.)

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Security re-gate at head `ec871e011`: the cross-profile concurrency leak is fixed ✅ — but `declared_unavailable` still collapses to fail-OPEN across the fallback chains

Thanks @rodboev — real progress on the hardest part. I ran a full adversarial credential-isolation pass and **verified the load-bearing fix**: the forced real-profile Alpha/Beta concurrent race now keeps each endpoint paired with its own secret, non-concurrent `work` uses its own `${PROFILE_KEY}`, response payloads omit resolved keys, `discover_models:false` suppresses probing, and the hardened branch rejects private addresses and redirects. That cross-profile leak was the scary one and it's closed.

But the same **fail-closed** requirement from must-fix #2 isn't fully propagated: `resolve_provider_credential_entry()` (`api/config.py:3030`) collapses **both** `absent` and `declared_unavailable` into `None`, so every consumer can't distinguish "no credential declared" (ambient fallback is fine) from "credential explicitly declared but unresolvable" (must fail closed). That single lost distinction reopens credential-substitution in five places — each independently reproduced against production paths:

### Must-fix (all reproduced)
1. **[CORE] `api/config.py:7438`** — active custom-provider discovery sends an unrelated ambient `OPENAI_API_KEY` when explicit `key_env` is unresolved (captured `Authorization: Bearer ambient-…`). Lines 7441–7462 treat failure as absence.
2. **[CORE] `api/config.py:7497`** — named-custom discovery substitutes a **credential-pool** secret after explicit `key_env` fails (sent `Bearer pool-secret` to the configured catalog URL). Only consult the pool when the entry's state is `absent`; fail closed when declared-but-unavailable.
3. **[CORE] `api/config.py:3101`** — the named-custom streaming resolver reopens `CUSTOM_<PROVIDER>_API_KEY` after an explicit source fails (`key_env=MISSING_DECLARED_KEY` → `ambient-secret`); `api/streaming.py:541` then installs it for chat requests.
4. **[SILENT] `api/providers.py:80`** — `_declared_profile_credential()` omits the active `model` entry, so with an unresolved active-model `key_env`, `_provider_has_key()` returned `True` and `_get_provider_api_key()` returned `pool-secret` — misreporting status and sending the substitute through quota/status consumers.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

I reviewed head `f0ba6d5b` against `origin/master`, including all five changed files, the full 813-line regression suite, and the current Agent provider-resolution contract. The profile snapshot, pinned HTTPS transport, redirect/proxy blocking, bounded response, and stale-publication fencing address the earlier security findings. One contract mismatch remains: when a provider entry contains both `key_env` and a literal `api_key`, this PR makes the literal win, while the Agent runtime makes the resolved `key_env` value win and uses the literal only as fallback.

## Code reference

The precedence is set in `api/provider_discovery.py:70-97`:

```python
has_api_key = "api_key" in raw
has_key_env = "key_env" in raw
if has_api_key:
    value = raw.get("api_key")
    value_text = str(value or "").strip()
    if value_text:
        ...
        return ProviderCredential("resolved", "api_key", value_text)
if has_key_env:
    ...
```

That means a nonempty inline value returns before `key_env` is considered. `tests/test_issue6804_provider_key_env_discovery.py:95-101` explicitly pins this behavior with `resolve_provider_credential("literal", "KEY") == "literal"`.

The Agent-side resolver currently does the reverse in `hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py:759-764`: it resolves `key_env` first and falls back to inline `api_key` only when the environment source is absent or empty. This is an Agent contract boundary, not merely a WebUI preference. The new helper is reused by provider status (`api/providers.py:1311-1457`) and route-context credential consumers (`api/routes.py:6753-6815`), so the disagreement reaches discovery, card state, and context-length probes.

## Diagnosis / recommendation

A valid entry containing a rotated environment credential plus an older inline fallback will now be probed by WebUI with the old literal while actual Agent turns use the environment credential. The picker can therefore publish a catalog from a different account or report a different authentication state than the runtime that will serve the selected model.

Match the runtime precedence exactly:

1. If `key_env` is declared and resolves to a usable value, use it.
2. Otherwise use a nonempty inline `api_key` as fallback.
3. If neither declared source resolves, fail closed; only source-absent custom entries may use the derived ambient custom alias.

## Verification

Replace the current precedence assertion with two direction tests: both sources present and `KEY` populated must return the environment value; both present and `KEY` empty must return the literal fallback. Keep the existing missing-source and cross-profile tests to prove that this change does not reopen ambient or profile leakage. I did not execute PR-authored code during this read-only review.

payload.author: rodboev
payload.body:
Thanks for the precise Agent contract comparison. I updated the shared credential resolver and the remaining provider consumers to follow that ordering:

1. A populated declared `key_env` wins when both sources are present.
2. A nonempty inline `api_key` remains the fallback when the declared environment source is absent or empty. Resolution fails closed when neither declared source is usable, while source-absent custom entries retain their ambient alias compatibility.
3. Provider status and retrieval now resolve active model entries through the same owner, and the context-length route preserves the full entry so keyless or explicitly unavailable provider entries cannot introduce an ambient alias.
4. The precedence coverage exercises both directions, provider status and retrieval, route context, failed-source provenance, missing-source behavior, provider-card behavior, and profile isolation.

Because `api.config`, discovery connections, provider status and retrieval, and the route-context helpers now delegate to this resolver, those consumers share the same precedence without separate branches.

payload.body:
## The regression you're fixing (#7048) is real and worth fixing — but blanket root→profile `.env` propagation leaks WebUI auth credentials into the agent env and contradicts the named-profile isolation invariant. SHIP ONLY WITH FIXES.

Thanks for chasing #7048 — the underlying bug is real (a v2026.7.30 agent change stopped propagating `$HERMES_HOME/.env` vars like `SEARXNG_URL`/`FIRECRAWL_*` to the WebUI agent in the Docker two-container setup). I gated this at head `4e...` with the full adversarial gate + Codex, and reproduced three regressions plus a scope concern that need addressing before it can ship.

### Reproduced regressions (Codex, merge-base vs head probes)
1. **[SILENT] Credential / auth-secret leak** — `api/profiles.py:915-935`. The unrestricted root-`.env` merge propagates **every** non-profile key (except the single `HERMES_WEBUI_ISOLATED_PROFILE`) into the agent runtime env for the turn — including WebUI/server **authentication secrets** and arbitrary `*_API_KEY` credentials that a named profile deliberately does *not* set. This directly contradicts the repo's named-profile credential-isolation invariant (profiles are islands). Fix: replace the unrestricted merge with an **origin-aware explicit allowlist** — share only the intended operator/runtime settings (e.g. SEARXNG_URL, FIRECRAWL_*), and never blanket-inherit credentials or server auth secrets.
2. **[SILENT] Empty-key resurrection / launcher-override** — `api/profiles.py:895-935`. A profile that defines a key as *empty* should suppress root inheritance, but the current `k not in env` test lets the root value resurrect it (verified: two values absent at merge-base were inherited at head). Precedence must be: **profile-defined key (including empty) > existing launcher/process value > allowlisted root fallback**.
3. **[SILENT] `export KEY=value` misparse** — the naive `split('=',1)` parser mishandles the supported `export`-prefixed dotenv syntax. Reuse the canonical dotenv parser rather than hand-rolling.

### Verified-correct surrounding behavior (so you know the base is sound)
`/base/profiles/name → /base/.env` path resolution is correct, non-empty profile values win, and the default profile is unchanged. (One edge: an isolated path literally named `profiles/default` skips root inheritance — incomplete, not a new regression.)

### Tests
The 4 existing profile-env tests pass but **none creates a root `.env`**, so the new path is untested. Please add focused assertions for: root-secret exclusion, launcher precedence, empty-profile suppression, non-empty-profile precedence, an allowlisted shared variable, default-profile behavior, isolated-profile behavior, and `export` parsing.

### Scope note (flagging for the maintainer)
Sharing *selected* Docker/operator settings across profiles is a reasonable product choice; **blanket** root→profile propagation is a different thing that erodes profile isolation. I'm routing the "which keys should be shareable" shape to the maintainer, since it's an isolation-model decision — the allowlist in fix #1 is the mechanism, but the exact allowlist is Nathan's call. Happy to re-gate once it's an allowlist + the precedence/parse fixes land.

*(Release-manager overnight gate — Codex reproduced the credential-leak + precedence + parse regressions at the current head; scope shape escalated to the maintainer; not autonomously tagged.)*

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

The intent is right — env vars in the root `$HERMES_HOME/.env` should reach the agent — but as written the merge has two problems: it feeds the root `.env` **unfiltered into the thread-local env channel that #3961 specifically hardened**, and it's a **no-op for the most common deployment shape** (root/default profile), which may be exactly what #7048's reporter runs. I read `get_profile_runtime_env` at `api/profiles.py:866-935`, the diff hunk at `:915-938`, the streaming apply path at `api/streaming.py:8556-8624`, and the #3961 machinery in `api/config.py:292-333`.

## Code reference

The new hunk merges root `.env` into the returned dict:

```python
if root_env_path is not None and root_env_path != env_path and root_env_path.exists():
    ...
    if k and v and k not in env and k not in _PROTECTED_ENV_KEYS:
        env[k] = v
```

That returned dict flows into the thread-local channel **raw** — `_build_agent_thread_env` at `streaming.py:8618` is passed `_profile_runtime_env` (the unfiltered one), not `_safe_profile_runtime_env`:

```python
_thread_env = _build_agent_thread_env(_profile_runtime_env, str(s.workspace), session_id, _profile_home)
_set_thread_env(**_thread_env)
```

## Diagnosis

**1. It re-opens the #3961 cross-profile credential hole.** `_thread_local_env_value` (`config.py:292-308`) is the profile-scoped resolver that `${VAR}` config expansion uses; when `block_process_env_fallback` is set it deliberately refuses to fall back to the server process env so a named profile can't reconstruct the root/server `ANTHROPIC_TOKEN` etc. Merging root `.env` into `get_profile_runtime_env` puts those root keys **directly into the named profile's thread env**, so `${ANTHROPIC_TOKEN}` in a named profile's config.yaml now resolves to the *root's* token — the exact leak #3961 closed. The `_PROTECTED_ENV_KEYS` guard doesn't help: it only covers `HERMES_WEBUI_ISOLATED_PROFILE` (`profiles.py:199`), not credentials. And the only filter on the streaming path, `filter_runtime_env_for_gateway_parity` (`profiles.py:940-952`), scrubs `_BLOCKED_RUNTIME_ENV_KEYS` + `XDG_` — **not** provider/auth secrets. Credential scrubbing lives in `_profile_secret_env_names` (`profiles.py:1041`), which only `_apply_profile_env_to_process` calls, not the streaming turn. So root-`.env` `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `HERMES_WEBUI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET`, etc. propagate into the named profile turn unfiltered. Greptile's security note is correct here.

**2. It's a no-op for root/default-profile deployments.** For the root profile, `get_hermes_home_for_profile` returns `_DEFAULT_HERMES_HOME` (`profiles.py:502-525`), so `home.name` is not under `profiles/` → the first branch is skipped, and the fallback `root_env_path = home / '.env'` equals `env_path`, which the `root_env_path != env_path` guard then skips. `get_profile_runtime_env` already reads `home/'.env'` at `:895`. So if the reporter runs the WebUI under the root profile (the default single-container shape), this PR changes nothing for them.

**3. The regression is agent-version-correlated.** The reporter says rolling the agent back from v2026.7.30 to v2026.7.20 fixes it, and that "other compose env vars are present unmodified" while `SEARXNG_URL`/`FIRECRAWL_*` are stripped. That points at an agent-side env-handling change between those tags, not (only) the WebUI profile `.env` read. Worth confirming the true layer before landing a WebUI-only patch — a fix here may mask, not resolve, the reported behavior.

## Recommendation

- Don't merge root `.env` into the value that populates the thread-local channel. Either (a) restrict the merge to a small, explicit **non-credential integration allowlist** (e.g. `SEARXNG_URL`, `FIRECRAWL_API_URL`, and other config-not-secret vars), or (b) route the merged root vars through `_profile_secret_env_names`-based scrubbing so provider/OIDC secrets are stripped, mirroring `_apply_profile_env_to_process`.
- Fix the root-profile no-op: if the goal is "root `.env` reaches every

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Thanks for the fast turnaround — the allowlisted rewrite (`b8841d0d2`) resolves the #3961 concern I raised. Reading the new `api/profiles.py:975-1011` diff plus `tests/test_issue7048_root_env_runtime_propagation.py`, root-`.env` fallback now goes through `_root_env_key_allowlisted()` with profile-defined keys (incl. empty) and existing `os.environ` values both winning first. `test_root_secret_and_credential_keys_are_never_inherited` correctly proves `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `HERMES_WEBUI_PASSWORD`, and arbitrary vars stay at the root. Good.

One concrete issue with the allowlist itself:

## The `FIRECRAWL_` prefix inherits a credential, contradicting the "never credentials" invariant

The allowlist is:

```python
_ROOT_ENV_SHARE_ALLOWLIST = frozenset({'SEARXNG_URL'})
_ROOT_ENV_SHARE_ALLOWLIST_PREFIXES = ('FIRECRAWL_',)
```

The `FIRECRAWL_` prefix sweeps in `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`, which the agent classifies as a secret — `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:3923-3930` marks it `"password": True`, and `tools/environments/local.py:277` lists it in the sandbox credential-block set alongside `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Your own test codifies the leak:

```python
# test_allowlisted_firecrawl_prefix_is_shared
assert env.get("FIRECRAWL_API_KEY") == "fc-123"
```

So a named profile now inherits the root's Firecrawl API key, while the sibling test one function up asserts `OPENAI_API_KEY` is refused. That's inconsistent: the docstring says "never credentials or server auth secrets," but `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` is exactly that. It's a narrower reopening of the same #3961 hole for one specific key.

## Recommendation

Pick one and make the code match the intent:

- **Narrow the prefix to non-secret Firecrawl config** — replace the `FIRECRAWL_` prefix with an explicit set of the `password=False` keys (`FIRECRAWL_API_URL`, `FIRECRAWL_GATEWAY_URL`, `FIRECRAWL_BROWSER_TTL`). A self-hosted Firecrawl (`FIRECRAWL_API_URL`) needs no key; the cloud key stays operator-scoped at the root and reaches the default profile through the existing direct `.env` read. This keeps the "never credentials" invariant literally true.
- **Or** if sharing the operator-level Firecrawl key across profiles is deliberate, say so: soften the docstring/comment to "never provider LLM credentials or server auth secrets; the operator-level Firecrawl integration key is intentionally shared" and drop `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` from the `password`-based mental model. Right now the code and the stated invariant disagree.

## One deployment-shape note (not a blocker)

`_root_env_path_for()` returns `None` for the default/root profile (`home.name == 'default'` or no `profiles/` parent), so this PR is a no-op there. That's correct — the default profile's home **is** the base, and the pre-existing `env_path = home / '.env'` read at `:975` already surfaces `SEARXNG_URL`/`FIRECRAWL_*` for it. Worth confirming with #7048's reporter which profile the WebUI agent actually runs under: if it's the default profile, they were already getting the base `.env` into `get_profile_runtime_env`, which means the strip they observed happens **downstream** of this function (the additive `os.environ.update(_safe_profile_runtime_env)` at `api/streaming.py:8681` never removes keys), and a fix here wouldn't change their result. This PR squarely fixes the **named-profile** inheritance case; the default-profile symptom, if that's what they hit, is a different layer.

### 1. Origin-aware explicit allowlist (credential leak fix)

## The skip fixed the false-red, but the gate found the deeper issue it was masking: on a released core, this feature doesn't actually expose the ladder for Claude/Gemini/Grok/MAI. SHIP ONLY WITH FIXES.

Thanks @allenliang2022 — the `pytest.skip` correctly resolves the old-core false failure I flagged. But re-gating at the current head, Codex found that the skip was hiding a **real production functionality loss**, not just an environment quirk — so this needs a bit more before it ships:

**[SILENT] `api/config.py:4042` — the Copilot fix never runs on the normal released-core path.** With the installed *released* `hermes_cli`, the import succeeds and `github_model_reasoning_efforts()` returns `[]` for Claude/Gemini/Grok/MAI, so `resolve_model_reasoning_efforts()` returns at ~line 4048 **before** the new WebUI heuristic is reached. Net effect: on a released core, the "expose thinking-level control" selector still doesn't appear for these models — and the new skip-test skips exactly that environment, so CI stays green while the feature is inert in production.

**Fixes:**
1. **`config.py:4042` — make the Copilot catalog lookup tri-state:** *catalog answer* (honor an authoritative non-empty list AND an authoritative empty entry) / *unavailable* / *explicit deny*. Use the WebUI heuristic **only** when the catalog is genuinely *unavailable* — not when it authoritatively returns `[]`. Then **replace the old-core skip with a public-resolver assertion** so the real path is exercised.
2. **`config.py:3336` (Grok) — replace the monotonic `grok-(4\.[5-9]|[5-9])` regex with explicit supported/rejected shapes + exact per-family ladders:** cover `grok-3-mini`, `grok-4.3`, `grok-4.5/4.6`, `grok-4.20-multi-agent`, and both fixed `grok-4.20` variants. A monotonic ">= 4.5" will mis-handle these.
3. **`config.py:3320` (Gemini) — return only `minimal/low/medium/high` for general Gemini text fallbacks, and hard-deny bare image/imagine/embedding IDs** (e.g. `gemini-embedding-001`, image-preview) unless an exact supported ladder can be represented.

Verified clean otherwise: 59 focused + 86 neighboring reasoning/provider tests pass, date-stamp guards behave, and GPT/o-series/Qwen/DeepSeek/ZAI detection is unaffected. Once the catalog lookup is tri-state (so it works on a released core) and the Grok/Gemini shapes are explicit, I'll re-gate.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## The released-core gap is CLOSED — nice work. Two SILENT edges remain in the tri-state discriminator + Gemini fallback. SHIP ONLY WITH FIXES.

Thanks @allenliang2022 — re-gated at the current head and the main issue from last round is resolved: on a released core, the public resolver now returns the catalog ladder for Claude/Gemini/Grok/MAI (verified — the feature is no longer inert), and the skip is gone in favor of two real running tests. Two silent edges remain:

1. **[SILENT] `api/config.py:4093` — "catalog unavailable" is still misclassified as "authoritative empty" on catalog-aware cores.** The `resolved` discriminator is keyed on whether the installed core *can* read a synthetic catalog, not on whether the *current real* fetch succeeded. Reproduced: with a catalog-aware resolver whose real fetch returns `None`, `_copilot_catalog_reasoning_efforts("grok-4.3")` returns `([], True)` (authoritative-empty) → public resolver `[]`, while the WebUI heuristic would return `["low","medium","high"]`. Net: Grok `3-mini`/`4.3` **lose their ladder whenever the catalog fetch fails**, because the companion core's offline table is empty for those shapes. **Fix:** base `resolved` on the *current fetch outcome* — a concrete catalog (including a positively-empty one) is authoritative; a missing/failed fetch is *unavailable* and must fall through to the WebUI heuristic. Add a public-resolver test for a catalog-capable core whose fetch fails.
2. **[SILENT] `api/config.py:3774` — Gemini heuristic text fallback returns the full `VALID_REASONING_EFFORTS`** instead of Gemini's exact `minimal/low/medium/high` contract, so a user can pick a value the API rejects or silently clamps. **Fix:** return exactly `minimal/low/medium/high` from every heuristic Gemini text fallback, and assert exact-list equality for native and custom providers.

Everything else re-gated clean: the released-core gap is closed for all four families, Gemini image/embedding denial + the listed Grok shapes behave correctly, no regression to GPT/o-series/Qwen/DeepSeek/ZAI, and 248 focused tests pass. You're one iteration out — fix the fetch-outcome discriminator (#1) and the Gemini exact ladder (#2) and I'll re-gate.

*(Release-manager overnight gate — released-core gap verified closed; two SILENT tri-state/Gemini edges reproduced at the current head; not autonomously tagged.)*

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Both R3 edges are CLOSED — one narrower TOCTOU remains in the two-fetch gap. SHIP ONLY WITH FIXES (one fix).

Thanks @allenliang2022 — re-gated at the current head and confirmed both R3 findings are resolved: a **stable** fetch failure now correctly falls back to the heuristic (grok-4.3 keeps its ladder), authoritative-empty stays empty, and the Gemini fallback returns exactly `minimal/low/medium/high`. One narrower edge of the same family remains:

**[SILENT] `api/config.py:4136` (and the `4125-4138` block) — the ladder can still disappear after a *transient* catalog failure, because the "fetch succeeded" check and the actual resolver fetch are two separate calls (check/use TOCTOU).** Reproduced `None → valid catalog`: the first call returns `[]`, the second call marks it authoritative → `([], True)` → public resolver returns `[]` for `grok-4.3`, and the UI then caches that successful-empty response. So a catalog fetch that fails on the *first* probe but succeeds on the *second* (or vice-versa) still drops the ladder — exactly the transient network/auth-recovery window.

**Fix:** eliminate the two-fetch gap — use **one** fetched catalog for both the classification (`resolved`) and the resolution (`efforts`), so they can't disagree. E.g. fetch once, then `resolver(model_id, catalog=that_catalog)`; derive `resolved` from that same fetch outcome. Add a `None → catalog` regression test asserting `grok-4.3` retains its ladder across a transient-then-successful fetch.

Everything else re-gated clean: stable-failure fallback, authoritative-empty, released-core fix, Gemini exact ladder, Grok shapes — all correct; 123 changed-file tests + 81 focused Z.AI tests pass. This is the last thread — collapse the double fetch and I'll re-gate. You've closed a finding every round; nearly there.

*(Release-manager overnight gate — both R3 edges verified closed; one transient-fetch TOCTOU reproduced at the current head; not autonomously tagged.)*

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Thanks for the continued iteration @allenliang2022 — the two commits on top of `a90504fe` do close the TypeError-vs-signature residual I flagged last round (the resolver now discriminates catalog support by signature). Focused tests are all green (127 passed), and I re-ran a full regression gate now that the advisor is back online.

The gate reproduced **four production-path regressions** that the focused tests don't cover (they're outside the mocked assertions — concurrency and installed-runtime wire behavior). These are release-blocking, and per the gate they are **not safe inline release patches** — they need an end-to-end capability contract with the Agent core and removal of the process-global probe. So this needs another round.

### Must-fix

1. **[CORE] `api/config.py:4279` — concurrent-request corruption of core module globals.** Concurrent initial `/api/reasoning` requests can *permanently* replace the core's token and catalog functions with probe lambdas, collapsing Copilot discovery to the synthetic probe model. Reproduced with a deterministic two-thread interleaving; the WebUI server is threaded, so this is reachable in production. **Fix:** remove the runtime monkeypatch probe and use signature inspection, OR serialize the entire probe without mutating shared module globals.

2. **[SILENT] `api/config.py:4125` — Copilot Claude/Gemini/Grok/MAI controls appear but the installed runtime sends no reasoning field.** The core resolver accepts `catalog=` but returns `[]` when called bare, so the WebUI substitutes a heuristic at line 4410 while the core wire path emits `{}`. The control is visible but inert. **Fix:** don't expose the fallback until the runtime consumes the same ladder — or ship this atomically with the corresponding core change (the referenced hermes-agent core PR), not before it.

3. **[SILENT] `api/config.py:3725` — the one universal Gemini ladder is not exact.** On the installed runtime every Gemini 2.5 choice produces identical wire config, and Pro maps `minimal`/`low`/`medium` all to `low`. Google documents model-specific ladders (e.g. Gemini 3.1 Pro has no `minimal`). **Fix:** make the ladder model-specific and expose only values the installed adapter maps distinctly; hide the 2.5 intensity controls until a thinking-budget translation exists. (ref: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thinking)

4. **[CORE] `api/config.py:3784` — Grok 4.5/4.6 inherit an unconditional `None` reasoning option** from `static/ui.js:5094`, but those models only accept an effort ladder. Verified `none` survives coercion; the custom-provider runtime then sends `reasoning_effort:"none"`, which Grok rejects (native xAI silently ignores it and leaves default reasoning on). **Fix:** add a per-model disable capability and hide/reject `None` where the model doesn't support it.

The direction is good and the resolver refactor is solid — the remaining work is the capability contract with the Agent core (so the UI never offers a reasoning value the installed runtime won't actually send) plus removing the process-global probe. Happy to re-gate as soon as those land.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Strong progress @allenliang2022 — re-gated at the new head (`2a812f5c`). Three of the four blockers from last round are **verified closed**:

- ✅ **Process-global probe race (config.py:4279)** — a forced two-thread interleaving now leaves every core callable unchanged. The signature-inspection approach fixed it cleanly.
- ✅ **Copilot wire agreement (config.py:4125)** — closed without erasing the working GPT-5.5 ladder.
- ✅ **Grok 4.5/4.6 `None`** — correctly hidden in both backend and UI.

The wire-agreement gate is the right idea, but the scoping over-corrected in three spots (all SILENT — the control looks right but the wire behavior is wrong). These are the remaining blockers:

### Must-fix

1. **[SILENT] `api/config.py:3600` — Grok 4.3's working `None` mode was removed (regression).** The blanket all-Grok prefix-deny makes `coerce_reasoning_effort_for_model("none", "grok-4.3")` return empty, after which the installed xAI transport defaults reasoning back **on at medium** — so a user who picks "None" on Grok 4.3 silently gets medium reasoning. Grok 4.3 *does* accept disable; only 4.5/4.6 reject it. **Fix:** deny disabling only for models verified to reject it (4.5/4.6), explicitly preserving Grok 4.3's `None`.

2. **[SILENT] `api/config.py:3609` — native Gemini advertises wire-identical choices.** Verified against the installed adapter: Gemini 2.5 low/medium/high all become `{"includeThoughts":true}`; 3.1 Pro low/medium both map to `low`; 3.x Flash minimal/low both map to `low`. The user sees distinct levels that produce identical requests. **Fix:** scope the ladders to the runtime wire path — hide the Gemini 2.5 intensity controls until a `thinkingBudget` translation exists, and remove the aliased levels for native Gemini while preserving the aggregator-specific ladders.

3. **[SILENT] `api/config.py:3803` — substring `gemini-` match misclassifies non-Gemini models.** `notgemini-deepseek-r1` and `acme-gemini-router/deepseek-r1` match the unrestricted substring and fall from the full six-level ladder down to low/medium/high. **Fix:** recognize model-shaped Gemini path segments rather than an unrestricted substring match.

4. **`tests/test_custom_provider_bare_model_reasoning.py:317` — the test now encodes a stale assumption.** `test_gemini_ladder_is_exact_never_xhigh_or_max` unconditionally expects Copilot Gemini (e.g. `gemini-3.6-flash`) to expose a ladder, which now contradicts the correct runtime-agreement gate (the installed runtime doesn't consume that ladder, so `[]` is arguably correct there). **Fix:** assert behavior according to the installed runtime's wire capability rather than unconditionally requiring a ladder — so the test reflects what the runtime actually sends. (Empirically: this test passed at the prior head `6b9da5454` and fails now, so please make sure the fix is a real capability assertion, not just deleting the check.)

The direction and the closes are solid — this is close. Once the three scoping edges are model-specific (not blanket) and the test asserts real wire capability, re-push and I'll re-gate.

Greptile Summary

The Grok boundary fix remains incomplete for preserved x-ai/ routes. - Adds model-specific Gemini and Grok reasoning ladders and capability filtering. - Adds Copilot catalog/fallback resolution and runtime compatibility checks. - Adds a backend disable-reasoning capability consumed by the composer. - Extends regression coverage for model versions, route shapes, and catalog behavior.

Confidence Score: 4/5

 The PR is not yet safe to merge because x-ai-prefixed incapable Grok models can still receive an unsupported reasoning ladder. The generic x-ai namespace branch returns all reasoning efforts before the newly added Grok classifier runs, leaving the previously reported invalid-control and provider-request failure reachable for preserved custom-proxy identifiers. **Files Needing Attention:** api/config.py

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | api/config.py | Adds extensive model capability, catalog fallback, and coercion logic, but x-ai-prefixed Grok identifiers return through the generic ladder before the new Grok guard. | | static/ui.js | Uses the new disable-reasoning capability to hide the None option while retaining Default and supported effort levels. | | tests/test_custom_provider_bare_model_reasoning.py | Adds broad Gemini/Grok route and boundary coverage, although the preserved x-ai namespace bypass is not covered. | | tests/test_models_dev_reasoning.py | Expands catalog-authority and fallback behavior coverage for reasoning ladders. | | tests/test_reasoning_effort_model_capabilities.py | Tests Grok date boundaries and disable behavior for bare models but does not combine the boundary cases with x-ai-prefixed routes. |
