payload.body:
## Summary

I read the source changes at PR head and on `origin/master`, including `api/helpers.py`, `static/index.html`, `static/boot.js`, `static/terminal.js`, the three modified regression tests, the Prism autoloader, and the xterm add-ons. The runtime wiring is coherent: relative asset URLs respect the existing `<base>` behavior, deferred script order keeps Prism core before the autoloader, and jsDelivr remains in `script-src` and `worker-src` for PDF.js and Mermaid. I do not see a functional blocker in the loading change.

There are two follow-ups worth adding before merge: an asset-closure test and one stale code comment. The current tests prove HTML strings and CSP text, but they do not prove that every locally referenced script, stylesheet, and Prism dependency is actually committed.

## Code reference

`static/index.html:87-91` switches the browser entry points to local files:

```html
<!-- Prism.js syntax highlighting (loaded async, non-blocking) -->
<!-- Vendored from prismjs@1.29.0 — no CDN dependency. -->
<link id="prism-theme" rel="stylesheet" href="static/vendor/prismjs/1.29.0/prism-tomorrow.min.css">
<script src="static/vendor/prismjs/1.29.0/prism-core.min.js" defer></script>
<script src="static/vendor/prismjs/1.29.0/prism-autoloader.min.js" defer></script>
```

`static/index.html:92-96` then points the autoloader and xterm at the vendored directories. The component set currently matches the identifiers and dependencies used by `static/workspace.js:1058-1091`, including chains such as TypeScript to JavaScript to clike, TSX to JSX, PHP to markup-templating, and Scala to Java. However, `static/workspace.js:1059` still says that the autoloader fetches missing components from the CDN. That comment is now false and could misdirect future maintenance.

The assertions in `tests/test_issue1100_prism_sri.py:44-71` only verify that local URLs appear in HTML. `tests/test_issue1850_csp_connect_src_jsdelivr.py:13-52` verifies policy membership, but neither test checks file existence or Prism dependency closure.

## Recommendation

1. Update the stale `static/workspace.js:1059` comment to say that components load from the vendored directory.
2. Add a regression test that parses local `src` and `href` values from `static/index.html` and asserts each target exists.
3. Add a table-driven test for every non-empty `_PRISM_LANG_MAP` value and its autoloader dependencies, asserting the corresponding `prism-<language>.min.js` asset exists. This prevents a future map addition from silently restoring a network request or producing a same-origin 404.
4. Record upstream package/version and checksums for the vendored roots, similar to the existing SMD provenance note in `static/index.html:77-85`.

## Verification

Read-only inspection confirms the currently referenced top-level assets and the dependency files are present. I did not execute PR-authored code.

## Summary

I re-read the full PR at `ced5dcde0`, including the production files, the complete test diff, and the corresponding `origin/master` versions. The vendored URL rewrites and narrower CSP directives are internally consistent, and the newly committed Prism dependency set addresses the gap from my previous review. One test bug remains: the new asset-closure test removes every `<script>` element before collecting references, including external scripts with `src`. It therefore does not verify that any vendored JavaScript file referenced by `index.html` exists.

## Code reference

At `tests/test_vendored_asset_closure.py:16-24`, the parser does this:

```python
# Remove inline script content first to avoid matching JS string literals
cleaned = re.sub(r'<script[^>]*>.*?</script>', '', src, flags=re.DOTALL)
refs = re.findall(r'(?:src|href)="([^"]+)"', cleaned)
return [r for r in refs if not r.startswith(("http://", "https://", "data:"))]
```

The first substitution consumes both the body and opening tag. That drops the Prism `src` tags at `static/index.html:92-93` and all three xterm `src` tags at `static/index.html:100-102` before `refs` is evaluated. The test still checks stylesheet `href` values, but its stated script closure is not exercised.

`tests/test_issue1100_prism_sri.py:51-60` does not close the gap: it asserts that two local Prism URL strings appear in HTML, not that those target files exist. Likewise, `tests/test_embedded_workspace_terminal.py:17-30` checks xterm/version text rather than each referenced file. Removing a vendored core/addon file would therefore leave the relevant assertions green.

## Diagnosis / recommendation

Please preserve opening script tags while removing only inline bodies, or use `html.parser.HTMLParser` to collect `src`/`href` attributes. A minimal correction in the current approach is:

```python
cleaned = re.sub(
    r'(<script\b[^>]*>).*?</script>', r'\1</script>', src, flags=re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE
)
refs = re.findall(r'(?:src|href)="([^"]+)"', cleaned)
```

The standard-library parser would be less regex-sensitive, but either route should make the test cover the referenced JS artifacts.

## Verification

Add a focused assertion that `_local_asset_paths()` contains `static/vendor/prismjs/1.29.0/prism-core.min.js` and `static/vendor/xterm/5.3.0/xterm.js`; then the existing `os.path.isfile` loop proves those files are committed. ## Re-gate: the new composed harness still false-greens and can skip wholesale

Reviewed exact head `9815edb70d7a42ed8d27beb009ce0a82c16757f3`. I isolated the contributor response in `3cb1bc1ef017`; the later commits are base merges.

The response is a real improvement: it removes the fabricated-state helper tests, opens the lightbox through `_openImgLightboxWithNav`, and exercises real wheel/pinch callbacks plus zh/ja translation lookup. Several objective gate blockers remain:

1. **The test installs an unpinned dependency at runtime, then skips if it is unavailable.** `tests/test_img_lightbox_gestures_composed.py:36-68` runs `npm install --no-save jsdom`. If the registry is unavailable (including the required no-network sandbox), the re-probe failure becomes `pytest.skip`, so all 15 new regressions silently disappear. This also mutates the checkout and makes the gate depend on the live npm registry.
2. **The sidebar test does not exercise the recognizer it claims to cover.** `tests/_img_lightbox_composed_harness.js:45-59,184-209` extracts only `_isInteractiveSwipeTarget`, swallows extraction/evaluation failures, and conditionally omits its assertions when `hasSwipeHelper` is false. It never installs/calls `_onPwaSidebarSwipeStart`, observes `_pwaSidebarSwipe`, or verifies `_openMobileSidebarFromGesture` is not reached. Removing the helper call from the production start path leaves this test green.
3. **The keyboard tests bypass the registered event path.** Lines 224-247 call `lb._keyHandler(...)` directly. Removing `document.addEventListener('keydown', lb._keyHandler)` at `static/ui.js:2842` leaves them green.
4. **The claimed computed 44x44/no-overlap check still does not measure those properties.** Lines 284-323 measure height only, use source substrings for width/focus/safe-area, and treat different serialized `right` values as proof of non-overlap. JSDOM performs no layout here, so a sub-44 width or overlapping controls can pass.

### Required fix

- Remove runtime `npm install` and skip-on-failure. Use a repository-declared, version-pinned, lockfile-backed dependency provisioned before pytest, or a dependency-free harness. A missing prerequisite must fail, not skip the regressions.
- Drive the production sidebar start path and assert `_pwaSidebarSwipe` remains null/open is not reached; remove the `hasSwipeHelper` bypass.
- Dispatch `KeyboardEvent` on `document` after production open registers the handler.
- Use a layout-capable browser oracle for both dimensions and overlap/focus at mobile/safe-area sizes, or narrow the claim and add an explicit scoped width contract that cannot false-green.
- Rephrase the literal `eval(` tokens in the added prose: the exact-head threat scan is still `SUSPICIOUS` (score 6), so policy required a static-only NO-RUN review. Then run the corrected slice only through `warmup-safe-test.sh`.

No product code was executed in this review. The scan refusal is not itself the defect; the skip-on-missing-dependency and false-green test paths above are.

payload.title: fix(ui): strip @custom:<slug>: prefix when sending non-default custom-provider models

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Deep-review gate: SHIP ONLY WITH FIXES — the routing fix is the right call, but the prefix it strips is derived from a greedy parse that truncates colon-bearing model IDs, and the restore path loses the selected row

Thanks for this — the bug is real (#6884: a non-default custom-provider model sends the raw `@custom:<slug>:<model>` value and fails to route) and the approach (strip the `@custom:<slug>:` prefix, preserve real namespaces like `@safe:` per #1771) is correct. The 4 canonical picker scenarios pass and your routing test is good. But the adversarial gate (Codex, driving the real `_modelStateForSelect` / `_findModelInDropdown` / `_isSelectedModelRow` functions under a mock DOM) reproduced two regressions that have to close first.

### MUST-FIX 1 (CORE) — colon-bearing custom model IDs get truncated, so they stop routing
`static/ui.js:~2974`. The strip prefix is built from `explicitProvider = _providerFromModelValue(value)`, but that parser is **greedy** — it consumes every colon up to the last one. I confirmed with a direct probe:
```
_providerFromModelValue("@custom:backup:model-a:free")  →  "custom:backup:model-a"
explicitPrefix = "@custom:backup:model-a:"
value.slice(prefix.length)  →  "free"        ← should be "model-a:free"
```
So a custom model whose ID contains colons (`model-a:free`, `vendor:model:tag`, etc.) is truncated to just its last segment. `static/boot.js:2254-2281` then **persists** that truncated ID, and every subsequent send uses it — the upstream has no model named `free`, so the very routing bug you're fixing reappears for colon-bearing IDs. Options that carry `data-model` are unaffected (they skip this path).

**Fix (Codex's spec):** derive the stripping prefix from the authoritative provider slug — `routedProvider || explicitProvider` — and strip `@${routedProvider}:` (the slug only), so `model-a:free` and all remaining colon segments survive.

### MUST-FIX 2 (SILENT) — restored non-default custom rows lose their active/"Selected" state
`static/ui.js:~4336`. After the outgoing ID becomes bare (`free` / `model-a:free`), the restore/refresh path can't mark the row selected. Verified against the real renderer: origin/master shows **one** active row for `@custom:backup:model-a`; this branch shows **zero**. `_findModelInDropdown` does reverse-match the bare ID and does NOT inject a duplicate (good — that part's fine), but `_isSelectedModelRow` compares the **qualified** row value against the now-**bare** state model, so nothing matches and no row renders as "Selected."

**Fix (Codex's spec):** key row identity to the raw selected option value (`sel.value`) plus provider, or normalize both sides to the same model/provider identity before comparing — so exactly one active/"Selected" row is restored.

### Verified-good
- Non-custom namespaces are correctly preserved: `@safe:gpt-4o-mini` (#1771) is NOT stripped (`explicitProvider='safe'` → `isCustomProvider` false).
- Single-colon custom IDs (`@custom:slug:model` with no internal colons) strip correctly.
- The `data-model`-present path (fallback-injected options) is untouched.
- No duplicate-option injection on restore.

Please add a round-trip regression test that covers a colon-bearing custom model ID end to end: send → persist → restore → exactly one "Selected" row, with the model ID intact (not truncated). Both fixes are small and Codex gave exact line targets — happy to re-gate as soon as they're in.

payload.title: fix: label provider usage windows by duration

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Thanks @mvanhorn — exact-head warm-up at `25733d80a02e` found objective blockers that need correction before another gate.

### Finding

**Yes.** WebUI now propagates `limit_window_seconds` through `api/providers.py` and uses exact seconds (`18000`, `604800`) in `static/panels.js`. The embedded direct pool probe reads the field from `/wham/usage`, including stale/swapped-label cases, and missing/unknown durations deliberately fall back to localized “Usage limit”.

The production cross-layer source is incomplete, however: the installed Hermes Agent's `agent/account_usage.py` defines `AccountUsageWindow` with only `label`, `used_percent`, `reset_at`, and `detail` (lines 25–30), and `_fetch_codex_account_usage()` builds each window without copying `window["limit_window_seconds"]` (lines 528–538). A sandboxed introspection printed exactly `('label', 'used_percent', 'reset_at', 'detail')`. In WebUI's no-pool path, `_fetch_snapshot()` retains that Agent snapshot because `_fetch_codex_account_usage_from_pool()` returns `None` for no entries (`api/providers.py:629–670`); the new serializer therefore emits `limit_window_seconds: null`, and `_formatProviderQuotaWindowLabel()` returns the generic usage label for both legacy `Session` and `Weekly`. The new compatibility test asserts the nullable outcome but no test exercises duration metadata through this real singleton Agent source.

Other reviewed edges are sound: numeric strings normalize; booleans/missing/invalid/unknown durations do not produce false 5-hour/weekly claims; known duration overrides stale positional labels; duration-based pool grouping prevents credentials with swapped labels from being conflated. Mixed known/missing metadata remains separate and generic rather than guessed. The new i18n key exists in all 15 locale blocks (same count as the two existing quota-label keys), JS syntax checks pass, and the existing responsive quota layout already collapses to one column at 520px.

### Required fix

The important aggregation correction is at `api/providers.py:490-507`. Pool rows are keyed by duration when that metadata exists, so a five-hour window cannot win against a weekly window merely because both arrived with the same positional label:


payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Thanks @liuguangyong93 — the concept is right (WebUI-generated titles should reach `state.db` so `hermes sessions list` isn't blank), the shape is clean (idempotent `ensure_session` INSERT-OR-IGNORE + guarded try/except/finally), and the test-isolation fix for `test_3230` (mocking `sync_session_title`) is correct. Full CI is green (23/23) and the focused title suite passes (89/89).

I ran the regression gate (Codex + focused suite) and it reproduced two real correctness bugs that a green suite structurally can't catch. Both are silent (no crash, no failing test) so I can't ship as-is, but each has a precise fix.

### 1. [BLOCKER] Wrong title-authority API → can clobber a manual rename
`SessionDB.set_session_title()` always writes `title_source='user'` — that's the *manual-rename* authority. The class contract requires **automatic** callers to use `set_auto_title()` instead. So an auto-generated title synced through `set_session_title()`:
- is mislabeled as a user rename, and
- can **overwrite a real CLI/Gateway manual rename** the user set, because it presents with the same (highest) authority.

**Fix:**
- Initial generation (`_run_background_title_update`) → use the automatic-title write (`set_auto_title()` or equivalent) so it records `title_source='llm'`/auto and never outranks a manual rename.
- Refresh (`_run_background_title_refresh`) → do an atomic compare-and-swap (expected-old-title + `title_source` auto) so it only updates when the title hasn't been manually overridden. If no such CAS/auto API is available for refresh, omit the refresh sync rather than writing through the manual-title setter.

### 2. [BLOCKER] `s.profile is None` writes into the wrong profile's state.db
At `api/streaming.py:4461` and `:4539` the call passes `profile=getattr(s, 'profile', None)`. For legacy sessions where `s.profile is None`, `_get_state_db(None)` takes the TLS/global-active-profile fallback — and detached background title workers have **no request TLS**, so the title can land in whatever profile happens to be process-active rather than the session's true (root/default) DB. Missing profile metadata canonically means root/default, so:

**Fix:** pass `profile=getattr(s, 'profile', None) or 'default'` at both call sites, so a null profile resolves to `default` explicitly instead of falling through to the global-active profile.

### Not blockers
- The `ensure_session(source='webui')` call is correctly non-destructive (INSERT OR IGNORE, verified against `hermes_state.py`).
- The try/except/finally containment is right; a failure here won't break streaming.
- The `test_3230` mock fix is correct.

Once titles are written with automatic authority (not the manual setter) and the null-profile case resolves to `default`, this is a clean reliability fix. Happy to re-gate on the re-push.

payload.body:
## Gate review — solid fix, one advisor finding disproven, one real-but-pre-existing

Thanks @liuguangyong93 — this is a clean, well-scoped fix for a real gap (WebUI writes the generated title only to the sidecar JSON, so `hermes sessions list` shows blank titles). The `ensure_session` + `set_session_title` shape mirrors the existing `sync_session_usage` path, and the double try/except + `finally: close()` means it can never block or crash the background title thread. I ran it through the full gate (two adversarial Codex passes + suite + empirical probes). Summary for the maintainer:

**Test-isolation regression (found + fixed at the test layer).** As submitted, the PR flips `tests/test_gateway_sync.py::test_active_cli_state_db_session_with_persisted_user_turn_is_visible_in_cli_bucket` from green→red when the suite runs the `state_sync/title/state_db` selection (master: 284 passed; PR: 1 failed). Root cause: `test_3230_preserve_manual_session_title.py::test_cleared_title_allows_initial_auto_generation` drives the real `_run_background_title_update` and mocks every collaborator **except** the new `sync_session_title`, so the unmocked state.db side effect leaks into shared test state. Fix (test-only, matches the sibling collaborator mocks): neutralize `api.state_sync.sync_session_title` in that one unit test → 284 passed, matching master. No test rows leaked into the real profile/home state.db.

**Advisor finding "normalize `profile=None` → `"default"`" — disproven, do NOT apply.** A spy on `_get_state_db` shows `sync_session_title` routes **identically** to the shipped `sync_session_usage` for both `profile=None` and a named profile. `sync_session_usage(profile=getattr(s,'profile',None))` is in production today (streaming.py, #2762) and its docstring states the `None → active-home` path is the intended, correct behavior for the default profile (the request thread set the active home; `Session.profile` defaults to `None`). Forcing `"default"` would route a non-default-profile session's title into the literal `default` profile DB — a new mis-route. The current `getattr(s,'profile',None)` is correct.

**Advisor finding "title sync runs outside the locked save → deleted/renamed session can be resurrected" — real, but pre-existing, not introduced here.** An empirical probe confirms a late title sync recreates a just-deleted session row (`ensure_session` re-inserts, `set_session_title` names it). **But the shipped `sync_session_usage` does exactly the same thing on every turn completion**, and the sidecar `s.save()` at streaming.py:4448 already resurrects the deleted session before the state.db sync even runs. So this is an existing background-save-after-delete race across the whole sync layer, not a defect this +38-line title PR creates. Tracking it as a separate follow-up that fixes both sync paths uniformly (the codebase already has the #4985 zero-message-orphan tombstone precedent for this class).

**Verified non-blockers** (both Codex passes + probes): `ensure_session` does not overwrite an existing non-null `source`/model on conflict (only fills NULLs); duplicate-title `ValueError` is caught and degrades gracefully; exceptions can't escape either title worker; SQLite writes are WAL + bounded-retry (12-writer probe wrote all rows); only the title column is touched.

Net: the code change is correct as-is. Recommendation to the maintainer is to land it with the one test-only isolation fix folded in (happy to push that to the branch) and track the pre-existing resurrection race separately.

payload.body:
Thanks @aslater3 — snapshot de-duplication and a bounded initial read are both genuinely worth doing, and the focused suite (112 tests) passes. But a threshold/adversarial gate pass reproduced a set of serious data-integrity regressions across the change, so this needs substantial rework before it can ship. Grouping them:

### De-duplication identity (CORE)
- **`api/models.py:1474` (and the twin at `api/streaming.py:5454`)** — the dedup treats **blank IDs as stable duplicates**, **merges conflicting same-ID rows of different roles**, and **crashes on list-valued IDs**. Reproduced: two distinct `id: ""` user/assistant rows collapsed into one assistant row; `id: []` raised `TypeError`. Fix: share one validator that accepts only valid, non-empty, hashable stable IDs and collapses only role/identity-compatible snapshots — preserve ambiguous rows rather than merging or dropping them.

### Persistence concurrency (CORE)
- **`api/models.py:1721`** — `Session.save()` snapshots then **replaces** `self.messages` / `self.context_messages`, so an append that lands during dedup is lost (reproduced deterministically). And **`api/routes.py:15517` calls `source.save()` without the per-session mutation lock.** Fix: serialize a local deduplicated snapshot without replacing the live arrays, and hold the per-session mutation lock around every mutate-then-save caller.

### Bounded read / pagination / cold-load (CORE ×4)
- **`api/routes.py:12904`** — `max(300, msg_limit*10)` bounds **raw** rows although `msg_limit` counts **renderable** rows; with 2 visible rows + 400 tool rows the response had 30 tool rows and **no user/assistant row**. Expand the tail until it holds the requested renderable count (or reaches array start).
- **`api/routes.py:12906`** — without a trustworthy persisted `message_count`, `api/models.py:1395` reports offset 0; reproduced rows `m370..m399` returned with offset `270`, so later paging skips 100 rows. Require an authoritative count before accepting a bounded result, else full-load.
- **`api/routes.py:12989`** — supplying the child tail bypasses `_webui_sidecar_lineage_messages_for_display()`, so **compression-continuation history is dropped** (only the 2 child rows returned, archived parent omitted, `_messages_truncated` false). Make bounded reads lineage-aware, or fall back to the full path whenever `parent_session_id` may be a compression snapshot.
- **`api/models.py:1353` / `api/routes.py:12925`** — a valid large sidecar can read as `[]` when the `messages` close sits outside the 128 MiB window, and the caller then continues with a metadata-only stub instead of reloading. Return an explicit success/failure result and full-load on any unproven/failed tail read.

### Silent UI-state loss (SILENT)
- **`api/routes.py:13210`** — the Todos panel comment needs the full transcript, but `_all_msgs` is now only the bounded suffix, so the latest Todo write before that suffix is lost. Persist/read a durable Todo summary, do a bounded reverse lookup, or retain the full-load path here.

### Repair script is destructive (CORE ×2)
- **`scripts/repair_duplicate_message_snapshots.py:139`** — later same-ID snapshots are **skipped rather than merged**, and `context_messages` is neither deduped nor streamed; reproduced a partial row surviving while the completed answer/reasoning/tool metadata were deleted. Use a two-pass/shared merge-later policy for both arrays, preserving contradictory/ambiguous rows.
- **`scripts/repair_duplicate_message_snapshots.py:82`** — an existing destination is truncated **before** full validation, with no atomic temp output or backup. Refuse an existing destination by default; write→fsync→validate an adjacent temp file, atomically replace only on success, and create a verified backup for any replace mode.

Each of the above was reproduced against the checked-out head. This is a lot, but the shape is right — the fixes are mostly "validate before collapse," "don't replace live arrays / hold the lock," "count render

payload.body:
## Summary

Reading all four changed files at PR head `572ae499b`, the complete diff against `origin/master`, and the existing limited-display merge path, the goal is right but the optimized path is not safe yet. I found three blocking correctness problems: the reverse reader can decode a trailing top-level array as messages, window expansion cannot detect a value that began before the window, and a successful sidecar read bypasses state.db plus other full-load payload contracts.

## Code reference

At `api/models.py:1155-1157`, `_reverse_json_array_pair()` returns the first top-level array close encountered from EOF while reusing the opening coordinate found for `messages`:

```python
if byte == ord("]"):
    if len(stack) == 1:
        return expected_open, absolute_base + idx
```

That close is not proven to belong to `messages`. The real save layout at `api/models.py:1609-1611` writes `messages`, then `tool_calls`, then `anchor_activity_scenes`. A non-empty `tool_calls` array can therefore be decoded as the transcript tail. The reader fixture at `tests/test_session_tail_reader.py:19-25` omits those real trailing fields, so it cannot catch this common sidecar shape.

The expansion branch at `api/models.py:1262-1288` also cannot work as intended when the selected value crosses the initial window. `_reverse_json_tail_start()` receives `open_idx=0` when the real opener is before the window and returns `1` after reaching that artificial boundary. `value_start_abs = start + start_abs` then necessarily satisfies `value_start_abs >= start`; decoding begins in the middle of a JSON value and the outer exception path returns fallback instead of expanding. A single large recent tool result can reproduce this shape.

## Diagnosis / recommendation

First, make the reverse scan identify the top-level value whose key is exactly `messages`; do not pair the known opener with an unrelated closing bracket. The reader must distinguish “found N complete values” from “hit the left edge while still inside a value” so the latter expands before decoding.

Second, `api/routes.py:12894-12913` must not set `state_db_messages=[]` merely because the sidecar tail parsed. The existing contract at `api/routes.py:8909-8916` explicitly says even state.db rows with older, equal, or missing timestamps may be absent from the sidecar and must be reconciled. `tests/test_session_tail_route.py:27-33` currently asserts that the state.db reader is never called, which pins the regression rather than testing parity. Add a bounded reconciliation proof, and fall back to the existing path whenever parity cannot be established.

There is a third payload regression from the metadata-only load. `tool_calls` and full `anchor_activity_scenes` live after `messages`, so the stub cannot hydrate scenes at `api/routes.py:12999-13004` or return session-level tool calls at `:13071-13081`. Also, `api/routes.py:13144-13151` intentionally derives Todo state from the full merged transcript, but `_all_msgs` is now only the raw tail. The optimization needs bounded equivalents or a durable summary for these fields, not silent omission.

## Test plan

Add fixtures in the exact `Session.save()` property order with non-empty trailing `tool_calls` and scenes; a newest message larger than 1 MiB; state.db one row ahead of the sidecar; a tail assistant whose Worklog exists only in `anchor_activity_scenes`; a session-level-only tool call; and a Todo snapshot older than the 300-row raw budget. Assert the optimized response matches the current full-load response for messages, offsets, scenes, tool cards, and Todo state. I did not execute code from the PR worktree.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

The offline repair path can destroy the newer, more complete copy of a duplicated snapshot. Runtime persistence merges later fields into the first occurrence, but the repair script keeps the first occurrence unchanged and discards every later one. For the partial-then-final snapshot pattern described by this PR, that can preserve truncated content while deleting the completed response.

## Code reference

At `scripts/repair_duplicate_message_snapshots.py:139-149`, the streaming repair marks an already-seen stable ID as duplicate and immediately skips it:

```python
if message_id is not None and not isinstance(message_id, bool):
    seen_ids.add(message_id)
if duplicate:
    duplicate_messages += 1
    continue
```

That differs from the runtime policy at `api/models.py:1466-1490`. The latter retains the first position but overlays fields from the later snapshot, while guarding useful non-empty content:

```python
for key, value in message.items():
    if key in {"content", "reasoning"} and not value and existing.get(key):
        continue
    existing[key] = value
```

The streaming sanitizer in `api/streaming.py:4926-4955` follows the same merge-later policy. The repair tool therefore does not implement the invariant used by either live path.

## Diagnosis and recommendation

This is data loss for a sequence such as ID 42 with partial content first and final content plus tool metadata later. Running the documented repair keeps the partial row and drops the final one. Because the script advertises a non-destructive repair and defaults to a separate output file, silent semantic truncation is especially surprising.

Please either buffer duplicate-bearing messages so later snapshots can merge into the retained row, or make a first pass that records the last merged value per stable ID and a second pass that writes the original order. The merge policy should be shared with `api/models.py` if practical so the three code paths cannot drift.

## Test plan

`tests/test_repair_duplicate_message_snapshots.py:6-16` currently checks only same-source rejection. Add a source containing a partial assistant snapshot followed by the same ID with completed content, reasoning, and tool metadata. Assert that output contains one row, preserves first-occurrence ordering, and contains the merged final fields. Also cover a later empty content field so it cannot erase earlier non-empty content.

payload.author: b3nw
payload.title: fix(sidebar): keep profile-agnostic Claude Code sessions visible under named profiles

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## The listing fix is right for non-isolated deployments ✅ — but it leaks across the profile-isolation boundary in 3 places

Thanks @b3nw — the core idea is correct: profile-agnostic Claude Code sessions (`profile: None`, `source_tag: claude_code`) should stay visible under a named profile in a normal multi-profile deployment, and `_is_profile_agnostic_foreign_session` gated by `not _is_isolated_profile_mode()` is the right shape. Ordinary root behavior, other-profile tagged rows, `_profiles_match()` semantics, read-only serialization, mutation refusals, and duplicate suppression all check out.

I ran the full gate (Codex + 5-shard suite) with a focus on profile isolation, because that's the load-bearing invariant here (profiles are islands). The suite is clean, but Codex reproduced 3 isolation leaks — the exemption doesn't fully respect isolated mode. Since these are cross-profile boundary breaks, I can't ship it yet, but they're all the same missing guard applied in different spots.

### 1. (CORE) `api/routes.py:2454` — cross-profile leak in an isolated `profiles/default` deployment
In an isolated `default` deployment, `_profiles_match(None, "default")` succeeds *before* the isolation-gated exception is evaluated, so global Claude Code transcripts stay listed. A probe reproduced the leak. **Fix:** when isolated, explicitly exclude `_is_profile_agnostic_foreign_session(s)` even when `_profiles_match()` returns true — and add an isolated-`default` regression case (the current tests omit it).

### 2. (CORE) `api/routes.py:13220` (+ `:26265`, `:5429`) — the hidden sessions are still directly *accessible* in isolated mode
This is the bigger one: visibility was gated, but access wasn't. The detail-load exemption ignores `_is_isolated_profile_mode()`, so `GET /api/session` returned **200** for a global Claude Code transcript in an isolated `user1` probe — even though the sidebar hides it. The same gap exists in `/api/session/import_cli` (`:26265`) and external sharing (`:5429`). Hiding a row in the list but leaving it readable/importable/shareable across the isolation boundary defeats the purpose. **Fix:** fail closed with 404 for profile-agnostic foreign rows in isolated mode *before* loading messages, importing, or sharing.

### 3. (CORE) `api/routes.py:556` — the predicate is broader than genuine read-only external rows
`_is_profile_agnostic_foreign_session()` currently accepts `profile=None` plus a Claude source marker **even with `read_only=False` and `session_source="webui"`** — so it can widen beyond true external rows. **Fix:** require all of: absent profile, canonical supported `source_tag`, `read_only=True`, and external-agent provenance. Update the new fixtures to match the real producer shape (right now they don't exercise the writable/non-external negative case).

### The through-line
The visibility exemption needs to travel with an isolation guard *everywhere* the row is touched — listing (1), access/import/share (2) — and the predicate that identifies these rows needs to be exactly the producer's shape, not a superset (3). Add a single `is isolated AND profile-agnostic-foreign → fail closed / exclude` check applied at the list scope and each access entrypoint, tighten the predicate, and this holds. Marking `gate-fail`; happy to re-gate as soon as it lands. Good concept — it just needs to respect the isolation boundary fully.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Thanks @b3nw — this is real progress. The three isolation leaks from my last review are addressed: the sidebar scope now excludes profile-agnostic external rows in isolated mode even when `_profiles_match(None, "default")` is true (1), the predicate is correctly tightened to require `read_only=True` + `session_source="external_agent"` (3), and detail-load + share now have isolated-mode guards (2, partially). The main sidebar predicate and the non-isolated common case both verify clean, and the tightened predicate correctly rejects writable/non-external rows.

I re-ran the profile-isolation gate (Codex + suite, isolation-focused) at the exact head `8c0b93b`. The suite is green, but the guard doesn't yet travel with the row at **four more session-read entrypoints** — same defect class as before ("hide the row in the list, but it's still directly reachable"), just in spots the last round didn't cover. Two are CORE (content actually served), two are SILENT (full load before the guard). Marking `gate-fail`; these are all the same one-line `isolated AND profile-agnostic-foreign → fail closed` check applied at the missed entrypoints.

### 1. (CORE) `api/routes.py:26180` — CLI import returns a hidden transcript in isolated mode
The import handler (`_handle_session_import_cli`) has no profile-agnostic guard before `Session.load()` / `get_cli_session_messages()`, so an isolated client can import and receive a global Claude Code transcript that the sidebar hides. **Your new test `tests/test_claude_code_profile_agnostic_detail_load.py:197` is vacuous here** — it only passes because the test environment returns zero messages, so it never proves the reader is blocked. **Fix:** add the isolated-mode metadata guard immediately after resolving `sid`, before any sidecar/message load; and make the test return NON-empty messages while asserting they're never read.

### 2. (CORE) `api/routes.py:18290` — gateway SSE snapshot leaks agnostic rows + titles
`/api/sessions/gateway/stream`'s initial snapshot calls unscoped `get_cli_sessions()` instead of applying the new isolated predicate, so isolated clients still receive profile-agnostic Claude rows (including content-derived titles) over SSE. **Fix:** filter the snapshot with the same active-profile/agnostic rules the sidebar builder now uses.

### 3. (SILENT) `api/routes.py:12847` — detail load fully hydrates before the guard
The stored external session is fully loaded (and may undergo reconciliation) before the isolated detail guard runs. **Fix:** fetch metadata only, run both visibility checks, then upgrade to a full session only for an authorized `messages=1` request.

### 4. (SILENT) `api/routes.py:5416` — share does a full load before authorization
Sharing a stored external sidecar performs a full `get_session()` load before the auth check. **Fix:** call `get_session(sid, metadata_only=True)` here; the existing `_ensure_full_session_before_mutation()` at line 5431 already does the post-authorization upgrade.

### The through-line (same as last time)
The isolation guard has to travel with the row at *every* entrypoint that can resolve it by id and return its content or title: listing ✅, detail ⚠️ (guard runs too late), share ⚠️ (loads first), import ❌, gateway SSE ❌. Add the `isolated AND profile-agnostic-foreign → fail closed` check (metadata-only, before any load) at import (1) and gateway SSE (2), and move the existing detail/share guards ahead of the full load (3, 4). Then de-vacuum the import test. Once those land I'll re-gate — the concept and the listing/predicate work are solid.

payload.author: Paladin173
payload.title: Scope gateway SSE probe and honor Last-Event-ID on /api/chat/stream

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Good direction — honoring `Last-Event-ID` is the right call — but the resume logic collapses "no cursor" and "invalid cursor" into one `None`, which breaks replay in 3 places

Thanks @Paladin173 — scoping the gateway probe and honoring `Last-Event-ID` is exactly the right fix for the hermes-android#58 contract, and the docs + tests are a nice touch. I ran a full gate (Codex correctness pass + 5-shard suite). The suite is clean, but Codex reproduced 3 CORE issues with route-level probes. They all trace to one root cause, so they collapse into a single clean fix.

### Root cause: cursor *presence* and cursor *validity* are conflated into `None`
Right now a malformed / foreign / ahead-of-stream cursor resolves to the same `None` as "no cursor supplied at all." Those are semantically opposite: "no cursor" means fresh-subscribe (no replay), but "invalid/foreign cursor" means the client *asked* to resume and we couldn't honor it — which must **replay from the start** so no events are silently skipped. Carrying a distinct `resume_requested` (presence) flag alongside the parsed seq fixes all three findings below.

### 1. (CORE) `api/routes.py:17457` — `Last-Event-ID` can override an explicit query cursor
A malformed/foreign explicit query cursor (`after_seq`/`after_event_id`) resolves to `None`, which then lets the `Last-Event-ID` header override it. That can skip journal events that previously replayed from start. **Fix:** decide explicit-cursor precedence by query-parameter **presence**, not successful parsing — never consult the header when an explicit cursor was supplied (even an unparseable one).

### 2. (CORE) `api/routes.py:17611` (+ `:17681`, `:17887`) — invalid/foreign cursor silently drains a truncated buffer, and a huge same-run cursor filters the terminal event
Because `None` conflates "no cursor" with "bad cursor," a malformed/foreign reconnect cursor bypasses replay + gap detection and silently drains a truncated buffer. Separately, a huge same-run cursor is clamped to the snapshot's terminal sequence at `:17681`, so the terminal event gets filtered at `:17887` and a dead stream returns an empty replay. **Fix:** preserve cursor presence separately, and normalize invalid / foreign / ahead-of-stream cursors to **replay-from-start** *before* gap-checking and dedup — don't clamp an ahead-of-stream cursor onto the terminal fence.

### 3. (CORE) `api/routes.py:17831` — the runner-local path ignores the resolved header cursor → duplicate events
The configured `runner-local` path calls `_runner_stream_cursor_from_query(qs)`, which returns `None` for header-only reconnects, so it ignores the `Last-Event-ID` you resolved upstream. Runner clients therefore replay from the beginning and **duplicate events** — the exact bug this PR sets out to fix, just on the runner adapter. **Fix:** pass the resolved cursor into `_stream_runner_run_events` (retaining explicit-query precedence), and add a focused header-only runner-reconnect regression test.

### What's already solid
29 focused tests pass for valid replay boundaries, fresh subscribe, gateway probe states, runner streaming, and Kanban cursor behavior — so the happy paths and the probe-scoping both check out. It's specifically the invalid/foreign/ahead-of-stream cursor edges + the runner fallback that need the presence/validity split.

Introduce the `resume_requested` presence flag + normalize-invalid-to-replay-from-start rule, thread the resolved cursor into the runner path, and this becomes a clean ship. Marking `gate-fail` — happy to re-gate as soon as it lands. Nice work.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## r2: the precedence split landed cleanly ✅ — 2 of the 3 r1 findings are resolved. Ahead-of-stream normalization + the runner path still need work, and the rewrite added one equality off-by-one.

Nice turnaround, @Paladin173 — the `(after_seq, resume_requested)` split is exactly right, and it fully fixed the main-stream precedence: a malformed/foreign explicit query cursor is no longer overridden by `Last-Event-ID`, and an invalid/foreign cursor now replays-from-start instead of draining a truncated buffer. Two down.

I re-gated the new head (Codex + 5-shard suite). The suite is clean (only the 2 known env flakes). But 3 CORE issues remain — and they share one theme, so there's a clean meta-fix.

### The meta-issue: each consumer re-derives instead of consuming the resolved cursor
The resume decision has ~4 consumers — the active snapshot buffer, the dead-stream journal reader, runner-local, and kanban. The precedence split fixed the *entry* resolution, but the individual consumers still make their own ahead/equality/re-parse decisions, so the invariant leaks at the edges. Findings 2 and 3 are both "a consumer didn't use the resolved `(resume_after_seq, resume_requested)`." Centralizing — every consumer derives *only* from that pair, with ahead-of-stream normalized to replay-from-start exactly once, upstream — collapses all three.

### 1. (CORE) `api/routes.py:17703` — a valid cursor *equal* to the snapshot cutoff double-sends retained events
`after_seq < snapshot_cutoff_seq` treats equality as "ahead," leaving the cutoff at the buffer-head fence. A probe with cursor `105` emitted IDs `100..106`, and `static/messages.js:5591` appends the duplicated token text with no event-ID dedup. This is a new off-by-one from the rewrite. **Fix:** define ahead as strictly `after_seq > snapshot_cutoff_seq`; equality must contribute `after_seq` to the drain dedup bound (the event *at* the cursor is already delivered, the ones after are not).

### 2. (CORE) `api/routes.py:17653` (+ `:17899`) — numeric ahead-of-stream cursors are still never normalized to replay-from-start
This is the other half of r1 finding #2. On a truncated active buffer, `floor >= replay_max_seq` falsely declares coverage, replays nothing after `999`, and drains only the retained `100..106` tail — silently losing `1..99`. And the dead-stream path at `:17899` passes `999` straight to the journal reader, emitting an empty SSE response for a journal that actually holds events `1..2`. **Fix:** normalize `after_seq > snapshot_cutoff_seq` to `0` before active gap-coverage/replay; for dead streams, retain the journal summary and normalize against its authoritative `last_seq` before `_replay_run_journal`. (Also: the mock at `tests/test_run_journal_routes.py:1122` needs to filter by `after_seq` and assert the actual replay body — right now it can't catch this class.)

### 3. (CORE) `api/routes.py:17868` — runner-local still discards the resolved precedence decision
This is r1 finding #3 — still open. The runner path reparses `after_event_id` (without `stream_id`) and re-reads `Last-Event-ID` instead of consuming the resolved cursor. Probes forwarded header `run_1:9` despite an explicit `after_event_id=malformed`, and forwarded `2` for a foreign `after_event_id=foreign:2` — both can skip runner events. **Fix:** preserve explicit opaque-`cursor` precedence, but derive all `after_seq`/`after_event_id`/header behavior exclusively from `(resume_after_seq, resume_requested)`; invalid/foreign cursors pass no cursor (full replay), and numeric ahead cursors get validated against the runner's authoritative last event first.

### Bottom line
You're genuinely close — the hard conceptual part (presence vs validity) is done and correct. What's left is making every consumer honor that decision instead of re-deriving it, and normalizing ahead-of-stream in one place. Marking `gate-fail`; happy to re-gate as soon as this lands. Thanks for the fast, precise iteration.

## Gate at head `2a2f838c45`: the runner-cursor provenance finding is fixed ✅ — one adjacent live-reconnect edge remains

Great iteration, @Paladin173. I re-gated fresh at the current head and confirmed the CORE finding from the last round is genuinely resolved:

- ✅ **All four required runner-provenance probes pass**: `Last-Event-ID: event:2` (header-only opaque) resumes; `after_event_id=event:2&after_seq=2` (paired) resumes; a malformed cursor *without* a valid paired seq still blocks the header and replays from start; a malformed cursor *paired* with a valid `after_seq` forwards the resolved seq. The 4-tuple `_chat_stream_resume_cursor()` → `_handle_sse_stream` runner handoff carries provenance correctly now.
- ✅ 71 focused neighboring SSE/gateway checks pass (cutoff equality, dead-stream 404 ordering, fresh-subscribe no-replay, gateway probe scoping, the 4 consumers).

One new blocker on an **adjacent** path — a live reconnect can silently lose its initial events:

### [CORE / data-loss] Ahead `Last-Event-ID` + unknown snapshot cutoff drops every initial event — `api/routes.py:17765`
The ahead-cursor normalization is guarded by `snapshot_cutoff_seq is not None`:
```python
if snapshot_cutoff_seq is not None and after_seq > snapshot_cutoff_seq:
    after_seq = 0
```
When the subscription snapshot has **no** `last_event_id` (`snapshot_cutoff_seq is None`), a positive ahead cursor is *not* normalized — it stays as the live dedup bound. Reproduced against the real handler: header `run_1:999`, unknown snapshot cutoff, then `run_1:1` + `stream_end` at `run_1:2` → **empty SSE body**; `999` is installed as the dedup bound (line ~17823) and both events — including the terminal `stream_end` fence — are discarded (line ~18080), stalling the stream on heartbeats. `origin/master` ignored the header on this path and delivered both events, so this is a new regression.

**Fix:** treat an unknown, non-truncated snapshot cutoff as fence `0` before the ahead-cursor normalization (so a positive client cursor can't become the live dedup bound with no cutoff to bound it); if frames were dropped while the cutoff is unknown, keep fail-closed recovery rather than silently draining nothing. Add a handler regression asserting events `1` and `2` emit exactly once and the subscriber is released, for `Last-Event-ID` ahead + `snapshot_cutoff_seq=None`.

That's the only thing left — the hard part (runner-cursor provenance) is done and every other consumer path is clean. Re-request review when it lands and I'll re-gate at the new head.

Thanks @nesquena-hermes — the presence/validity conflation was exactly the bug, and your three findings all traced to it. Fixed in 1331e845 (on top of the merged master).

**Why I missed it:** I treated the parsed seq as the whole signal and didn't carry cursor *presence* separately, so "no cursor" and "invalid/foreign/ahead-of-stream cursor" both collapsed to `None`. My tests only covered the valid-cursor and no-cursor happy paths — I never exercised the invalid/foreign/ahead edges, and the runner path reused the query-only helper. The fail-before checks I ran confirmed the new tests failed pre-fix, but I didn't have tests for the edges Codex caught.

**What changed:**

- `_chat_stream_resume_cursor()` now returns `(after_seq, resume_requested)` instead of a bare seq. Presence and validity stay separate: any supplied cursor (query params, `replay=1`, or `Last-Event-ID`) sets `resume_requested=True`; an invalid/foreign/unparseable one resolves to `after_seq=None` and is normalized to **replay-from-start** so no events are silently skipped.

1. **Query-over-header precedence by presence** (`_chat_stream_resume_cursor`): a supplied-but-unparseable explicit cursor never falls through to the header. Covered by `test_chat_stream_resume_cursor_explicit_unparseable_query_blocks_header`.
2. **Invalid/foreign → replay-from-start, and no clamp onto the terminal fence** (`_sse_replay_run_journal_gap_checked`): invalid cursors are normalized to `after_seq=0` before gap-checking/dedup; an ahead-of-stream cursor no longer clamps onto the snapshot cutoff (which was filtering the terminal frame and emptying the dead-stream replay). 3. **Runner path honors the header cursor** (`_handle_sse_stream`): the resolved `Last-Event-ID` is carried into `_stream_runner_run_events` (explicit query params still win), so header-only runner reconnects resume instead of duplicating. Covered by `test_runner_observe_reconnect_uses_last_event_id_header`.

**Fail-before proof:** with only the routes change stashed, the 4 new/updated edge tests fail (including the runner one returning `('run-1', None)` instead of `('run-1', 'run-1:5')`); applied, they pass.

payload.body:
## Summary

Reading `api/routes.py:17439-17918` at the current PR head (`3d70160bf`) and comparing the r2 delta against `1331e845f`, the query/header precedence, runner cursor handoff, dead-stream ahead-cursor handling, and equality dedup changes now address the earlier review findings. One live-stream edge remains: an ahead numeric cursor is still trusted when the subscribe snapshot has no parseable cutoff.

## Code reference

At `api/routes.py:17652-17668`, ahead-cursor normalization only runs when `snapshot_cutoff_seq` is known. Later, `api/routes.py:17725-17732` treats an unknown cutoff as permission to install the client cursor as the drain dedup bound:

```python
if snapshot_cutoff_seq is not None and after_seq > snapshot_cutoff_seq:
    after_seq = 0
...
if after_seq is not None and after_seq > 0:
    if snapshot_cutoff_seq is None or after_seq <= snapshot_cutoff_seq:
        replay_cutoff_seq = after_seq
```

For a newly created live channel whose snapshot has `last_event_id=None`, a request such as `after_seq=999` therefore replays after 999 and then filters every queued same-run frame with `seq <= 999`. Normal first events, including a terminal frame, can disappear and leave an empty/stalled SSE response. This is the same ahead-cursor failure mode that the known-cutoff and dead-stream branches now prevent (`api/routes.py:17904-17910`).

## Diagnosis / recommendation

An unknown snapshot cutoff cannot prove that a positive client cursor is in range. Normalize it to replay-from-start as well:

```python
if snapshot_cutoff_seq is None or after_seq > snapshot_cutoff_seq:
    after_seq = 0
```

This is conservative and consistent with the invalid/foreign cursor policy already documented by `_chat_stream_resume_cursor`. Once the channel has emitted a journaled event, `StreamChannel` supplies a parseable `last_event_id`, so valid reconnect cursors still use the normal in-range path.

## Test plan

The new equality test at `tests/test_run_journal_routes.py:1115-1167` correctly includes `offline_first_event_id` and exercises a known cutoff. Please add its unknown-cutoff counterpart: return a subscribe snapshot with `last_event_id=None`, queue `run_1:1` plus terminal `run_1:2`, request `after_seq=999`, and assert both frames survive (and the subscriber is released). The runner precedence probes at `tests/test_run_journal_routes.py:1334-1375` otherwise match the revised resolver contract.

I did not execute code from the PR worktree; this finding is from full-file and diff inspection.

Thanks @nesquena-hermes — the provenance framing is the precise root cause. The tuple carried the cursor *value* but not its *provenance*, so the runner handoff judged everything through the journal's `stream_id:seq` lens. That's wrong for the runner adapter, whose cursors are opaque. Fixed in `7a522724`.

**Why I missed it:** I fixed the runner to consume the resolved pair (r2) but kept gating the raw cursor on *journal* validity — so an opaque runner id like `event:2` (which the journal parser reads as a foreign run) was rejected, and a paired `after_seq` was read through the `after_event_id`-first journal parser, which swallowed it. I verified the r2 precedence probes but never probed an opaque/paired runner cursor.

**Fix:** the resolver now computes a distinct runner cursor *with provenance*, centrally, and the runner handoff passes it unchanged to `_stream_runner_run_events()`:

- **Paired opaque id resumes.** `after_event_id=event:2&after_seq=2` → runner gets `2`. `after_seq` is now read directly (new `_parse_run_journal_after_seq_value`) instead of through the `after_event_id`-first journal parser, which read `event:2` as a foreign run and returned `None` before reaching the seq.
- **Header-only opaque id resumes.** `Last-Event-ID: event:2` → runner gets `event:2`. The header branch no longer rejects a colon-cursor as "foreign" for the runner — the journal path still rejects it (`after_seq=None`), but the runner keys cursors per run independently.
- **Malformed + valid paired seq uses the seq.** `after_event_id=malformed&after_seq=5` → runner gets `5` (not the raw `malformed`).
- **Malformed/foreign WITHOUT a paired seq still replays from start.** `after_event_id=malformed` (+ header) and `foreign:2` both → runner gets `None` — the r2 malformed-blocks-header guarantee is unchanged.

**Verified against all your probes** (live, against the real resolver + runner handoff):

| Probe | Runner receives |
|---|---|
| `event:2` + `after_seq=2` | `2` ✓ resume |
| `malformed` + `after_seq=5` | `5` ✓ resume |
| header-only `event:2` | `event:2` ✓ resume |
| `malformed` only + header | `None` ✓ replay-from-start |
| `foreign:2` | `None` ✓ replay-from-start |
| `cursor=opaque-xyz` | `opaque-xyz` ✓ opaque precedence |

## Summary

Reading the complete PR diff, the full changed tests, and both production files at PR HEAD and `origin/master`, the session-aware routing direction is correct. The initial path now preserves the pre-canonicalization provider identity and passes it into current-upload and historical-image routing. There is one blocking retry-path regression: both credential-heal branches replace that preserved identity with the already-canonical provider before sanitizing retry history.

## Code reference

The initial path at `api/streaming.py:9183-9189` captures the requested identity before `_resolve_custom_provider_runtime_overrides()` can rewrite a named custom provider to `custom`. The retry path at `api/streaming.py:10220-10230` does this instead:

```python
if not resolved_provider:
    resolved_provider = _heal_rt.get("provider")
resolved_base_url = _runtime_preferred_base_url(
    _heal_rt, resolved_provider, configured_base_url
)
_session_requested_provider = resolved_provider
resolved_provider, resolved_api_key, resolved_base_url = _resolve_custom_provider_runtime_overrides(
```

At this point `resolved_provider` is normally already `custom`, so the guard does not reload the named provider and `_session_requested_provider` is downgraded from the original name to `custom`. The same overwrite is repeated at `api/streaming.py:11455-11465`. The retry sanitizer then receives the degraded value at `api/streaming.py:10257-10264` and `api/streaming.py:11492-11499`.

## Diagnosis / recommendation

Please preserve the original requested identity across healing, or take the explicit requested identity from the refreshed runtime result when it is available. The fix should have one helper or assignment shared by both retry branches, for example: prefer the refreshed runtime requested identity, then the existing `_session_requested_provider`, and only then `resolved_provider`. Do this before canonicalizing the refreshed provider.

The current tests in `tests/test_session_aware_vision_routing.py:73-102` prove direct helper behavior, but they do not exercise either credential-heal call site. That is why this regression remains invisible despite the helper assertions passing.

## Verification step

Add one regression per healing branch using a named provider whose text-only capability exists only under `providers.<name>.models.<model>`. Start with a canonical runtime provider of `custom`, trigger credential healing, and assert the retried `_sanitize_messages_for_api()` still receives the named requested provider and strips historical `image_url` parts. payload.author: X-Shihai
payload.title: fix(sidebar): last-writer-wins title reconcile for state.db renames (#3986)

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## The reconcile direction is right, but `last_activity_at` is the wrong clock — it loses renames

Thanks @X-Shihai — the goal (make agent-side renames win when they're genuinely newer) is real and #3986 is worth fixing. But an adversarial gate found the core mechanism is unsound as written, plus one brick-class edge. Two blockers at exact head `e0e6e31af`:

### 1. (data-loss) Later ordinary agent activity silently overwrites a legitimate WebUI rename — `api/models.py:6069`
`last_activity_at` is a **coarse activity clock, not a title-write clock.** On the agent side, `touch_session_activity()` advances `last_activity_at` on *any* activity (every TUI/CLI/Desktop message), while `set_session_title()` does **not** advance it. So the "state.db wrote the title last" inference is wrong: a user renames a session in the WebUI, then sends one ordinary message in the TUI, and `last_activity_at` now exceeds the sidecar `updated_at` — so the reconcile replaces the fresh WebUI rename with the stale state.db title. Verified through `all_sessions()`: `title="New WebUI rename"` → `display_title="Old state title"`.

**Fix:** drop `state_db_is_newer` and restore `_sidebar_title_is_generic_webui(title)` as the *only* override condition (i.e. state.db title wins only when the WebUI title is still a generic auto-name). Reintroduce non-generic last-writer-wins reconciliation **only** once both stores expose a **title-specific** timestamp/revision that is bumped atomically by every title mutation on both sides (WebUI save *and* agent `set_session_title`) — an activity clock can't stand in for a title-write clock. That's a coordinated agent+WebUI change, so it's a larger design step than this PR.

### 2. (brick) Unguarded `float()` on sidecar `updated_at` — `api/models.py:6071`
A nonnumeric/malformed sidecar `updated_at` raises `ValueError` from `all_sessions()`, which breaks `/api/sessions` entirely → sidebar session switching and restore stop working for everyone with such a row. The new `float(...)` is unguarded. **Fix:** parse defensively, treat invalid/non-finite values as unknown, and preserve the sidecar title in that case.

Focused suite is green (69 tests) and the column-absence guard + equal/missing-timestamp handling are correct — the issue is specifically the clock choice and the unguarded parse. Happy to re-gate once the override reverts to generic-only (the safe, shippable subset) or a title-specific revision lands.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Re-gate at `a04e9acb7`: the `float()` guard is fixed, but the core mechanism still loses WebUI renames

Thanks for the quick turnaround @X-Shihai — the unguarded `float()` on `_state_db_last_activity_at` is now try/except-wrapped, so the `/api/sessions` brick edge is closed. 👍

But I want to be precise about the original bounce, because the re-push comment reads it as a stale-base issue — it wasn't. My finding was about the **authority signal itself**, and it still stands at this head. The PR decides the state.db title is authoritative when:

```python
state_db_is_newer = bool(
    state_db_last_activity_at
    and state_db_last_activity_at > float(session.get('updated_at') or 0)
)
```

`last_activity_at` is **not a title-write clock — it's a coarse activity clock.** I verified this against the agent source that writes it (`hermes_state.py`, the `_touch_activity` durable-activity stamp):

> "Stamp durable mid-turn session activity (observation-only). Called (rate-limited) from `AIAgent._touch_activity` so gateway/CLI surfaces and stall consumers observe **API/tool/compaction activity even when no new message row has been written yet**."

So `last_activity_at` advances on **any** agent turn, tool call, or compaction — not on title changes. That breaks the intended last-writer-wins semantics on the exact flow #3986 cares about:

1. User renames a session in the WebUI → sidecar `updated_at` = T1, title = "My rename".
2. The same session does *any* ordinary agent activity later (one TUI message, a tool call, a compaction) → state.db `last_activity_at` = T2 > T1, **with the state.db title unchanged** (still the old auto-title).
3. Next sidebar build: `state_db_is_newer` is true, so the stale state.db title clobbers "My rename". **The user's rename is silently lost** — the exact data-loss #3986 is trying to prevent, now triggered by unrelated activity.

The `updated_at`-vs-`last_activity_at` comparison is comparing a *title-write* timestamp on one side against a *general-activity* timestamp on the other, so they're not comparable as "who wrote the title last."

### What a correct fix needs
A real title-write clock on the state.db side — compare like-for-like. Options:
- If the agent stamps a title-specific timestamp (e.g. a `title_updated_at` column, or a `last_activity_provenance`/`last_activity_description` that marks a rename), key off *that*, not `last_activity_at`.
- If no such signal exists in state.db today, this needs a **coordinated agent-side change** (add a title-write timestamp) before the WebUI can reconcile correctly — the WebUI can't derive title-write-recency from the data it currently has.

I'd rather not merge a heuristic that trades one silent title-loss (#3986's WebUI-loses) for another (rename-then-any-activity → WebUI-rename-loses). Happy to help scope the agent-side signal if you want to take that route. Keeping `gate-fail` until the authority signal is title-specific.

payload.body:
## Summary

Reading both substantive files at PR HEAD and on `origin/master`, plus the complete diff for #6871, this change is correctly scoped. The new base control rule fixes the browser-native exception to inherited typography, while the table-filter override avoids changing the intentional monospace behavior of technical controls inside message tables. I do not see a blocking issue and recommend merging.

## Code reference

At `static/style.css:26-30` and `static/style.css:2414-2420` on the PR branch, the relevant cascade is:

```css
button,input,select,textarea{font-family:var(--font-ui);}
.msg-body table{border-collapse:collapse;width:100%;margin:8px 0;font-size:12px;}
.markdown-table-filter{display:block;/* ... */font:inherit;font-family:var(--font-ui);font-size:12px;}
.markdown-table-sort{display:flex;/* ... */font:inherit;font-weight:inherit;/* ... */}
```

The explicit `font-family` after `font:inherit` on `.markdown-table-filter` is necessary. The shorthand resets the family, so the new global element selector alone would not fix that component. Conversely, `.markdown-table-sort` intentionally keeps `font:inherit`; it inherits the technical font established by `.msg-body table` at `static/style.css:5956`. The unrelated cron/editor surface remains protected by the more specific `.detail-form-row textarea` rule at `static/style.css:6535`.

The regression fixture at `tests/test_typography_contract.py:161-175` now includes all four native control types and representative specialized controls. Its computed-style assertions at `tests/test_typography_contract.py:279-288` cover both sides of the contract:

```python
for control_id, font in native_control_fonts.items():
    assert "UiFontSentinel" in font, f"{control_id} computed {font!r}"
assert "UiFontSentinel" in component_fonts["markdownTableFilter"]
assert "MonoFontSentinel" in component_fonts["markdownTableSort"]
assert "MonoFontSentinel" in component_fonts["detailFormTextarea"]
```

## Diagnosis / recommendation

The cascade behavior matches the stated intent. Plain `button`, `input`, `select`, and `textarea` elements receive `--font-ui`; later class rules and higher-specificity component declarations can still select or inherit `--font-mono`. This avoids a blanket `font:inherit` reset, which could also alter native control sizing and weight. No code change is requested.

## Verification

The GitHub `test` check is green for commit `3be73657f976b4c6664391c7664426a1f37bcfae`. I reviewed the Playwright fixture and assertions statically; per read-only review policy I did not execute code from the contributor worktree. A final manual smoke check should switch between a proportional UI skin and the monospace Nous skin, then compare a plain settings control, the markdown table filter, table sort headers, and a cron detail textarea.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

I reviewed both commits and the four-file diff. The data flow is coherent: release-channel responses keep `latest_version`, branch-channel responses gain `latest_tag`, and the status renderer consumes either shape through one WebUI-first fallback. The spacing follow-up in `9f4b6a4` fixes the only visible formatting defect in the original revision. I do not see a blocker.

## Code reference

At `api/updates.py:1223-1267`, the release check remains authoritative and the tag probe is reused only for the branch fallthrough:

```python
release_info = self._check_repo_release(repo, repo_name, channel)
if release_info:
    return release_info
latest_tag, current_tag = self._release_tags(repo)
```

The branch payload adds fields only when values exist, at `api/updates.py:1260-1266`, preserving the previous response shape for repositories with no release tags. The new cases in `tests/test_updates.py:384-438` cover both populated tags and the absence case.

The UI side at `static/panels.js:11922-11951` uses `webui.latest_tag || webui.latest_version` before falling back to the agent values. That ordering is correct for mixed response modes and keeps the displayed tag tied to the WebUI update status whenever WebUI data exists. Both up-to-date and updates-available branches append the same localized suffix. `static/i18n.js:15` and the corresponding locale entries use the existing positional placeholder convention rather than interpolating text directly.

## Diagnosis and recommendation

The change is display-only and does not alter update eligibility, channel selection, or the `behind` computation. It also handles the stable-channel early return correctly because that response already exposes `latest_version`; the frontend fallback means it does not depend on `latest_tag` being present.

One non-blocking test gap remains: the backend assertions do not protect the frontend fallback order or the separator that required the follow-up commit. A short source-shape test around `checkUpdatesNow()` should assert both `latest_tag || latest_version` and the explicit space before `t("settings_latest_tag_suffix", ...)`. That would prevent a later refactor from recreating the cramped status text or selecting the agent tag while WebUI tag data is available.

## Verification

I inspected the complete changed backend/test files and the relevant full frontend files, without executing PR-authored code. Greptile is green. GitHub reports the branch behind `master`; update it and rerun the update tests before merge.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Solid optimization — one real gap: the compact payload drops the live message `_ts` (timestamp)

Thanks @allenliang2022 — this is a well-scoped payload reduction, and an adversarial gate confirmed almost all of it is safe:

- At most one live assistant message exists, so `messages=[]` + `last_assistant_text`/`last_reasoning_text` faithfully reconstructs it; interleaved tools stay in `tool_calls` + `activity_rows`. ✓
- Divergent `preview`/`snippet` values survive; only genuinely display-equivalent equal pairs are dropped. ✓
- `tid` is safely redundant with the retained `id`; thinking text stays in `row.text`; removed row metadata (`order_index`, `display_hint`, null event IDs) is genuinely redundant given array order + scene identity. ✓
- The pagination guard (`not load_messages or msg_limit is None`) is safe — `messages=0` still carries the snapshot, paginated follow-ups don't replace `S.session`, and a snapshot-availability race replays the journal from cursor zero. ✓
- The projection never mutates canonical state (every container copied, nested values read-only). ✓
- 20 focused projection/route/reattach/replay/Anchor-scene tests pass and the base RED conditions are real (non-vacuous). ✓

### The blocker — `_ts` is lost on the synthesized live message

When `messages=[]` is substituted, the compact payload no longer carries the canonical live assistant message's **`_ts` (timestamp)**. The frontend rebuilds that single live row from the `last_*` strings, but with no `_ts` it gets a wrong/missing timestamp for the recovered in-flight turn — a real, if small, recovery regression. Your added tests don't assert `_ts`, so it slips through green.

**Fix (small):**
1. `api/routes.py:~3776` — preserve the canonical live message's `_ts` in the compact payload (e.g. carry it as a top-level `last_message_ts` or keep a metadata-only message skeleton with just `_ts`).
2. `static/sessions.js:~1036` — restore that `_ts` onto the synthesized assistant message when reconstructing from `last_*`.
3. Add an end-to-end projection/recovery assertion that the recovered `_ts` equals the canonical value.

Everything else is ready — full 5-shard suite is green (only the 2 known pre-existing box flakes). Fix the `_ts` round-trip + add the assertion and re-request; this is close.

## Summary

Reviewed the updated head `bafd601` against `origin/master`, including the full changed test files and the surrounding session-route/recovery code. I do not see a static code blocker. This matters because the same canonical snapshot can be reused by stream recovery after the response has been serialized.

```python
call = dict(raw_call)
```

The transport boundary is the right layer for this optimization. It avoids changing durable recovery data or teaching the browser another versioned snapshot shape. payload.body:
## Summary

The partial-body fix in `static/panels.js:11873-11879` is correct, but the fallback mirror is scoped more narrowly than the setting it mirrors. Reading the PR head `f82cb0f` alongside `api/config.py:80-89` and the GET/POST settings routes, `auto_scroll_follow` is stored in the one WebUI `settings.json`; `/api/settings` calls `load_settings()` directly at `api/routes.py:12493-12495` and does not select a profile-specific settings file. The new browser mirror is instead keyed by `S.activeProfile` at `static/boot.js:1364-1387`.

That mismatch leaves the original failure reproducible. If the global server setting is OFF, profile A has already populated its mirror, and the browser later opens profile B for the first time while the settings request fails, the deferred read at `static/boot.js:3629-3635` finds no B entry and returns ON. The saved global OFF value exists, and the browser has a last-known copy, but the profile namespace prevents using it.

## Code reference

The fallback explicitly treats a missing current-profile entry as a fresh default:

```js
const v=map[_autoScrollFollowProfileKey()];
if(v!==undefined&&v!==null) return v===1;
return true;
```

Meanwhile the backend authority is global:

```python
SETTINGS_FILE = STATE_DIR / "settings.json"
...
settings = load_settings()
```

The behavioral test at `tests/test_issue6819_auto_scroll_follow_persistence.py:188-197` currently codifies per-profile divergence, but that is not a state the server can persist.

## Diagnosis / recommendation

Please make the mirror contract match the backend contract. The smallest fix is one global last-known boolean (or a JSON record with one authoritative value), rather than a profile map. If per-profile appearance settings are intentional, that needs a backend storage/routing change first; the current hybrid cannot reliably recover the server value.

## Verification step

Add a regression that saves OFF successfully while one profile is active, changes `S.activeProfile` to a profile with no mirror entry, simulates the next settings fetch failing, runs the deferred reapply, and still expects OFF. Keep the existing partial-body assertions and the successful-fetch deferred-write ordering; both of those parts look sound.

Fixed in `0f3e5496` — reverted to a **single global last-known value**:

- `_persistAutoScrollFollow` / `_readPersistedAutoScrollFollow` now store one scalar (`'1'`/`'0'`) under `hermes-auto-scroll-follow` — no profile map.

Removed `_autoScrollFollowProfileKey`, `_autoScrollFollowDeferredPersist`, `_autoScrollFollowDeferredReapply` entirely — net −99 lines vs the previous head.

One note for the record: the earlier profile-namespacing came from Greptile's review advice ("must be profile-namespaced rather than global") which assumed per-profile settings — your review correctly identified the global backend contract. Happy to adjust anything else.

payload.body:
## Summary

I reviewed the final five-commit series, including the maintainer-requested change in `0f3e549`. The current implementation now matches the backend ownership model: `auto_scroll_follow` is a global setting, so its outage fallback is a single global last-known value rather than a profile-keyed map. The patch also keeps partial settings responses from turning the option back on. I do not see a blocking correctness issue in the current diff.

## Code reference

The mirror is deliberately small and fail-safe at `static/boot.js:3234-3251`:

```javascript
function _readPersistedAutoScrollFollow(){
  try{
    const raw=localStorage.getItem(_AUTO_SCROLL_FOLLOW_STORAGE_KEY);
```

The full helper distinguishes an explicit saved off value from a missing or malformed value, with the latter retaining the established default-on behavior. The successful boot path persists the server value at `static/boot.js:3280-3291`; the settings-fetch failure path reads the mirror at `static/boot.js:3422-3432`. This is consistent with the global `SETTINGS_FILE` and unscoped `load_settings()` contract in `api/config.py:89` and `api/config.py:9439-9470`.

The second half of the fix is at `static/panels.js:8526-8554`. `_applySavedSettingsUi` now checks ownership before touching runtime state, so a partial response cannot reinterpret an absent property as enabled. The checkbox and save paths at `static/panels.js:9032-9055` and `static/panels.js:11931-11953` update the mirror only from an explicit boolean value returned or submitted by the settings flow.

## Diagnosis

The latest revision removes the earlier timing problem entirely. There is no profile resolution dependency, no deferred write/read flag, and no cookie visibility assumption. A successful request refreshes the global mirror immediately; a failed request restores the last explicit value immediately. If storage is unavailable or contains an unknown value, the helper returns enabled, preserving the product default rather than creating an accidental opt-out.

## Verification

`tests/test_issue6819_auto_scroll_follow_persistence.py:15-178` covers the scalar storage shape, saved off, missing/corrupt fallback, profile changes, partial-body no-clobber, and both persistence paths. I inspected that extracted-helper test and all changed source files but did not execute PR-authored code under the scheduled read-only policy. Greptile is green.
