payload.body:
## Re-review: one prior identity blocker remains, plus one label-provenance gap

The prewarmed-row ordering fix is good: a configured label such as `Operator Label` now wins over the endpoint label on the live path. The targeted authority/grammar files pass in the sandbox (`6 passed`), and the existing IPv4/dotted-host/localhost identity slice passes (`3 passed, 15 deselected`).

Two deterministic gaps remain at exact head `25b159cb5cde`:

1. **A valid single-label `host:port` provider ID is still misparsed.** `_custom_endpoint_slugs_for_base_url()` accepts any `urlparse(...).hostname` and emits `custom:{host}:{port}`, so `http://llm:8080/v1` produces `custom:llm:8080`. Backend `_custom_slug_rest_looks_like_host_port()` and frontend `_customSlugLooksLikeHostPort()` accept only IP literals, `localhost`, or names containing a dot. Both therefore reject the producer's valid `llm:8080` shape and parse `@custom:llm:8080:qwen3` as provider `custom:llm` with model/label `8080:qwen3`.

2. **An explicit label equal to the model ID loses its configured-label authority.** Both new maps treat `label == id` as proof that no label was supplied. That collapses the distinct inputs `models: ["model-a"]` and `models: [{"id":"model-a","label":"model-a"}]`; in the explicit-dict case, an endpoint or derived label can replace the operator's literal label.

### Required fix

- Make the backend and frontend parsers accept every hostname shape the endpoint-slug producer can emit, including single-label Docker/LAN names. Prefer a single unambiguous grammar or longest-known-provider-prefix match over mirrored heuristics. Define IPv6 behavior explicitly.
- Preserve label provenance from the raw configured item. Check for a nonblank `label` field on a dict (or carry an `explicit_label` bit) rather than inferring explicitness from `label != id`.
- Add production-path regressions for:
  - `http://llm:8080/v1` → `custom:llm:8080` → `@custom:llm:8080:qwen3`, expecting provider `custom:llm:8080` and model/label `qwen3`;
  - the tagged-model variant;
  - cold and prewarmed paths with `{"id":"model-a","label":"model-a"}`, alongside the existing bare-string controls.

The current tests are green for their covered cases, but none exercises these two omitted contracts.

## Gate at head `4a017d5419`: both prior must-fixes are genuinely fixed — one new routing-vs-display inconsistency remains

Thanks @rodrigogs — this is excellent convergence work. I independently confirmed both items from the last review are properly closed at this head:

- ✅ **single-label `host:port` parse**: `http://llm:8080/v1` → `custom:llm:8080`, and `@custom:llm:8080:qwen3` parses correctly in **both** Python and the JS mirror. The consolidation into "the ONE grammar" (`_custom_slug_rest_is_endpoint_authority`) with an explicit IPv6 bracketed-literal contract, and the `_PY_WS_CLASS` whitespace-class parity between `static/ui.js` and Python, is exactly the single-unambiguous-grammar the review asked for.
- ✅ **`label == id` provenance**: reading a nonblank `label` key off the raw config item (rather than inferring from `label != id`) preserves `{"id":"model-a","label":"model-a"}` authority on both cold and prewarmed paths, and bare strings still derive. Confirmed.
- ✅ Both new test files are substantive and cover the required production cases (including a real loopback endpoint); 81 new + 57 neighboring custom-provider tests pass; `node --check` clean; full suite green.

One new blocker, reproduced — a **route-vs-display divergence** the longest-prefix union introduces:

### [CORE] A named custom provider can route to a different provider/model than the picker shows — `api/config.py:2679`
For `{name:"gw", base_url:"http://gw:8080/v1", models:["8080:free"]}`, the catalog emits `@custom:gw:8080:free` under `provider_id=custom:gw`. But `_known_custom_provider_slugs()` also adds the endpoint-derived alias `custom:gw:8080`, and longest-prefix parsing then resolves that ID as **provider `custom:gw:8080` / model `free`** — while `origin/master` (and the frontend, which honors the catalog's `custom:gw` boundary) resolve the same emitted row as **provider `custom:gw` / model `8080:free`**. So the backend route disagrees with both master and the displayed catalog boundary — the model is sent to a different provider than the picker shows (the #5511/#6817 route-hijack class).

And the new collision test `tests/test_custom_provider_label_grammar.py:188` (`test_configured_endpoint_beats_named_slug_for_same_shape`) currently **codifies this endpoint-first result** as expected, so it locks in the wrong behavior rather than catching it.

**Fix:** keep actual named/catalog provider IDs authoritative over endpoint-derived aliases — apply endpoint-authority parsing only when no named-provider prefix matches. Then correct `test_custom_provider_label_grammar.py:188` to expect provider `custom:gw` / model `8080:free`, and add an end-to-end catalog-row → resolver regression asserting the emitted `@custom:gw:8080:free` resolves to the SAME provider the catalog emitted it under.

That's the only thing between this and a merge — the grammar work itself is genuinely well done. Re-request review when the named-provider precedence is fixed and I'll re-gate at the new head.

## Re-gate at exact head `952c476e1cd1`

The named-provider precedence change closes the 2026-08-18 route-vs-display blocker. The resolver now checks named catalog slugs before endpoint-derived aliases, and the new catalog-row round trip pins the intended `custom:gw` / `8080:free` boundary.

One objective label-authority bug remains at `api/config.py:1401-1435`:

### [CORE] An ignored later duplicate can still supply the displayed label

`_configured_model_ids()` keeps the first occurrence of a model ID across both bare-string and dict entries. `_configured_model_label_overrides()` says it mirrors that first-occurrence contract, but it skips bare-string entries before recording their IDs in `seen`.

For this supported input:

```yaml
models:
  - model-a
  - id: model-a
    label: Later Duplicate
```

`_configured_model_ids()` accepts the first bare `model-a` and ignores the later duplicate, while `_configured_model_label_overrides()` returns `{"model-a": "Later Duplicate"}`. Both catalog paths can therefore combine the accepted first row with a label taken from an ignored later row. The displayed label no longer has the same configuration authority as the accepted model entry.

**Required fix:** resolve each list item's candidate ID and record it in `seen` before deciding whether that winning item can carry a label. Only the first occurrence may contribute an override, and only when that first occurrence is a dict with a nonblank `label`. The only difference between the two commits is the upstream rebase (`api/models.py`, `api/routes.py`, `static/i18n.js`, `static/index.html`, `static/messages.js`, docs, 7 unrelated test files). So "pre-fix" below means exactly the tree you read.

---

### 1. Gap 1 — single-label `host:port` misparse

Confirmed and fixed, and your diagnosis of the cause was exact: the producer accepted every `urlparse().hostname` shape while the two consumers demanded an IP literal, `localhost`, or a dot.

The predicate is no longer a name-shape heuristic; it is the grammar for the endpoint half of a slug, renamed to say so:

- backend `_custom_slug_rest_looks_like_host_port` → **`_custom_slug_rest_is_endpoint_authority`**
- frontend `_customSlugLooksLikeHostPort` → **`_customSlugIsEndpointAuthority`**

The rule, in full:

- `port` — 1–5 ASCII digits, 1..65535.
- `host` — any nonempty token holding no character a URL authority host cannot hold (no whitespace, `:` `/` `?` `#` `@` `[` `]`), not starting with `-` or `.`, not ending with `-`. A **trailing** dot is accepted: `ollama.internal.` is a legal root-anchored FQDN, `urlparse` hands it back verbatim, so the producer can emit `custom:ollama.internal.:8443`. Covers single-label Docker/LAN names (`llm`), dotted DNS names, IPv4 literals, `localhost`, punycode.
- `host` — or a bracketed literal whose contents are a **real IPv6 address**. Brackets alone are not enough.

**Longest-known-provider-prefix, as you suggested, in addition to the grammar.** One shape stays genuinely ambiguous by inspection: `@custom:gw:8080:free` is a valid reading either way. `_parse_provider_qualified_model_id` therefore takes an authoritative config lookup first (`_known_custom_provider_slugs` — named slugs ∪ endpoint slugs for every `custom_providers[].base_url` ∪ the active `model.base_url`), longest prefix wins, and only falls back to the grammar when config says nothing. A configured `custom:gw` gives model `8080:free`; a configured `http://gw:8080` gives model `free`. The frontend does the same against `_dynamicProviderIds`, the server-reported `provider_id` set from `/api/models` group metadata. The lookup is skipped entirely for ids with fewer than 3 colons, which is the common case.

**IPv6, explicit contract.** `urlparse` strips the URL's brackets, so a raw `custom:::1:11434` spelling is irreducibly ambiguous — `::1:11434` is itself a valid IPv6 address, so "address" and "address + port" cannot be told apart. Decision: **the bracketed `custom:[::1]:11434` form is the one the grammar parses**, and the producer emits it first. The unbracketed spellings stay in the slug set for backwards-compatible *matching* only (that set feeds membership checks, never new ids). `test_ipv6_unbracketed_form_is_not_part_of_the_grammar` pins the rejection so this is a contract, not an omission.

**The frontend was not actually a mirror, and I only established that by differential testing.** Two divergences, both in the bracketed branch, both shapes no hand-written table happened to hold:

| input | JS before | Python |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[dead:beef]:80` | `true` | `False` |
| `[1.2.3.4::]:80` | `true` | `False` |

Rebased onto current `master` (`1f5e4552`) and pushed — new head `952c476e`, **9 ahead / 0 behind**. The route-vs-display blocker is fixed.

## The fix — named tier first in `_parse_provider_qualified_model_id`

The longest-prefix pass no longer matches one union of named + endpoint-derived slugs. It now runs in two tiers:

1. **Named slugs only** (`_named_custom_provider_slugs`) — the catalog emits every configured row under its named `provider_id` (`custom:<name>`), so a named prefix is authoritative over any longer endpoint-derived alias. `@custom:gw:8080:free` with `{name:"gw", base_url:"http://gw:8080/v1"}` now resolves to **provider `custom:gw` / model `8080:free`** — the boundary the catalog emitted the row under.
2. **Endpoint-derived authority slugs** (`_known_custom_provider_slugs`) — consulted only when no named prefix matched, so endpoint-only providers (no `name`) still route through `custom:<host>:<port>`.

This is exactly what the frontend already did: `_dynamicProviderIds` carries only catalog `provider_id`s, so the JS mirror (`_customModelFromQualifiedId`) resolved this id to `8080:free` all along — the picker label and the backend route now agree again (no JS change needed; the existing `test_authoritative_provider_id_resolves_shape_ambiguity` covers that half).

## Tests

- `test_configured_endpoint_beats_named_slug_for_same_shape` → renamed `test_configured_named_provider_beats_endpoint_alias_for_same_shape`, now asserting provider `custom:gw` / model `8080:free` (was the codified endpoint-first result the review flagged).
- `test_one_malformed_base_url_does_not_hide_its_valid_siblings` re-pointed at the endpoint tier (`@custom:llm:8080:qwen3` vs a malformed sibling), so per-entry degradation is still exercised under the new precedence.
- New `test_catalog_row_resolves_to_the_provider_that_emitted_it`: cold-catalog round trip — config `{name:"gw", base_url:"http://gw:8080/v1", models:["8080:free"]}` emits `@custom:gw:8080:free` under `provider_id custom:gw`, and `resolve_model_provider` on that emitted id returns the same provider/model boundary.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Thanks @en-he — the byte cap, exact-byte accounting, MRU/active/pending protections, metadata-stub weighting, and earlier reconciliation fixes are thoughtful. One objective ABA race still breaks the core “resident state equals durable state before eviction” guarantee.

`Session.save()` hashes `payload_data`, serializes that shallow object graph in a separate unlocked traversal, installs it, then hashes live `self` in a third traversal. A nested field can move **A → B → A** across those traversals: the first/final fingerprints both say A while the serialized sidecar contains B. `_cache_persisted_fingerprint` is then accepted, byte pressure validates resident A against that fingerprint, and eviction discards A; reload returns B.

The current `replace_then_mutate` test only covers a one-way mutation and cannot catch ABA. There is a sibling validation→pop window as well: mutation can begin after `_session_matches_persisted_state()` succeeds but before removal.

Please:

1. Capture and serialize one immutable public-state snapshot under per-session mutation ownership, or use a monotonic mutation generation that proves it stayed unchanged through atomic install. Derive the persisted fingerprint from those exact installed bytes/snapshot.
2. Tie eviction validation and cache removal to that same generation/ownership so state cannot mutate between proof and `SESSIONS.pop()`.
3. Preserve the non-reentrant global `LOCK` contract and audit lock order with callers already holding the session/agent lock.
4. Add deterministic A→B→A during fingerprint/serialization and mutation-after-validation-before-pop regressions; retain the existing one-way and accounting/protection matrix.

This is correctness, not a sizing preference: the byte-only eviction path can discard resident state that was never durably installed. The branch is also currently conflicting, so rebase and fresh exact-head gates are needed after the fix.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Re-gated this at current master (rebased head `2ecaf41c9`) before shipping, and a fresh adversarial pass reproduced a **new data-consistency race that the byte-eviction introduces** — so this needs one more fix before it's shippable. (Heads up: the earlier `gate-pass` was from a parallel agent 2 days ago at `5207b631`; this finding post-dates it, so I've removed the stale label.)

### Must-fix — stale-generation cache after byte eviction (SILENT)

**`api/models.py:4978` (byte-eviction) + `api/models.py:1623` (detached-writer post-save check).**

Reproduced with a forced three-thread eviction / writer / reader interleave: a concurrent composer-draft `save()` succeeds on disk (`disk=new`) while the cache permanently serves the old draft (`cache=old`).

Mechanism:
1. A writer resolves its `Session` object and starts saving.
2. Byte-pressure eviction pops that session. The `_session_matches_persisted_state(candidate)` + session-agent-lock guard at :4978 ties validation-to-removal, but the writer resolved its object *before* the lock, so eviction can still pop the entry the writer is about to republish.
3. An interposed reader cold-loads the **old** sidecar and re-caches it.
4. The detached writer's post-save enforcement at :1623 (`if SESSIONS.get(self.session_id) is self`) no-ops because object **identity** differs (the cache now holds the reader's freshly-loaded object, not `self`), so the writer never republishes its `new` state.

Result: disk has `new`, cache serves `old` indefinitely. Verified that `origin/master` does **not** evict this case (it's a two-entry, below-count-cap session that only the new byte-pressure path evicts), so this is a regression introduced by the byte bound, not pre-existing.

**Fix:** make eviction / save / cold-load reconciliation **generation-aware (CAS)** rather than object-identity-based:
- A detached save must republish itself when the cache is absent **or** still holds an unchanged reload of the evicted generation (compare a sidecar generation/fingerprint, not `is self`).
- `_resolve_session()` must reject a cold snapshot whose sidecar generation changed before insertion.
- Extend `test_byte_eviction_coordinates_validation_and_removal_with_session_writer` with the **interposed reader** and assert both disk and cache return the `new` draft.

Codex also flags that other same-count metadata writes may exhibit the same stale-generation failure (the composer-draft path is the one directly reproduced), so the generation check should be the general reconciliation primitive, not a draft-specific patch.

Verified clean separately: the deepcopy snapshot correctly drives fingerprint / prefix metadata / JSON bytes / measured size; the two-thread save-vs-mutation probe preserved live unpersisted state; byte accounting and LRU/lazy-reload probes passed; 198 focused cache / save / load / list / chat-start / profile-isolation tests passed.

The byte-bound direction is right and the snapshot/ABA work is solid — this is the last concurrency edge. Once the generation-aware reconciliation lands with the three-thread regression test, re-push and I'll re-gate.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Re-gate at `ce4eb6b43390`: generation fix is still incomplete

Thanks for the focused follow-up. The prior immutable-snapshot/fingerprint repair remains correct, and the new three-thread regression closes the originally demonstrated `disk=new / cache=old` interleave. The targeted sandbox gate is green (13 focused tests across the prior ABA, new generation, accounting, and deadlock slices).

One blocking issue remains: the new path-stat tuple is not a coherent generation token, and cache publication still is not compare-and-swap.

### Must fix: bind loaded bytes, durable generation, and cache publication atomically

Three current-head paths leave deterministic stale-publication windows:

1. `Session.save()` installs the payload at `api/models.py:1572`, then separately stats the path at `:1588`. Another writer can replace the path between those operations, pairing this object's snapshot/fingerprint with the other writer's stat signature.
2. The cache-hit refresh at `api/models.py:5115-5122` loads outside the cache/session locks, then unconditionally assigns `SESSIONS[sid] = disk_session`. A newer writer/cache publication between load and assignment is overwritten by the stale load; there is no identity/generation CAS.
3. The cold-load guard at `api/models.py:5179-5193` retries only once and inserts the retry without revalidating its generation. Missing signatures also take the insertion branch, so an unverifiable snapshot fails open.

The same mismatch appears in state.db reconciliation: `_sync_sidecar_from_state_db_if_newer()` transfers public state, weight, and sometimes fingerprint, but does not transfer or invalidate the matching `_sidecar_stat_sig` as one authority unit.

Please make the generation token describe the exact bytes that were read/installed (for example, read once and `fstat()` that descriptor with inode/device plus timestamps/size, then revalidate the path before publication), use bounded retry with fail-closed exhaustion, and make every cache replacement a CAS against both the observed cache identity/state and the still-current durable generation. Reconciliation must transfer or invalidate fingerprint and generation together.

Add deterministic shipping regressions for:
- replacement between save install and generation capture,
- a second replacement during cold-load retry plus missing-token/retry-exhaustion behavior,
- a newer cache publication between cache-hit load and assignment,
- state.db reconcile preserving a matching fingerprint/generation pair.

Threat scan: CLEAN. Mandatory sandbox: 13 passed, 0 failed across focused slices. No full suite was run in this review-only warm-up.

## First review at `9c1c1d80` — full gate PASS. Correct, well-scoped fix. One non-blocking doc tidy.

**Head:** `9c1c1d80` (on current `origin/master`) · **Full suite: 13,868 passed / 0 failed** · **Codex: SAFE TO SHIP.**

Nice fix @happy5318 — the analysis holds up end-to-end. I traced the emitters in the installed agent and Codex reproduced the status stream; the change does exactly what it claims and nothing more:

**Why it's correct (not a suppressed-real-card regression):**
- The `📦 Preflight compression:` status is emitted from `turn_context.py:842` only when compression is *about* to run — but when compression actually proceeds, `_compress_context` → `compress_context` emits `🗜️ Compacting context — summarizing…` (`conversation_compression.py:~1418`), and **that marker is still a positive match** in `_is_agent_compression_start_status` (`api/streaming.py:591`). So every real compaction still raises the card.
- The cases you're suppressing are genuinely false: Codex confirmed preflight-only statuses occur when compression **exits before compaction** (refreshed durable guard at `conversation_compression.py:1365-1379`; Codex-Hermes mode with no active thread at `:2430-2442`) — no compression happens, so no card is correct.
- Skip/defer/cooldown guards (`streaming.py:578-585`) stay correct; `Pre-API compression:`, `Context too large`, `— compressing (`, and `compression attempt` all still match; the gateway noise filter is untouched (no status reworded).
- The changed test is a real fail-before/pass-after oracle — its new assertion fails on `origin/master` and passes on the head, and it keeps the positive assertions for Pre-API / Compacting-context / too-large / 413.

**SHOULD-FIX (non-blocking) — keep the comments honest:**
Two comments still assert the now-refuted premise that preflight is a positive marker:
- `api/streaming.py:568-570` — the docstring still lists `turn_context` **preflight** among the positive markers, but the code no longer matches it.
- `tests/test_auto_compression_card.py:476-478` — the comment repeats the "system-prompt-alone exceeds threshold → false card" framing; the real reason it's excluded is that the later `Compacting context` marker is the authoritative signal.

Please reword both to describe preflight as *intentionally ignored in favor of the later authoritative compaction marker* and push — happy to approve-merge once that lands (or I can fold the two-line comment fix into the merge if you'd rather not re-push).

**BONUS (out of scope, FYI):** while probing I noticed the idle-resume compaction status `💤 Resumed after {N}s idle — compacting ~{tokens} tokens…` is **not** matched by this predicate on master either (it says "compacting" not "compacting context"). It's a pre-existing gap, not something your PR changes — but if the idle-resume path can compact without a following `Compacting context` status, that card may be silently missing. Worth a separate look; not a blocker here.

Excellent, tightly-scoped first contribution — thank you.

payload.title: fix: prevent duplicate user messages on session switch after stream completion

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Thanks for the fix and the clear write-up @happy5318. I gated this at head `72e88322` (rebased clean onto current master, full suite 13,895 passed / 0 failed, Codex regression-clean) — but the committed change does **not** actually fix the duplicate-user bug it targets. It's behaviorally a no-op versus master.

### Why it's inert

The diff replaces the `_hasCurrentTailUserDuplicate(merged, candidate)` call inside `_mergeInflightTailMessages` with an inline backward walk. But that inline walk is logically identical to the helper it replaced. Both:

- skip `_live` and `tool` rows,
- dedup against the first non-compaction `user` row they reach,
- and **stop (return `false`) the moment they hit a completed (non-`_live`) `assistant` row.**

I fuzzed 1,550 transcript shapes (base × inflight-tail combinations of user/assistant/live-assistant/tool/compaction rows) running the real function from both `origin/master` and this branch — **zero divergences.** The output is byte-identical on every shape, including the exact bug scenario.

### The bug scenario still duplicates

For the case your PR describes — the `done` event is lost, so the base ends `[user:"q", assistant:"ans"]` (completed, non-live) and the INFLIGHT recovery re-supplies `user:"q"`:

```
committed diff  dedup? false   → user appended → DUPLICATE persists
```

The reason is the line:

```js
// Non-live assistant: turn is complete, don't dedup
// against a historical user message.
if(role==='assistant') return false;
```

This is exactly the short-circuit your PR body says the fix should *remove*. Your description says:

> Add a `continue` clause for completed (non-live) assistant messages … so the function skips past them and finds the actual last user message.

But the committed code does `return false` there instead of `continue`, so it never walks back to the real user row — same as master.

### Fix

Change that branch from `return false` to `continue` so the walk skips past the completed assistant and reaches the earlier user turn:

```js
// Skip past a completed (non-live) assistant to reach the current
// turn's user message that _dropCurrentTurnAssistantMessages left behind.
if(role==='assistant') continue;
```

With that one change the same scenario dedups correctly:

```
intended fix   dedup? true    → user NOT re-appended → bug fixed
```

### Also please add a regression test

This lands in the transcript-merge family (`_mergeInflightTailMessages`), which is where green suites hide behavior nothing asserts — so a test is required, not optional. `tests/test_inflight_stream_reuse.py` already extracts this function and drives it under node; add a case there:

- **fix:** base `[user:"q", assistant:"ans"]` + inflight `[user:"q", assistant(_live):"…"]` → asserts exactly **one** `user` row in the merged output.
- **anti-regression:** confirm a legitimately new user turn (e.g. one that repeats earlier text but belongs to a *different* live turn) still survives — so the `continue` doesn't over-dedup.

One caution on the `continue`: it will now walk past *any* number of completed assistant rows to the nearest user. That's correct for the current-turn recovery case, but please make the test also cover a multi-turn transcript (`[u1, a1, u2, a2]` + inflight re-supplying `u2`) to confirm it dedups against `u2` and not `u1`.

Happy to re-gate as soon as you push the `continue` + the test.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Thanks @happy5318 — the re-push does now genuinely change behavior (the previous no-op is fixed: dropping the completed assistant lets the optimistic user row dedup, and the id/timestamp identity matching is the right direction). Full suite is green. But re-gating this crown-jewel INFLIGHT-recovery path, the regression gate found four issues — one is a real data-loss risk — that need one more pass before it can ship.

### Must fix

**1. Data-loss: unconditional assistant drop can lose the authoritative response — `static/sessions.js:2117-2124`.**
Making `_dropCurrentTurnAssistantMessages` unconditional removes a settled assistant BEFORE its content is guaranteed to be preserved in a live row. When there is no live assistant with text yet, the real completed response is dropped and not restored. **Fix:** restore the `liveTailPrepared` guard — remove the settled assistant only after its content has been preserved into a live row (drop-and-replace, never drop-then-maybe-empty).

**2. Gateway timestamp parity — `api/gateway_chat.py:1194-1200`.**
For the optimistic↔persisted user-row timestamp match to work on Gateway sessions, the persisted Gateway user message must be stamped with the turn's captured `pending_started_at` (same server stamp the client syncs to), not a fresh stamp.

**3. Timestamp-only user match can collapse two distinct turns — `static/sessions.js:3272-3275`.**
`_sameTranscriptMessage` matching user rows on timestamp equality alone will over-match two genuinely different user messages sent in the same millisecond. **Fix:** require normalized user-text equality IN ADDITION to timestamp equality.

**4. `_ts` sync can be swallowed by a throwing post-start UI op — `static/messages.js:1830-1837`.**
`userMsg._ts = startData.pending_started_at` currently runs after a guarded `localStorage.setItem` (line ~1849) that can throw; if it does, the sync is skipped, the client keeps its old timestamp, and the duplicate-row behavior returns. **Fix:** move the `_ts` sync BEFORE any optional/throwing post-start UI operation.

### Not blockers
Suite is green; the two shard-4 failures (`test_issue2513_custom_provider_remote_models`, `test_ttl_cache::test_mtime_invalidation`) are pre-existing environment flakes on our CI box, identical on clean master.

Once these land I'll re-gate the exact head (Codex + full suite) and take it to release. Attribution preserved.

payload.body:
## Summary

I do not see a behavioral change in the new user-message predicate. It is an inline expansion of the existing tail helper: both implementations skip live rows, tool rows, and compaction markers, return a comparison when the current tail is a real user row, and stop when a settled assistant row is encountered. The reported base transcript that already ends in the completed assistant therefore still appends the optimistic user row.

## Code reference

Reading static/sessions.js:3270-3289 and static/sessions.js:3595-3637 on this HEAD, the previous helper stops at the first settled non-tool row. The replacement preserves that stop at static/sessions.js:3626-3629:

~~~javascript
if(role==='tool') continue;
// Non-live assistant: turn is complete, don't dedup
// against a historical user message.
if(role==='assistant') return false;
~~~

The resulting branch then executes:

~~~javascript
if(!duplicate) merged.push(candidate);
~~~

For base = [user A, assistant A] and inflight = [user A, live assistant A], the reverse scan sees assistant A first, returns false, and appends a second user A. That is the same result as _currentTailUserMessage returning null before this patch.

The other path does not establish a new fix either. static/sessions.js:3570-3592 prepares a visible live assistant, then the load path drops current-turn assistant rows before calling the merge. Once the base ends at user A, the existing _hasCurrentTailUserDuplicate helper already removed the duplicate.

## Diagnosis / recommendation

Please add a failing regression test before changing the predicate. The test needs to model the claimed state exactly, including a base that ends with the persisted completed assistant and an INFLIGHT tail containing the same user. At present this PR changes no test file, and the existing coverage in tests/test_inflight_stream_reuse.py:331-386 only exercises the assistant-drop path where master already deduplicates correctly.

A safe fix needs turn identity, not a broader content-only backward scan. Identical text can be a legitimate later turn. If the active stream or run-journal identity proves that the persisted assistant and INFLIGHT snapshot belong to the same turn, either purge the stale INFLIGHT entry as terminal or deduplicate against that turn's user before merging. Then add a second test proving that a genuinely new identical prompt after a completed assistant is preserved.

## Verification step

The minimum pair is:

1. Completed same-turn assistant plus stale INFLIGHT snapshot produces one user row.
2. New identical user prompt after a completed assistant produces two user rows.

Without those two assertions, this replacement is equivalent to the current code and does not demonstrate the reported fix.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

The new call fixes the reported duplicate in the same-turn recovery case, but it also removes the only turn-boundary signal used to distinguish a genuinely repeated prompt. Reading `static/sessions.js:2114-2124`, the helper definitions at `:3274-3293` and `:3342-3348`, and the added regression block at `tests/test_inflight_stream_reuse.py:1473-1540`, I think the current patch can collapse two real turns into one. This is a blocker because the affected state is a normal conversation: a user can submit the same text twice.

## Code reference

The INFLIGHT path now prepares a live tail, unconditionally deletes every assistant after the last persisted user, and only then performs text-based deduplication:

```js
_prepareRunningLiveTail(S.messages,inflightMessages);
S.messages=_dropCurrentTurnAssistantMessages(S.messages);
S.messages=_mergeInflightTailMessages(S.messages,inflightMessages);
S.toolCalls=(INFLIGHT[sid].toolCalls||[]);
```

That is at `static/sessions.js:2116-2125`. `_currentTailUserMessage()` at `:3274-3288` intentionally stops when it encounters a non-live assistant; that assistant is a completed-turn boundary. `_dropCurrentTurnAssistantMessages()` at `:3342-3348` removes the boundary before `_mergeInflightTailMessages()` at `:3599` can inspect it.

## Diagnosis / recommendation

Consider this valid sequence:

1. Persisted transcript contains user `hello`, then completed assistant `answer`.
2. The user starts a second turn with the same text, `hello`.
3. INFLIGHT contains the second user row and its live assistant.

After the unconditional drop, the base ends at the first `hello`. The merge sees equal role/content and treats the second `hello` as a duplicate, so the two turns become one. `_prepareRunningLiveTail()` at `static/sessions.js:3574` may also seed the new live tail from the prior completed assistant before that boundary is removed.

The test notices this scenario at `tests/test_inflight_stream_reuse.py:1534`, calling it a “genuinely new identical prompt,” but the following comment says it should dedup. That assertion encodes the bug instead of protecting the valid repeated-prompt case.

Please preserve explicit turn identity when deduplicating. The safest narrow fix is to compare stable message identity or timestamps when available, and only fall back to text equality when the persisted user and INFLIGHT user can be shown to be the same turn. Do not delete the completed assistant merely to make text-only matching succeed.

## Test plan

Keep the current regression with the same user-message identity and assert one user row. Add a second case with distinct timestamps or message identifiers but identical text, and assert that both user rows and the completed assistant boundary remain. Also cover different live-assistant text so prior completed output cannot be copied into the new turn. I reviewed the worktree statically and did not execute its test code.

payload.author: happy5318
payload.body:
## Round 4 re-gate — all four findings addressed on `6e11f78e`

Thanks for the detailed review. Each finding verified against the code and fixed:

### 1. [DATA-LOSS] Unconditional assistant drop — `static/sessions.js:2116`
Restored the `liveTailPrepared` guard: `_prepareRunningLiveTail()` result is now captured and the settled assistant is dropped **only** when its content has been preserved into a live row (drop-and-replace). When the live assistant has no text and nothing is preserved, the completed assistant survives.

### 2. [TIMESTAMP] Gateway parity — `api/gateway_chat.py:1172`
Persisted Gateway user row is now stamped with the turn's captured `pending_started_at` (same server stamp the client syncs to), falling back to `now` only when absent. Normalized to `float`; `assistant_ts` is forced strictly greater (`turn_started_at + 0.000001`) so ordering is preserved.

### 3. [OVER-MATCH] Timestamp-only user match — `static/sessions.js:3272`
`_sameTranscriptMessage` now requires normalized user-text equality **in addition to** timestamp equality. Two different messages in the same millisecond no longer collapse; same-timestamp same-text still dedups.

### 4. [SYNC] `_ts` swallowed by throwing post-start UI — `static/messages.js:1837`
The `userMsg._ts = pending_started_at` sync now runs **before** `_runOptionalPostStartUiStep(...)`, so a throwing `localStorage.setItem` (or any guarded post-start op) can no longer skip the sync. The duplicate in-step assignment was removed.

### Tests
- 4 new regression tests (one per finding): `test_load_session_keeps_completed_assistant_when_live_tail_not_prepared`, `test_gateway_user_msg_timestamp_uses_pending_started_at`, `test_same_transcript_message_requires_text_match_on_equal_timestamp`, `test_message_js_ts_sync_moved_before_throwing_post_start_ui`
- **211 passed** across the inflight/session/gateway suites
- **Revert-sensitivity matrix verified**: reverting each fix independently makes its test fail (test is load-bearing)

Ready for re-gate on exact head `6e11f78e`.

payload.body:
**CI now fully green at `3c9c4ffe`: 23/23 checks passing.**

The previous red check on `47e61953` (`live-to-final (normal, tests/browser_conversation_lifecycle.py, normal)` → `Run settlement frame proof` step) was a **flake, not a regression**. The empty commit `3c9c4ffe` only re-triggers CI — no code changed, so the tree at `3c9c4ffe` is byte-identical to `47e61953`.

### Evidence that it is a flake

I reproduced the exact CI invocation locally (same env vars, same script, same Playwright chromium) on the PR head:

```
LIFECYCLE_SCENARIO=normal LIFECYCLE_TEST_BITE=settle-worklog-frame-proof \
  python tests/browser_conversation_lifecycle.py
```

- **6 consecutive runs, all EXIT=0** — including the `settle-worklog-frame-proof` assertion the CI step failed on.
- `settledWorklogRemovals` was empty on every run (the `#6414` invariant this bite guards).
- Sampled frames per run: 10. Breakdown of which clause satisfied `valid_live_surface or valid_settled_surface`:
  - 8–9 frames passed via the **settled** surface (collapsed group with a non-empty summary),
  - 1–2 frames passed via **both** live and settled,
  - **0 frames passed via live-only.**

That last number is the interesting one for this gate's stability in general: on this machine the live-activity window is never the sole thing keeping a sampled frame valid, so the proof leans entirely on the settled surface being observable in the frame the sampler happens to catch. The sampler runs `requestAnimationFrame` + `setTimeout(0)` in a loop and is stopped after a fixed `page.wait_for_timeout(100)`, so under CI's slower/noisier scheduling it can land on a frame during the settle rebuild where neither surface has materialised yet. That is a timing-sensitivity in the bite's sampling, not a behavioural difference in the PR's code.

I also re-ran the other two lifecycle matrix legs against the same head:

- `terminal-error` scenario — passed. (First attempt failed on an unrelated wall-clock artifact: the assertion diffs settled vs reloaded terminal rows, and the run straddled a minute boundary, so `'…10:41 AM'` vs `'…10:42 AM'` differed in the rendered timestamp text only. Immediate re-run passed.)
- `historical-transcript-hydration` — passed.

And the PR-scoped unit suites remain green: `tests/test_inflight_stream_reuse.py` + `tests/test_regressions.py` → **111 passed**.

### Review status

All four Round-4 findings remain addressed as described in my `47e61953` comment (data-loss guard restored, gateway timestamp parity covered natively by the `_active_turn_authority()` refactor, user-row matching requires text equality alongside timestamp, `_ts` sync moved ahead of throwing post-start UI ops). payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Thanks @happy5318 — the core direction is right and verified: your `_slug_from_name` matches the Hermes agent's `_normalize_custom_pool_name` byte-for-byte (`name.strip().lower().replace(" ", "-")`, credential_pool.py:440), and the colon round-trip guard correctly resolves canonical providers first. The full suite is green. But an authoritative regression gate reproduced three issues on this credential-resolution path that need one more pass before it can ship — two are the fail-closed edges this PR is specifically about, and one is a live-catalog regression the change introduces.

### Must fix

**1. Fail-closed on ambiguity isn't airtight — `api/config.py:3086` (`resolve_custom_provider_connection`).**
The legacy-slug path can still resolve to a provider when the legacy slug matches more than one configured entry. Unify canonical + legacy matching into one lookup that: (a) canonicalizes the incoming id first, (b) requires exactly ONE unique configured provider match, and (c) returns `(None, None)` IMMEDIATELY on 0-or-2+ matches (never fall through to an arbitrary/first entry), before any profile-scoped runtime/pool lookup. A wrong resolution here is a cross-provider credential mix-up.

**2. Inferred custom-provider env-name aliasing isn't collision-resistant — `api/config.py:1614`.**
The inferred env-var names for custom providers can collide for distinct providers, and ambiguous legacy env aliases don't fail closed. Make the inferred name collision-resistant (disambiguate distinct providers) and fail closed (skip, don't guess) when a legacy env alias is ambiguous.

**3. Live-catalog regression — `api/routes.py:20216`.**
When a custom provider has a plural `models` list configured, this branch now FILTERS the live `/v1/models` result against the configured entries, whereas master MERGES them. Repro: with live `[assistant, assistant-pro, remote-extra]` and only `[assistant]` configured, `assistant-pro`/`remote-extra` VANISH from the picker. Restore the master merge behavior (union live + configured) while keeping your new singular-`model` fallback logic.

### Not blockers
Suite is green; the two shard failures I saw (`test_issue2513_custom_provider_remote_models`, `test_ttl_cache::test_mtime_invalidation`) are pre-existing environment flakes on our CI box, identical on clean master — not yours.

Once these three land, I'll re-gate the exact head (Codex + full suite) and take it to release. Attribution preserved — this stays your PR.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

The one-line change fixes the narrow empty-slug case, but it also changes the provider-ID alphabet from ASCII to arbitrary Unicode without carrying that decision through the other slug and credential paths. Reading the complete `api/config.py` at PR head `160da20e2` and on `origin/master`, plus the route fallback, provider serialization, existing tests, and the agent-side custom-provider resolver, I would not merge this as-is. The fix needs one canonical slug contract and regression coverage.

## Code reference

At `api/config.py:1355-1369`, the PR changes the canonical WebUI slugger to:

```python
slug = re.sub(r"[^\w]+", "-", str(name).strip().lower(), flags=re.UNICODE).strip("-")
if not slug:
    return ""
return f"custom:{slug}"
```

That makes a pure CJK name nonempty, but two adjacent contracts remain inconsistent:

* `api/routes.py:6517-6531` has an exception fallback that still uses the old ASCII-only expression. The same name can therefore resolve to an empty provider ID on that path.
* `api/config.py:1577-1592` derives the default API-key environment name with `[^A-Za-z0-9]`. Multiple Unicode-only provider IDs therefore collapse to the same ASCII result rather than receiving distinct credential names.

The agent-side resolver at `hermes_cli/providers.py:711-718` also preserves non-space punctuation, while this PR removes it. A name containing CJK punctuation can still produce different provider IDs in the WebUI and agent, even though a punctuation-free Chinese name happens to match.

## Diagnosis / recommendation

Please define the identifier contract once, then reuse it in the normal WebUI path, the route fallback, and the agent boundary. I recommend keeping the persisted ID ASCII-safe and adding a deterministic fallback for names whose ASCII slug is empty, for example a readable prefix plus a short stable digest of a Unicode-normalized name. That avoids empty IDs, punctuation disagreement, visually confusable IDs, and credential-variable collisions while leaving the display name unchanged.

If Unicode itself is intended to be valid in persisted provider IDs, normalize it (at least NFC), specify punctuation handling, and update every downstream sanitizer rather than changing only this regex.

## Test plan

No test changes are present. Add cases beside `tests/test_custom_provider_display_name.py:22-98` and `tests/test_custom_providers_in_panel.py:209-260` for: a pure CJK name, CJK punctuation, canonically equivalent composed/decomposed names, two distinct Unicode-only providers, route-fallback parity, and distinct API-key environment names. Also assert the resulting `custom:<slug>` round-trips through model listing and provider resolution. I inspected the worktree read-only and did not execute PR-authored code.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

Reading the full `api/config.py`, `api/routes.py`, and new regression file at latest HEAD `067eefbfd`, then comparing both implementation files with `origin/master`, the new pure-Unicode fallback does fix the empty-slug case. The latest commit still has a correctness blocker, though: mixed Unicode/ASCII names can collapse onto existing ASCII-only names because the hash is used only when the ASCII projection is completely empty.

For example, `我的Proxy服务器` and `Proxy` both become `custom:proxy`; `东京-1` and `大阪-1` both become `custom:1`. Those are separate provider names but still share the internal provider ID and downstream credential mapping. That contradicts both the PR goal and the helper docstring claim that distinct names map to distinct slugs.

## Code reference

The collision is introduced by the early return at `api/config.py:1368-1375`:

```python
slug = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9._-]+", "-", raw).strip("-")
slug = re.sub(r"-{2,}", "-", slug)
if slug:
    return slug
# Fallback: deterministic hash of Unicode-normalised name
normalized = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", raw)
```

`api/config.py:1381-1391` then prefixes that result with `custom:`, so every caller sees the collision. The duplicated fallback at `api/routes.py:6520-6537` has the same condition. The current test at `tests/test_custom_provider_unicode_slug.py:43-46` actually locks in the unsafe behavior by asserting that `我的Proxy服务器` becomes exactly `proxy`.

## Diagnosis / recommendation

Keep legacy IDs unchanged for names containing only ASCII, but include the normalized-name digest whenever a name contains non-ASCII code points, even if some ASCII survives. A narrow shape is:

```python
has_non_ascii = any(ord(char) > 127 for char in raw)
if slug and not has_non_ascii:
    return slug
digest = hashlib.sha256(raw.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]
return f"{slug}-{digest}" if slug else f"provider-{digest}"
```

That preserves `My Provider` as `my-provider`, distinguishes mixed-script names from their ASCII projections, and keeps NFC-equivalent spellings stable. I would also avoid maintaining a second hand-copied implementation in `api/routes.py` if the import boundary can be made reliable; otherwise both copies need identical tests. Using more than eight hex characters would also make accidental digest collisions substantially less likely for installations with many custom providers.

## Test plan

Please add pairwise assertions for `Proxy` versus `我的Proxy服务器`, and `东京-1` versus `大阪-1`, through `_ascii_slug_from_name`, `_custom_provider_slug_from_name`, the credential-name mapping, and `_custom_provider_slug_for_context`. Keep the existing NFC-equivalence control and add an ASCII compatibility control proving existing ASCII provider IDs do not change. I did not execute the PR code because review worktrees are read-only/untrusted; this verdict is from static inspection of the latest diff and full files.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

The collision fix is now consistent between the two slug-producing helpers, but the runtime connection resolver still uses the old, Unicode-preserving matcher. With two or more custom providers, a generated hashed provider ID cannot be mapped back to its configured endpoint. That means the exact multi-provider case covered by the new collision tests can still fail before agent construction.

## Code reference

Reading `api/config.py:1355-1397`, `api/config.py:3026-3083`, and the streaming handoff at `api/streaming.py:442-471` on this HEAD, `_ascii_slug_from_name` now emits a digest for every non-ASCII name:

~~~python
digest = hashlib.sha256(raw.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]
return f"{slug}-{digest}" if slug else f"provider-{digest}"
~~~

However, `resolve_custom_provider_connection` does not call that helper. At `api/config.py:3071-3079` it compares the digest suffix against `_slugify(name)`, which only lowercases and replaces spaces or underscores:

~~~python
entry_slug = _slugify(name)
if entry_slug != slug:
    continue
~~~

For a configured name such as `我的提供商`, the requested suffix is `provider-<digest>`, while `entry_slug` is still `我的提供商`. The single-provider fallback at `api/config.py:3085-3092` masks this when there is only one entry, but it deliberately does not run when the user has two distinct CJK providers. `api/streaming.py:458-470` then receives no connection and cannot convert the named provider into the generic custom runtime.

## Diagnosis / recommendation

Please make `resolve_custom_provider_connection` use `_custom_provider_slug_from_name(name)` as its canonical comparison. It should also accept the prior ASCII-projection slug for existing mixed-script providers. Without that legacy alias, an existing provider such as `我的Proxy服务器`, previously persisted as `custom:proxy`, changes identity on upgrade and old sessions stop matching.

The same legacy check should cover the previous generated API-key environment name, or the migration should document why that credential lookup cannot be retained.

## Test plan

Add an integration test with two configured entries and distinct endpoints:

1. Generate each provider ID through `_custom_provider_slug_from_name`.
2. Call `resolve_custom_provider_connection` for each ID.
3. Assert that each resolves its own endpoint and key.
4. Add a persisted `custom:proxy` case for a mixed-script display name and assert that it still resolves after upgrade.

The current `tests/test_custom_provider_unicode_slug.py:146-240` proves slug uniqueness and route-helper parity, but it never exercises the runtime resolver where the mismatch occurs.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

The Unicode-preserving direction is good, but the latest implementation still does not match the Hermes credential-pool naming contract. I read the full `api/config.py` change, the new `tests/test_custom_provider_unicode_slug.py`, the call sites in `api/routes.py`, and the agent-side normalizer in `agent/credential_pool.py:389`. The WebUI and agent now preserve Unicode, but they still produce different pool keys for several supported names. Because custom-provider lookup ultimately joins these two layers, I consider this a correctness blocker rather than only a naming concern.

## Code reference

At `api/config.py:1366-1372`, the WebUI applies NFC normalization, replaces colons and every Unicode whitespace run, strips edge hyphens, and collapses repeated hyphens:

```python
raw = str(name or "").strip().lower()
raw = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", raw)

slug = re.sub(r"[:\s]+", "-", raw).strip("-")
slug = re.sub(r"-{2,}", "-", slug)
return slug
```

The agent contract at `agent/credential_pool.py:389` only trims, lowercases, and replaces each literal ASCII space. The new tests currently pin the divergence: NFC equivalence at `tests/test_custom_provider_unicode_slug.py:68`, edge-hyphen stripping at `:74`, whitespace-run collapse at `:79`, and colon replacement at `:90-91`.

## Diagnosis / recommendation

These concrete names resolve differently across the boundary:

- `a:b` becomes `a-b` in WebUI but remains `a:b` in the agent.
- `a   b` becomes `a-b` in WebUI but becomes `a---b` in the agent.
- `---hello---` becomes `hello` in WebUI but retains its edge hyphens in the agent.
- Canonically equivalent composed/decomposed Unicode is merged by WebUI but remains distinct in the current agent contract.

The internal WebUI call sites are consistent because `resolve_custom_provider_connection()` and the route context both use the same helper (`api/config.py:1395`, `api/routes.py:6517-6522`). The failure is at the provider-auth contract boundary: WebUI can request a different credential-pool key from the one the agent registered.

Please either mirror the agent transformation exactly in this PR, or change the agent contract in the same release and document the migration. Given this PRs scope, exact mirroring is safer. The helper name should also no longer say `ascii` once Unicode is intentionally preserved.

## Test plan

Add parity vectors copied from the agent contract for literal spaces, repeated spaces, colons, tabs, edge hyphens, composed/decomposed Unicode, and all-Unicode names. For every vector, assert that provider-id creation and connection lookup use the same expected agent pool key. I reviewed these tests statically only, as PR worktree code was not executed.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

Re-reviewing exact head `e02a3fa90`, the primary `api.config` path now matches the agent custom-pool naming contract, but one blocker remains: the exception fallback in `api/routes.py` still implements a different normalization algorithm. The new parity tests call the normal import path, so they do not execute that fallback and cannot catch the mismatch.

## Code reference

The canonical WebUI helper at `api/config.py:1355-1367` preserves every character except literal ASCII spaces, and `resolve_custom_provider_connection()` consumes that identity at `api/config.py:3011-3064`. I also confirmed that the contract owner is `agent/credential_pool.py:_normalize_custom_pool_name` on the agent side.

However, `api/routes.py:6517-6536` currently falls back to this:

```python
raw = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", raw)
# Replace only colon and whitespace with hyphens
slug = re.sub(r"[:\s]+", "-", raw).strip("-")
slug = re.sub(r"-{2,}", "-", slug)
```

That disagrees with the declared contract in several ways. It changes colons, tabs and other whitespace, collapses repeated hyphens, strips edge hyphens, and NFC-normalizes Unicode. For example, the canonical helper preserves `a:b`, preserves a tab, maps three spaces to three hyphens, and keeps composed/decomposed spellings distinct; the route fallback does none of those.

## Diagnosis / recommendation

Please make the route fallback byte-for-byte equivalent to the canonical transformation instead of maintaining a second policy. The fallback at `api/routes.py:6525-6536` can be reduced to:

```python
raw = str(name or "").strip().lower()
if not raw:
    return ""
if raw.startswith("custom:"):
    return raw
return "custom:" + raw.replace(" ", "-")
```

This also removes the need for `unicodedata` in that branch. Keeping the fallback is reasonable for defensive import isolation, but if it exists it must preserve the same provider identity as the normal path; otherwise the same request context can resolve to a different credential pool solely because an import failed.

## Test plan

The tests at `tests/test_custom_provider_unicode_slug.py:180-204` currently import and call `_custom_provider_slug_for_context()` while `api.config._custom_provider_slug_from_name` is available, so the `try` branch always wins. Add a test that temporarily removes that imported attribute before calling the route helper, then parameterize the existing parity vectors from `tests/test_custom_provider_unicode_slug.py:77-103`: colon, repeated spaces, tab, edge hyphens, and composed/decomposed Unicode. I reviewed the worktree statically and did not execute PR-authored tests.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Thanks @happy5318 — the Unicode/CJK slug-parity goal is right and the CJK canonical resolution itself checks out, but an adversarial gate (Codex, verified against the real resolver, on top of a full 13,913-pass suite) reproduced **three production-path defects** that the current tests miss. Holding for a revision:

### 1. CORE — colon-bearing provider names corrupt send-time routing
A provider named `Local (127.0.0.1:15721)` now slugs to `custom:local-(127.0.0.1:15721)`, but `_parse_provider_qualified_model_id()` reads that hint as provider `custom:local-(127.0.0.1` + model `15721):deepseek-v4-flash`. The canonical slug must round-trip through every provider/model parser without altering the model.
- **Fix:** parse against the exact configured canonical provider (or pass provider/model separately) *before* applying colon-suffix heuristics. Add coverage for the newly-generated IDs, not the obsolete sanitized ID still asserted at `tests/test_model_resolver.py:920`.

### 2. CORE — existing sessions lose custom-provider credentials after upgrade
Working legacy IDs are re-keyed with no migration. Verified: `My  Proxy` (double space) previously produced+resolved `custom:my-proxy`; it now produces `custom:my--proxy`, and a restored `custom:my-proxy` session resolves `(None, None)` when more than one custom provider exists — a silent credential-loss / send-failure on upgrade.
- **Fix:** accept legacy normalization only when it identifies exactly one entry, rewrite it to the canonical slug before runtime credential lookup, and **fail closed on ambiguous aliases** (never pick credentials from an arbitrary entry).

### 3. SILENT — singular `model` now hides the rest of the live catalog
`api/routes.py:20069`: a provider's singular `custom_providers[].model` (sticky/default metadata) is now treated as a filter, so a live catalog of `assistant`, `assistant-pro`, `remote-extra` returned only `assistant`. Real `_handle_live_models()` probe confirmed.
- **Fix:** treat only a non-empty `models` dict/list as the allowlist signal; for a `model`-only provider preserve the full live list and merge the sticky fallback. Replace the simulated #3718 tests with a real `_handle_live_models()` assertion.

Focused verification: 124 changed-path + 15 neighboring parser/profile tests passed and profile-scoped credential isolation held — so the parity intent is sound; these three are edge/migration/routing gaps. Once they're addressed I'll re-gate the exact head. No rush — take the time to get the migration + colon round-trip right.

payload.body:
## Round 2 re-gate — review findings 1/2/3 addressed on `523912dd`

### 1. [AMBIGUITY] First-match-is-arbitrary — `resolve_custom_provider_connection` (config.py)
Unified canonical + raw-name + legacy matching into a single `_matches` lookup that requires **exactly one** configured provider match. Ambiguous slugs (2+ entries match, e.g. two distinct display names that both normalize to `my-proxy`) return `(None, None)` with a logger.warning. Incoming `provider_id` is **canonicalized first** (`_slug_from_name`) so old persisted shapes like `custom:My Provider` with a space still resolve correctly.

### 2. [COLLISION] Inferred env-name clash across providers — `_lookup_custom_api_key_env` (config.py)
New `_api_key_env_name_is_ambiguous` helper: iterates all configured custom providers and checks whether any **other** provider infers the same env name (both sanitized `CUSTOM_*_API_KEY` and legacy shapes). payload.author: happy5318
payload.body:
Closing this — I no longer need the behaviour, and the PR is not in a shape worth asking a reviewer to spend more time on.

## Why I'm closing rather than pushing another round

The bug is real and still present upstream: `_slug_from_name()` in `api/config.py` builds custom-provider slugs with `re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9._-]+", "-", raw).strip("-")`, so a provider name with no ASCII alphanumerics collapses to an empty slug. Measured on the current regex:

```
'tokenrhythm' -> 'tokenrhythm'
'基元律动'     -> ''
```

An empty slug means the provider never appears in the model picker, and a `model_aliases` entry pointing at `custom:<that name>` cannot resolve.

On my side I hit this with a single non-ASCII provider name. I've now renamed that provider to an ASCII identifier, which makes the upstream regex behave correctly and removes my dependence on this change entirely. Renaming one config value was a far better trade for me than carrying a 149-line local patch across every release — it was conflicting on nearly every upstream release that touched `api/config.py`.

## State of the PR, honestly

I am not leaving this in a "ready except for nits" state, so I'd rather not imply otherwise:

- **CI is red** — 3 test shards plus the lifecycle gate.
- **Three credential-parsing findings from the last review are unaddressed.** These are the risky part: the slug is used for credential lookup, so a normalization change that gets round-tripping or collision handling wrong can cross provider boundaries and hand one provider's key to another. That is exactly the class of bug that deserves a careful reviewer, and I'm not in a position to give it the attention it needs now that I don't use the feature.

## If someone wants to pick this up

The branch stays at `d91947bf` on my fork. My read on what a mergeable version needs:

1. Guarantee slug round-tripping and collision handling before touching the credential lookup path — the collision case (two distinct non-ASCII names normalizing to the same slug) is the one to nail down first.
2. Keep the ASCII fast path byte-identical so existing installs see no slug churn. Any change to an existing provider's slug silently orphans its stored credential.
3. Address the three credential-parsing findings from the last review round.
4. Consider whether the narrower fix is enough: instead of broadening the character class, fall back to a stable derived slug (e.g. a short hash of the raw name) only when normalization yields an empty string. That keeps every currently-working name untouched and confines the new behaviour to the case that is broken today.

Sorry for the noise, and thanks for the review time already spent on it.

payload.body:
Thanks @ruizanthony — exact-head warm-up at `0672574e6b4c` found objective blockers that need correction before another gate.

### Finding

**Yes.** Current-head evidence establishes all three issues.

### A. Successful native fallback leaves live metadata on the primary

- WebUI only re-emits effective `run_meta` when `_agent_status_callback()` classifies a lifecycle message as fallback (`api/streaming.py:8359-8414`).
- Its classifier accepts `rate limited`, `switching to fallback`, `falling back`, `fallback activated`, or `trying fallback` (`api/streaming.py:556-569`).
- The installed Hermes runtime mutates `agent.model`, `agent.provider`, and `agent.reasoning_config` during activation, but buffers `Primary model failed — switching to fallback...`; on successful recovery it later emits the one-shot lifecycle text `Switched to fallback model: ...` (`agent/chat_completion_helpers.py:2146-2153,2283-2322`; `agent/conversation_loop.py:7403-7411`).
- `switched to fallback` does **not** match WebUI's predicate. Therefore the successful-fallback lifecycle event produces neither the fallback warning nor `_emit_effective_run_meta()`. The live footer keeps the initial primary model/effort through the fallback response. Only final settlement reads the mutated agent and becomes correct (`api/streaming.py:10825-10850`, `11237+`).
- The added test at `tests/test_reasoning_effort_footer.py:82-89` checks source ordering (`warning` before refresh) but never feeds the actual successful runtime message through the predicate/callback, so it false-greens this integration mismatch.

### B. Gateway path records requested, not actually used, runtime

- Gateway `run_meta` is emitted before the request from the WebUI-selected `model`, `model_provider`, and locally computed requested effort (`api/gateway_chat.py:925-937`).
- Success persistence then unconditionally stamps those same request-side values as `_usedModel` and `_reasoningEffort` (`api/gateway_chat.py:1228-1232`) and repeats requested effort in `done.usage` (`1373-1377`).
- No post-run reconciliation updates these values from Gateway routing/fallback output. `_gateway_stream_usage()` retains only token/cost fields (`api/gateway_chat.py:408-416`), and both runs and legacy stream loops ignore effective `runtime`/routing identity when parsing terminal payloads (`672-705`, `1168-1183`).
- Consequently a Gateway route, retry, provider switch, or fallback can be displayed and persisted as the originally requested model/effort even when another provider/model/config actually answered. This contradicts the PR's “effective”/“used model” contract and makes live and reload consistently wrong rather than transiently stale.

### C. Transparent settled footer duplicates effort

- The generic settled footer always appends `.msg-reasoning-inline` when `effortText` exists (`static/ui.js:17397-17404,17447-17452`).
- Transparent-mode ownership suppression exists for the model only (`_transparentFooterOwnsModel`, `17430-17445`); there is no equivalent reasoning-effort ownership guard.
- The later transparent footer pass reads the same message effort and adds `.lf-effort` (`17505-17531`; `_transparentTurnFooterHtml` at `12099-12111`).
- Thus a settled transparent turn with event rows and `_reasoningEffort` renders the same effort twice: once in the normal message foot and once in the transparent footer. Existing tests only assert both classes are wired (`tests/test_reasoning_effort_footer.py:176-195`) and do not compose a transparent turn or count labels.

The normal persistence/reload spine itself is otherwise sound: `_reasoningEffort` is allowlisted in `api/models.py`, native settlement stamps it before save, the done handler carries it onto the last assistant row, and helper tests round-trip `_reasoningEffort`/`_usedModel` through `Session.save()`/`Session.load()`.

### Required fix

Please address the exact-head blocker above and add a regression that exercises the real production path.

### Focused verifica

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

The settled-turn path now records the post-run effort correctly, and the added persistence test covers reload. One live-status gap remains: run_meta is emitted only once, before the conversation starts. If Hermes activates a fallback during the run, the Agent changes both model and reasoning_config, but the WebUI only emits a warning. The live footer therefore continues to display the primary model and effort until the terminal done event replaces them.

## Code reference

Reading api/streaming.py:9432-9442 on this HEAD, the only structured live metadata emission occurs before run_conversation:

~~~python
_run_meta_effort = _effective_reasoning_effort_label(agent, _reasoning_config)
put('run_meta', {
    'session_id': session_id,
    'model': getattr(agent, 'model', None) or resolved_model or model,
    'provider': resolved_provider or '',
    'reasoning_effort': _run_meta_effort,
})
~~~

The frontend at static/messages.js:5756-5770 supports repeated run_meta events and replaces its current meta, so it is ready for an update. However, api/streaming.py:8044-8078 handles a fallback lifecycle notice by sending only warning. There is no second run_meta emission there.

The settled path is different: api/streaming.py:10459-10484 reads agent.model after the run and stamps _usedModel plus _reasoningEffort, while api/streaming.py:10872-10876 adds the final effort to usage. That is why the footer becomes correct only after completion.

I also cross-checked the Agent contract. agent/chat_completion_helpers.py:1870-1884 mutates the active model/provider during fallback, and agent/chat_completion_helpers.py:2014-2028 re-resolves reasoning_config for the fallback model before the lifecycle notice is surfaced. This is a WebUI event-bridging gap, not an effort-resolution gap in the Agent.

## Diagnosis / recommendation

When _agent_status_callback recognizes a fallback notice, emit a deduplicated run_meta update after the warning, using the current agent.model, agent.provider, and _effective_reasoning_effort_label(agent). Track the last emitted tuple so repeated fallback status text does not create redundant journal entries. Reusing run_meta is preferable to parsing the human-readable warning in JavaScript.

## Test plan

The current tests/test_reasoning_effort_footer.py:67-74 verifies only the initial emission. Add a fallback case that:

1. Starts with a primary model and one effort.
2. Mutates a fake Agent to a fallback model and a different resolved effort.
3. Invokes the fallback lifecycle bridge.
4. Asserts that a second run_meta payload carries the fallback model, provider, and effort.

Also assert that the final persisted assistant metadata still matches that second payload. This keeps live and settled attribution on the same contract.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## First-round gate at `cfff8bd9` — SHIP ONLY WITH FIXES: the default-unbounded path is safe, but the new bounded path has 3 verified holes

**Head reviewed:** `cfff8bd9` (already on current `origin/master`)
**Base:** `origin/master`
Full suite: **13,870 passed / 0 failed**. I confirmed the make-or-break regression surface is safe: every existing caller of `read_run_events()` (`models.py:2454/2545`, `routes.py:3183/17207/17266`, `runtime_adapter.py:362`) calls it without `max_bytes`/`max_rows`, so they all hit the early-return unbounded branch and are byte-for-byte unchanged. Good instinct to make the bounds opt-in.

But the adversarial gate reproduced **three SILENT correctness holes in the new bounded path** (each verified with a crafted probe), and they undercut the exact guarantee this PR is meant to provide — that the caps are a *real* bound:

### 🔴 Must fix

1. **Recovered markers bypass the byte cap** — `api/run_journal.py:495` & `:616`.
   With `max_bytes=1`, the function returned a **396-byte** marker and reported `complete=True`; crafted retained top-level fields produced an **8,397-byte** marker with `max_bytes=32`. So `_recover_legacy_overcap_terminal_event()` emits a marker whose size is never charged against `max_bytes` — the cap is bypassable.
   **Fix:** reconstruct a canonical, type-bounded envelope (don't copy arbitrary top-level fields through), charge the serialized marker against `max_bytes`, and never append it when it doesn't fit.

2. **Zero-progress cursor → infinite loop on an oversized non-terminal row** — `api/run_journal.py:570` & `:608`.
   A single oversized *non-terminal* row returns zero events and an **unchanged** `next_after_seq`. A caller that resumes from the returned cursor gets the identical result forever.
   **Fix:** return an explicit bounded recovery/fallback disposition that **consumes** the row and **advances** `next_after_seq`, while keeping `complete=False` and `limit_reason="replay_limit_bytes"`.

3. **Byte enforcement runs before window/row classification (ordering bug)** — `api/run_journal.py:562`.
   With `max_seq=1`, an oversized terminal row at seq 2 wrongly flips an otherwise-complete `[1]` window into `complete=False / replay_limit_bytes`. And when both limits are exhausted, an oversized ordinary row reports `rows` while an equivalent terminal row reports `bytes` — nondeterministic limit_reason.
   **Fix:** one deterministic order — validate the envelope and apply `after_seq`/`max_seq` **first**, then row capacity, then byte/recovery capacity. A row outside the `[after_seq, max_seq]` window must never affect completion.

### Direction
The opt-in design and default-preservation are right; the bug class is entirely inside the new bounded branch. Please make the cap genuinely inclusive of the recovery marker, guarantee forward cursor progress on every non-empty row (no zero-progress return), and fix the classification order so window filtering precedes capacity checks. Add unit tests that pin each: (a) marker-size charged against `max_bytes`; (b) two-page bounded read where `page1.next_after_seq` strictly advances and `page2` resumes with no skip/dup; (c) an out-of-window oversized row leaves `complete=True`. Re-push and I'll run a clean full gate.

## Re-gate at `36ab162d55` — changes requested: marker accounting converged, but bounded paging still drops or strands rows

Thanks for closing the recovered-marker cap: the current code builds a canonical fixed envelope, charges its compact serialized size plus newline, and refuses it when it cannot fit. That first-round item is fixed.

Two blocking paging defects remain on the exact head:

1. **A physical row over the 16 MiB hard-line ceiling is not resumable.** `read_run_events()` reads only the first `MAX+1` bytes and returns immediately at `api/run_journal.py:602-614`. It does not drain the physical line or reach the following row. Every page reopens the file at byte zero, so page 2 reads the same prefix again. In the sandbox, a >16 MiB seq-1 row followed by valid seq 2 returned empty page 1 and empty page 2; seq 2 remained unreachable. If the top-level seq is beyond the retained prefix, the function fabricates cursor values from `baseline + 1` while rereading the same bytes.
2. **The row/byte boundary candidate is advanced past even though it was never emitted.** When `max_rows` is already full (`api/run_journal.py:632-637`) or an ordinary row does not fit the remaining byte budget (`:639-647`), `_cursor_after_row()` includes that candidate in `next_after_seq`. A three-row journal with `max_rows=1` emitted seq 1 on page 1 and seq 3 on page 2: seq 2 was permanently skipped. The same loss occurs when two rows each fit an empty byte page but only one fits the current page.

The hard-line branch also still runs before JSON/type/top-level-seq classification, `after_seq`/`max_seq`, and row-cap precedence. `_SEQ_PREFIX_RE.search()` can pick a nested `"seq"` from an incomplete payload, so it is not authoritative cursor identity.

Threat scan was CLEAN. The committed targeted journal files pass in the no-network sandbox (**41 passed**), but reviewer-owned sandbox diagnostics reproduced the hard-line repeat and ordinary row/byte page loss. Temporary probes were removed and the exact-head worktree was rerun clean.

### Required fix

- Read/drain one complete physical JSONL row with bounded allocations, or carry a genuine opaque physical-offset cursor. Do not return after an unterminated prefix and then reopen at byte zero.
- Keep the cursor at the last emitted or deliberately dispositioned authoritative positive sequence when a row/byte page is full. Leave a fresh-page-fit candidate for the next page instead of consuming it in `next_after_seq`.
- Do not synthesize logical sequence authority from an incomplete regex prefix. Define fail-closed handling for missing, nonpositive, duplicate, and out-of-order seq values.
- Apply classification and window filtering before row/byte admission in every branch, including over-hard rows. Preserve the now-correct canonical marker accounting.
- Add two-page regressions for an actual >16 MiB row followed by a valid row, 1/2/3 rows with `max_rows=1`, two individually-fitting byte-page rows, hard-row `after_seq`/`max_seq`, nested/missing/nonpositive seqs, and duplicate/out-of-order seqs.

This is a real partial convergence, but bounded callers can still loop without reaching later data or silently skip valid rows, so the PR is not ship-ready yet.

- `max_rows < 1` now fails immediately with `ValueError`, closing the zero-progress row-cap loop.

The hard-row branch still bypasses that validation, so the scanner-authority blocker remains for rows above `_LEGACY_TERMINAL_RECOVERY_MAX_BYTES`.

### Reproduced blocker

At `api/run_journal.py`, JSON decoding runs only under `if raw_bytes is not None`. For a hard row, `_read_bounded_physical_row()` returns `raw_bytes=None`; `_TopLevelEnvelopeScanner.authoritative_seq()` then supplies the sequence, `last_physical_seq` is updated, and the hard-row branch advances `next_after_seq` without any full JSON-grammar validation.

The scanner accepts a balanced-but-invalid top-level trailing comma. In the mandatory CLEAN/no-network sandbox, I wrote:

1. an over-hard-cap malformed row with authoritative-looking `seq=999`, exact session/run/event IDs, and `...,"payload":{"text":"..."},}`;
2. a valid `seq=1` row immediately after it.

Current head returned:

```text
events=[]
next_after_seq=999
limit_reason=replay_limit_bytes
```

The malformed hard row therefore gains cursor authority and suppresses the following valid row as out-of-order. This is the same silent-loss class the prior fix-spec required to close, only beyond the retained-row boundary.

The same early hard-row return also consumes a valid over-hard-cap terminal row without producing the canonical `consumed_non_materializable` recovery marker. 1. Make `_TopLevelEnvelopeScanner` validate the complete streaming JSON grammar at every depth, not only balanced braces/strings and selected authority fields. A hard row may update `last_physical_seq` or `next_after_seq` only after that validation and exact owner/event-ID checks succeed. A malformed hard row must be recorded as malformed without suppressing a later valid lower sequence.
2. Capture and validate the bounded top-level terminal envelope before hard-row disposition. 3. Add production-file regressions for both cases: malformed over-hard `seq=999` followed by valid `seq=1` must return the valid row, and a valid over-hard terminal must produce the fixed recovery disposition (including next-page behavior when the current page lacks room).

- Required sandbox target: `tests/test_run_journal.py` — **31 passed**.

Thanks for the follow-up. Two parts of the prior review are now fixed:

- both recovery-marker-too-large branches keep `next_after_seq` at the candidate row until the terminal marker is actually returned;
- bounded replay now has aggregate scan-byte, physical-row, and malformed-diagnostic caps.

2. Reject a modified token as `replay_cursor_invalid` without seeking or advancing sequence authority.
3. Charge the boundary-validation byte to the same physical-work budget (and report it), or validate the boundary without extra unaccounted I/O.
4. Add regressions that mutate an otherwise valid token's offset/sequence fields to a later valid newline and prove no rows can be skipped, plus a resumed-call oracle that counts every physical read against the aggregate cap.
