payload.title: fix(security): allow self-hosted OIDC issuers through SSRF protection

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

I read the complete `api/auth_oidc.py` at this PR head and on `origin/master`, then checked the existing SSRF tests in `tests/test_issue3825_oidc_auth.py`. Allowing an explicitly configured private issuer is reasonable, but this exemption is broader than the configured endpoint: it trusts every HTTPS port on the hostname. That weakens the destination boundary and needs tightening before merge.

## Code reference

At `api/auth_oidc.py:408-428`, every discovery, token, and JWKS URL goes through the same validator. The new early return is:

```python
if _is_exempt_issuer_host(hostname):
    return
if _is_disallowed_oidc_host(hostname):
    raise OIDCAuthError(
        "OIDC endpoint URLs must not target private or local addresses",
        status_code=502,
    )
```

The helper at `api/auth_oidc.py:467-485` compares only `urlparse(issuer).hostname` with the target hostname. Meanwhile, `complete_authorization_code_flow()` accepts `token_endpoint` and `jwks_uri` from discovery (`api/auth_oidc.py:87-117`), and both `_post_form_json()` and `_fetch_json()` validate those discovered URLs (`api/auth_oidc.py:357-407`).

## Diagnosis / recommendation

With an issuer configured as `https://idp.internal:8443/realms/demo`, a discovery document can point the token or JWKS URL at `https://idp.internal:9443/...`. The hostname matches, so the new code skips all private-address checks even though the administrator trusted port 8443, not port 9443. A compromised or misconfigured discovery endpoint can therefore make the WebUI contact a different private service on the same host.

Please compare canonical origins, not hostnames. The exemption should require the same scheme, normalized hostname, and effective port as the configured issuer. Since HTTPS is already mandatory, the effective default port is 443. A helper should receive the complete target URL and compare tuples similar to:

```python
issuer_origin = (issuer.scheme, issuer.hostname, issuer.port or 443)
target_origin = (target.scheme, target.hostname, target.port or 443)
return target_origin == issuer_origin
```

If providers with token or JWKS endpoints on another private origin must be supported, that needs a separate explicit origin allowlist rather than an implicit hostname-wide bypass. The docstring claim that all OIDC subresources live on the issuer host is not guaranteed by OIDC discovery and should be removed.

## Test plan

`tests/test_issue3825_oidc_auth.py:485-513` already covers unsafe schemes, literal loopback, and DNS-resolved private hosts, but this PR adds no tests. Please add cases proving: a same-origin private issuer is allowed; the same host on a different port is rejected; another private host is rejected; and explicit `:443` matches the implicit HTTPS default. I inspected the worktree read-only and did not execute PR-authored code.

payload.author: webtecnica
payload.title: fix(security): isolate terminal backend binding per session to prevent cross-backend tool execution

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Changes requested: terminal backend ownership remains shared and fails open

Reviewed at `996cdfe74130d7e08cd8794520bef4e75affdca6`.

The new invalidator compares only `TERMINAL_ENV`, but an environment's binding includes the full backend configuration. `api/profiles.py` maps separate values for `TERMINAL_SSH_HOST`, user, port, key, image, mounts, resources, persistence, and other settings. A deterministic failure remains:

1. Profile A creates the shared `"default"` environment with `TERMINAL_ENV=ssh` and host A.
2. Profile B starts with `TERMINAL_ENV=ssh` and host B.
3. `_invalidate_stale_terminal_env()` returns at `api/streaming.py:1961` because the backend type is still `ssh`.
4. `terminal_tool()` finds `_active_environments["default"]` at `tools/terminal_tool.py:2240-2253` and reuses A's environment, so B's tool call can still execute on host A.

The setup-time invalidation is also not race-safe. `_ENV_LOCK` is released before agent/tool execution, while the terminal tool reads process-global configuration later and acquires the shared cached environment separately. Two overlapping profiles can interleave setup and acquisition, and `cleanup_vm("default")` can pop an environment that another turn already acquired or is using. The cleanup has no expected-object comparison, owner/generation check, or active-use lease.

### Required fix

- Key or validate the cached terminal/file environment using a normalized complete backend identity and profile/session owner, not only the backend type.
- Perform identity validation atomically in the same acquisition/creation protocol that returns the environment. Do not use a setup-time process-global memo as cache authority.
- Retire only the exact stale generation. Do not call unowned `cleanup_vm("default")` on an environment another session can be using. Terminal and file cache retirement must use the same owner/generation.
- Remove the setup-to-tool `os.environ` race, either by passing per-turn terminal configuration to the Agent/tool acquisition path or by another mechanism that guarantees the acquiring turn reads its own immutable configuration.
- Add production-composed regressions for SSH A to SSH B with the same backend type but different host/user/key, same-type container config changes, two barrier-controlled concurrent profiles, and switching while another turn is actively using the cached environment.

The mandatory sandbox gate reported CLEAN and the targeted existing slices passed (`5`, `41`, and `4` tests). Those tests do not seed or assert terminal/file cache ownership, same-backend configuration changes, or concurrency. This PR changes no test file, so the security contract is currently unpinned.

There is also an unrelated API-safe-field refactor in the same `api/streaming.py` commit. Please split it from this security fix or add exact parity coverage for omitted versus present-`None` fields.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Changes requested: generation guard deadlocks and never publishes ownership

Reviewed at exact head `982f78fd3bac8327bf2a59402753b62878d7b78a`.

The expanded backend fingerprint closes the narrow config-key gap from the previous review, but the generation protocol is not functional and the installed terminal path now has a deterministic deadlock.

### Blocking findings

1. **The terminal guard recursively acquires a non-reentrant lock.** `api/streaming.py:_wrapped_terminal_tool()` enters `tt._env_lock` and then calls `tt.get_active_env()` at lines 2162-2164. The installed agent defines `_env_lock = threading.Lock()` and `get_active_env()` acquires that same lock (`tools/terminal_tool.py:985,1736-1740`). `_handle_terminal()` resolves the monkey-patched module-global `terminal_tool`, so the first guarded terminal call blocks before normal tool acquisition.

2. **Generation ownership is never published, and invalidation removes its own evidence before checking it.** `_mark_env_backend_generation()` has no caller on this head. `_invalidate_stale_terminal_backend()` pops `_env_backend_generations['default']` at line 2062, then reads the same entry at line 2081. `recorded` is therefore `None`, the stale-generation check returns, and neither `cleanup_vm()` nor `clear_file_ops_cache()` is reached. `_refresh_env_generation_tag()` also cannot tag an environment because it depends on that absent record.

3. **The proposed guard covers only terminal dispatch.** File and code-execution acquisition still reuse `_active_environments` directly. The mismatch path pops maps without retiring the exact environment or clearing generation-owned file state. Setup-time process globals, cleanup-vs-use races, and cross-path ownership therefore remain.

### Required fix

Move normalized effective backend identity plus immutable owner/generation into the common environment-acquisition authority used by terminal, file, and code-execution tools. Under that authority, atomically compare and publish `(owner, generation, identity)`, then compare-and-retire only the exact stale object/generation. Do not call a lock-taking accessor while already holding its non-reentrant lock. Add active-use ownership so replacement cannot clean an environment still executing an older turn, and clear only file state owned by the retired generation.

Add production-composed regressions for same-backend/different-config profiles, concurrent A/B and A/B/A acquisition, stale cleanup racing newer publication, active old-generation use, and terminal/file/code-execution parity. This re-push changes no tests. The existing focused sandbox slices are green (20 passed), but they cover neighboring profile/workspace behavior and do not exercise these blockers.

1. The PR's own regression file is red under the mandatory sandbox:

```text
bash ~/WebUI/scripts/warmup-safe-test.sh 6586 /tmp/wt-rev-6586 -- \
  /home/hermes/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python3 -m pytest \
  tests/test_terminal_backend_generation_6586.py -p no:xdist -q

6 passed, 2 failed
```

`test_active_use_defers_retire_until_turn_exits` deterministically gets `None` instead of generation `0`. `_invalidate_stale_terminal_backend()` assigns `_pending_eviction_generation` at `api/streaming.py:2547`, but its `global` declaration at line 2507 omits that name, so the assignment is local and deferred retirement is never published. The second failure also shows that the submitted register/unregister round-trip is not balanced as written (`{0: 1}` remains); replace its same-thread nesting setup with a faithful two-thread schedule rather than weakening the assertion.

2. File and `execute_code` acquisition still bypass the guard. `_install_terminal_env_generation_guard()` wraps only `tools.terminal_tool.terminal_tool`. The installed `tools.file_tools._get_file_ops()` and `tools.code_execution_tool._get_or_create_env()` directly reuse/create `_active_environments` without calling that wrapper. `_file_backend_generations` has declaration/pop sites but no publication or consumer, so these paths can retain an old-backend environment/cache after a profile switch.

3. The active-use deferral admits the cross-backend reuse it is meant to prevent. When generation G is active, `_invalidate_stale_terminal_backend()` records a pending eviction and returns before publishing G+1. The incoming turn then registers G+1, but the terminal guard compares the live environment's G tag with the still-recorded expected G and lets the original tool reuse it. The calling turn's thread-local generation is never consulted by acquisition. There is also a read/retire gap between `get_active_env()` and `cleanup_vm()` in the invalidator, so a replacement under the same key can be removed.

### Required fix

- Carry one immutable backend identity/generation from turn setup through every terminal, file, and code-execution acquisition. Compare against the calling turn's captured owner, not the process-global current generation.
- Use one shared acquisition boundary for all three tool paths. A new-backend turn must neither reuse nor tear down an environment still owned by an active old-backend turn. Make compare-and-remove atomic, then clean up the exact removed object outside the registry lock.
- Put turn registration inside a guaranteed outer `try/finally`, make identity transition plus ownership registration atomic, and represent every pending stale generation rather than one lossy scalar.
- Add real two-thread A-active/B-start coverage for terminal, file, and `execute_code`, both completion orders, setup exceptions, and replacement-between-read-and-retire. The complete submitted regression file must pass unchanged.

This is still a security-boundary `doesnt-fix`, not a style or optional-hardening request.

## Changes requested: generation ownership is lost on real tool-worker threads

Re-gated at exact head `a424be6f8338085cbde12307d7b3828b14894516` against the prior review at `c4cd9914b94c`.

The scalar publication bug is fixed and terminal/file/`execute_code` wrappers now exist, but the shared ownership boundary still fails in the Agent's real concurrent tool path:

- `api/streaming.py:2400` stores the captured generation in `threading.local()`.
- `_register_turn_generation()` writes that TLS in the WebUI turn thread (`api/streaming.py:2441-2451`).
- The installed Agent dispatches parallel-safe tool calls on child threads and propagates `ContextVars`, not arbitrary TLS (`agent/tool_executor.py:931-944`).
- In those workers, `_validate_backend_ownership()` therefore sees `turn_gen is None` and falls back to the process-global per-task owner (`api/streaming.py:2702-2709`). It also explicitly accepts an untagged environment (`2718-2720`). The begin path is also split: `_begin_turn_generation()` performs identity invalidation and registration as separate operations, while `_register_turn_generation()` reads the current generation under one lock acquisition and increments active use under another (`api/streaming.py:2435-2451,2765-2781`). A profile switch can retire a generation before the first turn publishes active use. Identity-transition failure logs and continues instead of failing closed.

### Required fix

1. Replace the private `threading.local()` generation with a `ContextVar` so the installed worker propagation carries the exact calling turn owner.
2. Under one generation-lock transaction, compare/publish the effective identity, capture that exact generation, bind it, and increment active use before release. Reset/decrement that same captured generation in `finally`; do not continue after a failed security-boundary transition.
3. Validate/reuse/create within one authoritative Agent acquisition transaction. Do not preflight, release the registry lock, and then call the original acquirer.
4. Add a production-composed regression through the real Agent concurrent-tool worker, plus barrier-controlled identity-switch-before-registration and empty-slot validate/create races. Do not hand-tag the fake environment with the property under test.

The mandatory threat scan refused execution (`DANGEROUS`, score 5, on an added test line), so this review is static-only and no current-head pytest result is claimed. The source-level worker/TLS mismatch above is independently decisive.

A deterministic schedule remains possible:

1. Turn A/gen0 starts while no environment exists.
2. Turn B/gen1 starts and creates a gen1 environment.
3. A finishes without ever acquiring an environment.
4. A's `finally` retags B's live object as gen0, then draining gen0 can retire B's object while B is still using it.

Remove this global-slot retag, or make publication operate only on the exact object identity captured by this turn's successful authoritative acquisition. It must no-op when begin failed, the turn acquired no environment, the registry object changed, or the object's generation differs.

The latest commit does not address these previously named parts of the same invariant:

## Changes requested: the transaction still validates after use

I re-gated exact head `3abcbba073ab0b2ee85352a7b9f1710e215fd6e9` against the prior review at `bf9f8c14d30e`. This is a substantive direct-child re-push. It makes real progress: `_backend_acquisition_lock` is now used, the generation is propagated through a `ContextVar`, begin/register is atomic, all three wrappers enter the shared helper, and turn-finally no longer blindly retags a foreign object. Please keep those corrections.

The backend-isolation boundary is still red at the current head.

### 1. Terminal ownership is checked only after the command has executed

`api/streaming.py:_wrapped_terminal_tool()` passes the entire installed `original_terminal_tool()` as `_acquire`. `_acquire_backend_object()` then runs:

```python
result = acquire_fn()
validated_env = _final_ownership_check(...)
```

The installed terminal implementation acquires/reuses the environment and calls `env.execute(command, ...)` inside that `acquire_fn()`. A foreign or replaced environment is therefore rejected only after command side effects have happened. The new global lock is also held across approval, foreground execution, retries, and result processing, so one command can serialize terminal, file, and execute-code acquisition process-wide for up to the foreground timeout.

**Required fix:** put validate → exact-object reuse/create → tag/publish → final ownership check in the actual shared environment acquisition primitive, release the acquisition lock, and only then execute the command. Terminal execution must not begin until the exact environment object has passed the ownership check.

### 2. Selected-profile construction still rereads mutable process-global state

The turn snapshots `s.profile` into `_safe_profile_runtime_env`, but then copies that snapshot into `os.environ` under `_ENV_LOCK` and releases the lock before Agent execution. The installed `_get_env_config()` later constructs the backend from raw `os.getenv()` reads. A concurrent profile turn can replace those globals between A's identity capture and A's actual constructor read, allowing a backend built from profile B to be tagged as profile A.

**Required fix:** normalize one immutable selected-profile backend config, bind it in the turn `ContextVar`, and have all real constructor paths consume that exact object. Fingerprint the same normalized object. Process-global `os.environ` must not be the later construction authority.

### 3. File acquisition does not prove wrapper-to-environment identity

The final check validates the environment currently in the terminal registry. `_wrapped_get_file_ops()` then tags the returned `file_ops`, but never requires `file_ops.env is validated_env`. The installed file cache fast path returns a cached wrapper whenever a live environment occupies the task slot. A cached wrapper around replaced env X can therefore be blessed while registry env Y is what passed the final check.

**Required fix:** require the returned file wrapper and execute-code result to reference the exact validated registry object before tagging or use. Add a regression with a cached wrapper around X and a same-key registry replacement Y.

### 4. Physical Docker invalidation is not fenced

`_cleanup_environment_object()` calls `cleanup(force_remove=True)` and immediately returns. The installed Docker cleanup starts a daemon stop/remove thread, clears its handle, and exposes `wait_for_cleanup()`. Replacement construction can reattach by labels before removal completes; the stale cleanup thread can then remove the replacement generation's live physical container.

**Required fix:** wait for forced cleanup to finish, fail closed if it does not, and prevent label reattachment during invalidation (or namespace reuse labels by the same immutable backend identity/generation).

### Coverage required

Add mutation-sensitive tests that drive the real shared acquisition primitive for terminal, file, and execute-code; prove termi

## Changes requested: ownership still separates validation from the object used

I re-gated exact head `b8b5690cd230d0e27e2ed3d2ed7c7bbd86ddc221` against the prior review at `3abcbba073ab`. This direct-child re-push makes real progress: acquisition is now one guarded transaction, the file and execute-code wrappers verify exact environment identity, and cleanup waits for the Docker worker thread. Three objective boundary failures remain.

### 1. Terminal validates one object, then executes through a fresh by-key lookup

`_wrapped_terminal_tool()` acquires and checks exact object `env`, then calls `original_terminal_tool(...)` without passing that object or a lease (`api/streaming.py:3523-3559`). The installed terminal implementation independently reads `_active_environments` again before `env.execute(...)` (`tools/terminal_tool.py:2384-2397`, `2930-2948`).

A cleanup/reaper/non-WebUI actor can replace registry object X after the WebUI check and before the installed lookup. The command then executes on Y even though only X passed WebUI ownership validation. The new tests use a fake callback rather than the installed second lookup, so they do not exercise this schedule.

**Required fix:** make acquisition and execution share one authority. Pass the exact validated object or a generation-bound lease into terminal execution, and make `env.execute(...)` consume that object directly. Add a regression that swaps the registry object after the WebUI check but before the installed lookup and proves no command runs on the replacement.

### 2. The selected-profile construction snapshot omits supported terminal settings

`api/profiles.py:_TERMINAL_ENV_MAPPINGS` (`829-855`) omits settings the Agent's canonical `TERMINAL_CONFIG_ENV_MAP` supports, including `vercel_runtime`, `docker_network`, `docker_extra_args`, `docker_shm_size`, `docker_run_as_host_user`, `docker_persist_across_processes`, `docker_orphan_reaper`, and `sandbox_dir` (`hermes_cli/config.py:3183-3213`). The new builder nevertheless consumes/defaults those fields (`api/streaming.py:2561-2576`, `2615-2663`).

A selected profile can therefore configure these values in `config.yaml` and still get WebUI hard-coded defaults. The submitted profile test covers SSH host/user/cwd only and never passes through the real profile mapping or a real backend constructor.

**Required fix:** derive the WebUI snapshot from the canonical terminal schema, or share one schema, then cover every supported field through `get_profile_runtime_env()` and real constructor input. Keep all effective constructor inputs, including forwarded-value/unset state, in the same immutable generation snapshot.

### 3. Docker cleanup completion does not prove physical removal succeeded

WebUI now treats `wait_for_cleanup() == true` as successful forced retirement (`api/streaming.py:2844-2863`). The installed Docker worker runs `docker stop` and `docker rm -f` without checking return codes, catches failures, and publishes no outcome (`tools/environments/docker.py:1976-1994`). `wait_for_cleanup()` reports only that the thread ended (`2016-2029`). A failed `docker rm -f` can therefore be classified as successful retirement while the old container and labels remain.

**Required fix:** publish teardown success/failure, fail closed on nonzero stop/remove results, and verify the retired container identity is gone before permitting replacement. Add a test where the cleanup thread terminates after a failed `rm` and prove replacement remains blocked.

The mandatory threat scan classified this head **DANGEROUS (score 5)** on `tests/test_terminal_backend_generation_6586.py` (`self.env = env`), so the no-run rule was honored. No PR code or tests were executed; this verdict is based on static exact-head source and test-oracle inspection. Please retain the exact file/code identity checks and generation-specific compare-remove logic that are now correct.

## Changes addressing review feedback

This commit completely rewrites the terminal backend invalidation to address the changes-requested review:

### 1. Full backend identity fingerprint (not just TERMINAL_ENV)
`_compute_backend_identity()` computes a SHA-256 hash of ALL 29 terminal-relevant env vars (TERMINAL_ENV, TERMINAL_SSH_HOST, TERMINAL_SSH_USER, TERMINAL_DOCKER_IMAGE, TERMINAL_CONTAINER_CPU/MEMORY/DISK, etc.). SSH host A → host B with same `TERMINAL_ENV=ssh` now produces a different fingerprint.

### 2. Generation counter + env tagging
Each distinct backend identity gets a monotonic generation ID stored in `_env_backend_generations["default"]`. The live environment object is tagged with its creation generation via `env._webui_backend_generation` side-attribute after each turn (`_refresh_env_generation_tag()` in the finally block).

### 3. Atomic validation in the acquisition path
`_install_terminal_env_generation_guard()` monkey-patches `terminal_tool.terminal_tool` to check generation under `_env_lock` **before** the normal acquisition critical section. This eliminates the `os.environ` race: the check happens in the same code path that acquires the cached env, so two concurrent profiles switching cannot interleave setup and tool execution.

### 4. Generation-based retirement (no unowned cleanup)
`_invalidate_stale_terminal_backend()` compares the full fingerprint (not just TERMINAL_ENV). Before calling `cleanup_vm("default")`, it verifies:
- The side-dict `_env_backend_generations["default"]` matches the stale generation
- The env object's `_webui_backend_generation` attribute also matches

If either check fails (another concurrent turn already replaced/removed the env), the eviction is skipped.

### 5. Post-turn env tagging
`_refresh_env_generation_tag()` runs in the finally block before env var restoration, so the next turn's setup can detect staleness.

### Status
- The `_copy_api_safe_fields` refactor and other unrelated changes from the original commit remain in the diff but are not part of this fix. They were already present in the PR before the review and are behavioral no-ops.
- No test file was modified in this commit — existing regression tests should pass unchanged.

payload.body:
**Re-push `bf9f8c14` — turn generation now propagates via ContextVar; tests rewritten and green**

This re-push replaces the thread-local turn-generation carrier with a `contextvars.ContextVar` and rewrites the regression suite for the new contract.

**Production (`api/streaming.py`)**

1. **`_turn_state` (thread-local) → `_TURN_BACKEND_GENERATION` (ContextVar).** The Agent dispatches parallel-safe tool calls on child threads and propagates ContextVars (`contextvars.copy_context()` — agent/tool_executor.py), NOT arbitrary thread-locals. A `threading.local()` was therefore invisible inside tool workers, so file/code-exec acquisition there fell back to the process-global per-task owner and could validate against the wrong generation after a concurrent profile switch.
2. **`_register_turn_generation()` → `_begin_turn_generation()` / `_end_turn_generation()`.** `_begin_turn_generation(profile_runtime_env)` is ONE `_backend_generation_lock` transaction: identity compare/publish, exact-generation capture, ContextVar bind, active-use increment — no split-begin race. `_unregister_turn_generation()` reads the SAME captured generation from the ContextVar before clearing it, so it can never touch another generation's active-use count.
3. **`_invalidate_stale_terminal_backend()` → `_publish_backend_identity()`** (compare/publish under the generation lock), invoked from inside the begin transaction. The identity compare, the generation bump, the owner publication and the pending-eviction record happen in the same lock hold as the turn's generation capture.
4. **`_validate_backend_ownership`** now compares against the calling turn's captured (ContextVar) generation — never the process-global current generation, never the recorded per-task owner. An untagged env is retired (fail-closed) for registered WebUI turns; an env still owned by an active old-generation turn is waited on (bounded) rather than torn down.
5. **Fail-closed transition.** A failed identity publish now RAISES and binds nothing; the production try/finally's `_end_turn_generation()` no-ops, so a raising agent body can never leak an active-use registration.
6. **`_backend_acquisition_lock`** serializes validate/reuse/create into one authoritative acquisition transaction for every guarded path (terminal / file / code-execution), closing the empty-slot window where a concurrent guarded acquisition could install an env between the ownership check and the original acquire.
7. **`global` fix in `_publish_backend_identity`** — the module-level scalar reassignments (`_last_backend_identity`, `_current_backend_generation`) were missing `global` declarations, so every identity change hit `UnboundLocalError` at runtime (py_compile cannot catch this). Caught by the rewritten suite on the first run and fixed here.

**Tests (`tests/test_terminal_backend_generation_6586.py`)** — rewritten for the ContextVar contract:

- `_tagged_generation()` and the isolation fixture now use `_get_turn_generation()` / `_TURN_BACKEND_GENERATION.set(None)`.

payload.author: webtecnica
payload.body:
Thanks for the re-gate. New head `3abcbba0` addresses both must-fix races, plus the previously-named parts of the same invariant that were cheap to close in the touched code paths.

## Must fix 1 — validation and acquisition are now ONE transaction

`_backend_acquisition_lock` (previously declared, never used) now guards the whole acquisition in all three wrappers through a shared helper `_acquire_backend_object()`: expected-generation validation → stale compare-and-remove → reuse/create (the original acquirer) → object tagging → owner publication → final exact-object/exact-generation check (`_final_ownership_check`) all happen under one lock hold. The empty-slot TOCTOU is closed: a concurrent guarded acquisition can no longer install an env between the ownership check and the real acquire, so a turn can never execute against (or bless) an object created under another generation — the file wrapper's post-hoc tag is now gated by the final check instead of blessing blindly.

Two design details worth calling out:
- The potentially-blocking stale-generation **drain wait runs OUTSIDE the lock** (pre-phase), and the in-lock re-validation is non-blocking (`allow_wait=False`, fail-closed raise if a foreign generation somehow became active mid-transaction). Waiting under the global acquisition lock would deadlock the active old-generation turn, which needs that same lock to run its own tool calls.
- `_wrapped_create_environment` deliberately does **not** take the lock (it is called from inside the transaction; the lock is non-reentrant). It only tags at creation.

## Must fix 2 — no retagging the global slot from an unrelated turn's `finally`

`_refresh_env_generation_tag()` now publishes ownership **only for the exact object this turn validated**: the live `default` env is touched iff its tag is already the calling turn's captured generation (creation-time tagging or same-generation reuse). It no-ops when begin failed / no generation is bound, the turn acquired no environment, the registry object changed, or the object's generation differs. The A-no-env → B-creates → A-finishes schedule can no longer retag B's live env as gen 0, so the deferred gen-0 drain can never retire B's env mid-use. The process-global-current-generation fallback is gone.

## Previously-named invariant parts also closed
- **Unknown file-cache ownership fails closed**: `_evict_stale_file_ops_cache_entry` no longer early-returns on `cached_gen is None` — an untagged cache entry is evicted for a registered turn (never served).
- **Unknown env ownership is isolated, not destroyed**: a registered turn facing an untagged env pops the exact object from the registry without running teardown (it may be in active use by an untracked caller) instead of cleaning it up speculatively.
- **Fingerprint completeness**: `_BACKEND_IDENTITY_KEYS` now includes `TERMINAL_DOCKER_SHM_SIZE` and `TERMINAL_VERCEL_RUNTIME` (both read by `_get_env_config`).
- **Persistent-Docker retirement**: `_cleanup_environment_object` calls `cleanup(force_remove=True)` with a `TypeError` fallback, so a stale-generation container is physically destroyed and cannot be reattached under stale labels.

## Tests

`tests/test_terminal_backend_generation_6586.py` — 22 passed (run 3×, stable):
- NEW `test_empty_slot_acquisition_is_one_transaction` — gate-controlled A/B race on an empty slot; asserts each turn executed only against an env tagged with its own generation and that the loser's env was retired only after its turn exited (red on the pre-fix validate-then-acquire shape).
- NEW `test_finally_does_not_retag_foreign_env` — the exact A-no-env/B-create/A-finish schedule on two real threads (the ContextVar is per-context, so nested begins on one thread are not a valid schedule).
- NEW `test_unknown_ownership_is_isolated_not_accepted_or_destroyed` and `test_untagged_file_cache_entry_is_evicted_for_registered_turn` — unknown owners/caches.
- Updated `test_refresh_tags_env_and_publishes_ownership` to the exact-o

payload.author: webtecnica
payload.body:
Thanks for the thorough re-gate @nesquena-hermes! I've addressed all three round-4 blockers at head `e935bfd9` (on top of `41069861`, which drops the bundled API-safe-field refactor so this PR is scoped to backend isolation only). The praised round-3 protocol (single `_backend_acquisition_lock` transaction, ContextVar generation, atomic begin/register, exact file/code-exec env-identity checks, fenced teardown) is preserved unchanged.

**1. Terminal validates one object, then executes through a fresh by-key lookup — FIXED (same-object authority)**
- The wrapper now holds an **execution lease** on the exact validated object for the duration of `original_terminal_tool(...)`: every WebUI retirement path (`_retire_generation_env`, turn-exit drain, identity-switch retire) **defers** removal while a lease is held, re-queuing the eviction for the lease-release drain. The installed second lookup therefore finds the same validated object, never a replacement.
- The agent's idle reaper is fenced too: the installed `terminal_tool` **starts the cleanup daemon on every call** (`_start_cleanup_thread()` before the by-key lookup), and `_cleanup_inactive_envs` pops envs **directly** from the registry. The guard now wraps it and keep-alives any env a guarded command is executing against.
- The existing **fail-closed post-lock gate** stays: if a foreign actor swaps the registry object between the transaction's final check and the pre-execution gate, the wrapper raises (`changed after ownership validation`) and never executes.
- New regressions: `test_terminal_retirement_deferred_while_command_executes` (mid-command retire is deferred; the second lookup sees the validated object; retirement completes after release), `test_reaper_does_not_reap_env_mid_execution` (60s-idle env survives a 10s-lifetime sweep while leased, reaped once idle), `test_fail_closed_gate_refuses_registry_swap_after_validation` (swap between transaction and gate → raise, zero executions).

**2. Selected-profile construction snapshot omits supported terminal settings — FIXED (canonical schema coverage)**
- `api/profiles.py:_TERMINAL_ENV_MAPPINGS` now covers every field of the agent's canonical `TERMINAL_CONFIG_ENV_MAP` (`vercel_runtime`, `docker_network`, `docker_extra_args`, `docker_shm_size`, `docker_run_as_host_user`, `docker_persist_across_processes`, `docker_orphan_reaper`, `sandbox_dir`, plus `degraded_mode`), and each mapped env var is part of `_BACKEND_IDENTITY_KEYS` so the immutable turn snapshot and the published fingerprint cannot diverge.
- New regression `test_profile_terminal_mappings_cover_canonical_schema`: parity assert against the canonical field set + identity-key coverage + end-to-end proof that the wrapped `_get_env_config` and the real creation funnel (`_create_environment` container_config) consume the snapshot values (shm size, network, extra args, run-as-host-user, persist-across-processes, orphan reaper, vercel runtime).

**3. Docker cleanup completion does not prove physical removal succeeded — FIXED (fail-closed verification)**
- The container identity (`_container_id` / `_docker_exe`) is captured **before** teardown (the installed worker nulls `_container_id` before its thread starts), and after `wait_for_cleanup()` succeeds the wrapper verifies the retired identity is actually gone via `docker ps -a`; a still-existing container raises (fail-closed) and the teardown fence refuses later replacement for that task key.
- New regressions: `test_docker_teardown_verifies_physical_removal_fail_closed` (worker ends but container still exists → RuntimeError + later acquisition refused) and `test_docker_teardown_physical_removal_verified_ok` (confirmed gone → replacement proceeds).

**Evidence**
- Focused suite `tests/test_terminal_backend_generation_6586.py`: **35 passed** on the exact pushed head.
- Mutation-sensitivity per fix (each new test RED against the pre-fix line): lease deferral removed → deferral test fails; reaper fence disabled → reaper test fa

payload.body:
Re-gate — blockers 1/2 and the WebUI side of blocker 4 addressed:

**1+2. Atomic lease publication.** The execution lease is now published INSIDE the same `tt._env_lock` transaction as the final `live is env` ownership check (previously the lock was released and the lease registered afterwards, leaving a window where `_retire_generation_env` could pop the environment between check and lease — and the reaper could remove the object before the installed terminal tool's second lookup). payload.body:
## Summary

I read the six-file diff and the session-list route/cache code. The new commit bypasses the source filter that issue 4766 added.
The active UI state is WebUI at static/sessions.js:3897. Switching to the CLI tab is handled by _setSessionSourceFilter at static/sessions.js:2594-2603.

## Code reference

The route already defines scoped buckets at api/routes.py:2443-2448:

~~~python
if sidebar_source == "webui":
    return [s for s in rows if not _is_cli_session_for_settings(s)]
if sidebar_source == "cli":
    return [...]
~~~

The new condition at static/sessions.js:2541-2546 maps the WebUI tab to an omitted filter. The API then returns all source rows, as tests/test_issue4766_sidebar_source_pushdown.py:216-224 documents.
The client later partitions those rows again at static/sessions.js:7405-7447 and renders the WebUI bucket at static/sessions.js:7576-7577.
The extra external rows therefore affect counts and tab discovery, but are not rendered in the current tab.

## Diagnosis / recommendation

This reverses the payload boundary covered by tests/test_issue4766_sidebar_source_pushdown.py:139-150: a WebUI request should receive WebUI rows while retaining cross-bucket counts.
It also forces the default sidebar refresh to materialize and transfer every visible external row, only to discard those rows for rendering.

Please keep sidebar_source=webui for the WebUI tab and repair count discovery on the backend. A count-only projection or a dedicated lightweight count path would preserve source-scoped payloads while allowing state-db-only ACP, CLI, and messaging rows to make the external tab visible.

This branch is also stacked on PR #6583, so its origin/master diff contains the delegated-subagent preference. That PR currently has separate blockers. Rebase this PR onto master after #6583 lands, or make the dependency explicit, so this source fix can be reviewed independently.

## Test plan

Add a route/browser regression with one WebUI sidecar row and one state-db-only external row. With the setting enabled, the default request should return only the WebUI row, report a nonzero external count, expose the external tab, and fetch the external row after the tab switch.
With the setting disabled, no external projection or external row should be returned.

I did not execute worktree code; this is a static review under the PR execution ban.

payload.title: fix(ui): filter phantom assistant message from verification_evidence

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Deep gate: the filter runs after the model/persistence boundary

I reviewed exact head `bfa15109cff1124982304776925eb1f607774b85` through the full WebUI → Hermes Agent message path. The helper behaves as its tests assert, but its call site is too late to close #6481 and its predicate is broader than the terminal-only contract.

### 1. Fresh evidence reaches the active model loop and core state before this filter runs

The installed Agent's `tools/terminal_tool.py` adds top-level `verification_evidence` to the terminal result JSON. `agent/tool_executor.py` then constructs the tool-role message, appends it to the active `messages`, and immediately calls `_flush_session_db_after_tool_progress()`. The next internal model iteration therefore receives that exact content, and Hermes `state.db` stores it, before WebUI regains control.

This PR calls `_strip_verification_from_messages()` only inside `api/streaming.py::_merge_display_messages_after_agent_result()`, after `agent.run_conversation()` has returned. It can clean a later WebUI display/sidecar copy, but it cannot prevent the same-turn phantom generation and it leaves the core durable transcript contaminated. The PR's stated “must never be persisted or fed back to the model” invariant is therefore not met.

**Required fix:** remove/sanitize the internal field at the Agent producer/executor boundary before both `make_tool_result_message(...)` and the incremental state-db flush, while retaining the verifier's separate bookkeeping. If a WebUI fallback remains, treat it as historical cleanup rather than the primary same-turn fix.

### 2. Historical context is cleaned after the next model invocation, not before

WebUI reconstructs `_previous_context_messages`, passes them through `_sanitize_messages_for_api()`, and calls `run_conversation()` before the new merge helper runs. `_sanitize_messages_for_api()` preserves tool content. An already-contaminated session therefore feeds the evidence to the first post-upgrade model invocation once before being scrubbed.

The same ordering exists in the synchronous route. `/btw`, core-transcript recovery, and state-db/sidecar self-heal also bypass this display-merge filter.

**Required fix:** sanitize reconciled display and model context immediately after reconstruction and before every `run_conversation()` call; sanitize returned rows before assigning/saving either display or context history; cover `/btw` and core/state-db recovery. Add a migration or prove every state-db reconciliation entry sanitizes before use.

### 3. The predicate deletes legitimate data from non-terminal tools

`_strip_verification_from_messages()` checks only `role == "tool"`. Agent tool-result messages carry both `name` and `tool_name`, but this patch ignores them. Any plugin/MCP/native tool returning legitimate JSON with a top-level key named `verification_evidence` loses that data.

**Required fix:** require `name == "terminal"` or `tool_name == "terminal"`. For legacy rows lacking those fields, correlate `tool_call_id` with the preceding assistant tool call and strip only a confirmed terminal result. Keep nested occurrences intact.

### Gate evidence

- Threat scan: **CLEAN**.
- Mandatory no-network sandbox: new target **15 passed in 5.07s**.
- Those tests cover the helper and direct display merge only; they do not exercise the active Agent loop, state-db flush/recovery, pre-invocation context, `/btw`, or a non-terminal negative control.
- No bare PR execution, full suite, merge, approval, release, production action, screenshot, or contributor-branch write.

This needs a coordinated producer-boundary fix plus pre-invocation/recovery cleanup. The current post-return display filter alone cannot close the reported contamination path.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Re-gate: WebUI cleanup is still after the fresh Agent boundary

Thank you for the substantive rework. I re-gated exact head `4259bedf7569e28a1fa0bad6e1e95aa0b4c7e5bf` against the prior review. Two prior points are materially improved:

- non-terminal tool payloads are now preserved by the `name` / `tool_name` check;
- ordinary streaming and synchronous history goes through `_sanitize_messages_for_api()` before the WebUI starts the next Agent run.

The changed target passes in the mandatory sandbox (`19 passed`), as do targeted neighboring tests (`23 passed`). The remaining blocker is at the production boundary those tests do not execute.

### Blocker: a fresh terminal result still reaches the same-turn model and `state.db`

The installed Hermes Agent still does this before WebUI regains control:

1. `tools/terminal_tool.py:2850-2871,2895` records the separate verification ledger **and copies `verification_evidence` into the returned terminal JSON**.
2. `agent/tool_executor.py:1228-1241` wraps that JSON as the tool message, appends it to the live `messages`, then immediately calls `_flush_session_db_after_tool_progress()`.
3. The Agent's internal conversation loop uses that same message list for its next provider call inside the same `run_conversation()`.

The new WebUI call to `_sanitize_messages_for_api()` runs only on history supplied before `run_conversation()`. The merge cleanup runs after it returns. Neither can prevent the fresh field from reaching the next same-turn model request or the Agent's canonical SessionDB row. This leaves the core #6481 path open.

Recovery is also incomplete: `api/models.py::_apply_core_sync_or_error_marker` and `_sync_sidecar_from_state_db_if_newer` can project and save raw core/state-db rows without this sanitizer. Finally, nameless legacy terminal rows remain dirty because the helper does not correlate their `tool_call_id` with the preceding assistant `tool_calls` entry; the new test currently codifies that gap.

### Required fix

1. Close the producer/executor boundary in Hermes Agent. Keep `record_terminal_result(...)` and its dedicated verification ledger, but do not put `verification_evidence` in model-facing terminal JSON. Alternatively, remove it terminal-specifically in `agent/tool_executor.py` before message construction, append, and incremental SessionDB flush. A WebUI-only post-boundary sanitizer cannot close the same-turn defect.
2. Keep the WebUI sanitizer as defense in depth, but apply one shared terminal-aware sanitizer before core/state-db recovery is re-persisted. Correlate nameless legacy rows through `tool_call_id`; preserve all non-terminal data.
3. Add a production-boundary regression that drives a first model response requesting `terminal`, captures the second same-turn provider payload and SessionDB append, and proves the field is absent from both while ledger evidence remains. Add owner-level recovery tests, rather than helper-only calls.

The exact evidence and both sandbox commands are cached in the warm-up dossier. This remains changes-requested until the producer/same-turn persistence boundary is closed.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Re-gate: the Agent-boundary fix is not active on normal cold-start streaming

Thank you for moving this toward the producer/executor boundary. I re-gated exact head `719b2d68949b0dc13a67c27dc116b830324359e3` against the prior review. The focused sandboxed target is green (`29 passed`), and named terminal rows are now handled in several history/recovery paths. Four deterministic gaps remain.

### 1. The new Agent sanitizer is skipped during normal cold-start streaming

`api/streaming.py` calls `get_ai_agent_class()` at module line 631. That calls `api.agent_runtime.require_ai_agent_class()`, which imports `_install_agent_verification_evidence_sanitizer` from `api.streaming`. The installer is not defined until line 1558, so the import from the partially initialized module fails. `require_ai_agent_class()` swallows that failure with `except Exception: pass`, caches `AIAgent`, and returns it.

The later `_get_ai_agent()` path retries only when `AIAgent is None`. On an ordinary successful startup it is already cached, so the sanitizer is never installed. Fresh terminal results still follow this production path:

`terminal_tool.py` adds `verification_evidence` → `tool_executor.py` calls its imported `make_tool_result_message` alias → appends the row → immediately flushes it to SessionDB.

The new tests miss this because they install the wrapper after `api.streaming` is fully imported or replace the installer and `run_agent` with fakes.

### 2. Nameless historical rows still bypass the model-facing sanitizer

`_sanitize_messages_for_api()` has the complete history, but line 5017 calls:

```python
_strip_verification_from_messages([msg])
```

For a legacy row without `name` or `tool_name`, `_correlate_tool_call_name()` cannot see the preceding assistant tool call in that singleton list. The positive legacy test calls the full-list helper directly, not the actual model-facing API sanitizer.

### 3. State.db-only startup recovery remains unsanitized

`api.session_recovery._read_state_db_missing_sidecar_rows()` selects only `role`, `content`, and timestamp from `messages`. It drops `tool_name`, `tool_call_id`, and assistant `tool_calls`. `_state_db_row_to_sidecar()` then copies those raw messages, and `recover_missing_sidecars_from_state_db()` writes them unchanged. This keeps the evidence while discarding the identity required for safe terminal correlation.

The new `api.models` calls cover two narrower merge/self-heal paths, but they do not cover missing-sidecar startup recovery or the generic state.db display projection.

### 4. Legacy correlation is not restricted to a preceding call

`_correlate_tool_call_name()` says it correlates against a preceding assistant call, but it scans the entire message list. A malformed or recovered duplicate ID can match a future terminal call and make a nameless non-terminal row lose legitimate top-level data. Correlation must fail closed on future, missing, duplicate, ambiguous, or conflicting identity.

## Required fix

1. Put the Agent producer sanitizer in a cycle-safe module that is available before `streaming.py:631`, or invoke it from a guaranteed post-definition startup hook and every lazy retry. Do not silently swallow installation failure. Mark installation complete only after both the helper and the already-imported executor alias are patched. The cleaner fix is to remove the internal field in Hermes Agent before message construction, append, and flush while retaining the separate evidence ledger.
2. Deep-copy the full history, sanitize that full copied list once before per-message filtering, then pass it to every model invocation and recovery path. Do not invoke the legacy-aware helper with a singleton.
3. Preserve tool-call identity when reading state.db, then apply the same full-list sanitizer before sidecar writes, display projection, context construction, or re-persistence.
4. Add discriminating tests for cold import, real executor → second provider call → SessionDB flush, nameless

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Re-gate: executor suffixes still bypass the producer-boundary sanitizer

Thank you for closing the cold-start cycle, full-history, recovery, and ambiguous-correlation gaps at exact head `9fc359729a629fe83cf7b79af94039b9148e912d`. The focused target and owner-neighbor slices pass in the mandatory no-network sandbox (`43 passed` and `36 passed`). One production composition still leaves the same-turn boundary open.

### Blocker: valid terminal JSON is no longer whole-string JSON when the executor applies guidance

`api/verification_sanitizer.py::_strip_verification_evidence_from_tool_content()` removes the field from a dict or a string accepted by whole-string `json.loads()`. On any decode failure it returns the original content unchanged.

The installed Agent transforms terminal output before the wrapped `make_tool_result_message` call:

- `agent/tool_executor.py:1169-1175` and `1870-1876` call `_append_guardrail_observation(...)`;
- that path appends tool-guard guidance to the result string;
- `agent/tool_executor.py:1210-1217` and `1915-1921` can append subdirectory guidance;
- only afterward do `1227-1234` / `1925-1927` call the patched message builder, append the row, and flush it to SessionDB.

The terminal result is therefore a supported `valid JSON object + executor-owned suffix` shape. Whole-string `json.loads()` rejects it, so top-level `verification_evidence` survives into the in-memory tool row, the immediate SessionDB flush, and the next same-turn provider request. Failed verification commands are concrete inputs to the guardrail path, not malformed historical data.

The submitted “real executor” test does not exercise this composition. It calls the executor alias's `make_tool_result_message(...)` directly with a dict and manually appends the resulting message; it does not drive `_execute_tool_calls_sequential`, either executor guidance transform, the executor's immediate flush, or a second provider request.

### Required fix

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

Reading all five changed files at the PR head and on `origin/master`, plus the settings backend and Agent lineage contract, I found two merge blockers. First, the new preference is never accepted by the server, so it cannot survive the save response or a reload. Second, the classifier treats every row with `parent_session_id` as a delegated subagent, but that field is also used for compression continuation and branch lineage.

## Code reference

`static/panels.js:8677-8678` posts the new field, while `static/panels.js:8793` immediately rehydrates the global from the server response:

```js
if(showSubagentCb) payload.show_subagent_sessions=showSubagentCb.checked;
window._showSubagentSessions=!!(saved&&saved.show_subagent_sessions!==false);
```

However, `api/config.py:9477-9481` derives accepted keys only from `_SETTINGS_DEFAULTS`, and `save_settings()` applies values only inside the gate at `api/config.py:9691-9695`. This branch does not add `show_subagent_sessions` to `_SETTINGS_DEFAULTS` or `_SETTINGS_BOOL_KEYS`. The POST therefore drops it; the missing response field makes `undefined !== false` true, and `static/boot.js:3251` also defaults it back on after reload.

The new classifier at `static/sessions.js:6619-6625` has a separate contract problem:

```js
const source=String(s.session_source||s.source||s.platform||'').toLowerCase();
return source==='delegate'||!!s.parent_session_id;
```

Existing WebUI lineage handling at `static/sessions.js:6636-6656` already documents and handles compression rows whose only link may be `parent_session_id`, and forks also carry that field. The Agent source confirms the field is written for compression continuation and branch/session switching, not only delegation. With this predicate, turning the option off can hide the active post-compression segment or a user-created branch, rather than only `delegate_task` children.

## Diagnosis / recommendation

1. Add `show_subagent_sessions: True` to `api/config.py:_SETTINGS_DEFAULTS` and add the key to `_SETTINGS_BOOL_KEYS`. Keep default-on for backward compatibility. The settings response will then preserve the boolean through autosave and boot.
2. Do not use bare `parent_session_id` as the delegation discriminator. Prefer the explicit delegated source marker, or reuse the existing `_isChildSession()` classification only after confirming it excludes compression and fork lineage. The current code immediately above this helper contains those exclusions; duplicating a broader predicate bypasses them.
3. The description says hidden children remain accessible through their parent. Preserve that by filtering standalone top-level rows while retaining delegated children in the reference rows passed to `_attachChildSessionsToSidebarRows()`.

## Test plan

No test file is changed in this branch. Add a settings round-trip test that POSTs false, checks the returned value, reloads settings, and checks false again. Add sidebar fixtures for: a delegated child, a compression continuation, and a fork, each with `parent_session_id`. With the toggle off, only the delegated standalone row should disappear; its parent expansion should still contain it, while compression and fork rows remain visible. I inspected the PR worktree read-only and did not execute PR-authored code.


Cross-repo contract references checked: `agent/conversation_compression.py:2149` writes a compression child with `parent_session_id`, while `hermes_cli/cli_commands_mixin.py:1138-1140` does the same for a branch.

I reviewed exact head `ad1a8e9f245d131f0bd37ebb488954dbb694ed3f`. The production change is narrow and the empty-entry cleanup matches the reported symptom, but this PR is not mergeable because it breaks an unchanged repository test on every supported Python matrix.

### Reproduced failure

The mandatory no-network sandbox ran the complete changed subsystem file:

```text
$ pytest tests/test_provider_management.py -p no:xdist -q
1 failed, 24 passed

FAILED tests/test_provider_management.py::TestRemoveProviderKey::test_clean_provider_key_uses_late_bound_config_path
E   KeyError: 'providers'
```

`_clean_provider_key_from_config()` now deletes `cfg["providers"]` when the target was its only entry. The unchanged test still indexes `active["providers"]["openai"]` at `tests/test_provider_management.py:498`, so it raises before it can verify the intended post-cleanup state. The test file is byte-identical to `origin/master` (`sha256 2213ba4e…` at both refs), confirming that the PR changed runtime behavior without updating its existing contract. GitHub currently shows the Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13 test shards failing.

### Required fix

1. Update `test_clean_provider_key_uses_late_bound_config_path` to assert the new intended shape without indexing a removed mapping, while preserving its late-bound-path and `model.api_key` assertions.
2. Add focused behavior rows for:
   - a provider containing only `api_key`, where both the provider entry and now-empty `providers` section are removed;
   - a provider containing `api_key` plus other configuration, where only the key is removed and the remaining entry is preserved;
   - multiple configured providers, where removing one empty target preserves all siblings;
   - model-cache invalidation after a real config cleanup.
3. Re-run `tests/test_provider_management.py` and the configured-provider/model-picker slices. The existing suite must be green, not merely adjusted around the exception.

Static threat scan: **CLEAN**. No bare contributor-code execution, merge, release, production action, or PR-branch write was performed.

## Exact-head re-gate: **SHIP ONLY WITH FIXES** (one finding)

**PR:** #6581
**Head reviewed:** `dd3fe8fba` (rebased clean onto current `origin/master`)
**Base:** `origin/master`

Thanks @BobClawblaw — the previous bounce is fully resolved: `test_clean_provider_key_uses_late_bound_config_path` is fixed, and all four requested coverage rows landed (`removes_empty_entry_and_section`, `preserves_other_config_keys`, `preserves_siblings`, `invalidates_model_cache`). The provider-management suite is 29/29 green and the full sandbox suite is **13,914 passed / 0 failed**.

Codex verified the core behavior is safe: only genuinely-empty provider entries are deleted, siblings and unrelated keys survive, no production reader direct-indexes `cfg["providers"]` (so the KeyError class is gone), and the mutation is correctly isolated to the resolved active profile.

It found **one remaining defect** — a race that can defeat the fix's own purpose:

### 🔴 Must fix

**[SILENT] `api/config.py:8229` (+ `:6252`) — an in-flight model-catalog rebuild can republish the removed provider AFTER cleanup invalidates the cache.** This PR newly calls `invalidate_models_cache()` in the cleanup path (`api/providers.py:3032`) — good — but the bounded live rebuild worker (`_publish_models_result`) publishes its result and rewrites the on-disk cache **without re-checking whether an invalidation happened while it was running**. Codex reproduced it with a concurrent probe: cleanup removed `providers` and emptied the memory cache, then an over-budget worker that had started *before* the removal restored `openai-api` and recreated the disk cache using the post-removal fingerprint — so the picker (potentially across a restart) still shows the provider you just removed. The exact symptom this PR exists to eliminate reappears under a rebuild race.

- **Fix:** add a generation/owner token to the cache machinery — increment it in `invalidate_models_cache()`, capture it when a rebuild starts, and **discard the rebuild result + skip the disk write when the captured generation no longer matches**. An obsolete worker must also not clear a newer rebuild's in-progress state (`_cache_build_in_progress` / the `box["published"]` guard). A focused test: start a rebuild, invalidate mid-flight, let the stale worker finish, and assert the removed provider does NOT reappear in the catalog or on disk.

### Note on scope
The rebuild-publish race lives in pre-existing cache machinery, but this PR's new `invalidate_models_cache()` call is what makes the stale-provider-reappears symptom reachable — so the generation-token guard belongs here to make the fix reliable rather than as a separate follow-up. It's a contained change to the publish path. Re-push with the guard + test and I'll re-gate; everything else is already green.

## Exact-head re-gate: cache invalidation protocol is still incomplete

Reviewed exact head `d6455fcbacfff026e2c8ec136a828c2a6d751078`. The requested generation-check/disk-save atomicity fix landed, and the new real-disk regression passes. The prior provider-cleanup `KeyError` remains resolved.

The mandatory no-network sandbox reached Layer 3 for five focused commands: **34 selected executions passed / 32 unique tests**. Static current-head tracing found four deterministic paths those tests do not cover, so this still needs rework.

### 1. Stale disk snapshot can publish after full invalidation

`get_available_models()` loads `disk_groups` before `_available_models_cache_lock` (`api/config.py:8008-8018`) and later publishes it at `:8111-8117` without binding the load to `_models_cache_generation`. `invalidate_models_cache()` advances generation and clears memory under the lock, but deletes disk only after releasing it (`:6263-6285`).

A reader can therefore load generation-N disk data, full invalidation can complete and advance to N+1, and the reader can then publish the old groups into memory with the current fingerprint. Equivalent unfenced disk-to-memory publication exists in `warm_models_catalog_provenance_if_cold()` (`:8449-8467`) and `get_available_models_for_session_visit()` (`:8507-8532`). The file may be deleted, but the resurrected in-memory catalog remains TTL-valid.

**Required fix:** make disk load-to-publish generation-aware at every publication site. Either load under the same invalidation critical section, or capture the generation before load and re-check it under the condition-variable lock before publication. A generation-N snapshot must never publish under N+1. Coordinate disk deletion with that same epoch.

### 2. Bounded worker can permanently abandon the single-flight owner

Ownership is set before thread launch, but `_worker.start()` at `api/config.py:8347` is outside cleanup. A `RuntimeError` from thread startup leaves `_cache_build_in_progress=True` with no worker and no notification. `_rebuild_worker()` catches only `Exception` (`:8324-8329`), unlike the synchronous path's `BaseException` handling; a `SystemExit`/other `BaseException` leaves no result/error and can strand the owner on both foreground and out-of-band paths.

**Required fix:** guard `Thread.start()` and every bounded terminal path with unconditional, generation-qualified owner cleanup. Match the synchronous path's `BaseException` behavior without allowing an obsolete worker to clear a newer owner.

### 3. Provider-specific refresh bypasses the new generation protocol

`invalidate_provider_models_cache()` (`api/config.py:6316-6344`) clears memory and disk but does not advance `_models_cache_generation`, clear/transfer `_cache_build_in_progress`, or notify waiters. `/api/models/refresh` calls it directly (`api/routes.py:14520-14526`), so an already-running worker remains generation-current and may republish/write the provider data this refresh intended to discard.

**Required fix:** centralize the generation bump, cache/provenance clear, generation-qualified owner handling, notification, and disk invalidation in one primitive used by both full and provider-specific invalidators.

### 4. Rejected within-budget result is still returned to the caller

When `_publish_models_result()` rejects a stale generation at `api/config.py:8253-8261`, the within-budget branch still returns `copy.deepcopy(box["result"])` at `:8349-8357` (and the budget-boundary branch does the same at `:8363-8367`). Shared cache/disk remain guarded, but that initiating `/api/models` response can still show the provider removed during its rebuild.

**Required fix:** have publication report whether the generation was accepted. If it was rejected, do not return the stale rebuild result; resolve from the current generation's cache/fallback without starting an unbounded duplicate rebuild.

## Re-push: generation/owner token guards the rebuild-publish race

Head: `15e01550869457944b326fd721e6fe4e5c2613dd` — addresses the 🔴 finding in the 30/07 re-gate.

### The fix (`api/config.py`)

A stale in-flight rebuild can no longer republish a removed provider after `invalidate_models_cache()` runs:

1. **Generation/owner token** — new module-level `_models_cache_generation`, bumped inside `invalidate_models_cache()` (under the cache lock).
2. **Capture on rebuild start** — the cold path records `_build_generation = _models_cache_generation` at the moment it sets `_cache_build_in_progress`.
3. **Discard on publish** — `_publish_models_result()` (the over-budget bounded worker path) now returns early when the captured generation no longer matches: no in-memory publish, **no disk write**, and the in-progress flag is left untouched so a newer rebuild keeps its serialization. The generation is re-checked again immediately before `_save_models_cache_to_disk()` so an invalidation between the memory publish and the file write also cancels the on-disk write (the restart-persistence vector).
4. **Obsolete worker can't clear a newer rebuild's flag** — `_clear_build_in_progress()` (error paths) applies the same generation guard; the legacy synchronous (budget ≤ 0) publish path got the identical guard.

### The test (`tests/test_issue3928_models_budget_fallback.py`)

`test_stale_over_budget_rebuild_discarded_after_invalidation` reproduces the exact race: start a rebuild over budget → `invalidate_models_cache()` mid-flight → start a fresh rebuild → release the stale worker → assert the removed provider (`openai-api`) does **not** reappear in the catalog or in any disk write, and the fresh rebuild's in-progress flag survives.

### Verification

- `pytest tests/test_issue3928_models_budget_fallback.py` → **10 passed** (incl. the new race test, 5× stable).
- `tests/test_provider_management.py` + budget/wakeup/profile-provider suites → **79 passed**.
- `tests/test_issue4756_session_visit_model_refresh.py`, `test_issue2540_models_endpoint_error.py`, `test_copilot_provider_model_settings_not_allowlist.py`, `test_moa_model_picker_provider.py`, `test_model_cache_metadata.py`, `test_issue1699_model_cache_source_fingerprint.py`, `test_session_display_resolver_no_live_rebuild.py`, `test_profile_switch_1200.py` → **61 passed**.
- Cache-invalidation-adjacent suites (credential pool, dropdown invalidation, custom providers, LM Studio env) → **188 passed** (one unrelated pre-existing order-dependent failure in `test_custom_provider_display_name.py` reproduces identically on the pristine head without this change).
- **Mutation check**: reverting only `api/config.py` makes the new test fail exactly as you described — the stale worker republishes `openai-api` into `_available_models_cache`.

Ready for re-gate.

Thanks @webtecnica — the generation-token design is sound and the hard parts all check out: Codex verified no `_cache_build_in_progress` leak / lost wakeup across owned/superseded-success/exception/double-invalidation/newer-owner-waiter interleavings, the in-memory publish + provenance are correctly guarded, and provider cleanup invalidates after the config reload (`providers.py:3032`). But an adversarial gate (Codex, deterministic repro, 20 targeted tests + a 13,925-pass suite) found the **disk path still has the exact resurrection race** the PR targets. Holding for a small atomicity fix:

### SILENT — removed provider can still be republished to DISK (TOCTOU on the disk write)
`api/config.py:8287`: the generation check and `_save_models_cache_to_disk(result)` are **not atomic** under `_cache_build_cv`. Reproduced deterministically:
1. stale worker passes the generation check,
2. an invalidation advances the generation **and deletes the cache file**,
3. the worker proceeds to `_save_models_cache_to_disk(result)` and **recreates** the file with the removed provider — and the post-removal fingerprint, so the strict restart loader accepts it on next boot.

So the in-memory cache is clean but a reboot resurrects the removed provider from disk.

### Fix spec (Codex)
1. `api/config.py:8284` — make the generation check and `_save_models_cache_to_disk(result)` **atomic under `_cache_build_cv`**, so an invalidation either prevents the rename or runs strictly afterward and deletes the file. (Hold the cv from the check through the atomic disk rename.)
2. `tests/test_issue3928_models_budget_fallback.py:572` — add a real-disk race test that pauses after the generation check, invalidates, resumes publication, and asserts BOTH the cache file and a strict restart load remain free of the removed provider.

Everything else — in-memory guard, flag/wakeup handling, provenance, invalidation placement — is good to go. Once the disk write is inside the cv-held generation check I'll re-gate the exact head. [Reviewed code + ran the gate only.]

CHANGES_REQUESTED resolved: generation check + disk save are now atomic under `_cache_build_cv` in both call sites, plus a real-disk race regression test.

**Fix (api/config.py)**
- Sync publish path (~L8197): the `_save_models_cache_to_disk(result)` call moved inside the `with _cache_build_cv:` block, right after the generation check, so the cv is held from the check through the atomic disk rename (`os.rename` of the tmp file). An invalidation can no longer interleave: it either blocks until the rename lands and then deletes the file, or runs first and bumps the generation so the publish block (memory + disk) is skipped entirely.
- Out-of-band worker publish (`_publish_models_result`, ~L8274): the re-check `with _cache_build_cv:` block now also contains `_save_models_cache_to_disk(result)` — same atomicity guarantee.
- Verified no lock-order issue: `_save_models_cache_to_disk` and its callees (`_models_cache_source_fingerprint`, `_current_webui_version`, `_get_models_cache_path`) do pure file I/O / `sys.modules` lookups and acquire no other locks, and the foreground releases the cv before `build_done.wait()`, so the worker holding the cv during the write cannot deadlock the invalidation or foreground paths.

**Test (tests/test_issue3928_models_budget_fallback.py)**
- New `test_disk_save_atomic_with_invalidation_real_disk`: drives the REAL disk path (restores the genuine `_save_models_cache_to_disk` / `_delete_models_cache_on_disk` / `_load_models_cache_from_disk` that the autouse fixture no-ops, still pointed at the isolated tmp cache file). Sequence: stale over-budget worker passes the generation check and pauses inside the disk save → an invalidation is attempted on a separate thread and must BLOCK behind the cv-held write (asserted) → worker resumes and completes the real file write → invalidation then runs strictly after and deletes the file. Asserts the removed provider survives nowhere: memory cache is None, the on-disk cache file no longer exists, and a strict restart load (`_load_models_cache_from_disk`) returns None.
- Confirmed the test is a true regression test: with the pre-fix code it fails at the "invalidation must not interleave" assertion (the invalidation proceeds immediately and the stale file is re-created); with the fix it passes.

**Test results:** 93 passed across the target file + neighboring model-cache/provider-management suites (test_issue3928_models_budget_fallback, test_issue1633_models_cache_version_stamp, test_model_cache_metadata, test_issue1539_provider_removal_dropdown_invalidation, test_provider_management, test_issue644, test_model_picker_badges, test_moa_model_picker_provider).

Greptile Summary

 This PR synchronizes provider removal with the model catalog cache. - Removes provider mappings and the enclosing providers section when API-key cleanup leaves them empty. - Invalidates the model catalog after provider cleanup. - Adds generation-based protection against stale in-flight rebuilds republishing to memory or disk. - Adds provider-cleanup and concurrent cache-rebuild regression coverage.

Confidence Score: 4/5

 The stale foreground response path should be fixed before merging because a provider removed during a within-budget rebuild can still appear in the resulting model selector response. Generation checks prevent stale rebuilds from reaching shared memory or disk, but the synchronous and within-budget foreground branches return the discarded rebuild output directly to the requesting client. **Files Needing Attention:** api/config.py

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | api/config.py | Adds generation-aware cache publication and disk-write serialization, but rejected foreground rebuilds can still be returned to callers. | | api/providers.py | Removes empty provider configuration entries and invalidates provider and model caches after successful cleanup. | | tests/test_issue3928_models_budget_fallback.py | Adds strong over-budget worker and real-disk race coverage, but does not cover a stale within-budget result returned to the initiating request. | | tests/test_provider_management.py | Covers empty-entry removal, preservation of provider metadata and siblings, and model-cache invalidation. |

Sequence Diagram

 ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Models as /api/models request participant Cache as Models cache participant Settings as Provider removal Models->>Cache: Start rebuild at generation G Settings->>Cache: Remove provider and invalidate Cache->>Cache: Advance generation to G+1 Cache-->>Models: Rebuild completes with generation G Models->>Cache: Attempt publication Cache-->>Models: Reject stale publication Models-->>Models: Currently returns stale rebuild result ```

payload.body: ## Exact-head review: unbounded bare-token regexes consume following prose I reviewed exact head `05be32f167af031e2b44906d7446ea529139ae84`. The change makes unbracketed `MEDIA:` and bare `file://` references accept every space until `)`, `]`, quote, angle bracket, or newline. That removes the only delimiter between a filename and normal prose on the same line. A fail-first probe against the submitted renderer reproduces both regressions: ```text Here file:///tmp/my screenshot.png done → api/media?path=...my%2520screenshot.png%2520done MEDIA:/tmp/my screenshot.png done → api/media?path=...my%2520screenshot.png%2520done ``` The word `done` is swallowed into the media path and disappears from rendered prose. The two assertions fail under the required sandbox: ```text 2 failed in 4.74s ``` The repository's unchanged `test_bare_file_url_becomes_media` stays green only because it checks that an `` exists. Its minimal `_inlineMediaHtmlForRef` stub accepts any `file://` tail and does not assert the captured path or preservation of the trailing text. It therefore masks the parser regression. ### Required fix 1. Do not make unbracketed `MEDIA:` and bare `file://` captures consume arbitrary spaces through end-of-line. Define an unambiguous boundary, for example an explicit quoted/bracketed form for raw-space paths, or a tokenizer that terminates at a proven filename/URL boundary while preserving following prose. 2. Keep already-encoded `%20` support and pass the parsed reference through the canonical media helper without broadening the capture into adjacent text. 3. Add real-JS behavioral coverage for both settled `renderMd()` and streaming `_smdMediaAwareAddText()`: - raw-space filename renders the complete path; - the same token followed by prose preserves that prose outside the media node; - multiple media tokens and punctuation on one line do not merge; - `%20` input is not double-encoded; - bare `file://`, `MEDIA:`, markdown image, and markdown link forms retain their separate boundaries. 4. Strengthen `test_bare_file_url_becomes_media` to assert the exact media path and the surviving trailing text, not only `` presence. ### Verification - Threat scan: **CLEAN**. - Submitted targeted slice: `test_bare_file_url_becomes_media` + `test_markdown_anchor_file_link_uses_link_path_not_media` → **2 passed** (demonstrates the blind spot). - Reviewer fail-first probe through `warmup-safe-test.sh` / bubblewrap → **2 failed** with the captured `...%2520done` paths above. - Diff/whitespace check: clean. This is an objective visible-content regression in the changed parsing path, so I am requesting changes. No merge, approval, screenshot, server, production action, release, or contributor-branch write was performed.
