payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

Reading the full `static/style.css` at PR head `af804a51c` and comparing it with `origin/master`, the intent is good, but the new width rule is overridden later in the same stylesheet. At current HEAD it does not make table or code messages wider. The new `white-space: nowrap` rule does take effect, so ordinary Markdown tables can become wider without gaining a horizontal scroll container.

## Code reference

The PR adds the content-sensitive width at `static/style.css:2304-2315`:

```css
.msg-body:has(table),
.msg-body:has(pre),
.msg-body:has(.csv-table-wrap){max-width:min(1100px,100%);}
.msg-body .csv-table th,.msg-body table th{white-space:nowrap;}
```

However, the later rule at `static/style.css:5948` wins by source order with equal specificity:

```css
.msg-body {
  padding-left: var(--msg-rail);
  padding-top: 8px;
  max-width: var(--msg-max);
}
```

`--msg-max` is `780px` at `static/style.css:5879`. There is a second parent ceiling at `static/style.css:6383-6386`: `.messages-inner` is only 780px, 820px at 1400px viewport width, and 860px at 1800px. Even moving the new body rule later would therefore still prevent the advertised 1100px result.

The overflow asymmetry is visible at `static/style.css:2422-2424` and `:2531-2538`: bare Markdown tables are `width:100%` with no wrapper, while only `.csv-table-wrap` has `overflow-x:auto`. The transcript container itself uses `overflow-x:hidden` at `static/style.css:2268`.

## Diagnosis / recommendation

Please move this into the final width section and widen the containing `.messages-inner` when it contains wide content, not only the child body. For example, use a shared wide-content selector on both levels, with the mobile rule at `static/style.css:3121-3122` remaining authoritative.

For tables, either omit the global header `nowrap`, or give ordinary Markdown tables a dedicated horizontal-scroll wrapper before applying it. CSS on the table alone cannot create a usable horizontal scroller when the ancestor clips overflow.

## Verification step

Add browser coverage for three cases at desktop and phone widths: prose remains at the normal measure; a long code block can reach the wider column and scroll internally; and a bare Markdown table with long headers remains horizontally reachable rather than clipped. The test should assert computed widths for both `.messages-inner` and `.msg-body`, because checking only that the new selector exists would miss the current cascade override.

payload.author: sand01chi
asorourx
payload.body:
Thanks @nesquena-hermes — addressed, and rebased onto current `master` first (the review was against `af804a51c`; head is now `7befc4c2`). Two things changed the picture:

**The width rule isn't a dead no-op on the rebased head.** The overriding rule is plain `.msg-body { max-width: var(--msg-max) }`, but the PR's rule is `.msg-body:has(table)` — `:has(table)` contributes a type selector, so its specificity is `(0,1,1)` vs `(0,1,0)` for plain `.msg-body`. It wins by **specificity**, not source order, so the widening applies. The parent ceiling is also gone: current `master` already widens `.messages-inner` to `1100px @1400px` / `1200px @1800px` (style.css:2287-2288), so the child body can actually reach 1100px. I added a test that computes selector specificity and asserts the `:has` rule out-specifies the plain override (rather than only asserting the selector exists — which, as you noted, would miss a cascade override).

**Bare Markdown tables now get a real horizontal-scroll container** — I took the "dedicated wrapper" option you offered. `enhanceMarkdownTables()` wraps each bare table in a `.markdown-table-scroll` div (its own `overflow-x:auto` scroller, idempotent, CSV tables excluded), cells wrap at word boundaries, and the filter/sort controls stay pinned above the scroll area. Because the wrapper is its own scroll container, it scrolls even though the transcript ancestors clip overflow-x — so the one-line header `nowrap` is now safe and the clipped-columns P1 is closed.

**Tests** (`tests/test_issue6517_wide_transcript_tables.py`): the wrapper/idempotency/filter-placement logic, the wrapper CSS + its source-order win over `.msg-body table`, the specificity proof above, and the `.messages-inner` parent widening. These are source-level guards per this repo's convention for CSS/layout regressions (cf. `test_issue4856` / `test_issue4553`, which note the runtime layout isn't reproducible in headless CI without a full browser); the specificity test targets your override concern directly rather than just selector presence.

The scroll-wrapper approach was contributed by @sand01chi (credited via `Co-authored-by`) — thanks for the complement. Ready for another look 🙏

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Request changes: profile-switch response still leaks the raw provider ID

The `212765f9` follow-up correctly implements the earlier recommendation: `_named_custom_provider_slug_for_provider()` now uses `_custom_provider_slug_from_name()` instead of maintaining a colon-only normalization rule. The PR's new regression file passes 10/10, and the existing `_get_provider_base_url` slice passes 8/8 through the sandbox gate.

One same-path producer is still unnormalized, so the colon-named provider bug returns immediately after a profile switch:

- `api/profiles.py::switch_profile()` assigns `model_cfg.get("provider")` directly to `default_model_provider` and returns it in `/api/profile/switch`.
- `static/panels.js::switchToProfile()` and `static/sessions.js::_switchProfileForSessionLoad()` immediately assign that response value to `window._activeProvider`; the main switch also uses it for dropdown option/provider and pending session state.
- For `model.provider: custom:192.168.5.242:8000`, the response therefore remains `custom:192.168.5.242:8000`, while the provider ID generated by this PR is `custom:192.168.5.242-8000`.

I reproduced this at the current PR head with a sandbox-gated behavior test:

```text
assert result["default_model_provider"] == "custom:192.168.5.242-8000"
AssertionError: assert 'custom:192.168.5.242:8000' == 'custom:192.168.5.242-8000'
```

### Fix specification

In `api/profiles.py::switch_profile()`, normalize the target profile's raw provider before returning it:

1. When `model_cfg` is a dict, call `_resolve_configured_provider_id(raw_provider, cfg, base_url=model_cfg.get("base_url", ""))`.
2. Fall back to `str(raw_provider)` only when resolution returns empty.
3. Pass the local `cfg` loaded for the target profile. This matters for `process_wide=False`, where the function intentionally does not use the process-global config cache.
4. Add a behavior regression to `tests/test_profile_switch_1200.py`: create a target profile whose `model.provider` is `custom:<ip>:<port>` and whose matching `custom_providers[]` entry has the same colon-bearing name, call `switch_profile(..., process_wide=False)`, and assert the response contains the canonical hyphenated slug.

Please keep the current canonical-helper follow-up and the three existing fixes intact. This is a bounded missing response surface, not a request to redesign provider routing.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Exact-head re-gate: **SHIP ONLY WITH FIXES**

**PR:** #6516
**Head reviewed:** `93812c11b` (rebased clean onto current `origin/master`)
**Base:** `origin/master`

Thanks @BobClawblaw — the previous bounce is resolved (the profile-switch response no longer leaks the raw provider ID; `_named_custom_provider_slug_for_provider()` uses the shared slug helper), your two regression files pass 27/27, and the full sandbox suite is **13,921 passed / 0 failed**.

But Codex found the shared-slug migration is **incomplete** — there's still a divergent slugger, and the normalization introduced two fresh regressions. All three verified with reproduction:

### 🔴 Must fix

1. **[CORE] `api/config.py:2613` — colon-named-model routing goes to the WRONG endpoint on slug collision.** Lossy slugging maps `foo:bar`, `foo bar`, and `foo-bar` all to `custom:foo-bar`; the new first-match list scan then overrides the active model's authoritative URL and routes `@custom:foo-bar:second-model` to the *first* matching provider's endpoint.
   - **Fix:** move the normalized active-model lookup *before* the list scan; return a list entry only when the slug match is **unique**, and fail closed on ambiguous matches.

2. **[CORE] `api/config.py:1442` (+ `:3032`) — canonicalizing `custom:host:8000` → `custom:host-8000` breaks sending entirely with multiple custom providers.** The separate slugger at `:3032` still uses the old normalization, so it misses the configured entry; the send path then substitutes `dummy-key` for the real key and every authenticated request is rejected.
   - **Fix:** replace the local slugger at `:3032` with `_custom_provider_slug_from_name()` for BOTH sides (this is the divergent path the PR meant to eliminate), and disambiguate collisions using the resolved base URL.

3. **[SILENT] `api/config.py:1492` — the new response call sites normalize builtin `x-ai` → nonexistent `xai`.** `/api/providers` then reports `active_provider: xai` while the catalog only contains `x-ai`, so the active provider isn't sorted/identified correctly.
   - **Fix:** preserve IDs already present in `_PROVIDER_DISPLAY` / `_PROVIDER_MODELS` (matching `_canonicalise_provider_id()` behavior) before applying aliases.

### Summary
Right direction — consolidating on one slug helper is correct — but the migration left a divergent slugger at `:3032` and the canonicalization introduced a wrong-endpoint route (#1) and a total send breakage under multiple custom providers (#2), plus the `x-ai`→`xai` regression (#3). Add adversarial coverage for: two custom providers whose names collide to the same slug (must fail closed / disambiguate by base_url), a colon-in-port custom provider with multiple configured (send must use the real key), and `x-ai` active-provider identity through `/api/providers`. Re-push and I'll re-gate.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Re-gate: two named blockers still remain at `0487d73d2859`

Thanks for the quick follow-up. I re-checked the current live head, including the one-file amendment that landed while the review was running. The `x-ai` identity fix is good, and `0487d73d` repairs the temporary `_custom_provider_name_matches()` tautology, so the submitted adversarial file is now 10/10 green through the mandatory sandbox.

Two blockers from the prior review are still present in their production paths:

### 1. Slug collisions are counted by nonempty URLs, not matching entries

`api/config.py::_get_provider_base_url()` appends only nonempty `base_url` values and uses `len(matching_base_urls)` as the ambiguity check. Two entries that both slugify to `custom:foo-bar`, one without a URL and one with a URL, therefore look unique and route to the sibling URL. The prior requirement was to fail closed whenever the slug match itself is not unique.

A sandboxed discriminator at the current head reproduced:

```text
assert _get_provider_base_url("custom:foo-bar") is None
AssertionError: assert 'http://sibling.example/v1' is None
```

Count matching entries before filtering URLs. Return a list URL only when exactly one entry matches and it has a nonempty URL. Canonicalize the active/requested IDs through the same rule before applying active-model precedence.

### 2. The real send resolver still uses the divergent slugger

The change to `api.providers::_custom_provider_name_matches()` fixes provider-management matching, but the message send path calls `api.config::resolve_custom_provider_connection()` via `api.streaming::_resolve_custom_provider_runtime_overrides()`. That resolver still has its private `_slugify()` which replaces spaces and underscores but not colons.

With two configured custom providers, picker ID `custom:192.168.5.242-8000`, and selected entry name `192.168.5.242:8000`, it misses the selected entry. Streaming keeps the already-resolved base URL but substitutes `dummy-key` instead of the selected real key. The current-head sandboxed production-path discriminator reproduced:

```text
assert api_key == "selected-real-key"
AssertionError: assert 'dummy-key' == 'selected-real-key'
```

Please remove the private slugger and use `_custom_provider_slug_from_name()` consistently for the requested suffix and each entry name. Select only a unique match; on a lossy-slug collision, use the already-resolved base URL as the second authority dimension and fail closed if still ambiguous. Add one production-composed test through `_resolve_custom_provider_runtime_overrides()` with two distinct keys/URLs and assert the selected real key is used, never the sibling key or `dummy-key`.

Verification at exact head `0487d73d2859`: threat scan CLEAN; submitted adversarial file **10 passed**; trusted residual discriminator **2 failed**. No bare PR-code execution was used.

## Re-gate at `c201d2cf5754`: current head cannot boot and still misses the send-path fix

The latest commit is not a bounded repair of the two findings from the `0487d73d2859` review. It replaces large parts of `api/config.py` and `api/providers.py` (316 additions, 1,725 deletions) and removes production APIs that unchanged current code still imports.

### 1. Current head is non-bootable

`api/routes.py` still imports `canonical_model_provider_lane`, but the latest commit deletes its definition from `api/config.py`. The same rollback also deletes `get_config_snapshot`, `warm_models_catalog_provenance_if_cold`, `gateway_supports_approval_identity_v1`, and `provider_has_process_wakeup_recovery_credential` while current callers remain.

The mandatory CLEAN sandbox gate collected 21 targeted tests, then all 21 errored during setup because the server process exited on:

```text
ImportError: cannot import name 'canonical_model_provider_lane' from 'api.config'
```

No selected test body ran.

### 2. The real custom-provider send path is still unsafe

The narrow ambiguity-count issue in `_get_provider_base_url()` is improved, but `resolve_custom_provider_connection()` still does not converge:

- It passes a full `custom:foo:bar` ID to `_custom_provider_slug_from_name()`, whose `custom:` fast path preserves the colon form, while configured entry names become `custom:foo-bar`.
- On colliding names it still selects the sole entry with a nonempty `base_url`, so a sibling URL/key remains an identity discriminator instead of failing closed.
- The detached streaming path resolves this tuple through ambient `get_config()` after leaving the target-profile scope, so the request/session profile still does not own the URL/key lookup.

### Required rework

1. Restore `api/config.py` and `api/providers.py` from the pre-push head (or rebase cleanly onto current master), preserving every current imported API. Reapply only a narrow custom-provider repair.
2. Canonicalize the suffix after removing the exact leading `custom:`. Use the same shared rule for the requested ID and each configured entry name.
3. In `resolve_custom_provider_connection()`, require exactly one identity match. On a collision, fail closed with `(None, None)`; do not choose by URL presence, key truthiness, list order, or a resulting `dummy-key` path.
4. Pass the request/session profile's config snapshot into connection resolution. Do not read process-global `get_config()` for the detached worker's URL/key tuple.
5. Add a server-import smoke test, a production-composed collision test that proves no sibling URL/key or `dummy-key` is selected, and a two-profile detached-worker test proving the target profile wins.

Threat scan was CLEAN. All PR-code execution used `warmup-safe-test.sh`; no bare execution was used.

payload.body:
## Re-gate at `c201d2cf` — the two named blockers are fixed, but this head no longer imports (breaks the whole app)

**Head reviewed:** `c201d2cf` (rebased clean onto current `origin/master`)
**Base:** `origin/master`

Thanks @BobClawblaw — the two blockers from the prior round are both genuinely resolved, and I want to acknowledge that first:
- **Blocker 1** (`api/config.py::_get_provider_base_url`) now collects slug-**matching entries** and fails closed (`return None`) when `len(matching) > 1` (`config.py:2466-2475`). Correct.
- **Blocker 2** (the send resolver) now routes through the shared `_custom_provider_slug_from_name()` in `resolve_custom_provider_connection()` (`config.py:2822-2890`); the divergent private slugger is gone.

But this re-push introduced a **hard regression** that blocks everything downstream:

### 🔴 Must fix — this head does not import

**`api/config.py` deletes `warm_models_catalog_provenance_if_cold`, but `api/streaming.py` still imports and calls it.**
- `api/streaming.py:44` — `from api.config import (… warm_models_catalog_provenance_if_cold …)`
- `api/streaming.py:8954` — `warm_models_catalog_provenance_if_cold()`
- The function is defined on `origin/master`'s `config.py` but is **absent** from this PR's `config.py` (the large `-1638` deletion swept it out).

Result: `ImportError: cannot import name 'warm_models_catalog_provenance_if_cold' from 'api.config'`. Because `api.streaming` is imported almost everywhere, the full suite **fails collection with 153 errors**, and — more importantly — the running app would fail to import `streaming` at startup. This is not an environment artifact: the function exists on master, other PRs import fine, and I reproduced the collection failure on a clean rebase of this exact head.

**Fix:** either keep `warm_models_catalog_provenance_if_cold` in `config.py` (if the refactor removed it unintentionally), or, if it was deliberately renamed/relocated, update `api/streaming.py:44` + `:8954` (and any other importers — please grep the tree) to the new name/location. Then run the **full** suite locally (`./scripts/test.sh`) to confirm collection is clean before re-pushing — CI shards will each surface this, but a local collection check catches it in seconds.

### One more thing to verify once it imports (couldn't reach it — collection failed)
The two collision resolvers now behave **differently** on a slug collision, which I'd like confirmed as intentional:
- `_get_provider_base_url()` fails closed **immediately** on `len(matching) > 1` (`config.py:2474`).
- `resolve_custom_provider_connection()` does **not** — on a collision it tries `base_url` as a second discriminator and returns the single URL-bearing entry (`config.py:2882-2890`), only failing closed if still ambiguous.

So for two entries that slug to the same `custom:foo-bar` where only one has a `base_url`, `_get_provider_base_url` returns `None` (ambiguous) while `resolve_custom_provider_connection` returns that entry's `(api_key, base_url)` — the two authoritative resolvers disagree for the same `provider_id`. Please confirm the send path can't end up using credentials/endpoint that the base_url lookup considers ambiguous (a crafted second entry with the same slug shouldn't be able to steer the send resolver). If the divergence is intentional, a comment + a test pinning both behaviors would make it defensible.

Re-push with the import fixed and I'll run a clean full gate (Codex + full suite) and finish the adversarial resolver check.

- `test_resolve_configured_provider_id_preserves_known_canonicals`

The direction is right and the profile-isolation motivation for `config_data` is legitimate, but the collision fail-closed regresse

## Summary

Reading the full `api/config.py` and `api/providers.py` at PR head `e7500f9ce`, plus the new regression file, the reported IP:port case is fixed at the right WebUI layer. The picker emits a name-derived ID such as `custom:192.168.5.250-8000`; `resolve_model_provider()` then parses that route hint and asks `_get_provider_base_url()` for the endpoint. On `origin/master`, that lookup only checks `providers` and the active `model` block, so a non-default legacy `custom_providers` entry has no URL and falls into the failing route. This patch adds that missing lookup and normalizes the active-provider surfaces consistently.

## Code reference

The decisive change is `api/config.py:2589-2626`:

```python
for entry in _custom_provider_entries():
    slug = _custom_provider_slug_from_name(entry.get("name"))
    if slug and slug.lower() == pid_lower:
        cp_base = str(entry.get("base_url") or "").strip().rstrip("/")
        if cp_base:
            return cp_base
```

That matches the existing route flow at `api/config.py:2823-2833`, where an explicit `@provider:model` hint returns `_get_provider_base_url(provider_hint)`. The response-side normalization at `api/providers.py:2845-2856` also makes `active_provider` comparable to the IDs generated for custom-provider cards instead of returning the raw colon-bearing config value.

## Diagnosis / recommendation

The implementation is sound for the reported IP:port shape. I would make one small follow-up before merge: at `api/config.py:1434-1454`, derive the comparison suffix with the existing slug helper rather than maintaining a colon-only normalization path:

```python
raw_slug = _custom_provider_slug_from_name(raw_suffix)
normalized_suffix = raw_slug.removeprefix("custom:")
```

Then compare `normalized_suffix == slug_suffix`. `_custom_provider_slug_from_name()` at `api/config.py:1354-1367` is already the canonical rule and also collapses repeated separators and handles other punctuation. The current `replace(":", "-")` fixes this report, but it can drift from the actual slugger for other valid display names.

## Verification

The tests at `tests/test_issue6516_colon_named_custom_providers.py:80-276` cover all three affected outputs: slug resolution without relying on a base URL, non-default endpoint lookup, and normalized provider/settings payloads. The non-default `resolve_model_provider()` assertion is especially useful because it exercises the exact 404-producing path. I performed static review only; CI should run this regression file and the existing config/provider suites.

payload.author: BobClawblaw
payload.body:
# #6516 Round-7 Re-gate Fix — Detailed Report

## Review being addressed

PR review `4837781398` (Round-7 re-gate at `7d12e75d6a79`) requested changes
with `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, citing two deterministic authority gaps in the
`custom:<slug>` provider resolution path of the WebUI:

**Gap 1 — "A truthy URL is still treated as proof of a unique matching target."**
`_custom_provider_authority_state()` returned `"unique"` whenever
`resolved_base_url` was truthy, which did not prove the URL came from the
*requested named provider*. Two concrete defects:

- `api/config.py:3294-3304` mapped a missing requested slug onto the sole
  configured `custom_providers` row even when its name did not match.
- `_resolve_custom_provider_fallback()` read `model.base_url` without first
  requiring `model.provider` to match the requested lane.

The review asked for explicit selection provenance (`selected` with matching
row/source and paired URL/key, versus missing/ambiguous/malformed/partial),
never reconstructing `selected` from a truthy URL, and for `model.base_url` to
be gated by a matching canonical `model.provider`.

**Gap 2 — "The ambient credential side bundle survives all three constructor paths."**
The runtime `credential_pool` (owned by the ambient/default profile) remained
attached unconditionally at:
- initial construction: `api/streaming.py:8937-8938`
- returned-401 retry: `9760-9762`
- raised-401 retry: `11006-11008`

That pool could carry another profile's credentials into a keyless/missing/
ambiguous custom target even after the URL/key tuple was cleared.

---

## What changed

### 1. Explicit selection provenance in `api/config.py`

- Replaced `_resolve_custom_provider_connection_inner`'s ad-hoc 2-tuple body with
  a proper classifier:
  - `_classify_custom_provider_selection(...) -> (status, api_key, base_url, source)`
    where `status ∈ {selected, missing, ambiguous}` and `source ∈
    {custom_providers, providers, model}` names the authority row.
  - `_resolve_custom_provider_selection(...)` is the provenance-rich public root
    the streaming send path consumes. It mirrors `resolve_custom_provider_connection`'s
    env-guard setup (`block_process_env_fallback`) so the send path and the public
    2-tuple API always agree.
- **Removed the sole-nonmatching-row fallback**: a missing slug is no longer
  rewritten onto the single configured `custom_providers` row when its name does
  not match — that pivot would attach an unrelated endpoint's credentials.
- **Gated `model.base_url`**: `_resolve_custom_provider_fallback()` now only reads
  `model.base_url` when `model.provider` canonically matches the requested
  `custom:<slug>` lane (or the collapsed `custom`), via a shared slug helper.
  It also now returns the authority `source` so callers know which row produced
  the URL.
- The public `resolve_custom_provider_connection()` 2-tuple contract is preserved
  (many `routes.py` callers unpack it); it is internally provenance-strict.

### 2. Fail-before-construct + credential-pool scrub in `api/streaming.py`

- `CustomProviderAuthorityError` — new exception raised when a
  `custom:<slug>` target's authority cannot be established uniquely
  (missing/ambiguous/malformed/partial).
- `_resolve_custom_provider_runtime_overrides()` now:
  1. calls `_resolve_custom_provider_selection()` for the **explicit authority
     verdict** (never reconstructs `selected` from a truthy URL);
  2. if `selected` with a URL → installs exactly the paired URL/key bundle
     (keyless ⇒ `_KEYLESS_CUSTOM_API_KEY` placeholder);
  3. otherwise falls back to the runtime connection resolver for the
     **keyless-unique, runtime-resolved endpoint** case (preserving the graceful
     `credential_pool_empty` / wakeup-pause behavior) — and raises
     `CustomProviderAuthorityError` when that also yields no URL, which is every
     production missing/ambiguous/malformed/partial case.
- Scrub applied **before every constructor path**: initial construction,
  returned-401

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

The bounded long-tail fix resolves the previous infinite-poll finding. The current head stops after attempt 16, reconciles an active/replayable stream, and otherwise takes a terminal path that preserves visible assistant prose while releasing the busy state.

There is one new async ownership race in that exhaustion path. `_reconcileStreamEndRecoveryExhaustion()` validates pane ownership before the status request, but after the `await` it checks only `_isActiveSession()` plus a stream-id mismatch. During `loadSession()`, `S.session` still points to the old session while `_loadingSessionId` points to the destination. In that window `_isActiveSession()` remains true even though `_isSessionCurrentPane(activeSid)` is false.

If the status request resolves `{active:true}` after the user starts switching sessions, the stale continuation reaches `_wireSSE(...)`. `_wireSSE()` then recreates `LIVE_STREAMS[activeSid]` after `loadSession()` deliberately closed old-session streams, leaving a background EventSource and orphaned callbacks.

## Code references

- `static/messages.js:2373-2389`: pane ownership is checked only before `await api(...)`; the post-await guard does not repeat it.
- `static/messages.js:76-82`: `_isSessionCurrentPane()` explicitly treats a different `_loadingSessionId` as ownership loss.
- `static/messages.js:2150-2152`: `_isActiveSession()` only compares `S.session.session_id`, so it remains true during the switch.
- `static/sessions.js:1713-1717, 1805-1810`: session loading marks the destination and closes old streams before the new metadata request completes.
- `static/messages.js:5412-5418`: `_wireSSE()` unconditionally writes a new `LIVE_STREAMS[activeSid]` owner.

## Required fix

Revalidate both current-pane ownership and the exact stream owner after every awaited boundary in `_reconcileStreamEndRecoveryExhaustion()`, before composer mutation, `_wireSSE()`, restore, or fallback side effects. If ownership was lost, close this source, clear recovery state, and return without touching the replacement pane. The restore path also needs an owner-scoped token/check if its own await can mutate state before control returns.

Add a deferred-promise regression test: start exhaustion reconciliation as the current owner, switch `_loadingSessionId`/pane (preferably install a replacement owner) while the status request is pending, then resolve `{active:true}`. Assert zero `_wireSSE` calls, no old `LIVE_STREAMS` entry, no composer mutation or recurring timer, and unchanged replacement owner/busy state.

## Verification

The two targeted PR test files passed through the enforced no-network sandbox: **17 passed in 5.57s**. They cover an owner replaced before entry, but not ownership loss during either awaited reconciliation request. This review was run on head `6cda807e5b06`; threat scan was CLEAN.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Re-gate summary

I re-reviewed exact head `f63e28918127e9412fa4fd9c594adcfeff230b8c` against the prior two findings.

The good part: the unsafe partial-answer preservation path is fixed. All current missing/error/exhaustion call sites now take the canonical rebuild path, and the three targeted files pass through the required sandbox gate (`34 passed`). The attempt-16 successful-status continuation also now checks pane/stream/token ownership after its `await`.

There is still an objective same-session/same-stream generation race in the new owner-token design, so this head is not safe to merge yet.

### Must fix

1. **Fence `_wireSSE()` at the mutation sink.** In `static/messages.js`, `_wireSSE()` currently closes/replaces `LIVE_STREAMS[activeSid]` unconditionally (around lines 5469–5475). Require this closure to be non-retired and still own `_currentLiveOwnerEntry()` before replacing the map. If it is stale, close only the newly-created candidate source and return.

2. **Close the reconnect-preflight rejection gap.** `attachLiveStream()` checks `_currentPaneRecoveryOwnerLost()` only after a successful status response. Its `catch(_){}` falls through to unconditional EventSource construction and `_wireSSE()` (around lines 6882–6926). If the pending status request rejects after navigation cleanup or an owner handoff, the retired closure can recreate its source and overwrite the replacement owner. Re-check ownership after the try/catch and before constructing the EventSource.

3. **Make settled restoration token-aware.** `_restoreSettledSession()` currently defines owner loss from pane and stream ID only (around lines 6693–6700). A replacement closure for the same session and same stream ID therefore leaves those checks true. After the session API await, the old closure can still clear inflight state, set `S.activeStreamId=null`, replace the transcript, render, and idle the pane. Include `_closureRetired || !_currentLiveOwnerEntry()` in the stale predicate, including the rejection path, and return the stale result before callers interpret `missing`/`error` as permission to mutate.

4. **Fence terminal and delayed-done callbacks by owner token.** `_bailOutOfTerminalEventsFromStaleStream()` admits a retired closure whenever session/stream IDs still match, and delayed `_finishDone()` has no generation check before its large shared-state mutation (around lines 2172–2179 and 5874–6160). Require the current token at terminal admission and again when the delayed completion runs.

### Required regression coverage

Please add behavioral tests for:

- reconnect preflight rejection after pane/token handoff, proving no EventSource is created and the replacement `LIVE_STREAMS` entry survives;
- real `_restoreSettledSession()` completion/rejection where session ID and stream ID stay the same but only `ownerToken` changes;
- delayed `done` completion after same-ID owner replacement;
- old `done`, `stream_end`, `apperror`, `error`, and `cancel` callbacks after same-ID token replacement.

The current owner tests cover successful status continuation and several timer/resume callbacks, but the restore tests stub the central restore function and the preflight test is source-order-only, so they do not exercise these mutation boundaries.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
I re-gated exact live head `02cb3274411013b80cb94bf678d50957c7516b68` against the prior owner-generation findings. The new token checks close most of the named stale-owner paths, but three objective same-generation defects remain. I also reviewed the final `2fa85e643` → `02cb327441` follow-up: it adds sink checks for the restore timeout and `_handleStreamError` plus harness wiring, but it does not change the retire-before-reconnect composition, anchor cleanup lease, or cancel continuation below.

## Must fix

1. **The new `_wireSSE()` guard disables the ordinary current-owner reconnect path.** In the live `error` listener, `static/messages.js` closes the failed transport and then calls `_closeSource(source)` before scheduling `_probeReconnect`. `_closeSource()` takes the non-`retainOwner` path, so `_retireLiveClosure()` sets `_closureRetired = true` and deletes this exact `LIVE_STREAMS` owner. A later active/replay status response cannot reconnect: `_currentPaneRecoveryOwnerLost()` returns true, and `_wireSSE()` also rejects any candidate because the closure is no longer active. This leaves a normal online transport error with no replacement EventSource.

   Keep the exact owner alive while retrying (the existing `_closeSource(source, {retainOwner: true})` mechanism is one possible shape), close only the failed transport, and retire the owner only when recovery actually terminates. Add a production-composed regression that drives the real error listener through the real close/retire helper and real `_wireSSE`: current owner T must register one replacement source after an active/replay response, while a T→T+1 replacement during the await must close T's candidate and preserve T+1.

2. **Anchor-registry cleanup is not owner-generation fenced.** A same-stream replacement intentionally reuses `window._liveAnchorRegistries.get(streamId)`, but `_scheduleAnchorRegistryCleanup()` deletes by registry-object identity only. An old T timer can therefore delete the same registry after T+1 has adopted it. Transfer or fence the cleanup lease by owner token, and test an individually controlled old timer firing after same-stream T+1 adoption.

3. **The `cancel` terminal path checks ownership only at admission.** Its unawaited `/api/session` continuation later calls `_applyCancelSessionPayload()` using session ID alone, and the rejection fallback also mutates/render-appends using only the session ID. If T+1 replaces the same session/stream token while that request is pending, stale T can overwrite or append into T+1's transcript. Re-check the exact current owner at the payload sink, after the await, and in the catch path. Add resolve and reject schedules with token-only replacement after admission.

The same sink-level owner check should cover delayed fade-drain steps, warning-clear timers, and the reconnect restore timeout before they mutate pane/global state.

The mandatory security gate was CLEAN at the live head. The targeted sandbox run passed all 48 selected tests (`test_issue6504_stream_settle_flash.py`, `test_1694_terminal_cleanup_ownership.py`, `test_stream_end_recovery_gating.py`, and `test_issue5224_terminal_error_transcript_preserve.py`), but those harnesses stub `_closeSource`, `_wireSSE`, and anchor cleanup in the relevant cases, and they replace the token before terminal admission rather than during the cancel await. The green slice therefore does not exercise these production compositions.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Re-gate summary

I re-gated exact head `02eed4a9bf93b08771067b94af63e08d0f805019` against the prior same-stream ownership findings.

Two named items are fixed. Ordinary current-owner reconnect now retains the owner claim while replacing the transport, and the cancel continuation revalidates owner, source, and pane after its await. The submitted targeted regression file is green through the mandatory sandbox gate.

The head is still not safe to merge. The reconnect change preserves one owner token across two physical `EventSource` instances, but the event ownership predicate does not distinguish those transports. Anchor cleanup also still lets a stale closure take back the replacement owner's cleanup lease. Several mutating listeners and the separately registered run-journal cursor remain outside the new fence.

## Must fix

1. **Fence the exact transport, not only the owner token.**

   `_closeSource(source, {retainOwner:true})` at `static/messages.js:2342-2352` closes the old source and stores `{source:null, ownerToken:<same token>}`. `_wireSSE()` then installs a replacement source under that same token. However, `_bailOutOfTerminalEventsFromStaleStream(source)` at `static/messages.js:2175-2182` accepts whenever `_currentLiveOwnerActive()` and stream ownership hold; it never requires `LIVE_STREAMS[activeSid].source === source`.

   An old-source callback that was already queued before `.close()` can therefore run during the null-source gap or after the replacement source is installed and still mutate the current generation. Add one authoritative event-owner predicate that requires the captured owner token, exact current `source`, and active/background stream ownership, and use it in every SSE callback.

2. **Do not let a stale closure reclaim the Anchor cleanup lease.**

   New-owner setup correctly stamps `_anchorRegistry._cleanupOwnerToken` at `static/messages.js:2756-2757`, but every `_scheduleAnchorRegistryCleanup()` call at `:2758-2767` overwrites that shared token with the calling closure's immutable token. After owner 2 takes the lease, a stale owner-1 terminal or cancel callback can write token 1 back and schedule a timer that deletes owner 2's same-stream registry.

   Transfer the lease only when installing the current owner. A stale closure whose token no longer owns the registry must not be able to rewrite the lease, schedule its deletion, or reclaim it.

3. **Fence every mutating listener and the replay cursor.**

   The `pending_steer_leftover`, `compressing`, `compressed`, and `metering` listeners at `static/messages.js:6223-6330` have no first-line owner/source check. `_rememberRunJournalCursor()` at `:5102-5122`, which is registered as a second callback for journal events, can also advance the replacement owner's persisted replay floor from a stale source. Apply the same exact-transport predicate before any queue, UI, Anchor, usage, cursor, `INFLIGHT`, or persistence mutation.

4. **Replace the false/missing race oracles.**

   The Anchor test changes one mutable token from 1 to 2, while production has two closures with immutable tokens. It never calls the stale owner-1 scheduler after owner 2 takes the lease. Use two distinct closure schedulers: owner 1 schedules, owner 2 takes the lease, owner 1 receives a stale callback and attempts cleanup, owner-1 timers leave the registry intact, and only owner 2 can clean it.

   For reconnect, register the real listener and cursor callbacks, retain the token while replacing the source, then dispatch an already-queued old-source event both before and after the replacement is wired. Assert that it changes no transcript, queue, compression UI, usage, Anchor, cursor, or `INFLIGHT` state, while the replacement source still works. Include `pending_steer_leftover`, `compressing`, `compressed`, and `metering`.

## Verification

All execution used `warmup-safe-test.sh` after a CLEAN threat scan:

- `tests/test_issue6504_stream_settle_flash.py`: **33 passed**
- focused owner

On the remaining Greptile note, I checked the delayed-callback paths directly.

The owner-loss returns that remain after the follow-up push are all one-shot callbacks after the old source is already closed, or preflight checks before any new EventSource is wired:

- `source.onerror` closes the old source before `_probeReconnect()` or the page-hidden deferred resume path is scheduled.
- `_probeReconnect()` only queues the next `setTimeout()` after the post-await owner check. If ownership flips during the awaited status call, that callback returns before any new retry is scheduled.

payload.body:
Requesting changes for one cross-repository provider-switch regression.

## Reproduction path

This PR makes `codex_reasoning_items` and `codex_message_items` survive WebUI's provider-agnostic `_sanitize_messages_for_api()` projection. Preserving them is correct for Codex Responses, but the installed Hermes Agent uses those keys before it reaches the provider-specific stripping cited in the earlier read-only review:

1. `agent/conversation_loop.py:1190-1191` calls `repair_message_sequence_with_cursor(agent, messages)` for every runtime.
2. `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py:519-531` treats any assistant message carrying either Codex field as a Codex interim. The check does not inspect `agent.api_mode`.
3. Pass 0 therefore leaves adjacent assistant turns unmerged after a session switches from Codex Responses to a strict Chat Completions provider.
4. Only later, at `agent/conversation_loop.py:1413-1416` and `agent/transports/chat_completions.py:228-237`, are the Codex fields dropped. Removing the fields there does not repair the already-preserved adjacent-assistant sequence.

The Agent's own repair contract at `agent_runtime_helpers.py:480-492` documents that strict providers reject this sequence, including the `assistant(tool_calls)` followed by another assistant shape. The Codex incomplete-continuation fixture at `tests/run_agent/test_run_agent_codex_responses.py:1867-1898` proves that the adjacent interim shape is real.

The PR's focused WebUI test is green through the required sandbox gate, **20 passed**, but it does not exercise the Codex-to-non-Codex transition.

## Required fix

Prefer fixing the Agent boundary rather than stripping durable Codex continuity state in WebUI:

- In `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py::repair_message_sequence()`, apply the Codex-interim exemption only for an explicit `api_mode == "codex_responses"`. Preserve the existing behavior for callers where no agent or mode is available if state-repair callers depend on it.
- Add an Agent regression with adjacent assistant turns carrying persisted Codex metadata under `api_mode="chat_completions"`. It must prove Pass 0 restores a valid sequence. Keep a paired Codex-mode case proving the encrypted replay turns remain separate.
- Re-run the WebUI sanitizer test plus a Codex Responses continuity turn and a Codex-to-strict-Chat-Completions provider-switch turn.

The one-line WebUI allowlist change itself is the right persistence boundary. This PR is blocked only until the Agent-side compatibility fix and regression are available.

## Summary

Reading `api/streaming.py` at head `e9863c14f` and the full sanitizer regression file on both `origin/master` and the PR head, this is the right boundary for the fix. WebUI already persists the Codex continuation fields; the loss occurs when `_sanitize_messages_for_api()` projects stored history onto the model-facing message shape. Adding the two existing fields to the allowlist preserves that state without admitting unrelated display metadata. I do not see a blocker in this head.

## Code reference

The production change is the allowlist at `api/streaming.py:1660`, which is consumed by the sanitizer projections at `api/streaming.py:4443`, `:4558`, and `:4889`. The focused assertion at `tests/test_context_history_sanitization.py:246-261` checks both sides of the contract:

```python
sanitized = _sanitize_messages_for_api(messages)

assert sanitized[0]["codex_reasoning_items"] == reasoning_items
assert sanitized[0]["codex_message_items"] == message_items
assert "_display_only" not in sanitized[0]
```

The cross-repo check also matches. On the Agent side, `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py:522-529` treats either field as Codex continuation state, `agent/conversation_loop.py:1415` retains replay state only for `codex_responses`, and `agent/transports/chat_completions.py:228-237` removes both fields from non-Codex provider payloads. That means the WebUI pass-through does not turn these into generic Chat Completions request keys.

## The bug is real, but please delegate to the agent's canonical Grok effort-capability source instead of hand-rolling a parallel heuristic — the new list is already stale

Thanks for this — the underlying bug is real: `xai/grok-4.5` routed through `provider=custom` (Vercel AI Gateway et al.) does lose the reasoning-effort chip, and the `xai/` vs `x-ai/` prefix gap is a genuine miss. But the implementation reintroduces a maintenance hazard we should avoid.

### The problem: this duplicates a contract the agent already owns — and the copy is already stale
The Hermes **agent** is the source of truth for which Grok models accept `reasoning.effort`. It's in `agent/model_metadata.py`:

```python
# _GROK_EFFORT_CAPABLE_PREFIXES — verified live against api.x.ai /v1/responses
_GROK_EFFORT_CAPABLE_PREFIXES = (
    "grok-3-mini",
    "grok-4.20-multi-agent",
    "grok-4.3",
    "grok-4.5",   # verified 2026-07-08: accepts low/medium/high
    "grok-4.6",   # drop-in successor of grok-4.5, same effort dial
)
def grok_supports_reasoning_effort(model: str) -> bool:  # strips x-ai/ , xai/ , openrouter/ prefixes
```

This PR's new heuristic in `api/config.py` hard-codes its own list — `grok-3-mini`, `grok-4-3`, `grok-4-5`, `multi-agent` — which:
1. **Omits `grok-4.6`**, which the canonical allowlist already includes. So a user on grok-4.6 through a custom gateway still loses the chip — the PR fixes 4.5 but immediately reintroduces the same bug one version up.
2. Forces every future Grok release (4.7, etc.) to be edited in **two** places that will inevitably drift — exactly what just happened with 4.6.

### The fix (clean, and there's a precedent one line away)
`api/config.py` already imports agent model-metadata in this very region — line 3678: `from agent.models_dev import get_model_capabilities`. So delegate:

```python
from agent.model_metadata import grok_supports_reasoning_effort
```
and use it in `_candidate_supports_reasoning` / `_filter_reasoning_efforts_for_provider` for the Grok branch, rather than the hand-rolled prefix set. The canonical function already strips `x-ai/`, `xai/`, and other aggregator prefixes, so it covers the exact `xai/` gap this PR set out to fix — and it stays correct as the agent's allowlist is updated. Keep your effort-ladder filtering (low/medium/high) for the UI dropdown; just source the *capability* decision from the agent.

### To unblock
1. Replace the hand-rolled Grok prefix list with a call to `agent.model_metadata.grok_supports_reasoning_effort()` (import precedent: config.py:3678).
2. Keep the `xai/` prefix handling only if the canonical helper doesn't already cover it (it does — confirm and drop the duplicate).
3. Update the test to assert grok-4.6 (and any allowlisted model) also gets the chip through `provider=custom`, so the two layers can't silently diverge again.

Rebase onto current master and I'll re-gate. The bug report is good; this just wants to lean on the source of truth the agent already maintains rather than a second copy.

## Changes requested: parser does not match the producer contract

I re-ran this head through the sandboxed warm-up gate against the actual async-delegation formatter in the installed Hermes Agent. The focused PR test is green (8 passed), but four producer-valid/adversarial cases are red:

1. **Real batch worker crashes stay as raw notices.** The producer emits the normal `A background fan-out of N ...` preamble, then optional metadata, `Role: ...`, and `--- ERROR ---`. `_parseProcessWakeupBody()` only recognizes the synthetic literal `A background fan-out could not be started.\n\n--- ERROR ---`, which the producer does not emit.
2. **Valid task headers without optional metrics are rejected.** `tools/process_registry.py` makes goal, `api_calls`, and duration conditional. The UI regex requires a goal and a comma after `status=...`, so a valid `--- ✓ TASK 1/1  (status=completed) ---`-class header has no statuses and falls back to raw text.
3. **Free-form single-task input can override the real status.** Goal/context are inserted before the producer's authoritative status line without newline sanitization. A goal containing `Status: completed` followed by a real `Status: failed ...` is rendered with a green `completed` chip because the parser selects the first `^Status:` line.
4. **An exact task-header lookalike inside result text still changes aggregation.** The regex scans the whole free-form body and does not validate declared count, unique indices, icon/status consistency, or where result sections begin. A completed 1/1 result that quotes a `TASK 2/2 ... status=failed` line renders `partial`.

The sandbox-only adversarial probe returned **4 failed / 4** at exact head `a7f97846942f3d61a1bfb1299a6025732e2e4f80`; the failures were respectively `null`, `null`, `completed` instead of `error`, and `partial` instead of `completed`. Layer 1 was CLEAN and the repository's submitted file remained **8 passed**.

### Fix specification

Please make display status authoritative from structured event metadata rather than reparsing free-form goal/context/result text. The server already has the async event and `_processWakeupInfo()` already prefers `_wakeup_meta`; carry `{type, task_id, status}` through the eager, deferred, and recovered process-wakeup message paths.

Keep text parsing only as a producer-faithful legacy fallback. It must:

- validate the canonical single/batch preamble and delimiters;
- recognize the actual no-results error layout;
- accept omitted goal/API-call/duration fields;
- constrain task headers to the structural task section;
- validate task count, unique ordered indices, and icon/status agreement;
- fail closed to the existing raw notice when the envelope is ambiguous.

Please add byte-for-byte fixtures from `tools/process_registry.py:_format_async_delegation` for the four cases above. Also preserve the untrimmed wakeup body through `api/background_process.py`, `api/routes.py:start_session_turn`, and `renderMessages`; those paths currently call `.strip()` before the card stores/renders the body, so the end-to-end "complete original envelope" claim is not yet true for outer trailing whitespace.

## Re-gate: route/count fixes landed, but two ownership classifiers still misattribute footers

Thanks for the substantive follow-up. I re-gated exact head `fe79e4e29f01a28cfd20b3fde1218c9571d6ef13` against the July 26 findings.

Two requested changes are fixed:

- both the persisted-sidecar and synthesized imported-session branches now call one response-only helper before pagination;
- `own_message_count` now mirrors the state.db reader's `active IS NULL OR active != 0` predicate, so compressed inactive rows no longer suppress valid footer recovery.

The targeted sandbox file is green, **20 passed**. Two deterministic ownership gaps remain.

### 1. `source_label="WebUI"` is omitted from the native-session deny gate

`_session_requires_cli_metadata_lookup()` treats `source_label` as a source marker, and the canonical `is_cli_session_row()` classifier treats `source_label == "webui"` as native authority. But `_session_source_is_webui()` and `_session_ran_outside_webui()` inspect only `source_tag`, `raw_source`, `session_source`, and `source`.

A persisted WebUI-native row whose only surviving native marker is `source_label="WebUI"` therefore passes the foreign-session gate when the other metadata authority does not supply a compensating WebUI marker. The route then opens state.db and can stamp same-ID session totals onto a native WebUI transcript. That is display-only, but it is still false model/duration/token attribution.

**Fix:** use the same complete normalized source set for both positive imported detection and the WebUI-native veto, including `source_label`, on both the sidecar and state metadata. A WebUI marker on either authority must deny backfill before the stats read.

Add route tests where `source_label="WebUI"` is the only native marker on (a) the sidecar and (b) state metadata while the other authority carries a foreign marker. Spy that footer-stat lookup is not called and assert no footer is added.

### 2. The legacy `tool_calls` fallback mistakes narrated tool segments for final answers

When the schema has no `tool_calls` column, `_is_settled_assistant()` now treats every nonblank assistant row as settled. That premise is false for real Agent data: the installed Agent's own `test_insights.py` records CLI tool-call assistants with non-empty content such as `"Let me search"`, followed by a tool row. On that legacy shape, the intermediate narrated tool segment receives model/duration metadata before the final answer.

There is a migrated form of the same problem. Agent startup adds missing message columns to legacy databases, so historical rows can have a present `tool_calls` column with NULL values. `tool_calls_column_present=True` then admits even blank historical tool segments as settled.

The new legacy test covers only a physically column-less database whose intermediate assistant content is empty. It therefore passes without exercising either production shape above.

**Fix:** select final assistants from transcript structure, not schema-wide column presence or content truthiness. Within each user-delimited turn, reject an assistant with explicit `tool_calls`; when metadata is absent/NULL, also treat an assistant followed by a tool row before a later assistant as intermediate. Fail closed on aborted/blank ambiguity rather than stamping a premature footer.

Add real-reader/stamper matrices for both a physically missing column and a migrated present-but-NULL column: narrated assistant → tool → final (only final stamped), narrated/blank assistant → tool with no final (none stamped), and a plain final-answer control.

## Summary

Reading all of `api/agent_sessions.py` at head `a6ef92d13`, the route insertion in `api/routes.py:13059-13072`, the imported-session tests, and the existing state.db projection in `api/models.py:7549-7738`, I found two blockers. First, a tool-using turn can contain an intermediate assistant row with `tool_calls` followed by tool rows and a final assistant answer; the new stamper treats every assistant row as settled. Second, the new pure-read stats helper opens state.db with a write-capable connection even though this module already has a read-only helper for live Agent databases.

## Code reference

At `api/agent_sessions.py:1221-1226`, the new reader does this:

```python
try:
    with closing(sqlite3.connect(str(db_path))) as conn:
        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        cur = conn.cursor()
```

That conflicts with `api/agent_sessions.py:10-39`, where `open_state_db_readonly()` documents why live state.db projections use a read-only URI. The existing projection at `api/agent_sessions.py:815` and `:954` already follows that rule.

The footer ownership issue is at `api/agent_sessions.py:1318-1360`. `assistant_idxs` includes every assistant row, and the loop stamps model and duration on every index. This is not only theoretical: `api/models.py:7611-7622` selects `tool_calls`, and `api/models.py:7717-7735` parses and preserves it in the transcript. The frontend contract at `static/ui.js:11764-11783` explicitly says settled metadata belongs on the last metadata-bearing assistant message of a multi-segment tool turn.

## Diagnosis / recommendation

Use the existing read-only opener:

```python
with closing(open_state_db_readonly(db_path)) as conn:
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
```

Then derive settled assistant indices, rather than all assistant indices. The state.db shape already gives the needed discriminator:

```python
def _is_settled_assistant(message):
    return (
        isinstance(message, dict)
        and _safe_lower(message.get("role")) == "assistant"
        and not message.get("tool_calls")
    )
```

Use those indices for model, duration, and the single-turn usage condition. This keeps an assistant row that requests tools from receiving a premature elapsed time, while the final answer receives the duration from the preceding user message to final completion. No Agent-side contract change is needed; the WebUI reader already retains the relevant field.

## Test plan

`tests/test_imported_session_turn_footer.py:106-131` covers multiple user turns but not one tool-using turn. Add a transcript shaped as user → assistant with non-empty `tool_calls` → tool result → final assistant. Assert that the intermediate assistant has none of `_usedModel`, `_turnDuration`, or `_turnUsage`, while the final assistant has model and the full user-to-final duration. Keep a direct assistant-only control.

Also add a read-only connection assertion beside the existing state.db read-only coverage, or patch the shared opener and prove `read_agent_session_turn_footer_stats()` goes through it. I reviewed source and assertions only and did not execute the untrusted PR code.

Both blockers were real. Fixed in `89dd9ca4`.

## 1. Intermediate assistant rows were getting footers

Confirmed by reading the path you pointed at. `api/models.py:7611-7622` selects `tool_calls` and `:7717-7735` preserves it, so an imported tool-using turn does arrive as `user -> assistant(tool_calls) -> tool -> assistant`, and my `assistant_idxs` took both assistant rows.

Adopted your discriminator:

```python
def _is_settled_assistant(message) -> bool:
    return (
        isinstance(message, dict)
        and _safe_lower(message.get('role')) == 'assistant'
        and not message.get('tool_calls')
    )
```

Those indices now drive model, duration, **and** the single-turn usage condition, as you suggested. The final answer takes the full user-to-completion duration; the tool-call segment gets nothing.

Worth naming the root cause of my error: I copied the in-process path's field *names* (`_usedModel`, `_turnDuration`, `_turnUsage`) but not its *ownership rule*. `_run_agent_streaming` walks `reversed(s.messages)` and `break`s, so it stamps exactly one assistant per turn. Matching the field contract while diverging on which row owns it is precisely the gap you caught.

## 2. Write-capable connection on a pure read

You're right, and the convention was 1200 lines above my own helper. Switched to `open_state_db_readonly(db_path)`, matching `api/agent_sessions.py:815` and `:954` and the #5455 rationale about checkpoint/lock surface on the live WAL database.

## Tests

Both of the cases you asked for, and both fail without this change rather than merely passing with it:

- `test_tool_using_turn_stamps_only_the_settled_assistant` — transcript shaped `user -> assistant(tool_calls) -> tool -> assistant`. Asserts the intermediate assistant has none of `_usedModel` / `_turnDuration` / `_turnUsage`, and that the final carries the model plus the full **8.5s** user-to-final duration, not the 2.0s tool-call segment. Without the fix: `AssertionError: assert '_usedModel' not in {...}`.
- `test_single_call_turn_without_tool_calls_is_the_direct_control` — the assistant-only control you asked to keep.
- `test_footer_stats_read_state_db_through_the_read_only_opener` — patches the shared opener and asserts the stats read goes through it. Without the fix: `AssertionError: stats read did not go through open_state_db_readonly`.

`./scripts/test.sh` on this branch, via the repo runner's `.venv` (Python 3.12.3):

```
13672 passed, 194 skipped, 2 xfailed, 1 xpassed, 34 subtests passed in 486.60s
```

## Unrelated finding while verifying

One test is sensitive to the ambient environment, independent of this PR — flagging it rather than folding it in:

`tests/test_gateway_lifecycle_controls.py::test_gateway_start_runs_profile_scoped_agent_cli_and_returns_status` asserts `kwargs["env"]["BROWSER"] == "echo"`, but `api/routes.py:1234` uses `env.setdefault("BROWSER", "echo")`. It reproduces on master-based branches without this PR's changes, and `env -u BROWSER` makes it pass. Not an issue in CI, where `BROWSER` is unset. Happy to open a separate issue or PR pinning the env in that test if you'd like it addressed.

Both gaps were real. Fixed in `fe79e4e2`. One correction on a third point below.

## 1. Only the no-sidecar branch was wired

You're right, and the consequence is worse than "some sessions miss it": the footer appeared on a CLI/TUI session's *first* load and vanished permanently once a sidecar existed. Same bug for a persisted read-only subagent sidecar.

Both branches now go through one helper, `_imported_session_response_messages()`, and it satisfies all four of your constraints:

**Response-only + detached.** `stamp_imported_turn_footers(..., detach=True)` returns a new list in which only the *stamped* rows are replaced by copies; untouched rows stay shared by reference, so the cost is one dict per settled turn rather than per transcript row. Nothing display-only reaches the sidecar or the reader that feeds model context.

**Full visible segment, before slicing.** The call sits immediately before `_message_window_for_display`, on `_all_msgs`. Two reasons, and the second one I hadn't considered until I wired it: the ownership check is a length comparison a window can never satisfy, *and* stamping pre-slice lets a windowed assistant resolve the user row that opened its turn even when that row is outside the window. This survives the slice because `_messages_for_limited_payload` and `_hydrate_anchor_activity_scenes` both copy rows rather than rebuild them — I checked rather than assumed, since a key-whitelisting transform there would have silently dropped the stamps.

**Ownership gate preserved.** `_session_ran_outside_webui()` reuses `_session_requires_cli_metadata_lookup` rather than inventing a second notion of foreign, then subtracts `_session_source_is_webui`. A `webui` marker on *either* the session or the sidebar row wins, and the two are checked separately — merging their markers into one dict would let an `api` marker on the sidebar row mask a `webui` marker on the sidecar, and backfill session-wide totals over correct per-turn ones.

## 2. Ownership count vs. the reader's visibility predicate

Correct, and it made the feature fail on exactly the sessions most likely to have long transcripts. The count now mirrors `get_state_db_session_messages`' predicate, with `include_inactive` to keep the two paired:


The stitched-segment rejection is unchanged. Worth noting the predicate is index-served — `idx_messages_session_active` is `(session_id, active, timestamp)`.

This one I need to flag rather than agree with. Your review credits "the schema guard added after the prior review" and calls it sound and fail-closed — but no such guard existed. Greptile's re-review of `89dd9ca4` still lists it, and it reproduces:

| `..._persisted_imported_sidecar_gets_the_footer_on

Thanks for the substantive follow-up. The lineage fix remains sound, the basic `role` / `tabindex` / `aria-expanded` / Enter / Space wiring is present, and the child-row height controls now pass. Two objective parts of the accessibility gate are still open at exact head `edade0eba457a6f3822f5ce2a62f54da7e72dd9d`.

### 1. The disclosure is not a 44×44 target for short locales

`static/style.css:5682` gives `.session-child-count::after` a 44px height but leaves `left:0; right:0`, so the hit width remains the pill's content width. The short production Japanese label `2 子` measures **32.4531×44px** at 390×844. Sandboxed Chromium hit tests 21.5px to either side of center both missed the disclosure.

`tests/test_child_disclosure_accessibility.py:35-50` reduces production to four source-string booleans, then lines 54-89 install a separate fixture-owned toggle. That fixture mutates one stable pill in place. Production instead calls `renderSessionListFromCache()` at `static/sessions.js:8128`, whose `list.innerHTML=''` at line 7601 removes the focused disclosure. An actual Enter expansion therefore loses focus; a subsequent Space key does not collapse it as the new test claims.

## Deep re-gate: changes still required

I re-gated exact head `564cb26f90f93f11c08a56e5c4069eab0948c0e5` against the two prior accessibility findings. The native button, real-render keyboard path, focus restoration, child-row sizing, and lineage controls are materially better. The targeted sandbox runs passed (`3`, `9`, and `14` tests). One deterministic mobile interaction regression remains, and the geometry oracle still does not close the required production-shell case.

### 1. A disclosure touch also enters the parent row gesture machine

The inner `.session-child-count` now has `pointer-events:none`, so a touchscreen event targets the outer `.session-child-disclosure`. That button stops `pointerdown`, `pointerup`, and `click`, but the session row separately handles `touchstart` and `touchend` at `static/sessions.js:8876-8892`.

`_isSessionActionTarget()` only recognizes the action-menu subtree, and `_finishSessionGesture()` excludes `.session-child-count` but not `.session-child-disclosure`. A disclosure-origin `touchstart` therefore calls `_beginSessionGesture()` and schedules the long-press path. Its `touchend` reaches the parent settlement and schedules `_openSidebarSession()` after 300 ms before the synthetic button click toggles the children. A mobile tap can both expand/collapse and navigate to the parent; a hold can enter the parent long-press path.

Required fix:

- Treat `.session-child-disclosure` as an interactive child target before `_beginSessionGesture()` and again before swipe/long-press/navigation settlement. Prefer one shared target predicate so the pointer and touch paths cannot drift.
- Add a real touch-context regression (`has_touch=True` plus `page.touchscreen.tap`) through `renderSessionListFromCache()`. Wait past 300 ms and assert one disclosure toggle, correct ARIA/focus state, and zero parent opens, menus, or swipes.

### 2. Exercise the 44×44 envelope in the production list composition

The rewritten browser test now executes production rendering, but its DOM has one top-level row and mounts `#sessionList` without the production `.session-list` class. The 44 px button uses `margin-block:-14px`, projecting outside the compact title row, while every `.session-item` has a transform and its own stacking context. The one-row fixture cannot prove the protruding edges remain hit-owned beside a real sibling row or inside the production scrolling shell.

Please mount the production `.session-list` shell, add an adjacent ordinary top-level row, and assert every corner/edge resolves to `.session-child-disclosure`, with no horizontal overflow and the session actions trigger still reachable. Narrow the selector to `.session-child-disclosure` and assert it is a native `button[type=button]`; the current fallback selector can still accept the earlier span shape.

### 3. Keep visible state and `aria-expanded` consistent during search

`aria-expanded` is derived only from `_expandedChildSessionKeys`, while search can force child rows visible independently. Cover search-forced visibility and ensure the button reports the visible state before and after user activation/query clearing.

## Summary

Reading `static/sessions.js:6883-7072` at head `21ce717f1` against `origin/master`, plus the new and neighboring lineage tests in `tests/test_session_lineage_collapse.py`, the fix is scoped correctly. The WebUI normalization contract maps an `api_server` parent to `session_source=api` at `api/agent_sessions.py:100-101`; the old parent allowlist therefore classified a gateway-backed WebUI conversation as external. Exempting only a child whose raw source is `subagent` repairs that mismatch without changing genuine cross-surface continuation behavior. I found no blocker.

## Code reference

The operative branch at `static/sessions.js:7041-7044` is narrow:

```js
if(parentRow&&child._cross_surface_child_session&&parentIsExternal&&!childIsDelegatedSubagent){
  if(childRenderable) orphans.push({...child,_orphan_child_session:true});
  continue;
}
```

The source marker is derived immediately above from `raw_source`, then `source_tag`, then `source`, matching the normalized sidebar payload. The exemption only matters when a visible parent row exists. The separate no-parent path remains intact at `static/sessions.js:7059-7071`, where a cross-surface child still stays suppressed instead of becoming a contextless top-level row.

## Diagnosis / recommendation

This is the right layer for the reported symptom. The server already exposes both lineage and raw source facts; the bug was in the client projection interpreting `api` as an external parent surface before deciding whether to orphan the child.

The deliberate widening to delegated children of visible messaging or CLI parents is internally consistent: a `subagent` row is execution lineage, not a user-owned continuation surface. Non-subagent children still take the old orphan branch. Existing coverage at `tests/test_session_lineage_collapse.py:728` pins the WebUI-child-under-messaging-parent case, and the archived-parent suppression case remains covered at `tests/test_session_lineage_collapse.py:868`.

## Correction — retracting the re-gate request on `edade0eb`

My previous comment reported the mobile disclosure hit height as 44 px. **That number does not hold in the real app.** Please do not re-gate `edade0eb` yet.

I had measured the computed `::after` height in a bare fixture. Re-measuring through the live app at 390×844 with the sidebar drawer actually open, and probing hit-testable points in 1 px steps rather than reading computed style:

```
pill visual height        16 px   (as intended)
computed ::after height   44 px
empirical tappable span   33 px   <-- from -11 px to +21 px around the pill centre
row height                60 px
```

So the overlay reports 44 px but only ~33 px of it actually receives the hit-test — short of the floor requirement 2 sets. The asymmetry is upward: the downward half reaches its full ~22 px, the upward half stops at ~11 px. The near ancestors (`.session-title-row`, `.session-item`, `.session-date-body`, `.session-date-group`) are all `overflow: visible`, and the only `overflow: auto` ancestor (`.session-list`) is 136 px away, so this is something painting above the overlay in the band above the pill rather than a clip. I have not yet pinned which element.

Two things worth recording from this, since both bear on how the fix should be judged:

1. **The transparent-`::after` approach is the wrong shape for this.** It measures well and behaves worse, and its correctness depends on the stacking context around it. A transparent hit *wrapper* — which your requirement 2 explicitly offered as an option — is not subject to that, and is the direction I will take instead.

Verified as still correct and unaffected: keyboard access works in the live app — focus lands on `.session-child-count`, `aria-expanded` goes `false -> true`, and Enter alone reveals the two nested children, at both viewports. Child-row targets measure 44 px on mobile and 24 px on desktop through the real render path, so requirement 2's second half holds; it is only the disclosure's own hit area that falls short.

I will push a corrected implementation with a test bound to the real render path, then re-request the gate. Apologies for the premature request.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Changes requested: several advertised commands cannot execute their Agent behavior

I reviewed exact head `d15029e7f43f4e0e6f913ed47f521da37b496c0f`. The static threat scan was clean, but the new command surface has deterministic runtime and test failures.

### 1. `/agents`, `/insights`, and `/rollback` call APIs that do not exist

`api/commands.py` imports:

- `agent.run.list_active_agents`
- `hermes_cli.insights.build_insights_report`
- `hermes_cli.checkpoints.list_checkpoints`
- `hermes_cli.checkpoints.restore_checkpoint`

The installed Agent has no `agent.run` module and no `hermes_cli.insights` module. `hermes_cli.checkpoints` does not export the requested checkpoint functions. These commands therefore return fallback prose with HTTP 200 instead of doing what the autocomplete promises. `/insights` also points users to nonexistent `/api/analytics`; WebUI's route is `/api/insights`.

For rollback, the real authority is `tools.checkpoint_manager.CheckpointManager`. Its list rows use `hash`, `short_hash`, `timestamp`, and `reason`; restore requires `(working_dir, commit_hash)` and returns a dict whose `success` field must be checked. The current code passes a list number to a nonexistent function, has no trusted working-directory authority, looks for nonexistent row labels, rejects hash targets, and would treat a failure dict as success.

### 2. `/fast` writes an unused setting

The new handler toggles top-level `fast.enabled`. Current Agent behavior consumes `agent.service_tier`; canonical `/fast` has status, session-level `fast|normal`, and explicit `--global` semantics. WebUI currently reports “enabled” while Agent behavior does not change. The handler also writes the whole expanded config without the config lock, which risks lost concurrent updates and materializing environment-expanded values.

### 3. `/learn` does not invoke the canonical learn handler

`hermes chat -q '/learn …'` enters one-shot mode, where the text is handled as a new YOLO-enabled agent prompt. It does not call the interactive `/learn` handler that builds the canonical learning prompt. The request profile is not transferred to the subprocess, there is no per-profile single-flight guard, and the subprocess return code is ignored. Missing/non-executable CLI, timeout, and nonzero/empty results can all become HTTP-200 “dispatched” or “processed” messages.

This command also widens the WebUI mutation/execution boundary (URL/path scanning and skill creation) and overlaps open #5417. That product/security decision belongs to the maintainer after the objective defects are fixed.

### 4. Profile/version and frontend contracts are incorrect

- `/profile` reads process-global `HERMES_PROFILE` and `HERMES_HOME`, so a cookie-selected named profile can be reported as `default`.
- `/version` imports absent `api.__version__`, so WebUI reports `?` instead of its real version source.
- `/resume [name]` ignores the name and only opens the browser.
- Async command handlers are not awaited on the normal idle path. Their output is appended only to in-memory `S.messages`, so it is not durable chat history.

### 5. Existing targeted tests are red

All PR-code execution used the mandatory no-network/no-secrets sandbox:

```text
2 failed, 96 passed, 18 skipped
```

The unchanged failures are:

- `test_cli_only_slash_commands.py::test_frontend_can_execute_agent_commands_via_api_endpoint`
- `test_goal_command_webui.py::test_frontend_has_goal_slash_command_and_status_event_handler`

The PR changes no tests.

### Required fix

Use the real Agent authorities and exact return shapes, bind every operation to the authenticated active profile and a trusted workspace, return non-2xx failures instead of success prose, implement the consumed `agent.service_tier` contract with a locked raw partial config update, and route learning through a dedicated bounded canonical handler rather than generic one-shot chat. Await/serialize mutation handlers, decide whether output is durable or explic

payload.author: greptile-apps
payload.body:
Good fixes overall, but there's one concrete bug introduced in `_run_learn_command` and `_run_profile_command`: both use `os` (and `_run_learn_command` uses `shutil`) but neither is imported at the module level. The top-level imports in `api/commands.py` are:

```python
from __future__ import annotations
from contextlib import nullcontext
import logging
import threading
from typing import Any
```

`_run_profile_command` calls `os.environ.get(...)` and `os.path.expanduser(...)`, and `_run_learn_command` calls `shutil.which(...)`, `os.path.expanduser(...)`, `os.path.isfile(...)`, `os.access(...)`, and `os.environ` — all without `import os` / `import shutil` in scope. Both functions will raise `NameError` at runtime when invoked (the `except Exception` fallback in `_run_profile_command` will also fail for the same reason, since it calls `os.environ` too).

Fix:

```suggestion
from __future__ import annotations
from contextlib import nullcontext
import logging
import os
import shutil
import threading
from typing import Any
```

Everything else looks good — the profile-scoped `_run_fast_command` pattern mirrors `_codex-runtime` correctly, the `_subprocess.TimeoutExpired` catch is now in scope (since `import subprocess as _subprocess` executes before the `.run()` call), and removing `/moa` from `COMMANDS` cleanly restores the `send()` dispatch path.

Tip: You can customize Greptile's behavior for this repo with [`.greptile/rules.md` and `.greptile/config.json`](https://www.greptile.com/docs/code-review/custom-standards).
