payload.author: franksong2702
payload.body:
I independently reviewed and executed the current head, `c0e68bc6e4f2f280bb3adbd790f67949d10f6a3c`. The token minting, persisted-token convergence, inbound `x-hermes-*` stripping, injection ordering, and response stripping all look sound. I am requesting changes for two remaining blockers.

### 1. Auth-off still makes WebUI a token-bearing forwarding oracle

I agree with the existing threat-model comment at https://github.com/nesquena/hermes-webui/pull/6331#issuecomment-5016760950, and the executed paths support it.

`api/extensions.py:1690-1701` permits a loopback `token-v1` target when WebUI authentication is disabled. Consent provisioning at lines 1605-1618 also does not require an authenticated operator. `api/routes.py:5594` requires browser provenance before proxying, but Origin, Referer, Host, and fetch-metadata headers are caller-controlled signals rather than credentials. Once those checks pass, core injects the token at lines 5613-5619.

The targeted suite currently pins both halves of this behavior: `test_token_v1_auth_off_allows_loopback_origin` proves an auth-off caller can obtain a token-bearing target after granting consent, while the same-origin proxy test proves caller-supplied provenance is sufficient to drive the route. The token blocks direct access to the sidecar port, but a caller that can reach WebUI can still ask core to access it with the token.

Please require configured WebUI authentication for both `token-v1` consent and resolution, regardless of the upstream loopback address. Replace the auth-off allow assertion with fail-closed coverage and add a route-level auth-off consent/proxy regression test. If auth-off support remains intentional, the claimed protection against another local UID must be removed because that caller can reach the WebUI listener without reading the token file.

### 2. The current head is red on every supported Python version

I ran the new proxy file through the repository test wrapper: `27 passed`. I then ran the complete extension-status endpoint file: `2 failed, 38 passed`. The same two failures occur in GitHub shard 4 for Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13.

Both failures come from adding `proxy_auth: legacy` and `posture: None` to legacy public status payloads while the existing exact-shape contract tests still expect the old payload. Please decide whether those fields are intended for all legacy records or only token-v1 records, then update the implementation/tests consistently. The branch should not merge with the three matrix jobs red.

The paired scaffold review is also currently `CHANGES_REQUESTED`: https://github.com/hermes-webui/hermes-webui-extensions/pull/65#pullrequestreview-4732183421. That review found fail-open config handling, manifest-independent CI discovery, and missing health CORS/cache headers. Since #65 consumes this core contract, the auth-off and status semantics should be settled here first and then verified across both heads.

Validation performed:

- `./scripts/test.sh tests/test_extension_status_endpoint.py -q` -> 2 failed, 38 passed
- `git diff --check origin/master...HEAD` -> exit 0
- current GitHub checks -> Python 3.11/3.12/3.13 shard 4 failed

Greptile Summary

 This PR introduces `proxy_auth: token-v1` — a per-extension shared secret that core mints, injects on every proxied request (`X-Hermes-Sidecar-Token`), and the sidecar validates — closing the gap where any local process could drive a loopback sidecar directly, bypassing the consent-gated WebUI proxy. - **`api/extension_sidecar_auth.py`** (new): atomic `os.link` create-or-fail token mint, fingerprint-bracketed `_stable_read` for live rotation, and `_valid_ext_id` using `fullmatch` to prevent trailing-newline path tricks. - **`api/extensions.py`**: `proxy_auth` manifest negotiation (absent/legacy unchanged; unknown = fail-closed), auth-off 403 at both consent time and resolution time, and `posture` field scoped to token-v1 status records only. - **`api/routes.py`**: inbound `x-hermes-*` strip (anti-forge), token injection after strip, and outbound `x-hermes-*` strip (anti-leak); also closes a pre-existing `X-Hermes-CSRF-Token` forward to the sidecar.

Confidence Score: 5/5

 Safe to merge. The core security properties — fail-closed on auth-off, atomic single-winner minting, live-rotation via fingerprint-bracketed reads, and inbound/outbound header stripping — are all correctly implemented and well-tested. The auth boundary logic is sound: consent and resolution both enforce the auth-off 403 independently, the `os.link` idiom correctly prevents token clobber across concurrent processes, and the `_valid_ext_id` fullmatch fix closes the trailing-newline filename trick. Legacy sidecars are byte-for-byte unchanged. api/extension_sidecar_auth.py — the `_stable_read` function uses `_TOKEN_RE.match` rather than `fullmatch`; all other files look correct.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Summary

Reading `api/extension_sidecar_auth.py` in full, the `api/extensions.py` and `api/routes.py` diffs, and the added proxy tests, the token creation/injection path itself is fail-closed and the inbound `x-hermes-*` stripping is sound. I think there is still one threat-model blocker: the auth-off branch turns the WebUI proxy into a token-bearing forwarding oracle. The loopback check applies to the upstream sidecar address, not to the caller reaching WebUI.

## Code reference

At `api/extensions.py:1684-1698`, token-v1 remains available whenever WebUI auth is off and the *sidecar* is loopback:

```python
if proxy_auth == "token-v1":
    from api.auth import is_auth_enabled
    if not is_auth_enabled():
        if not _sidecar_origin_is_loopback(sidecar["origin"]):
            raise ExtensionSidecarProxyError(...)
```

`api/routes.py:5594-5608` then checks browser provenance and asks the resolver for a target; it does not authenticate the caller or establish that the caller is the same operator. Origin, Referer, Host, and fetch-metadata headers are browser signals, not credentials, and a non-browser HTTP client can supply them. Once consent exists, core injects the secret at `api/routes.py:5612-5621`.

This means an auth-off client that can reach WebUI can grant consent and invoke the fixed proxy path without reading the token file. That includes the other-UID local process named in the PR threat model, because it can connect to the WebUI loopback listener, and it can include remote clients when WebUI is intentionally bound beyond loopback. The token still blocks direct access to the sidecar port, but not access through core.

## Recommendation

Require configured WebUI authentication for `token-v1` resolution and consent, regardless of the sidecar target address. If auth-off support is intentional, the security claim needs to be narrowed: `local_unprotected` does not protect against another local UID that can reach WebUI. Also fix the contract mismatch at `docs/EXTENSIONS.md:207-210`: the document says the panel surfaces `auth_required`, while `api/extensions.py:1188-1211` returns `posture` with `local_unprotected` or `protected`.

## Test plan

Replace `tests/test_extension_sidecar_proxy.py:1009` with a fail-closed auth-off assertion, add a consent-route case with auth disabled, and retain the authenticated injection/response-strip coverage. Legacy declarations should remain unchanged. I did not execute PR code because this review uses read-only inspection of the untrusted worktree.

payload.body:
Thanks @franksong2702 — both blockers and the Greptile P2 are resolved on the new head `db92d583c`. Summary of the changes:

### 1. Auth-off token-v1 is now fail-closed (both consent AND resolution), regardless of loopback

token-v1 now **requires configured WebUI authentication** at both entry points, with no loopback exception:

- **Consent** (`set_extension_sidecar_proxy_consent`, `api/extensions.py`): granting consent for a `proxy_auth: token-v1` sidecar raises **403** when `is_auth_enabled()` is false — before any token is minted or consent persisted.
- **Resolution** (`resolve_extension_sidecar_proxy_target`): the auth check runs unconditionally (removed the `_sidecar_origin_is_loopback` allow-branch entirely) and raises **403** with auth off. This is deliberately redundant with the consent gate so a consent granted while auth was enabled cannot be exercised after auth is turned off.

Per your point that loopback isn't a real guard (another local UID can reach the listener without reading the 0600 token file), the loopback allowance is gone completely. Tests updated to pin the fail-closed contract:
- `test_token_v1_auth_off_allows_loopback_origin` → replaced with `test_token_v1_auth_off_blocks_consent_and_resolution_fail_closed` (consent 403 with auth off, loopback origin).
- Added `test_token_v1_resolution_fails_closed_when_auth_disabled_after_consent` (consent granted under auth, then auth disabled → resolution 403 — the stale-consent case).
- Added the **route-level** regression you asked for: `test_extension_sidecar_proxy_consent_route_fails_closed_auth_off` drives the real consent function through `POST /api/extensions/sidecar-proxy-consent` with auth off and asserts the route returns 403 and persists nothing.

### 2. Status contract fixed — `proxy_auth`/`posture` are token-v1-only

Decided these fields belong **only on token-v1 records**, so legacy sidecars keep their original public payload byte-for-byte. Two leaks fixed: the nested `proxy` dict now only adds `proxy_auth`/`posture` when `proxy_auth == "token-v1"`, and the public sidecar record no longer spreads the internal top-level `proxy_auth` (`_extension_sidecar_records` builds the public record explicitly, dropping it). The two exact-shape contract tests (`test_extension_status_reports_sanitized_loopback_sidecars`, `test_extension_status_reports_sidecar_proxy_consent_and_origin_change`) pass unchanged, and the token-v1 posture test still asserts `posture == "local_unprotected"` inside `proxy`.

### 3. Greptile P2 — `_valid_ext_id` uses `fullmatch`

`api/extension_sidecar_auth.py:_valid_ext_id` now uses `_EXT_ID_RE.fullmatch(ext_id.strip())` (was `.match`, which accepted a trailing `\n` before `$`), matching the sibling `_valid_extension_id` in `extensions.py`.

## Summary

Reading the complete release workflow and both versions of `docs/docker.md`, the channel split for the floating tags is clear, but the proposed immutable-tag contract is ambiguous: stable and experimental releases publish into the same numeric Docker tag namespace. That can overwrite a supposedly pinned artifact when both Git tag forms exist for one semantic version. There is also a smaller workflow-hardening issue in the channel detector.

## Code reference

At `.github/workflows/release.yml:53-58`, both match rules discard the channel prefix and emit the same capture group:

```yaml
type=match,pattern=v(\d+\.\d+(?:\.\d+)?),group=1
type=match,pattern=exp-v(\d+\.\d+(?:\.\d+)?),group=1
```

The documentation makes the collision visible. `docs/docker.md:22` assigns `:X.Y` and `:X.Y.Z` to stable releases, while line 23 assigns those exact tag names to experimental releases. If `exp-v1.5.0` publishes first and `v1.5.0` publishes later, both writes target `:1.5.0`; the second push changes what the pinned experimental reference resolves to. The reverse ordering can also replace a stable pin with experimental content. Floating `:latest` and `:experimental` remain correct, but numeric pins do not preserve channel identity.

Separately, `.github/workflows/release.yml:20-27` interpolates the GitHub ref expression directly into a shell conditional. A tag name is command input, so it should be passed through a step-level environment binding and compared as data rather than inserted into the generated script text.

## Recommendation

Give experimental immutable images their own namespace, for example `:exp-X.Y` and `:exp-X.Y.Z`, while retaining unprefixed numeric tags for stable releases. Anchor the two match patterns so the stable rule cannot also match the `v...` suffix inside an experimental ref. Update the table to state the exact channel-specific pin syntax. If the project intentionally guarantees globally unique semantic versions across both Git tag prefixes, document and enforce that invariant before keeping the shared namespace.

## Verification step

Inspect metadata output for one stable ref and one experimental ref with the same version. The expected sets should be disjoint except for explicitly intended aliases: stable gets `latest` plus stable numeric pins; experimental gets `experimental` plus experimental-prefixed pins. I did not execute the PR workflow or any PR-authored code; this is a read-only workflow and documentation review.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Warm-up review: changes requested

Thanks for tackling #6316. The normal completed-turn sidecar path is compacted, and the targeted changed-file slice is green (`53 passed` in the sandbox), but the current head still persists image bytes on another production path and has two independent compaction-contract regressions.

### 1. Raw vision callback data is journaled before compaction

`agent/tool_executor.py:945-948` invokes `tool_complete_callback(..., function_result)` with the raw tool result. In WebUI, `api/streaming.py::_tool_result_snippet()` stringifies an envelope without `output` / `result` / `error` and keeps up to 4,000 characters (`:6131-6143`). `on_tool_complete()` then stores that string in shared live-tool state and emits it as `tool_complete.preview` (`:8221-8250`). `put()` appends every SSE payload to the run journal before queueing it (`:7370-7397`), and journal replay returns the payload unchanged (`api/routes.py:17040-17052`).

That means a raw `_multimodal` vision result can still put a base64 prefix into durable JSONL and replay it, even though the final transcript is compacted. Cancel/error recovery can also persist the shared snippet through `_partial_tool_calls`.

**Required fix:** derive callback previews and shared cancel/error tool summaries from a sanitized copy before calling `put()` or storing them in `STREAM_LIVE_TOOL_CALLS`. The run journal, replay, and partial snapshots must contain no encoded image bytes.

### 2. The helper removes image references that are not base64

`_compact_image_parts_for_persistence()` replaces every typed `image`, `image_url`, or `input_image` part without inspecting its source (`api/streaming.py:4255-4272`). A normal `https://` image, file/artifact reference, or other durable non-inline image is therefore destroyed even though the stated scope is base64 payloads. Conversely, nested shapes such as `_multimodal.content`, `tool_result.content`, and Anthropic-style `source: {type: "base64", ...}` are not inspected.

**Required fix:** compact only inline base64 image payloads, including the supported direct-string/dict data-URL and nested provider shapes. Preserve remote/file/artifact/reference images and unrelated fields/order exactly.

### 3. In-place compaction mutates shared result/cache objects

The helper intentionally mutates rows in place (`api/streaming.py:4240-4242`). Production history assembly derives display and context histories from the same `result["messages"]` dictionaries (`_assign_stable_message_ids()` documents the sharing at `:4574-4577`; the sync path assigns/merges those rows at `api/routes.py:22308-22331`). The new isolation test uses artificial `deepcopy()` inputs, so it does not cover the production alias graph. Compaction can therefore mutate the agent result and cached model-facing message objects rather than only a persistence copy.

**Required fix:** make compaction copy-returning (or deep-copy rows at the persistence/UI boundary) so the caller's `result["messages"]`, raw callback value, and agent cache remain unchanged while only durable/display copies are sanitized.

### Tests needed

Please add behavioral regressions that prove:

1. raw `_multimodal` callback → journal JSONL, journal replay, and cancel/error partial snapshots contain no data URL/base64 bytes;
2. caller/result/cached-agent graphs remain value- and identity-unmodified;
3. `https://`, file, artifact, and other reference images survive;
4. direct-string/dict data URLs, mixed-case/parameter variants, Anthropic base64 sources, `_multimodal` envelopes, and nested `tool_result.content` are compacted while unrelated values and part order remain intact;
5. the real sanitizer plus transcript compaction/replay still preserves provider-valid paired tool rows.

These are deterministic persistence and data-preservation gaps, so this needs a contributor re-push rather than a visual or product call.

## Re-gate: the persistence blockers remain

Thanks for the follow-up. The new commit strips inline image data URLs from the **live prompt estimate**, but it does not fix the persistence paths named in the previous review.

At current head `928df0caca05`:

## Re-gate: persistence boundary is still incomplete

Thanks for the substantive follow-up. Copy-on-write is now real and the modern completion snippet is scrubbed, but the current head `07b59ef4f8b1` still leaves objective persistence/replay gaps and adds a duplicate-compaction regression.

### 1. Raw vision data still reaches live state, journal, replay, and partial snapshots

`api/streaming.py` still stores raw callback arguments in both live mirrors:

- legacy start: `_live_tool_calls` and `STREAM_LIVE_TOOL_CALLS` at lines 8232-8244
- modern start: the same mirrors at lines 8361-8374

`_tool_args_snapshot()` only stringifies/truncates values; it does not remove inline image bytes. The legacy completion callback also sends raw `preview` to `put('tool_complete', ...)` at lines 8313-8320. `put()` journals before queueing, replay emits stored payloads, and cancel/error persistence takes snapshots of these rows. The modern completion snippet fix therefore closes only one producer.

**Fix:** create one recursive, source-aware projection for tool args/results and apply it before any write to either live mirror or `put()` in both callback APIs. Apply the same boundary to cancel/error `_partial_tool_calls` and sanitize historical journal replay. Preserve HTTP(S), `file:`, artifact, handle, and path references.

### 2. The compactor still destroys mixed nested content and misses provider shapes

`_part_is_inline_base64_image()` recurses into a `content` list, but its caller replaces the entire outer part with `[screenshot]` when one child is inline (`api/streaming.py:4314-4318, 4360-4365`). A mixed wrapper loses sibling text, metadata, and non-inline image references. A direct-string `image_url` is also missed at line 4304, while any Anthropic-style `source.type == 'base64'` is treated as an image without checking media provenance.

**Fix:** return a recursively projected copy that replaces only actual inline image leaves. Cover nested mixed wrappers, direct-string and object `image_url`, non-image base64 sources, unknown/scalar parts, idempotence, and shared aliases.

### 3. The rebase added redundant full-history compaction

Normal completion calls `_compact_session_image_parts_for_persistence(s)` at both lines 9271 and 9273. The exception self-heal branch has the same duplicate. Because the helper deep-copies each non-empty history even when nothing changes, every duplicate performs and discards two extra full-history copies. The tip commit changes the static test from three calls to five, blessing the regression even though there are only three success branches.

**Fix:** retain exactly one correctly ordered call in each of the three success branches and make the test assert branch-local ordering, not a global count of five.

### Required regression coverage

Add real legacy and modern callback lifecycle tests covering callback -> both live mirrors -> journal-before-queue -> replay, plus cancel/error save-and-reload checks for `_partial_tool_calls`. The current `test_callback_journal_no_base64` calls only `_tool_result_snippet()` and does not exercise that lifecycle.

Sandboxed targeted tests are green (`29 passed`), but they do not cover these paths. Please keep the copy-on-write improvement, close the remaining producer-to-sink boundary, remove the duplicate calls, and add the lifecycle regressions above.

## Changes requested: two journal/replay redaction paths remain open

I re-gated exact head `023bba141a7ef4df13f1f4cec4c79d45b564b6e7` against the prior persistence-boundary review at `4f2abd523fd7`. This force-pushed series contains substantial fixes worth keeping:

- legacy and structured callbacks now derive projected args/previews before the live mirrors and journal-before-queue `put()` calls;
- generic dict/list provider wrappers recurse copy-on-write while preserving safe siblings and references;
- cancel/error partial construction projects rows defensively;
- the successful-history compaction oracle is back to exactly three calls;
- 42 focused tests passed in the mandatory sandbox (`19 + 19 + 4`).

Two objective current-head gaps still allow inline image bytes through the boundary.

### 1. Valid image MIME subtypes bypass the shared string projector

`api/streaming.py:_strip_base64_data_urls()` matches only:

```python
r'data:image/[a-zA-Z]+;base64,[A-Za-z0-9+/=]+'
```

That does not match common valid subtypes containing punctuation, including `data:image/svg+xml;base64,...` and `data:image/x-icon;base64,...`. This helper is what the new callback arg/preview and replay projections use, so those encoded payloads survive the supposedly safe live mirrors, journal events, cancel/error rows, and replay payloads. Every new callback fixture uses png/jpeg/gif, so the green suite does not exercise this shape.

**Required fix:** use one case-insensitive image-data-URI recognizer that accepts valid subtype characters such as `+`, `-`, and `.`, and strips the complete encoded payload. Keep HTTP, file, artifact, non-base64 data, and ordinary text references byte-for-byte unchanged. Add `svg+xml`, `x-icon`, case-variant, and safe-reference controls through the real callback/journal/replay path.

### 2. Session-level journal replay still emits old raw payloads

The new `_project_replay_tool_payload()` is wired into `_replay_run_journal()`, but the nested `emit_replay()` in the session-events route still calls:

```python
_sse_with_id(handler, event, entry.get("payload"), event_id)
```

with the historical payload unchanged. That function is fed by `read_session_run_events()` both before attach and during reconciliation, so a pre-fix journal containing raw `tool`/`tool_complete` args or preview is replayed verbatim through `/api/session/<id>/events`. The submitted replay test calls only the leaf projector, not either producer, so deleting this missing call leaves all focused tests green.

**Required fix:** route every journal-to-client/materialization boundary through one projector before SSE emission, including session-level `emit_replay()`. Make it shape-complete for dict/list/tuple args and both preview/snippet strings, without mutating the stored journal entry. Add a route-composed test that seeds a pre-fix journal with nested image args and `svg+xml` preview/snippet, drives real session replay/reconciliation, and proves emitted SSE contains no encoded image bytes while preserving event IDs and safe content.

Please also retain the exact-three compaction oracle and the new copy-on-write/generic-recursion behavior. The missing real cancel/error/shared-alias lifecycle cases remain useful coverage, but the two source-proven leaks above are the current merge blockers.

## Changes requested: the claimed RFC 6838 subtype grammar is incomplete

I re-gated force-rebased exact head `89a5af57876270b705ae852206cecb7bd8515c47`. The replay projection, recursive copy-on-write behavior, both session replay paths, and current writeback compaction placements remain sound. The remaining blocker is narrow but objective.

`_strip_base64_data_urls()` uses:

```python
r'data:image/[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9+.\-]*;base64,...'
```

The docstring and tests claim any valid RFC 6838 subtype, but RFC 6838 restricted-name characters also permit `! # $ & ^ _` after the leading alphanumeric. Exact-head sandbox diagnostics confirmed valid forms such as `image/x_test`, `image/x!test`, `image/x$test`, and `image/x&test` remain byte-for-byte unstripped, while the existing `+` control is stripped. The submitted 47-test target passes because its “valid subtype” matrix covers only `+`, `-`, and `.`.

Please accept the complete restricted-name character set after the leading alphanumeric, extend the helper matrix with every omitted allowed character, and put at least one currently omitted valid subtype through both the no-live and post-attach real journal replay schedules. Preserve the converged projector recursion, safe-reference handling, replay call sites, and compaction placements; no broader rewrite is requested.

## Re-gate: the raw-env fix still breaks default-profile credentials

Thanks for the quick follow-up. I reviewed the new head `718b32862b2a` against the prior gate finding. The serial named-profile leak is improved, but the new root branch introduces a deterministic configured-but-fails regression and does not close the boundary under concurrent scopes.

### Must fix

1. **Preserve credentials owned by the default/root profile.**

   `profile_scope_for_detached_worker()` now removes every key in the process-global `_loaded_profile_env_keys` before entering a root worker (`api/profiles.py:1392-1408`). That set is also populated when `_reload_dotenv()` loads the default profile at startup (`api/profiles.py:1448-1507`). In the normal default-profile configuration, a legitimate root `.env` key such as `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is therefore removed for the worker body. At the same time, `block_process_env_fallback=True` is set without installing a root thread-local environment, so `_thread_local_env_value()` returns empty rather than the root credential (`api/config.py:291-307`). A configured default-profile provider can become unavailable inside the detached worker.

2. **Make the ownership/concurrency boundary explicit.**

   `_loaded_profile_env_keys` records key names but not which profile owns their current values. The root scope cannot distinguish root-owned keys from foreign named-profile keys. It also pops/restores outside the `_ENV_LOCK`, while a named `profile_env_for_background_worker()` may write its environment after the pop and before the root worker reads it (`api/profiles.py:1185-1205`), reopening the raw-`os.getenv()` leak under an overlapping scope.

   Please replace the ownerless pop/restore with a root-aware scoped environment: install the canonical root runtime/thread environment and context-local home, preserve root/operator credentials, scrub only values proven foreign to root, and use one ownership/synchronization protocol for any remaining process-env mirrors and raw reads. Restoration must be safe on normal and exception exits.

3. **Add fail-first coverage for the missing cases.**

   The amended tests strengthen the serial foreign-key case, but add no coverage for:
   - a root-active process with a root-owned provider key that must remain usable;
   - conflicting same-name root and named-profile keys;
   - barrier-controlled overlapping root/named scopes in both entry orders;
   - success and exception restoration of TLS, thread env, fallback state, and process env.

### Verification note

The mandatory threat scanner classified this head `DANGEROUS` because the added credential-isolation test text matched its credential-read rule. Per policy, this re-gate was static/diff-only and no PR code or tests were executed. The blockers above are direct current-source ownership and ordering defects, not conclusions inferred from a failed test run.

## Re-gate: the root credential scrub is removed, but the isolation boundary is still open

Thanks for the follow-up. I re-gated exact head `f02c9d486650aa0fab013c3d644f86324cb22097` against the previous request for changes.

One part is fixed: the default/root branch no longer uses the ownerless `_loaded_profile_env_keys` registry to pop and restore process credentials. Two objective blockers remain.

### Must fix

1. **Install root-owned thread/context credentials before blocking process fallback.**

   In `profile_scope_for_detached_worker()` (`api/profiles.py`), the root branch sets `block_process_env_fallback = True` but never installs a root thread env. `_thread_local_env_value()` therefore returns its empty default for every credential absent from the thread env. A credential owned by the default/root profile can remain present in `os.environ` while becoming unavailable to the TLS-aware provider/config paths inside the worker.

2. **Close the raw `os.getenv()` channel, including overlap with named-profile scopes.**

   A thread-local boolean cannot affect raw `os.getenv()`. The current test rewrite explicitly documents that the named profile's `.env` remains visible through raw `os.getenv()` inside the default worker, while credential/model readers reachable from this path still use process env. `profile_env_for_background_worker()` also holds `_ENV_LOCK` only during setup and restoration, not during the worker body, so overlapping named/root scopes still expose or restore foreign values without one ownership protocol.

   Please either migrate every raw credential reader reachable from the detached rebuild to explicit/context-scoped credentials, or serialize the complete process-env mutation and raw-read body for named and root scopes under one audited ownership protocol.

### Tests required

The sandbox-gated target is green (`35 passed`), but the changed tests weaken the decisive oracle:

- restore the named-active → root-worker raw-key assertions that this push removes;
- load a real root `.env` through `_reload_dotenv()` and assert both raw and `_thread_local_env_value()`/provider behavior preserve the root credential;
- add barrier-controlled named/root overlap tests in both entry orders with the same key carrying different values;
- cover success and exception restoration, including no stale reinsertion/overwrite.

The new root-preservation test only calls `monkeypatch.setenv()` and asserts `os.environ.get()`. It does not construct the prior `_loaded_profile_env_keys` precondition and does not exercise the TLS-aware credential path, so its green result does not prove convergence.

## Re-gate: detached scopes improved, but process-env ownership is still split

Thanks for the follow-up. I re-gated exact head `7d044def4622d38e07f46ce47370f89d0e45f7c4` against the prior credential-isolation findings.

The root-specific work has converged:

- root thread/context credentials are installed before process fallback is blocked;
- foreign named-profile values are scrubbed from the root raw-env channel;
- the isolation assertions are restored;
- the submitted sandbox target passes (`39 passed`).

One objective concurrency blocker remains.

### Must fix: use one full-body owner for every process-env-mirroring entrypoint

`profile_scope_for_detached_worker()` now holds `_DETACHED_SCOPE_ENV_LOCK` across the complete detached worker body (`api/profiles.py:1531-1547`). However, `profile_env_for_background_worker()` still documents and implements a narrow `_ENV_LOCK`: it snapshots and mutates process env at `api/profiles.py:1313-1328`, releases the lock for the caller body at `:1329`, then restores that stale snapshot at `:1332-1343`. `profile_env_for_active_request()` delegates to the same path at `:1475-1492`.

Those public production entrypoints therefore mutate the same process-wide credential environment under a different ownership boundary from the detached scope.

A deterministic sandboxed probe forced a direct or active-request-mirrored alpha scope to overlap a detached beta scope using the same credential key with different values. Both cases failed:

- beta entered before alpha released;
- alpha's raw read changed from `alpha-value` to `beta-value` while alpha's TLS value remained correct;
- alpha's stale restore changed beta's raw read to `ambient-value`;
- beta's final restore left stale `alpha-value` globally instead of restoring `ambient-value`.

Probe result: **2 collected, 2 failed** (`direct` and `active-request-mirrored`). This was a normal Layer-3 sandboxed pytest failure after a CLEAN threat scan, not a scan refusal. The contributor target was rerun after the temporary probe was removed and remained **39/39 green** on a clean exact-head worktree.

### Required change

1. Replace the detached-only lock with one re-entrant, full-body process-env ownership lock shared by every process-env-mirroring entrypoint.
2. Acquire it in `profile_env_for_background_worker()` before env resolution/snapshot and hold it through setup, the complete caller `yield`, and restoration. `profile_env_for_active_request()` should inherit that boundary.
3. Make the shared lock an `RLock` (or remove the redundant outer acquisition in the detached named branch) so the detached wrapper does not self-deadlock.
4. Keep one explicit lock order with `_SKILL_HOME_MODULE_PATCH_LOCK` and `_ENV_LOCK`.
5. Add a fail-first regression for direct and active-request-mirrored scopes overlapping a detached scope. Assert no early entry, owner-correct raw and TLS values throughout, and exact ambient restoration. Prefer both entry orders and named/root detached variants.

The current tests cover detached-versus-detached overlap only, so their green result does not exercise this split entrypoint boundary.

## Re-gate: named overlap is fixed, but root scopes still bypass ownership and the new lock order can deadlock

Thanks for the follow-up. I re-gated exact head `6654176ff558f56dd0e10b8bb161121c2f9e3374` against the prior process-environment ownership finding.

The named path is genuinely improved:

- `_PROCESS_ENV_OWNERSHIP_LOCK` is now an `RLock`;
- a named `profile_env_for_background_worker()` acquires it before environment resolution and holds it through setup, the complete caller body, and restoration;
- named active-request scopes inherit that boundary;
- the four new overlap tests use real context managers, threads, conflicting values, raw/TLS reads, and restoration checks;
- the sandboxed contributor target passes: **43 passed** after a CLEAN threat scan.

Two objective blockers remain.

### 1. Root direct and active-request bodies still run outside the shared owner

`api/profiles.py:1215-1217` makes `profile_env_for_background_worker("default")` yield and return before `_PROCESS_ENV_OWNERSHIP_LOCK` is acquired. `profile_env_for_active_request()` does the same for every root/default profile at `:1497-1500`.

Those root bodies can therefore overlap a named direct, active-request, or detached scope while that other scope owns and mutates process environment at `:1332-1340`. A root caller can observe the named profile's raw environment during the overlap, and the named scope can later restore its stale snapshot over a concurrent root-body change. The four new tests do not cover this schedule: where they include root, root is the **detached** entrant, which is already locked by `profile_scope_for_detached_worker()`.

Please route root/default direct and mirrored active-request bodies through the same full-body ownership protocol, with root-owned environment/context setup and exact restoration. Add deterministic direct-root ↔ detached-named and active-root ↔ detached-named tests in both entry orders, using an attempted-entry barrier rather than sleep alone. Re-read the holder after contention and verify conflicting raw/TLS values plus exact success/exception restoration.

### 2. The new production lock graph has a reachable AB/BA deadlock

The new comment declares this order:

`_PROCESS_ENV_OWNERSHIP_LOCK` → `_SKILL_HOME_MODULE_PATCH_LOCK` → `_ENV_LOCK`

The direct background path follows it: it acquires PROCESS at `api/profiles.py:1223` and can wait for SKILL at `:1322`.

The legacy/static streaming fallback does the reverse. It acquires `_SKILL_HOME_MODULE_PATCH_LOCK` at `api/streaming.py:7736`, keeps it for the full turn until `:10985`, and while still holding it enters `profile_scope_for_detached_worker()` at `:8455`, which waits for PROCESS at `api/profiles.py:1552`.

That gives a cross-thread cycle:

- streaming thread: **SKILL → waits for PROCESS**;
- direct background thread: **PROCESS → waits for SKILL**.

An `RLock` prevents same-thread self-deadlock; it does not break this cross-thread cycle.

Please remove every SKILL → PROCESS edge or choose and enforce one global order consistently. Add a forced legacy/static-module regression that composes the real streaming-held SKILL lock and nested detached/model-resolution scope against a direct named background scope, and assert both threads terminate. Audit the direct/background/active/detached and streaming callers for the chosen order.

This remains changes-requested because the first residual preserves the profile-isolation class from the prior gate, while the second is a source-proven deadlock introduced by the repair. No merge or branch mutation was performed by the warm-up lane.

## Re-gate: root ownership converged, but streaming still has two process-environment concurrency blockers

Thanks for the follow-up. I re-gated exact head `58d7d36b499f5d0b37e1b75bcec8091d67cc0427` against the previous request for changes.

The named and root scope work is materially improved:

- direct root and active-request root scopes now hold `_PROCESS_ENV_OWNERSHIP_LOCK` across setup, the full caller body, and restoration;
- the former legacy streaming `SKILL → PROCESS` inversion is now `PROCESS → SKILL → ENV`;
- the five targeted overlap/order tests pass in the enforced networkless sandbox (`5 passed, 43 deselected`).

Two objective blockers remain.

### 1. Make process-environment ownership unconditional in streaming

`_run_agent_streaming()` acquires `_PROCESS_ENV_OWNERSHIP_LOCK` only when a legacy/static skill-module patch is needed (`api/streaming.py:7742-7758`). It nevertheless snapshots and mutates raw `os.environ` unconditionally at `api/streaming.py:7770-7788`, keeps those values installed for the full turn, and restores them at `api/streaming.py:10641-10658`.

In the normal dynamic/nonlegacy branch, a direct profile scope can therefore run concurrently while streaming's raw profile environment is installed. The direct scope can snapshot or overwrite the stream's values, either body can observe the wrong profile, and reverse-order restoration can leave stale values after both scopes exit.

**Must fix:** acquire `_PROCESS_ENV_OWNERSHIP_LOCK` before every streaming raw-environment snapshot/mutation, not only for legacy skill modules. Keep the global order `PROCESS → optional SKILL → ENV`, and release PROCESS only after raw-environment restoration. Add a production-composed dynamic/nonlegacy streaming-versus-direct-profile overlap test that checks raw and TLS owner values plus exact final ambient restoration.

### 2. Remove the new checkpoint `AGENT → PROCESS` / stream `PROCESS → AGENT` deadlock

The legacy branch now holds PROCESS for the full streaming turn (`api/streaming.py:7754-7758`, released only at `11005-11010`). The periodic checkpoint takes `_agent_lock` and then calls `_save_streaming_checkpoint()` (`api/streaming.py:9029-9037`), which enters `profile_env_for_background_worker()` and waits for PROCESS (`api/streaming.py:5472-5482`). The stream owner later joins that checkpoint and then needs `_agent_lock` (`api/streaming.py:9115-9124`, `9160-9166`; the cancel/error/finally paths have the same shape).

Once the checkpoint owns AGENT while waiting for PROCESS, the stream owns PROCESS and waits for AGENT after the bounded join. Neither side can reach the release that would unblock the other.

**Must fix:** remove the checkpoint's `AGENT → PROCESS` edge. A read-only explicit-profile/context-local save scope that does not mirror `os.environ` is one viable design. A lock-order swap alone is not enough if the owner can still join a child that is blocked on an owner-held lock. Add a production-composed test that starts real legacy streaming, forces checkpoint activity, and proves both threads settle without deadlock or late writes on normal, cancel, and exception paths.

The current green lock-order test manually takes the locks and source-checks acquisition order. It does not execute `_run_agent_streaming()`, `_periodic_checkpoint()`, checkpoint joins, or unwind paths, so it cannot detect either remaining schedule.

- `_run_agent_streaming()` holds `_PROCESS_ENV_OWNERSHIP_LOCK` from `api/streaming.py:7764` through settlement, then waits for the per-session agent lock at `api/streaming.py:9202`;

```text
streaming:      PROCESS → waits AGENT
process wakeup: AGENT   → waits PROCESS
```

The process-wakeup path intentionally races active turns and relies on the later start backstop, but credential revalidation currently happens before that backstop while `AGENT` is held. Because this commit makes full-turn `PROCESS` ownership unconditional, the cycle also applies to dynamic/nonlegacy streams.

1. Move named-profile credential revalidation out of the `with _get_session_agent_lock(...)` region in `start_session_turn()`.
2. Revalidate outside `AGENT`, then acquire `AGENT`, re-read the live pause/provider/fingerprint, and apply the result only if that state still matches. Retry outside `AGENT` if it changed. An alternative is a canonical `PROCESS → AGENT` transaction, but it must release `PROCESS` before waiting for any spawned stream worker.
3. Add a production-composed two-thread regression covering a real named-profile `start_session_turn(source="process_wakeup")` contender against real streaming, with barriers rather than sleeps. Cover normal, cancel, and provider-exception settlement, and assert bounded completion plus exact lock/environment cleanup.

## Re-gate: the lock cycle is fixed, but the unlocked revalidation can target the wrong session owner

Thanks for moving credential revalidation out of the AGENT lock. I re-gated exact head `8ae5ce93ed59bd7944686510aa4c207980b0a059` against the prior `d0af839f1f1b` finding.

The prior `AGENT → PROCESS` / `PROCESS → AGENT` deadlock is closed. `start_session_turn()` now performs the named-profile credential lookup before entering AGENT, and retries outside AGENT when the pause dict changes.

One objective owner-handoff blocker remains.

### Must fix

Bind the out-of-lock credential result to the exact current session/profile generation before applying it or starting a run.

`_revalidate_process_wakeup_credential_outside_agent_lock()` currently returns only:

```python
{"pause_state": <dict snapshot>, "recovered": <bool>}
```

After the unlocked wait, `start_session_turn()` selects a lock from the earlier mutable `s.session_id`, reloads `get_session(session_id)`, and accepts the result when only the pause dictionaries compare equal. There is no exact object/SID/profile/home/credential-generation token.

That is unsafe across an owner transition. The production compression path mutates the live `Session.session_id`, preserves the old SID as a read-only pre-compression snapshot, moves `SESSIONS[old]` to `SESSIONS[new]`, and migrates the AGENT lock mapping. A wakeup blocked in the unlocked credential check can therefore resume with:

- a lock chosen from the moved continuation SID,
- `get_session(old_sid)` returning the archived predecessor,
- an equal pause dict that incorrectly authorizes the old-profile result,
- pause clear/suppression/save applied to that stale predecessor,
- and `_start_run()` called after AGENT has been released.

`_start_chat_stream_for_session()` then locks from the passed object's mutable SID but does not re-read the canonical cache owner, so the validation-to-start handoff is also unfenced.

### Required shape

1. Snapshot, under the canonical current owner's AGENT lock, an immutable token containing the requested/current SID, exact owner identity or monotonic generation, profile/home generation, route/model/provider lane, pause version/state, and credential-state generation/fingerprint.
2. Release AGENT and perform the PROCESS-owning credential lookup.
3. Reacquire the canonical current owner's lock and apply the answer only if every token field still matches. On replacement, SID rotation, profile/home change, route/pause movement, or credential-generation movement, retry outside AGENT within the existing bounded budget.
4. Treat compression explicitly: resolve an old SID to its live continuation atomically or fail/requeue. Never clear, suppress, save, or start a turn on `pre_compression_snapshot`.
5. Fence the validation-to-start gap. Either accept the run in the same owner epoch, or pass the token into `_start_run()` / `_start_chat_stream_for_session()` and revalidate the canonical owner before pending-state mutation. Do not reintroduce AGENT → PROCESS.

### Tests

The three new deadlock tests are useful for the original cycle, but they cannot catch this handoff: `get_session` always returns one permanent fake, the fake never rotates its SID or migrates cache/locks, `_start_run` is an append-only stub, and credentials are a profile-independent constant.

Please add deterministic barrier tests for:

- replacement under the same requested SID with an equal pause dict but a different profile/generation,
- compression old-SID → continuation migration while revalidation waits outside AGENT,
- profile/home or credential generation changing before apply,
- owner replacement after validation but before run acceptance.

Each test should assert that no stale object is saved/suppressed/started, no archived pre-compression snapshot is mutated, and no PROCESS acquisition occurs while AGENT is held.

This re-gate is static-only. The trusted threat scanner could not obtain the GitHub diff because

## Re-gate: owner-token fencing improved, but archived-session recovery can still start the wrong conversation

Thanks for the owner-token follow-up. I re-gated exact head `c5f8af610b6887b3f92019adc06265c73e08ed34` against the prior wrong-owner finding.

The earlier AGENT/PROCESS lock cycle is still fixed, and the immutable token now rejects a stale credential answer when an already-correct owner changes. One objective owner-selection defect remains:

Given archived parent A, true compression continuation C, and a newer fork F, wakeup can therefore resolve F as the live owner. The subsequent token checks are internally consistent for F, so they do not catch the initial wrong-owner choice. Credential clear/suppression/start can be attached to the wrong conversation. - `_worker_atomic_owner_claim()` computes a mismatch under the plain AGENT lock, releases it, and only then retires pending state, so it no longer recursively acquires that lock.

The submitted focused tests pass in the mandatory sandbox, but the side-effect ownership contract remains incomplete.

### 1. Replace check-return-call fences with accepted claims

`_worker_sink_owner_fence()` checks the owner under the AGENT lock and returns after releasing it (`api/routes.py:22428-22464`). The direct provider call and Gateway `/v1/runs` POST happen later. A same-SID replacement after the helper returns and before the sink still reaches the provider/network call under stale ownership.

The legacy Gateway `/v1/chat/completions` path has no sink fence at all (`api/gateway_chat.py:908-948`). Runner-local has the same gap between `_claim_runner_owner_fence()` and `adapter.start_run()`.

The new tests replace the owner before these final checks, so the checks catch the replacement. They do not schedule replacement after the check returns and before the actual sink.

Please replace the point-in-time checks with a versioned worker/run claim bound to the exact owner identity, SID, generation, route, and stream/run ID. Install and compare that claim under canonical owner authority, then make replacement/compression invalidate or transfer it before a newer owner can supersede the old one. Do not hold AGENT across network I/O.

Apply the same accepted-claim rule to direct, Gateway runs, legacy Gateway chat completions, and runner-local. For runner-local, a non-empty JSON dictionary is transport, not acceptance: require a complete schema and a real receiver compare-and-accept response before treating the run as started.

### 2. Do not finalize or save the stale owner after a sink refusal

On owner replacement, `_worker_retire_pending_state()` intentionally leaves the noncanonical object's pending fields untouched. The direct worker returns from the refusal branch, but its unconditional outer `finally` still sees `active_stream_id == stream_id` plus `pending_user_message` and calls `_last_resort_sync_from_core()` (`api/streaming.py:11093-11097`). That recovery helper can append rows, clear pending state, and save the stale session.

Add an explicit ownership-loss settlement state so the outer finalizer never repairs or saves a noncanonical owner. Retire provisional state with a versioned owner-generation compare-and-clear. Add a regression that forces sink refusal and proves `_last_resort_sync_from_core()` is not called, the stale object is not mutated/saved, wakeup redelivery remains durable, and current-owner success still works.

### 3. Validate before route-level pending-state mutation

`_start_chat_stream_for_session()` clears stale stream state and consumes pending goal/background markers before `_validate_start_owner_fence()` runs. Move owner-fence validation ahead of every owner/marker mutation. On mismatch, return without changing the stale object.

### Verification

Threat scan was CLEAN, and all execution used `warmup-safe-test.sh` Layer 3:

- owner-claim/sink slices: **4 passed, 58 deselected**
- runner-client file: **7 passed**
- generation/revalidation slices: **4 passed, 58 deselected**

Please add deterministic post-check/pre-sink barriers for direct, Gateway runs, legacy Gateway chat completions, and runner-local, plus stale-finalizer and pre-fence-mutation assertions. The current green tests do not exercise those windows.

## Re-gate: sink claims are still disconnected from owner publication

Thanks for the substantive follow-up. I re-gated exact head `b9bbdb3dee2c` against the prior sink-acceptance findings. The live-owner-first routing, nested-lock cleanup, and explicit direct-refusal finalizer path now converge, but three ownership boundaries remain open.

### Must fix

1. **Couple sink claims to the real owner-publication authority.**

   `_worker_sink_claim_guard()` holds `_WORKER_SINK_CLAIMS_LOCK` across the sink, but production same-SID replacement, deletion, cache refresh, and compression/rotation publication do not acquire that lock or call `_invalidate_owner_sink_claims()` before publishing a new owner. The only production invalidation call is in the post-mismatch retirement path.

   The new test encodes the missing production hook itself:

   ```python
   config.SESSIONS[sid] = replacement
   routes._invalidate_owner_sink_claims(sid)
   ```

   This publishes the replacement before invalidation blocks, so the old sink is already running after canonical ownership changed. Replace this disconnected process-global registry with a per-session generation/lease that every canonical owner publisher participates in before publication. Cover direct, Gateway runs, legacy Gateway, runner-local, and old→new compression migration. Do not hold one global mutex across an LLM/network turn.

2. **Make runner acceptance receiver-authoritative and pre-side-effect.**

   `HttpRunnerClient.start_run()` POSTs `/v1/runs` first, then accepts an `owner_fence` response that matches only `session_id` and `generation`. It does not require `accepted: true`, nonce/version, profile/home, or the complete route. A reflected payload after the POST does not prove the runner compared authority before creating the run or contacting the provider.

   Implement a receiver-side compare-and-accept before any run/provider side effect. Bind the response to the exact nonce/version and complete claim (or a canonical digest), return retryable 409 on mismatch, and make ambiguous post-POST failure idempotently reconcilable rather than asserting that no run started.

3. **Close the validate-unlock-mutate window in `_start_chat_stream_for_session()`.**

   The new owner check runs under `session_lock`, releases it, and then `_clear_stale_stream_state()` and the goal/background marker discards mutate state before the second check. A same-SID replacement in that interval still allows stale cleanup and marker consumption before the later 409.

   Put owner validation, active-stream disposition, marker consumption, and pending-state preparation in one owner-generation transaction. Add a barrier test that replaces the owner after the first validation but before the first mutation, then assert zero stale-object, marker, pending-state, and save changes.

Please also make Gateway refusal/error/finally cleanup compare `{owner identity, generation, stream_id}` rather than re-resolving by SID and stream ID alone, and clear installed claims on every pre-sink exception path.

### Verification note

The mandatory threat scanner could not fetch the exact-head diff because its GitHub REST credential returned HTTP 403 rate-limit, so policy required a static-only review. No PR code or tests were executed. The findings above come from exact-head control-flow and test-oracle inspection; the next re-gate still needs a successful threat scan and sandboxed targeted tests.

It also introduces `_root_profile_worker_env_scope` to scrub named-profile credentials from `os.environ` during a root-profile detached worker, and `profile_env_for_background_worker_readonly` for lock-free checkpoint threads. - **TLS fix for default profile**: `profile_scope_for_detached_worker` no longer skips `set_request_profile` for root/default names; all non-empty names now bind TLS, preventing fall-through to the process-wide `_active_profile`. - **Owner-fence protocol**: `_run_gateway_chat_streaming`, `_start_chat_stream_for_session`, and the runner client each install a compare-and-accept claim that prevents a same-SID replacement from reaching the network sink; `_build_browser_start_owner_token` fills the gap that previously made every browser runner-local start deterministically 409 before contacting the runner. - **Lease-coupled publication**: cold loads, cache refreshes, deletions, and evictions now route through `_publish_owner_publication_lease` / `_publish_owner_removal_lease` so the per-SID owner-generation lease is held across the exact `SESSIONS` write.

### Changes (`api/profiles.py`)

`api/profiles.py`:

The root branch now acquires `_PROCESS_ENV_OWNERSHIP_LOCK` for the complete body (setup, caller yield, restoration) and runs `_root_profile_worker_env_scope()` — the same protocol the detached wrapper uses: root-owned thread/context credentials installed before process fallback is blocked, raw `os.getenv()` scrubbed of values proven foreign to root (`_loaded_profile_env_owner`), and exact restoration on success and exception. The guard was widened from `profile == "default"` to `_is_root_profile(profile)` so root aliases (isolated-mode pinned names) get the same treatment.
- `profile_env_for_active_request()` now routes the root/default branch through that same wrapper instead of yielding lock-free, so a mirrored root body can never overlap a named direct/active/detached scope mid-mutation.

New deterministic tests (attempted-entry barrier via a recording lock proxy — the blocked thread's real `acquire()` call is observed, no sleeps):

- `test_background_worker_direct_root_overlap_detached_named_direct_first` — direct root enters first; detached named is blocked until release; conflicting raw (scrubbed) vs TLS (root) values; exact restoration.
- `test_background_worker_direct_root_overlap_detached_named_detached_first` — detached named enters first; direct root blocked.

Each re-reads the holder after contention and asserts owner-correct raw/TLS values plus exact pre-test env restoration.

`api/streaming.py`: the legacy/static full-turn block (`_SKILL_HOME_MODULE_PATCH_LOCK` held from turn setup to teardown) now acquires `_PROCESS_ENV_OWNERSHIP_LOCK` **before** the skill-module patch lock and releases it after, enforcing the single global order `PROCESS → SKILL → ENV` across every process-env-mirroring entrypoint. The mid-turn `profile_scope_for_detached_worker()` re-entry (model resolution) is then an RLock re-acquire on the same thread, and a direct background scope holding PROCESS while waiting for SKILL can no longer form a cross-thread AB/BA cycle with a streaming turn. Thanks for the thorough re-gate, @nesquena-hermes! Addressed the cross-module AB/BA cycle in `8ae5ce93`.

**1. Credential revalidation moved out of the AGENT lock — FIXED**

`start_session_turn()` no longer performs the named-profile credential revalidation inside `with _get_session_agent_lock(...)`. The flow is now:

1. **Preflight (outside AGENT):** when `source == "process_wakeup"` and the session's wakeup pause matches the resolved model/provider lane, the recovery-credential revalidation runs *before* AGENT is acquired. For a named profile this still enters `profile_scope_for_detached_worker()`, so it takes `_PROCESS_ENV_OWNERSHIP_LOCK` (PROCESS) with no AGENT held. The helper (`_revalidate_process_wakeup_credential_outside_agent_lock`) returns the pause snapshot it targeted plus the recovery outcome.
2. **Apply (under AGENT):** acquire AGENT, re-read the live session, re-check the pause lane and credential fingerprint, and apply the revalidation result **only when the live pause state still matches the snapshot** the revalidation targeted. `clear_process_wakeup_pause_if_model_changed`, `process_wakeup_pause_credential_state_changed`, and `suppress_process_wakeup_for_provider_pause` still run under AGENT exactly as before.
3. **Retry (bounded, outside AGENT):** if the live pause/lane/fingerprint moved while we revalidated (or the pause appeared after the preflight), the loop drops AGENT, re-runs the revalidation outside it, and re-enters. The budget is `_PROCESS_WAKEUP_REVALIDATION_MAX_RETRIES = 3`; after exhaustion the pause is treated as not recovered and the next drain cycle revalidates — no unbounded spin against a concurrent writer.

This removes the `AGENT → PROCESS` edge entirely: the wakeup thread now waits on the streaming turn's PROCESS ownership *before* taking AGENT, so the cycle (`streaming: PROCESS → AGENT`, `wakeup: AGENT → PROCESS`) is unreachable on both the legacy/static and the dynamic/nonlegacy branch.

**2. Production-composed two-thread regression — ADDED**

Three tests in `tests/test_issue3957_profile_providers_models.py` drive a **real** named-profile `start_session_turn(source="process_wakeup")` contender against a **real** `_run_agent_streaming()` turn on the dynamic/nonlegacy branch (unconditional full-turn PROCESS ownership), with barrier events rather than sleeps:

- `test_process_wakeup_revalidation_outside_agent_lock_normal` — normal settlement, credential recovered → pause cleared + run started.
- `test_process_wakeup_revalidation_outside_agent_lock_cancel` — cancel settlement, credential not recovered → 409 suppressed wakeup + suppression metadata recorded.
- `test_process_wakeup_revalidation_outside_agent_lock_exception` — provider-exception settlement, not recovered → 409.

Each asserts, mid-flight, that while the contender is **blocked on PROCESS** (recording-proxy barrier) the per-session **AGENT lock is still acquirable** — the deterministic AB/BA detector — plus bounded completion of both threads, no leaked ownership lock, and exact ambient-env restoration.

**Red-green evidence:** with only `api/routes.py` reverted to the previous head, all three fail with `AssertionError: wakeup contender held AGENT while blocked on PROCESS (AB/BA cycle)`; with the fix they pass. Full file: `54 passed`; adjacent profile/streaming files: `65 passed, 2 skipped`.

**Preserved as requested:** the unconditional streaming PROCESS owner, the read-only checkpoint scope, and the outer-finally release are untouched (no changes outside `api/routes.py` and its test file).

Happy to iterate if anything needs tightening!

## Immutable owner token: production shape (ba2daf52) + deterministic barrier tests (c5f8af61)

Addressing the review request for deterministic barrier coverage of the #6327 revalidation fence. Production was already in place as `ba2daf52`; this commit adds the 4 missing tests.

### What the immutable token does (ba2daf52, 5 points)

1. **`_build_immutable_session_owner_token`** — under the canonical current owner's AGENT lock, snapshots an immutable token: requested/current SID, exact owner identity, profile + home generation, model/provider lane, pause state/version, and credential-state fingerprint.
2. **`_revalidate_process_wakeup_credential_outside_agent_lock`** — the PROCESS-owning credential lookup runs OUTSIDE AGENT (fixes the AB/BA: streaming PROCESS→AGENT vs wakeup AGENT→PROCESS). Result is bound to the token, not to the mutable session.
3. **`_apply_process_wakeup_revalidation_once`** — re-acquires the canonical owner's AGENT lock and applies the answer ONLY when every token field still matches; on replacement / SID rotation / profile-home / pause / credential-generation movement it returns `retry` and the caller re-runs outside AGENT (bounded budget, `_PROCESS_WAKEUP_REVALIDATION_MAX_RETRIES = 3`).
4. **`_resolve_live_session_owner`** — resolves the canonical LIVE owner, following pre-compression continuations atomically (bounded + profile-matched) and never mutating an archived `pre_compression_snapshot`.
5. **`_validate_start_owner_fence`** — the validation-to-start fence inside `_start_chat_stream_for_session`: before touching pending state or starting a run, re-verifies the lock entry, canonical cache identity, and every token field under the held AGENT lock; on movement returns the retryable 409 `owner_fence` response.

### New deterministic barrier tests (c5f8af61)

All four drive the REAL token pipeline against a concurrent writer (Event-synchronized threads, no sleeps) and assert the stale answer is never applied/saved/suppressed/started, plus the no-PROCESS-while-AGENT invariant via the recording ownership-lock proxy:

Thanks for the review. ### 1. Accepted-claim rule replaces check-return-call fences (`api/routes.py`, `api/streaming.py`, `api/gateway_chat.py`)

- Removed `_worker_sink_owner_fence` (the re-verify → return → call pattern). `_worker_atomic_owner_claim()` now installs a **versioned sink claim** bound to the exact owner identity, SID, credential-state generation, route lane, and stream/run ID under the canonical per-session AGENT lock.
- `_worker_sink_claim_guard()` / `_worker_sink_accept_call()` compare-and-accept that claim under the same canonical authority immediately before the sink and **hold the claim lock across the actual provider/network call** (never AGENT across I/O). A replacement/compression that invalidates claims can therefore never interleave between acceptance and the sink; `_invalidate_owner_sink_claims()` serializes behind an in-flight sink.
- Applied to all four backends: direct worker (`agent.run_conversation`), Gateway runs (`/v1/runs` POST via `_run_gateway_runs_api_streaming`), the previously-unfenced **legacy Gateway `/v1/chat/completions`** path (claim accepted across the `urlopen` POST), and runner-local.

### 2. Ownership-loss settlement (`api/streaming.py`)

- Added an explicit `_ownership_loss_settled` state set on every owner refusal (worker-start claim refusal and sink refusal). The outer `finally` now **never calls `_last_resort_sync_from_core()` for a non-canonical owner** — the stale object is neither repaired nor saved.
- `_worker_retire_pending_state()` performs a **versioned owner-generation compare-and-clear**: the provisional sidecar is retired only when the canonical cache still maps the tokenized owner AND `_process_wakeup_owner_token_mismatch()` still passes (identity + SID + profile/home + credential fingerprint + route lane). Wakeup redelivery and stream-owner cleanup remain unconditional.

### 3. Validate before pending-state mutation (`api/routes.py`)

- `_start_chat_stream_for_session()` now runs `_validate_start_owner_fence()` **before** clearing stale stream state or consuming the pending goal/background markers; on mismatch it returns the retryable 409 with the stale object completely untouched (no cleanup, no marker consumption, no pending write, no save). ## Review 16 re-gate: both blockers fixed

### 1. Browser runner-local starts now carry the canonical per-session owner fence

`_start_run()` now establishes the owner authority for ordinary browser starts: when the selected adapter is `RunnerRuntimeAdapter` and no `owner_token` was passed (the process-wakeup drain path is the only caller that builds one), it builds one via the new `_build_browser_start_owner_token()` — under the canonical per-session AGENT lock, for exactly the route lane the caller resolved (never predecessor-derived routing, so the request/fence lane cross-bind stays exact) — then `_claim_runner_owner_fence()` mints the complete generation/route claim (SID + profile/home + generation + route lane + per-run version + per-session lease) that the real `HttpRunnerClient` compare-and-accepts. The receiver-authoritative schema in `api/runner_client.py` is untouched. A token-build failure (owner replaced / lock migrated / unreadable credential fingerprint) surfaces a retryable 409 — an unowned run is never acknowledged.

**Production-path test** (`tests/test_6327_browser_runner_local_fence.py`): drives browser `_handle_chat_start()` with `HERMES_WEBUI_RUNTIME_ADAPTER=runner-local` end-to-end through the REAL `HttpRunnerClient.start_run()` (fence schema validation, request/fence lane cross-bind, POST construction, receiver compare-and-accept) — only the HTTP transport is faked via the same `_opener` seam as `tests/test_runner_client.py`. Asserts the run is ACCEPTED (200 + stream id, no error), the POST reached `/v1/runs`, and the claimed fence is complete (`_runner_owner_fence_schema_error` is None, generation/route/version/lease present, root profile canonicalized to `default`).

### 2. `_resolve_session()` publication transaction is now complete (3 races closed)

- **Refresh CAS** (`_cached_session_lags_disk` and `_inactive_cache_tail_needs_disk_check` sites): the refresh still performs disk I/O outside the authority, but the publication now runs through a new compare-and-swap lease primitive — `_publish_owner_lease_if_current()` (routes) / `_publish_owner_publication_lease(..., expected=...)` (models) — which bumps the per-SID lease and writes ONLY while the refreshed-from owner is still canonical. A newer owner installed during the I/O is never overwritten, its lease is never bumped by the stale publisher, and it is returned.
- **Cold-load return identity**: when the cold-load publication CAS loses to a concurrent canonical winner, `_resolve_session` now RETURNS the winner (never the discarded loaded object).
- **Cold-load vs delete**: cold load captures the deletion authority (durable webui delete tombstone + per-SID owner-generation lease) BEFORE `Session.load()`, and the publication CAS refuses to install if the authority moved during the load (tombstone re-checked under the lease) — a concurrent deletion can no longer be followed by stale resurrection (`KeyError` instead). The delete route also now records the sidecar unlink + durable tombstone INSIDE the per-SID lease section, so any publisher that acquires the lease afterwards observes the deletion.

**Deterministic tests** (added to `tests/test_6327_lease_coupled_publication.py`, Event-barrier, no sleeps): refresh-vs-replacement (asserts winner kept AND returned AND lease not bumped), cold-load-vs-delete (asserts no cache entry + `KeyError`), returned-canonical-identity.

- `test_6327_lease_coupled_publication.py` + `test_6327_browser_runner_local_fence.py`: 9 passed (3.88s)
- `test_issue3957_profile_providers_models.py` (incl. `test_process_wakeup_revalidation_outside_agent_lock_normal` and `test_start_chat_stream_fence_before_pending_mutation`): 67 passed (5.68s)

The fallback lookup, persist, and cleanup steps are all correctly guarded by the `_stream_id===streamId` identity check, preventing stale registries from being reused across streams. Two minor style observations: operator precedence on the fallback read line could benefit from explicit parentheses, and the stream-ID transition block leaves a transient stale `_liveAnchorRegistry` in INFLIGHT that is harmless but slightly inconsistent. static/messages.js — specifically the stream-ID transition block around line 2044 and the INFLIGHT fallback read at line 2631.

Greptile Summary

 This PR fixes two related bugs that surface when a terminal error interrupts an agent stream: the turn duration was being computed after `pending_started_at` was cleared (yielding 0), and in-flight tool calls were left with `done: False` in the persisted partial snapshot, disagreeing with the settled error state. - **Duration freeze**: `_turn_duration_seconds` is now captured from `pending_started_at` before the three error cleanup call sites clear it, and the result is stored as `_turnDuration` on the error message dict. - **Tool call sealing**: `_snapshot_and_append_partial_on_error` mutates each not-yet-done tool call entry to `done: True` / `_sealed_by_terminal_error: True` before building the partial message, with the test updated to assert the new shape. - The fix is applied consistently across the in-stream handler, the outer `except Exception` handler in `_run_agent_streaming`, and the gateway-side `_settle_gateway_terminal_error`.

Confidence Score: 4/5

 The fix is targeted and correct across all three error call sites; the only noteworthy code smell is that the tool-call sealing mutates live buffer dicts through a shallow copy, which is harmless during teardown but could surprise future readers or concurrent SSE flushes. Both the duration-freeze and the tool-call sealing logic are straightforward and applied consistently. The shallow-copy mutation is a minor structural issue rather than a correctness failure on the current teardown path. The test gap (no assertion on `_turnDuration`) leaves the timing half of the fix unverified by tests. api/streaming.py around _snapshot_and_append_partial_on_error — the shallow-copy mutation pattern deserves a second look if that function ever gets called outside a teardown context.

payload.body:
## Summary

Reading the full PR versions of `api/gateway_chat.py`, `api/streaming.py`, and `tests/test_webui_gateway_chat_backend.py`, plus the unchanged rendering path on `origin/master`, the duration persistence is placed on the right partial assistant message. The tool-call sealing has a presentation bug, though: it marks an interrupted tool as done without marking it as an error, and the new private marker has no frontend consumer. The restored tool card can therefore look successfully completed rather than terminated by the stream error.

## Code reference

The new sealing logic at `api/streaming.py:6450-6456` is:

```python
for _tc in _snap_tool_calls:
    if isinstance(_tc, dict) and not _tc.get("done"):
        _tc["done"] = True
        _tc["_sealed_by_terminal_error"] = True
```

The settled renderer decides error state at `static/messages.js:3013` only from `tool.is_error` or `tool.error`. There are no references to `_sealed_by_terminal_error` anywhere under `api/`, `static/`, or `tests/` on `origin/master`, and this PR does not modify the frontend. As a result, `done: true` stops the spinner but the error styling/status remains false.

The added assertion at `tests/test_webui_gateway_chat_backend.py:618-624` locks in that incomplete shape: it expects `done: True` and `_sealed_by_terminal_error: True`, but does not require `is_error: True`. The same test also does not assert the newly added `_turnDuration` from `api/gateway_chat.py:592-597`, so the second half of the behavior change is not protected by the regression test.

## Recommendation

When terminal error sealing changes an unfinished tool call, also set `is_error` to true, or teach every historical-tool rendering path to interpret `_sealed_by_terminal_error` as an error. Setting the established public field is the smaller and safer change because live and historical rendering already consume it. Preserve an existing explicit `is_error` value for tool calls that were complete before the terminal failure.

## Test plan

Extend the gateway regression to assert all three properties on the persisted partial tool call: `done` is true, `is_error` is true, and `_turnDuration` is present and non-negative. Add the same assertions for the non-gateway error snapshot path around `api/streaming.py:9448-9470`, then verify reload rendering produces an error-state card rather than a success-state card. I did not execute code from the PR worktree; this finding comes from read-only source and test inspection.

## 🔴 Exact-head re-gate: lifecycle ownership and dedup bookkeeping remain incomplete

**Reviewed head:** `f5b54ab26e0802c1f1f71a56a03acdc10a2de73a`

This follow-up closes two items from the previous RED: it restores adjacent replay-pollution collapse, and the undefined `_strip_base64_data_urls` path is gone. The core lifecycle rework still has two deterministic blockers in `_deduplicate_context_messages`.

### 1. Anchor-owning settled rows do not supersede plain settled copies

At `api/streaming.py:4699-4725`, ownership replacement only happens when `_is_lifecycle_unsettled()` differs. A plain settled row and a settled row with `_anchor_stream_id` / `_anchor_activity_scene` are both classified as settled. Their lifecycle keys differ, so none of the adjacent collapse/replacement branches fires. Even with the same stable message ID, both copies survive instead of retaining the anchor-owning final.

Sandboxed fail-first probe:

```python
plain = {"role": "assistant", "content": "Hello", "id": 50}
anchored = {
    "role": "assistant", "content": "Hello", "id": 50,
    "_anchor_stream_id": "stream-a",
    "_anchor_activity_scene": {"stream_id": "stream-a"},
```

Current result contains both rows.

### 2. Partial→settled replacement can reinsert an already-seen stable key

At `api/streaming.py:4716-4725`, the replacement path discards only the displaced partial key, overwrites `deduped[-1]`, adds the settled key, and immediately continues. It never checks whether that settled key is already in `seen`.

## 🔴 Authoritative gate certificate — RED (correct #6310 fix, but it removes a self-healing dedup backstop and re-admits two pollution classes)

**Exact contributor head:** `82b0e762c4cf0c64e537ae2830c73f37b1aaf58f`

I transplanted this exact patch onto current master (`api/streaming.py` +25, tests +79/-6) and gated it on the crown-jewel context path. The core #6310 fix is correct and well-guarded, but converting the *final* context dedup from content-only to id-gated removes a backstop and provably re-admits duplicate pollution.

### The #6310 fix itself — verified correct

`_context_message_dedup_key` prepends a valid stable `id` to the content key so distinct turns with identical text are preserved; falls back to content-only when no id. I confirmed all the guards:
- distinct same-content turns with distinct ids → both preserved
- genuine same-id duplicate → removed
- no-id → content-only dedup still works
- `bool` id not mistaken for int (`isinstance(True, int)` trap guarded)
- negative id rejected → falls back
- compression/reference-marker carve-outs unchanged

### Reproduced blocking regressions

`_deduplicate_context_messages` is the every-turn **backstop** (master dedups by content-only identity, self-healing). Making it id-gated breaks two protections. I reproduced both directly against the rebased code:

```text
SHAPE1 adjacent_dup_distinct_ids -> kept 2   (master keeps 1) = REGRESSION
SHAPE3 idful_then_idless_dup     -> kept 2   (master keeps 1) = REGRESSION
```

- **Shape 1 — accidental adjacent duplicates with distinct minted ids no longer collapse.** Two identical assistant rows that each got a fresh id are both admitted, re-opening the #2620/#2705 pollution class, and permanently (once an id is minted the duplicate is locked in).
- **Shape 3 — an id-bearing row followed by an id-less content-duplicate is re-admitted.** The id-aware key `(10, …)` ≠ the id-less key `(None, …)`, so the id-less duplicate survives.

**Shape 3 is production-reachable, not theoretical.** The call site at `api/streaming.py:8803` dedups `_previous_context_messages` — merged from `context_messages` + `state.db` — with NO preceding `_assign_stable_message_ids`, and its own comment says the merge "can produce duplicates when context_messages and state.db share messages with different timestamps." Those merged rows routinely have missing/mismatched ids for the same logical turn, so the id-aware key fails to collapse exactly the duplicates this call site exists to remove.

### Gate results

- threat scan: CLEAN; current-master transplant clean
- focused `test_context_message_dedup.py`: 16 passed
- full current-master suite: **13,360 passed, 82 skipped, 1 xfailed, 2 xpassed; 14 known environment/baseline failures**
- Codex: SAFE TO SHIP — but it verified only the happy paths (distinct/same/invalid id); it did not probe adjacent-duplicate or idful-then-idless shapes
- Fable/Opus: **RED** — reproduced both regressions; classified Shape 1 & 3 as fixable (not inherent) and only non-adjacent replay-echo under-dedup as the irreducible dual of #6310
- my own probes: reproduced both shapes and confirmed the 8803 call-site reachability

Reproduced production-reachable regressions override the Codex happy-path pass.
