payload.title: fix: include terminal backend identity in agent cache signature (#5937)

payload.author: greptile-apps
payload.body:
Greptile Summary

 This PR fixes a stale-agent cache bug where an `AIAgent` constructed for an SSH terminal backend was incorrectly reused for a local session (and vice versa) because the cache signature did not include terminal backend identity. The fix appends `TERMINAL_ENV`, `TERMINAL_SSH_HOST`, and `TERMINAL_SSH_USER` to the `json.dumps` signature blob so that switching backends forces a cache miss. - The three new fields correctly differentiate local-vs-SSH and per-host SSH sessions, closing the originally reported scenario. - Container-based backends (Docker, Singularity, Modal, Daytona) share the same gap: when two profiles both use `TERMINAL_ENV=docker` but specify different images, their signatures are identical, and the cached agent from the first profile is reused for the second \u2014 the exact stale-backend problem this PR is fixing.

Confidence Score: 4/5

 The SSH-to-local stale-agent bug is correctly fixed, but the same gap remains for container-based backends when two profiles share the same backend type but use different images. The three new signature fields close the reported scenario cleanly. However, Docker, Singularity, Modal, and Daytona profiles that differ only in image or docker_env will still collide on the cache signature, reproducing the original stale-environment problem for container users. api/streaming.py — specifically the signature blob construction around lines 8333–8335, where container backend image fields are still absent.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | api/streaming.py | Adds TERMINAL_ENV, TERMINAL_SSH_HOST, TERMINAL_SSH_USER to the agent cache signature to prevent stale SSH backend reuse, but omits container image fields (TERMINAL_DOCKER_IMAGE, TERMINAL_SINGULARITY_IMAGE, etc.) that are also part of terminal backend identity. |
Reviews (2): Last reviewed commit: ["fix: include terminal backend identity i..."](https://github.com/nesquena/hermes-webui/commit/d22c478d259babc7a7d137e25ae2dff57f24e24b) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=44929375)

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Reading the diff at `api/streaming.py:8305-8314` against `origin/master`, plus `api/profiles.py:762-787` (`_TERMINAL_ENV_MAPPINGS`) and the gateway-parity filter at `api/profiles.py:873-885`, the direction here is right but the field list is narrower than backend identity actually requires.

## What the PR does

```python
_profile_home or '',
# Terminal backend identity ... (#5937)
_safe_profile_runtime_env.get('TERMINAL_ENV', '') or '',
_safe_profile_runtime_env.get('TERMINAL_SSH_HOST', '') or '',
_safe_profile_runtime_env.get('TERMINAL_SSH_USER', '') or '',
```

This closes the reported SSH↔local case, which is the primary symptom in #5937. Good.

## The gap

The agent's SSH endpoint identity is host + user + **port** + **key**, not just host + user. On the agent side `hermes_cli/config.py:293` lists `TERMINAL_SSH_KEY`/`TERMINAL_SSH_PORT` as consumed runtime vars, and `gateway/run.py:1574-1577` bridges all four (`ssh_host`, `ssh_user`, `ssh_port`, `ssh_key`) into the runtime env that the terminal backend connects with. So two SSH profiles that share host+user but differ by port or key still produce an identical signature and collide in `SESSION_AGENT_CACHE` — the exact class of stale-backend bug this PR is closing. Greptile flagged the port/key omission; that part is real.

Beyond SSH there's a wider hole: switching between two container backends (e.g. `TERMINAL_DOCKER_IMAGE`, `TERMINAL_MODAL_IMAGE`, `TERMINAL_CWD`) also changes where tools execute, and none of those are in the signature either (`_TERMINAL_ENV_MAPPINGS` has ~25 keys).

## Recommendation

Rather than enumerate individual keys (which will drift as new backends are added — the mapping already outgrew this PR's three fields), fold **all** `TERMINAL_*` keys from `_safe_profile_runtime_env` into the signature as one sorted sub-blob. The gateway-parity filter at `api/profiles.py:873` only strips `HOME/PATH/XDG_*`-class shell-identity vars, so every `TERMINAL_*` key survives into `_safe_profile_runtime_env` and is safe to hash:

```python
_profile_home or '',
# Terminal backend identity: any TERMINAL_* change (backend, SSH
# host/user/port/key, container image, cwd) must miss the cache so the
# fresh agent connects to the correct backend (#5937).
sorted(
    (k, v) for k, v in _safe_profile_runtime_env.items()
    if k.startswith('TERMINAL_')
),
```

`_json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True)` already normalizes ordering, and the tuple list is deterministic given the sort. This is one line of behavior instead of a hand-maintained allowlist, and it can't silently miss a future backend field.

## Test plan

Worth adding a regression test asserting `_agent_sig` differs across: (a) local vs SSH, (b) same SSH host+user with different `TERMINAL_SSH_PORT`, and (c) two distinct `TERMINAL_DOCKER_IMAGE` values. The current PR adds no test, so the port/key collision would go unnoticed on the next refactor. I did not execute anything from the branch — this is a read-only review of the diff and the agent-side contract.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## 🔬 Gate certification — RED ⛔ (full gate at head `d22c478d259b`)

**Certified head:** `d22c478d259babc7a7d137e25ae2dff57f24e24b` (clean-rebased onto `origin/master`; cumulative patch-id byte-identical before/after rebase, `2496fb2939c4`)
**Verdict:** The signature addition is **correct, regression-free defense-in-depth** — but the full gate reproduces that it **does not actually fix #5937**: the stale terminal backend lives in a *separate* process-global cache that a fresh agent never evicts. Extending the agent-cache signature is the wrong layer for the reachable bug.

Builds on (doesn't repeat) the 2026-07-16 maintainer review's field-list finding; adds the deeper reproduced root cause + formal gate label/record.

### What I ran
- **Codex** (reproduce): `SAFE TO SHIP` — "no regression introduced by these six lines"; independently noted SSH port/key + container isolation stay outside the patch so **#5937 is only partially addressed** (pre-existing, not a regression).
- **Opus review**: `REQUEST_CHANGES` (blocking) — the change doesn't fix #5937; the stale backend lives in the agent's process-global `_active_environments["default"]`.
- **My own runtime reproduction** (against the real `tools.terminal_tool` module): confirmed below.
- **Full pytest suite** to completion: `13356 passed, 14 failed` — all 14 reproduce on the clean-`origin/master` control (playwright-not-installed, git-check-ignore under detached worktree, test_issue609 monkeypatch, keyless isolation flake); **none touch `api/streaming.py`, none introduced by this diff.** Targeted `test_issue1897_profile_switch_agent_cache.py` + `test_streaming_agent_cache_lifecycle.py`: 9/9. Ruff-forward / scope_undef / py_compile CLEAN.

### The signature change is correct as far as it goes (verified)
Reproduced: local↔SSH, SSH-host change, and SSH-user change all produce a different `_agent_sig` → cache miss → fresh agent; unrelated config is stable (no spurious busting); the `TERMINAL_*` keys survive `filter_runtime_env_for_gateway_parity` (not a silent no-op); empty-config path is stable. ✅

### Reproduced blocker (RED) — wrong layer
`api/streaming.py` only rebuilds the **`AIAgent`**. But the terminal backend a session executes on is resolved by `tools/terminal_tool.py` from a *module-global* `_active_environments` dict, keyed on `task_id` — and the top-level WebUI agent collapses to `task_id="default"` (`_resolve_container_task_id`, terminal_tool.py:1207). The reuse check (terminal_tool.py:2246-2253) keys on **presence only, with no `env_type` comparison**, and the only eviction of `["default"]` is the idle-timeout sweep (line 1659) — never on a backend-identity change. A fresh `AIAgent` never touches that dict.

Reproduced against the real agent module:
```
session A (SSH) → _active_environments["default"] = ssh env
session B (local, same process, FRESH AIAgent via #6175's new _agent_sig)
  → _resolve_container_task_id(None) = "default"
  → reused_env.env_type = "ssh"   ⛔ local session executes on the stale SSH backend
```
This is exactly #5937's reachable case ("a local-backend profile session can execute shell/file tools on a remote host previously used by another profile"). Issue #5937 names the mechanism explicitly: "Hermes Agent's collapsed `default` terminal environment cache … WebUI still needs isolation/invalidation so profile switches cannot inherit another profile's backend." The signature change never touches it.

### Recommendation to the next agent
**Do not merge as the fix for #5937.** `gate-fail` at `sha:d22c478d259b`. The six-line signature addition is safe, regression-free, and worth keeping as **defense-in-depth**, but on its own it leaves the reachable backend-reuse bug open. The durable fix is WebUI-side isolation/invalidation of the terminal env on backend-identity change — call `cleanup_vm("default")` (exists at `tools/terminal_tool.py:1788`) when the resolved terminal backend identity changes for a session, and/or register a backend-identity task-env

payload.author: greptile-apps
payload.body:
Greptile Summary

 This PR fixes broken media in public share pages by scanning messages for `MEDIA:` and `file://` references and embedding small files (≤512 KB) as base64 data URIs at share-creation time, removing the need for authenticated `/api/media` calls at view time. - `_embed_share_media` is inserted into the `_sanitize_message` pipeline between credential redaction and path redaction; images become `` tags and other files become data-URI download links. - The regex `_SHARE_MEDIA_RE` handles both `MEDIA:` and `file://` forms and excludes external `MEDIA:https?://…` references.

Confidence Score: 1/5

 Not safe to merge: the new file-embedding code introduces multiple security vulnerabilities in the public share boundary. The new _embed_share_media function reads arbitrary filesystem paths into public share snapshots without a path allowlist, inserts raw filenames into HTML without escaping, and feeds unredacted file bytes past the credential-sanitization step that protects all other share content. api/shares.py — the entire _embed_share_media function and its integration into _sanitize_message.

Security Review

 - **Unrestricted local file read / path traversal** (`api/shares.py` line ~152): any path in a `MEDIA:` or `file://` reference is read and embedded as a base64 data URI in the publicly accessible share. (Flagged in prior review thread.) - **XSS via unescaped filename in HTML attributes** (`api/shares.py` lines ~179, 188): `p.name` is interpolated raw into HTML attributes without escaping. (Flagged in prior review thread.) - **Credential redaction bypass for embedded file contents** (`api/shares.py` lines ~174-190): raw bytes from disk are never credential-scanned before being base64-encoded into the share snapshot.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | api/shares.py | Adds _embed_share_media to inline local MEDIA:/file:// references as base64 data URIs; has unrestricted file-read (path traversal), XSS via unescaped filename, whitespace-eating regex, and credential redaction bypass for embedded file contents. |
Reviews (2): Last reviewed commit: ["fix: embed local media as base64 in publ..."](https://github.com/nesquena/hermes-webui/commit/d5b5d7276b67a258b467695146fe0b0aa90e4d5e) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=44929142)

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body: Read the full diff at `api/shares.py:115-192` against `origin/master`, plus the existing `/api/media` handler it's replacing (`api/routes.py:18544-18808`) and the client render path (`static/share.js:34`, `static/ui.js:7182-7194`). Greptile's two findings are both real, and the first is a **critical unauthenticated arbitrary-file-read** — I'd hold this PR until it's fixed. ## 1. Arbitrary file read on the public boundary (critical) `_embed_share_media` reads any path that resolves to a file, with no allowlist and no deny-list: ```python p = Path(raw).resolve(strict=False) if not p.is_file(): return "[*Local attachment omitted from public share*]" size = p.stat().st_size ... data = p.read_bytes() b64 = base64.b64encode(data).decode("ascii") ``` Compare the authenticated endpoint this replaces. `_handle_media` restricts reads to an allowlist (`api/routes.py:18601-18604`: hermes home, `/tmp`, active workspace — "Intentionally NOT the entire home dir — that would expose ~/.ssh, ~/.aws...") **and** applies the #3234 hard-deny for state/secret basenames (`api/routes.py:18654-18660`: `.env`, `auth.json`, `.signing_key`, `state.db`, `settings.json`, ...) **and** is auth-gated. `_embed_share_media` has none of those, and it runs on the *unauthenticated* share snapshot. Because it executes before `_redact_share_paths` (by design, per the comment), a `MEDIA:` reference in an agent message — which is attacker-influenceable via prompt injection into tool/model output that the snapshot captures — like `MEDIA:~/.hermes/auth.json` gets base64-embedded into a world-readable `/share/` page. The 512 KiB cap does not save you: `.env`, `auth.json`, `.signing_key`, `.pbkdf2_key`, and private SSH keys are all well under it. ## 2. Stored XSS via unescaped filename ```python name = p.name return f'' ... return f'{name}' ``` `p.name` is interpolated raw into `alt`/`download`/anchor text. On the client, `renderMd` stashes and restores ``/`` verbatim (`static/ui.js:7182`) and the `SAFE_INLINE` guard at `ui.js:7194` lets `img`/`a` tags through **without attribute sanitization**. A filename containing `"` (e.g. `x" onerror="…`) breaks out of the attribute. Lower severity than #1 since it needs a crafted on-disk filename, but it's a stored XSS on a public page. ## Recommendation - Before reading, require `target` to pass the **same** allowlist + #3234 deny-list as `_handle_media`. That validation is currently inline in `routes.py:18596-18808`; extract it into a shared helper (e.g. `_media_path_is_publicly_serveable(target) -> bool`) and call it from both places so the share path can't drift from the authenticated one. For the public boundary I'd tighten further to workspace + `/tmp` only (drop the whole-hermes-home carve-out). - `html.escape(p.name, quote=True)` before interpolating into any attribute or text node. - Consider capping total embedded bytes per snapshot, not just per-file — N references × 512 KiB × 1.33 base64 overhead can bloat a snapshot substantially. I did not execute anything from the branch; this is a read-only review of the diff against the current handler contract. Happy to re-review once the allowlist/deny-list reuse is in.

This bypasses the authenticated `/api/media?path=&session_id=` authorization the design relies on. Messaging-gateway (telegram/discord) sessions are shareable, so a **remote** party injecting `MEDIA:/home/…/.hermes/` or `file:///etc/passwd` gets that file published when the operator shares. **Reproduced:** a secret file referenced via `MEDIA:` → its bytes appear base64-encoded in the sanitized snapshot as ``. **2. [SECURITY] Embedded bytes bypass credential + path redaction.** Order in `_sanitize_message` (`:206-211`): `_force_redact_credentials(text)` → `_embed_share_media(text)` → `_redact_share_paths(text)`. The feature does not achieve its goal even setting the security aside — no reviewer had checked this end-to-end before. **4. I could not weaponize a clean `alt=`-breakout because the capture regex `[^\s\)\]>]+` truncates the path at whitespace/`)`/`>` (the chars a handler needs), so I'm rating this an unescaped-output hardening defect rather than a confirmed live exploit — but it must be escaped regardless. ### Minor No aggregate per-snapshot byte cap (N refs × 512KiB × 1.33 base64 → multi-MB anonymous snapshot); the `file://` regex captures leading whitespace so words run together on replacement; placeholder `[*…*]` renders as italic vs the issue's requested `[…]`; no test of `_embed_share_media` ships (zero existing coverage). ### Recommendation to the next agent **Do not merge.** `gate-fail` at `sha:d5b5d7276b67`. Two independent security blockers (arbitrary-file exfiltration + redaction bypass) are reproduced, and the feature addit

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Thanks for the contribution @webtecnica. This can't merge as-is — it breaks 5 pre-existing tests it doesn't touch, which will red the CI, and it reverses a deliberate ownership-boundary decision that needs maintainer sign-off. Details below, reproduced locally.

## Blocker 1 (objective, CI-red): removing `"cron"` from the denylist breaks 5 existing tests

The change deletes `"cron"` from **both** denylist sets in the shared `_is_claimable_cli_source()` helper (`api/routes.py`):
- the `cli_meta_source_tag` branch (was `{"claude_code", "cron", "external_agent", "gateway", "messaging", "subagent", "unknown"}`)
- the `state_db_source_tag` branch (was `{"claude_code", "cron", "messaging", "external_agent", "gateway", "subagent", "unknown"}`)

But `tests/test_chat_start_claim_cli_session.py` (which this PR does **not** modify) contains tests that explicitly pin cron **in** the denylist / require cron sessions to be refused. With the denylist change, those tests fail. Reproduced locally on this PR's head against the current test file:

```
tests/test_chat_start_claim_cli_session.py::test_helper_refuses_cron_session FAILED
tests/test_chat_start_claim_cli_session.py::test_helper_refuses_cron_via_state_db_source FAILED
tests/test_chat_start_claim_cli_session.py::test_branch_from_cron_state_db_returns_writable_fork_without_source_sidecar FAILED
tests/test_chat_start_claim_cli_session.py::test_chat_start_still_refuses_cron_state_db_source FAILED
tests/test_chat_start_claim_cli_session.py::test_helper_denylist_includes_gateway_and_unknown FAILED
5 failed, 6 passed
```

`test_helper_denylist_includes_gateway_and_unknown` fails with:

```
AssertionError: _is_claimable_cli_source must denylist 'cron' in both the cli_meta and
state_db branches — cron was added in the Greptile 4/5 P2 review to keep scheduled runs
CLI-owned; gateway/unknown were added in the residual #4911 review gap
```

A PR that reddens tests in a file it didn't touch can't merge. Whatever the final design, those tests have to be updated in the same PR so CI is green.

## Blocker 2 (design, needs maintainer sign-off): this reverses a deliberate cron-ownership guard, and the relaxation isn't scoped to reply/continue

`cron` was placed in that denylist intentionally (#4911 follow-up, Greptile 4/5) so scheduled runs stay owned by the cron runner and a stray WebUI POST can't claim a cron session in-place and disturb the next scheduled run. Removing it is a policy reversal that a maintainer should approve before it lands.

It also isn't scoped to just reply/continue. `_is_claimable_cli_source()` is a **shared** gate used by GET `/api/session`, POST `/api/chat/start`, share resolution, and branch/fork (`_load_branch_source_or_refuse`). Dropping cron from the denylist makes cron sessions claimable / writable-in-place across **all** of those, not only the advertised inline-reply path:
- in `/api/chat/start`, the cron session id itself is claimed as a writable WebUI sidecar (`synth.save()` + `SESSIONS[sid] = s`) — claim-in-place, not a fork;
- in the branch route, the new `materialized` return path does not set `_branch_source_readonly`, so `source.save()` runs and claims the cron source writable (previously the cron path set `_branch_source_readonly=True` → fork-only, source stayed read-only).

## What a mergeable version needs

1. Update the 5 tests in `tests/test_chat_start_claim_cli_session.py` to match the new behavior (flip cron from "refused" to "claimable"; drop `"cron"` from the asserted-literals tuple in `test_helper_denylist_includes_gateway_and_unknown`, keeping `gateway`/`unknown`).
2. Add a positive test for the **advertised** feature — POST `/api/chat/start` on a cron session → 200 + writable sidecar. The new test in `test_465_session_branching.py` only covers the branch/fork `materialized` path, not chat/start.
3. Decide + make explicit the intended branch behavior: if branching a cron session should fork (leave the cron source read-only) rather than claim it in place,

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Re-review — almost there, but one of your own tests is red

Thanks for the rework. The design side is resolved: I'd already confirmed the cron-claimable safety boundary is sound (fresh session id per cron run, mirror-delivery writes stay denylisted), and your re-push correctly flips 5 of the 6 previously-failing tests to assert the new claimable/materialized behavior. Those pass and the coverage is real.

**Blocker: `tests/test_chat_start_claim_cli_session.py::test_chat_start_still_refuses_cron_state_db_source` is RED at this head.**

Running the file: **1 failed, 42 passed**. The one failure:

```
assert handler.status == 200
assert 400 == 200
```

### Root cause — a test-body bug, not a route defect

You flipped this test (correctly) to expect `200` + a writable sidecar now that cron is claimable. But the request body it builds omits the required `message` field:

```python
# tests/test_chat_start_claim_cli_session.py:1165
handler = _FakePostHandler({"session_id": SID}, path="/api/chat/start")
```

Trace through `handle_post` → `_handle_chat_start`:

1. The cron session **is** claimed and materialized successfully — the writable sidecar `{SID}.json` is created (your second assertion would pass).
2. Then execution reaches the message guard at `api/routes.py:21863-21865`:
   ```python
   msg = str(body.get("message", "")).strip()
   if not msg:
       return bad(handler, "message is required")   # → 400
   ```
   With no `message` key, this returns **400** — which is why you see `400 == 200`.

The refusal path (`not_claimable`) returns **403**, not 400, so the 400 is provably the message guard, not a refusal. Your self-flagged worry ("the chat/start route handler may need additional changes beyond `_is_claimable_cli_source`") is not borne out — the route already works; the test just forgot to send a message.

### Fix (one line)

```python
handler = _FakePostHandler({"session_id": SID, "message": "continue"}, path="/api/chat/start")
```

With that, both assertions (`status == 200` and the sidecar exists) pass, and the whole file goes green.

### Minor (non-blocking, optional) — dead branch cleanup I'd asked about

The now-dead `not_claimable` + cron branch at `api/routes.py:8101-8102` is still present:

```python
if _reason == "not_claimable" and _foreign_session is not None and _source_kind == "cron":
    _foreign_session._branch_source_readonly = True; return _foreign_session
```

Since cron can no longer yield `not_claimable`, this is unreachable for the synthesized path. Either drop it or add a comment noting it only survives for a read-only-flagged synthesized cron stub. Not a blocker on its own, but worth folding into this fix.

Fix the red test and re-push — the rest is ready.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Read the full diff against `origin/master`: the `_is_claimable_cli_source` change (`api/routes.py:7834`, `7842`), the new `"materialized"` branch in `_load_branch_source_or_refuse` (`api/routes.py:8106-8109`), and the added test. The core design is sound — I verified the safety rationale against the agent's cron scheduler, and it holds — but there's a **failing pre-existing test** the diff doesn't touch, plus one dead-branch cleanup.

## The safety claim checks out (agent-side verification)

The docstring's "each cron run creates a new session" is correct. In the agent, `cron/scheduler.py:2802` mints a fresh id per run:

```python
_cron_session_id = f"cron_{job_id}_{_hermes_now().strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')}"
```

I also checked the `attach_to_session` / `cron.mirror_delivery` path (`cron/scheduler.py:585-612`): when mirroring is on, the cron output is appended to the *target chat's* gateway/messaging session, not the cron session — and those sources stay on the denylist here. So making `cron_*` claimable doesn't open a write path into a foreign-owned conversation. Good.

## Blocker: an existing test still asserts cron is denied

`tests/test_chat_start_claim_cli_session.py` is **not** in this PR's diff, but `test_helper_reason_distinguishes_cli_meta_vs_state_db_source` (line 1188) still asserts both cron branches are refused (lines 1228-1240):

```python
cli_meta_cron = {"source_tag": "cron", "raw_source": "cron", "session_source": "other"}
_, reason_cron_cli = routes_module._is_claimable_cli_source(cli_meta_cron)
assert reason_cron_cli == "cli_meta_source=cron"        # now returns ("", True)
...
_, reason_cron_db = routes_module._is_claimable_cli_source({}, state_db_source="cron")
assert reason_cron_db == "state_db_source=cron"          # now returns ("", True)
```

After this change `_is_claimable_cli_source` returns `(True, "")` for both, so these two assertions fail. This test needs to be updated in the same PR (flip them to assert `claimable is True` / `reason == ""`), otherwise CI goes red. The comment above the block ("...the new entry on the denylist") is also now stale and should be removed.

## Minor: the legacy `not_claimable`+cron branch is now dead

With cron off the denylist, `_claim_or_synthesize_cli_source` can no longer return `("not_claimable", ...)` for a cron `source_tag`/`state_db_source` — cron now falls through to `"materialized"`. That makes this branch (`api/routes.py:8102`) unreachable for the synthesized path:

```python
if _reason == "not_claimable" and _foreign_session is not None and _source_kind == "cron":
    _foreign_session._branch_source_readonly = True; return _foreign_session
```

The PR keeps it "for backward compat," and the persisted-source `read_only` cron branch a few lines down (`api/routes.py:8117-8120`) is still live and correct — that's the one that matters for a cron sidecar already stored as read-only. payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Changes requested — reachable `NameError` on the turn-completion path

Thanks for the PR. This introduces an **undefined-name reference that breaks every completing chat turn**, so it can't merge as-is.

### The defect

`api/streaming.py` line 9863 (inside `_run_agent_streaming`):

```python
usage['model_name'] = model_name
```

`model_name` is **not in scope here**. In `_run_agent_streaming`:
- it is **not a parameter** (the model parameter is named `model`, not `model_name`), and
- it is **never assigned** anywhere in the function body, and
- there is **no module-level `model_name`** and no `global model_name` declaration.

The only `model_name` in `api/streaming.py` is a **local of a different function**, `_explicit_text_signal(cfg)` (line ~2078) — it isn't visible from `_run_agent_streaming`.

So at runtime the compiler emits a `LOAD_GLOBAL model_name` that resolves to nothing → **`NameError`**. The `usage` dict is built on the mainline completion path and sent in the terminal `done` SSE payload, and the error is swallowed by the function's outer `except Exception` and re-emitted as a **stream error** — meaning a normal, successful turn errors at completion instead of finishing cleanly.

You clearly hit this uncertainty already: the sibling line you added at ~9475 guards it —

```python
_dm['model'] = model_name if 'model_name' in dir() else ''
```

— but line 9863 has no such guard, and the `dir()` guard would just emit `''` anyway (defeating the feature).

### Fix

Bind the turn's real model name to a local and use that at **both** sites. The function already tracks the resolved model nearby (e.g. `_turn_route_model` / `resolved_model` / the `model` parameter) — pick whichever holds the turn's resolved model on the success path and:

```python
usage['model_name'] = _turn_route_model or resolved_model or model or ''
```

and replace the `dir()` guard at ~9475 with the same real local so the value is actually populated.

### Test

Please add a regression test — the PR currently ships none. At minimum:
- assert `_run_agent_streaming` doesn't raise on a completed turn and its `done` payload carries a non-empty `usage['model_name']`, and/or
- a code-object assertion that `model_name` is a genuine local/parameter of `_run_agent_streaming` (not a `LOAD_GLOBAL`).

Once `model_name` resolves to the real per-turn model and there's a test covering the completion path, this is good to go.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## 🔴 Authoritative gate certificate — RED

**Exact contributor head:** `04bcc8300862c605fabe25d88859fc0ac99d089b`

I gated the actual diff after a clean transplant onto current `origin/master` (`deac1384f`) on `gate-rebase/6170-workdir` at `db6b834ca5a69982aa04cb7a908c8b6690ae4595`. The PR title/body are mismatched: this is the #5932 workspace **Go to directory** selector, not unified session search / #5890. The #6172 duplicate/supersede call remains a separate product dependency.

### Release-blocking findings

1. **Absolute in-workspace paths split display state from mutation state.** In the live browser, entering `/tmp/hermes-test-ws-8799-pr6170/images` rendered the workspace-root entries while setting `S.currentDir` and the create target to that absolute `/images` path. A user can see one directory and create/upload/delete in another.
2. **Failed navigation corrupts directory state silently.** A real 404 left the old root tree visible but changed `S.currentDir` to `definitely/not/a/real/directory`; subsequent create/refresh targets inherited that nonexistent path. The selector also closes before success and shows no error.
3. **The new permanent header action clips an existing control.** At a supported 204px resized workspace panel with Parent and Close Preview visible, Chromium measured Close Preview as 24px visible before this button and **0px visible** with it.
4. **Selector state leaks across interactions.** `.` and `~` leave the bar open; switching Files → Artifacts → Files restores the inline `display:flex`; Escape does nothing and leaves focus trapped in the input.
5. **Accessibility/localization are incomplete.** `workspace_go_to_dir` and `workspace_go_to_dir_placeholder` do not exist in `static/i18n.js`; the visible `Go` label is also hard-coded. The new mobile controls measure 24px high rather than the 44px mobile target bar.

Codex independently reproduced findings 1–4. Fable independently required navigation error handling, consistent close/focus behavior, i18n, `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`, Escape handling, and a less misleading folder-navigation glyph. My own real desktop and iPhone-14 browser passes reproduced the state, layout, focus, and mobile-target defects above.

### Verification

- Threat scan: CLEAN; low-trust code ran only in the isolated sandbox.
- Syntax: `node --check static/workspace.js` passed.
- Focused advisor gate: 18 workspace tests passed.
- Broad sandbox suite: `13,323 passed / 47 failed`; clean master under the same sandbox reproduced 14 environment/browser/path baselines. A focused rerun of the tail's streaming/runtime failures passed `159/159`, confirming substantial order-sensitive noise, but the suite was not green and does not override the direct browser reproductions.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
I traced this against both the WebUI respond path and the agent's approval handler on the read-only agent source, and the fix is correct — the contract claim in your description checks out. A couple of notes to give reviewers confidence, plus one optional robustness idea.

## The bug is real and this is the right layer

The empty-`approval_id` rejection you describe is at `api/routes.py:23696`, inside the gateway-relay branch of `_handle_approval_respond`:

```python
        if _run_id:
            if not approval_id:
                return bad(handler, "approval_id is required for gateway approvals")
```

So once a `run_id` is resolved (active stream or mirror recovery), an empty `approval_id` hard-fails before the relay ever fires. Your 2-line addition in `_gateway_runs_approval_event` (`api/gateway_chat.py:337-338`) fills that gap by minting a `uuid4().hex` when the upstream payload has neither `approval_id` nor `id`.

## Contract verified: the agent resolves by run_id, not approval_id

This is the part worth confirming since it's a cross-repo assumption. The agent's `POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/approval` handler (`_handle_run_approval` in `gateway/platforms/api_server.py:5086`) reads only `choice` (and `all`/`resolve_all`) from the body — it **never reads `approval_id`**:

```python
        run_id = request.match_info["run_id"]
        status = self._run_statuses.get(run_id)
        ...
        approval_session_key = self._run_approval_sessions.get(run_id)
        ...
        resolved = resolve_gateway_approval(approval_session_key, choice, resolve_all=resolve_all)
```

And on the emit side (`api_server.py:4835`), the `approval.request` event is built with `run_id`, `timestamp`, `choices` and no `approval_id` — exactly the omission you described. So a WebUI-minted `approval_id` is purely a local correlation key; it's safe on the relay path because the agent keys entirely off the URL `run_id`. Confirmed.

## Consistency within the streaming path holds

In the legacy relay path (`gateway_chat.py:891`), the single `approval_data` dict (carrying the generated id) is reused for both `put_gateway_event("approval", ...)` and `submit_gateway_pending_mirror(...)`, so the rendered card, the mirror entry, and the later `/api/approval/respond` all share the same id. That's what makes `_gateway_mirrored_pending_run_id(sid, approval_id)` recovery (`routes.py:23692`) work when the stream pointer is already cleared.

## Optional: a run-scoped deterministic id would be more robust than uuid4

One edge case: because the id is minted fresh on every call to `_gateway_runs_approval_event`, an SSE reconnect that re-delivers the same `approval.request` would generate a *different* id, submit a second mirror entry, and re-render the card with the new id — leaving the previously-rendered card's id stale. Approve/deny still works via the active-stream path (agent resolves by `run_id`), but the mirror-recovery lookup by `approval_id` could miss on the stale card.

Since there's normally one pending approval per run at a time, deriving the fallback deterministically from `run_id` (e.g. `f"gw-{run_id}"` when the payload omits an id) would make re-delivery idempotent and keep card/mirror ids stable across reconnects, at no extra cost. Not a blocker — the current uuid4 is functionally correct — just a hardening idea if you want to touch it.

## Changes requested — `api/routes.py` was emptied; the intended fix never landed

Thanks for working on the profile-switch cache issue, but this PR cannot merge in its current state — it has two blocking defects, both reproducible from the diff alone.

### 1. `api/routes.py` was truncated to an empty file (app-bricking)

The tip commit `95fc7255f` (`fix: make list_profiles_api call resilient on profile switch`) deletes **all 26,267 lines** of `api/routes.py`:

```
$ git show 95fc7255f -- api/routes.py
@@ -1,26267 +0,0 @@
-"""
-Hermes Web UI -- Route handlers for GET and POST endpoints.
...
```

The file is now git's empty blob (`e69de29`, 0 bytes). `api/routes.py` is the entire GET/POST route-handler layer extracted from `server.py`, so with it empty the server has no request handlers and is completely non-functional. This looks like an accidental editor/tooling truncation during the second commit.

**Fix:** restore `api/routes.py` to its master content, then re-apply only your intended one-line change. From your branch:
```
git checkout origin/master -- api/routes.py
```

### 2. The described fix was never applied — the bug it claims to fix is still present

`api/profiles.py` is byte-identical to master on this branch (`git diff origin/master...HEAD -- api/profiles.py` is empty). In `switch_profile()`, `_SKILLS_STATS_CACHE.clear()` is still called unconditionally at line 1543, *outside* the `if process_wide:` guard:

```python
    with _profile_lock:
        _SKILLS_STATS_CACHE.clear()      # <-- still unconditional (line 1543)
        if process_wide:
            global _active_profile
            ...
```

So per-client (`process_wide=False`) WebUI switches still blow away the whole skills-stats cache — the exact timeout the PR describes. Move the `_SKILLS_STATS_CACHE.clear()` call inside the `if process_wide:` block:

```python
    with _profile_lock:
        if process_wide:
            _SKILLS_STATS_CACHE.clear()
            global _active_profile
            ...
```

### To get this green
1. `git checkout origin/master -- api/routes.py` (restore the deleted file).
2. Apply the `_SKILLS_STATS_CACHE.clear()` move in `api/profiles.py` shown above.
3. Add a test that asserts a `process_wide=False` switch does **not** clear `_SKILLS_STATS_CACHE` while a `process_wide=True` switch does.
4. Confirm `git diff --stat origin/master...HEAD` shows only `api/profiles.py` (+ your test), never a mass deletion of `api/routes.py`.

payload.body:
Reviewed the two commits against `origin/master` (read-only worktree, nothing executed). The diagnosis in the description is correct, but the diff that landed does not implement it — and one commit is destructive.

## The branch is broken as submitted

```
$ git diff origin/master...HEAD --stat
 api/routes.py | 26267 --------------------------------------------------------
 1 file changed, 26267 deletions(-)
```

- `f2b34e6a4` ("only clear skills stats cache…") contains **no file changes** — it's an empty commit, so the intended `api/profiles.py` edit never made it in.
- `95fc7255f` ("make list_profiles_api resilient…") **deletes the entire `api/routes.py`** (all 26,267 lines — the whole route-handler layer). The server won't import with this applied.

Net result: `api/profiles.py` is byte-identical to master and `routes.py` is gone. This needs to be reset and resubmitted before it can be reviewed on substance.

## The fix you described is right, and it's one line

On master the clear runs unconditionally, one line above the `process_wide` guard (`api/profiles.py:1543-1544`):

```python
    with _profile_lock:
        _SKILLS_STATS_CACHE.clear()     # 1543 — runs on EVERY switch
        if process_wide:                # 1544
            global _active_profile
            _active_profile = name
```

Moving `.clear()` inside the `if process_wide:` block is safe. The cache is keyed per `profile_dir` and already guarded by a cheap mtime probe plus a TTL on read (`api/profiles.py:1794-1810`):

```python
current_mtime_ns = _skill_tree_max_mtime_ns(skills_dir, config_path)
...
if current_mtime_ns == cached_mtime_ns and now < expiry:
    return enabled, compat
```

So an out-of-band skill create/edit/delete is caught immediately by the mtime probe regardless of whether the cache was cleared — a per-client (`process_wide=False`) switch never changes any profile's on-disk skills, so blowing away every profile's entry on each cookie-scoped switch is pure waste. The corrected block:

```python
    with _profile_lock:
        if process_wide:
            _SKILLS_STATS_CACHE.clear()
            global _active_profile
            _active_profile = name
            _set_hermes_home(home)
            _reload_dotenv(home)
```

## Scope caveat re: #6135

This is worth fixing on its own merits, but I'd be cautious about "Closes #6135". The reporter just followed up there (2026-07-16) saying providers are reachable and that a *single long session* makes the whole UI unresponsive, with profile switch timing out at ~60s. A skills-stats recompute is bounded by profile/skill count, not session length, so it's likely a contributing factor at most — the ~60s wall points more at the synchronous model-catalog probe tracked in #6038. Suggest wording it "helps #6135" and keeping the issue open until the long-session path is addressed too.

payload.author: greptile-apps
payload.body:
Greptile Summary

 This PR adds `.msg-row` and `.msg-row *` to the existing CSS exclusion block that suppresses the global `div` color/background/border transition to prevent hover-triggered flicker on settled follow-up messages after `/continue`. - The approach correctly targets `.msg-row` at the container level, but using `transition-property:none!important` on the universal descendant `*` also wipes out the intentional `opacity .15s` fade transitions on `.msg-foot` (lines 6143, 6156) and `.msg-actions` (line 3389), snapping those hover reveals to instant instead of fading them in. - The global rule being suppressed only animates `background-color`, `border-color`, and `color`; a targeted fix that zeroes out only those three properties (instead of using `none`) would stop the flicker without affecting opacity animations.

Confidence Score: 4/5

 The fix targets the right element but uses an overly broad descendant selector that collaterally disables intentional hover animations. payload.author: greptile-apps
payload.body:
Greptile Summary

 This PR adds an opt-in `webui_oidc.allow_private_endpoints` config flag (also settable via env var) that bypasses the OIDC SSRF private-IP check, enabling self-hosted IdPs on internal networks (Authentik, Keycloak, Zitadel). Loopback, link-local, multicast, unspecified, and reserved addresses are still blocked regardless of the flag. - `_is_disallowed_oidc_ip` is refactored to check `is_loopback` unconditionally, then conditionally skip `is_private` when the flag is set, with the remaining category checks (`is_link_local`, etc.) always applied. - `_validate_outbound_oidc_url` reads the config on every invocation to fetch the flag value (noted as a redundant I/O concern in a prior review thread). - Four new tests cover private-IP literals, DNS-resolved private hosts, the config default, and loopback rejection — though the loopback test does not actually enable the flag (also noted in a prior thread).

Confidence Score: 3/5

 The change introduces a deliberate security bypass that is broader in scope than documented — non-RFC1918 private ranges are also unblocked — and the test suite has a gap where the loopback-rejection test does not actually activate the flag it claims to cover. The allow_private=True path skips is_private entirely, which in Python 3.10 covers benchmarking (198.18.0.0/15) and TEST-NET (198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24) addresses beyond RFC1918. Operators relying on the documented guarantee could be surprised that hosts in those ranges are reachable. api/auth_oidc.py — specifically _is_disallowed_oidc_ip and the non-RFC1918 ranges allowed when allow_private=True

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Reading the diff at `api/auth_oidc.py` on this branch vs `origin/master`: the core relaxation is clean and default-deny is preserved. `_is_disallowed_oidc_ip` now blocks loopback unconditionally, skips only `is_private` under the flag, and keeps link-local/multicast/unspecified/reserved always-on:

```python
if candidate.is_loopback:
    return True
if not allow_private and candidate.is_private:
    return True
return (candidate.is_link_local or candidate.is_multicast
        or candidate.is_unspecified or candidate.is_reserved)
```

That surgical shape matches what was asked for in the issue thread. Two things worth raising before merge.

## Design divergence: this is the blanket flag, not the allow-list the thread converged on

In #6136 both the maintainer and @7d4b9 explicitly preferred a **hostname allow-list** over a boolean bypass, citing consistency with the existing SSRF-trust pattern in `api/config.py:6879-6902`:

```python
_ssrf_trusted_hosts: set[str] = set()
...
is_known_local = any(k in host_l for k in ("ollama","localhost","127.0.0.1","lmstudio","lm-studio")) \
    or host_l in _ssrf_trusted_hosts
if not is_known_local:
    raise ValueError(f"SSRF: resolved hostname to private IP {addr[0]}")
```

The maintainer's words: "A hostname allow-list is the tighter of the two options, so I'd lean toward that over a blanket boolean." A `oidc_trusted_issuer_hosts: []` set threaded into `_is_disallowed_oidc_host(hostname, trusted_hosts=...)` would keep the private-IP block on for *every* host except the operator's named IdP, rather than opening all RFC1918 space at once. Worth confirming with the maintainer whether they still want the allow-list shape before this lands — otherwise a second PR may supersede it.

## Bypass is broader than "RFC1918" (already half-flagged by Greptile)

Python's `ipaddress.is_private` is a superset of RFC1918. When `allow_private=True` you also unblock `100.64.0.0/10` (CGNAT / Tailscale — probably desirable here) but also `198.18.0.0/15` (benchmarking) and the TEST-NET ranges. If the flag stays, the docs/config comment should say "private including CGNAT/TEST-NET" rather than implying RFC1918-only, so operators aren't surprised.

## Test gap

`test_...loopback...` should call the fetch path with the flag **enabled** to prove loopback stays blocked even under opt-in — as written it only exercises the default path, which the other default-case tests already cover. That's the one assertion that actually protects the "loopback is never relaxed" guarantee this PR is making.

Minor: `_validate_outbound_oidc_url` now calls `_resolve_oidc_config()` on every outbound fetch just to read one flag. Not hot-path, but you could pass `allow_private` down from the caller that already resolved the config.

payload.author: greptile-apps
payload.body:
Greptile Summary

 This PR fixes a phantom "waiting for permission" badge on parent sessions after a sub-agent's gateway approval resolves or times out. The stale mirror in `_pending` was never cleaned up on the attention-summary read path, so the fix adds a single call to `reconcile_gateway_pending_mirror_locked` inside `_session_attention_summary` before `_pending` is read. - **Core fix**: `reconcile_gateway_pending_mirror_locked(session_id)` is called inside `_session_attention_summary` under `_lock`, purging any gateway mirror entries whose tokens no longer match a live `_gateway_queues` head before the approval count is computed. - **Locking**: The call is correctly placed inside the existing `with _lock:` block, consistent with the function's documented contract. - **Non-gateway path unaffected**: Non-gateway (local) approvals are plain list entries without the `_GATEWAY_MIRROR_FLAG`, so the reconciliation loop passes them through unchanged.

Confidence Score: 4/5

 Safe to merge; the change is a 3-line, single-file addition on an already well-exercised reconciliation function, and all locking requirements are satisfied. The fix is minimal and the reconciliation function is already called in four other places in the same file under identical locking discipline. Two minor concerns keep it from a clean score: the reconciliation now runs on every session in every sidebar poll (introducing unnecessary churn via `_pending.setdefault` for sessions with no pending items), and there is a subtle edge case where a missing mirror re-created through this read path would not fire an SSE notification to already-connected subscribers. api/routes.py — the new reconciliation call in `_session_attention_summary` is the only changed site and deserves a second look for the per-session churn and the missing SSE notification edge case.

payload.title: fix: use durable claims for WebUI async delegation delivery

payload.author: greptile-apps
payload.body:
Greptile Summary

 This PR introduces a shared durable delivery layer (`api/process_event_utils.py`) for WebUI `async_delegation` completions, replacing the previously absent coordination between the background wakeup and next-turn drain consumers with atomic claim/complete/release semantics backed by Hermes Agent's SQLite store. The change correctly fails closed: formatter, queue, or ACK failures release the claim and requeue rather than silently dropping events. - **New `process_event_utils.py`**: provides `claim_async_delegation_delivery`, `complete_async_delegation_delivery`, `release_async_delegation_delivery`, `requeue_async_delegation_event`, and a single process-wide restore-sweep timer that acts as the durable retry backlog. - **`background_process.py`**: routes `async_delegation` events through `_process_async_delegation_event`, starts wakeup turns in daemon threads, and ACKs only after a 2xx response; non-2xx and exceptions release and requeue. - **`streaming.py`**: the next-turn drain now claims, defers ACK into `_pending_async_acceptances`, finalizes immediately before `agent.run_conversation()`, and releases any unaccepted claims in the `finally` teardown.

Confidence Score: 5/5

 Safe to merge; the change is a correctness improvement with extensive test coverage and no regressions to the existing proc_* delivery path. The durable claim lifecycle is handled consistently at every exit point across both consumer paths — background wakeup and next-turn drain — with release-on-failure and requeue wired into every exception branch. The finally teardown in _run_agent_streaming correctly releases any pre-acceptance claims that did not reach the acceptance helper. The bounded local dedupe prevents in-process duplicates, and the single shared restore-sweep timer avoids per-event thread proliferation. The test suite directly exercises the competitive-consumer race, ACK failure, queue failure, store unavailability, shutdown, and legacy-fallback scenarios. The one design asymmetry worth noting — unformattable async_delegation events retry indefinitely while proc_* events are consumed after one attempt — is documented as a deliberate tradeoff (durable events should retry rather than drop), and the impact is bounded in practice by the natural spacing between turns. No files require special attention. The most complex logic lives in api/process_event_utils.py and api/streaming.py; both are thoroughly tested by the new test_async_delegation_webui_bridge.py suite.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | api/process_event_utils.py | New shared utility module introducing bounded local dedupe, durable claim/complete/release wrappers, and a single process-wide restore-sweep timer. Logic is well-structured with correct lock ordering, proper fallback for legacy Agent builds, and bounded OrderedDict eviction. The no-op _cancel_async_delegation_claim_retry is correct by design: the shared sweep serves all pending records and must remain armed. | | api/background_process.py | Background wakeup path refactored to use durable claims and release-on-failure at every exit point; drain-stop event propagated into requeue helper to prevent post-shutdown enqueue. record_deferred_wakeup return-type change from None to bool is backwards-compatible. | | api/streaming.py | Next-turn drain correctly defers ACK into _pending_async_acceptances list (single-threaded, no race), finalizes claims immediately before agent.run_conversation, and releases unaccepted claims in the finally teardown. The asymmetry between proc_* events (consumed when unformattable) and async_delegation events (released and requeued when unformattable) is intentional due to durable recovery semantics. | | tests/test_async_delegation_webui_bridge.py | Comprehensive new test file with 25 cases covering claim

payload.body:
## 🔬 Gate certification — RED ⛔ (security sanitizer is sound; mixed-copy silently loses ordered-list numbering)

**Certified head:** `bd8acd06aead299264ff1e79e871d2b3e4c79042` (clean-rebased onto current `origin/master`)
**Verdict:** The new clipboard HTML sanitizer is conservative, fail-closed, and security-sound. However, the newly intercepted mixed-selection path silently changes ordered lists in both clipboard formats; the plain-text serializer also collapses generic non-enhanced table cells. Ship only with the small fidelity fixes below.

### What I ran
- **Codex adversarial gate:** `SHIP ONLY WITH FIXES` — reproduced the ordered-list loss against the real production helpers.
- **Senior advisor:** `COMMENT` — no security blocker; independently reproduced the ordered-list and generic-table plain-text regressions.
- **My adversarial Node probe:** verified `javascript:`, mixed-case/leading-space/tab-obfuscated variants, `data:`, `vbscript:`, and protocol-relative `//` hrefs are rejected; `https:`/`mailto:`/`tel:`/fragment/relative allowlist works; double/single quotes, angle brackets, and ampersands are correctly escaped.
- **Targeted:** `11 passed` in `tests/test_issue4945_markdown_table_copy.py`; ESLint runtime, scope-undef, and `node --check` clean.
- **Full serial suite:** `13438 passed / 6 failed`; all six are the established no-network Nous-catalog/picker/config failures reproduced on clean master, none from this diff.

### Verified security boundary — CLEAN ✅
- Semantic-tag allowlist; dangerous tags and their contents dropped.
- Attribute allowlist only (`href`, `ol[start]`, `td/th[colspan|rowspan]`); all values validated and escaped.
- Unknown tags serialize only their safe children, never raw markup.
- Clone/source table count and payload equality must match; every uncertain branch returns `null`, preserving native copy instead of writing a partial or unsanitized payload.
- Full-table fast path and fallback sort-label/header behavior are correct.

### Reproduced blocker
**[SILENT] `static/messages.js:536,721` — ordered-list numbering is lost in mixed copies.** `renderMd()` emits exact numbering through numeric `<li value="…">` (`static/ui.js:7373`), including non-default/non-sequential values. The sanitizer strips `li[value]` from rich HTML and `_markdownTableCopyPlainText()` serializes every `<li>` as `- `. Codex's real-function probe: a list with values `5` and `8` becomes ordinary sequential items in `text/html` and bullets in `text/plain`. This is a silent semantic regression relative to native copy on the path this PR newly intercepts.

**Fix:**
1. Allowlist numeric `value` on `<li>` (same validation discipline as `ol[start]`).
2. In `_markdownTableCopyPlainText`, emit ordered markers derived from `li[value]` / parent `ol[start]` rather than always `- `.
3. Add a mixed list-plus-enhanced-table regression with non-default/non-sequential values (for example 5 then 8), asserting both HTML and plain output preserve them.

### Secondary fidelity fix
Opus also reproduced generic non-enhanced tables inside an intercepted mixed range serializing as `A1B1A2B2` because `tr`/`td`/`th` have no plain-text separators. Add tabs between generic cells and newlines between rows, or explicitly defer this in the PR thread if native-copy parity is not part of this slice.

### Recommendation
**Do not merge this head.** Keep `gate-fail` at `sha:bd8acd06aead`. The core security design is strong and does not need a rewrite; preserve it, add the ordered-list fix/test (and preferably generic-table separators), then re-gate. This is small mechanical contributor-owned work, so I am not adding `changes-requested`. Preserve @heylaurens as author.

@heylaurens — the sanitizer itself held up well under adversarial testing. The release blocker is fidelity: mixed copies strip exact ordered-list numbering (`li[value]`) and turn every plain-text item into a bullet. Please preserve numeric `li[value]`, serialize ordered markers from `li[value]`/`ol

payload.author: webtecnica
payload.title: fix(settings): prefer live gateway health for agent_version in Docker (#6150)

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Changes requested — the fix as written is a silent no-op that **regresses** `agent_version`

Thanks for tackling #6150. Unfortunately this change breaks the very field it's trying to improve, at the code level — before any behavior even reaches the gateway-health path.

### The defect (reproduced statically, no runtime needed)

The new call site in `api/routes.py` references `_detect_agent_version_from_gateway_health`:

```python
try:
    from api.updates import AGENT_VERSION, WEBUI_VERSION      # ← import does NOT include the new fn
    settings["webui_version"] = WEBUI_VERSION
    settings["agent_version"] = (
        _detect_agent_version_from_gateway_health(timeout=2.0)   # ← NameError: not imported into routes.py
        or AGENT_VERSION
    )
except Exception:
    pass                                                        # ← swallows the NameError silently
```

- `_detect_agent_version_from_gateway_health` is **defined in `api/updates.py`**, but it is **never imported into `api/routes.py`**. The sibling `from api.updates import AGENT_VERSION, WEBUI_VERSION` on the line above only pulls the two version constants. There is no other import of that name anywhere in `routes.py`, and no `import api.updates` / star-import that would bind it.
- At runtime the assignment raises `NameError`, which is caught by the surrounding `except Exception: pass`.
- Net effect: `settings["agent_version"]` is **never assigned at all** — this *removes* the field the settings badge reads. Master today does `settings["agent_version"] = AGENT_VERSION` (works). So this PR turns a working assignment into a silently-dropped one — a **regression**, not the intended "prefer live gateway health."

Because the whole block is wrapped in `try/except Exception: pass`, the failure is invisible (green CI, no traceback) — which is exactly why it needs a test (see below).

Secondary: the continuation lines inside the assignment are mis-indented (the `_detect...`, `or AGENT_VERSION`, and closing `)` don't align under the `try` body). It's syntactically valid inside parens, but please align it.

### Fix-spec

1. **Import the function** in the same block:
   ```python
   from api.updates import AGENT_VERSION, WEBUI_VERSION, _detect_agent_version_from_gateway_health
   ```
2. **Fix the indentation** so the assignment body aligns under the `try` block.
3. **Add a targeted test** that asserts `settings["agent_version"]` is populated on the `GET /api/settings` payload — both (a) from the gateway-health value when the health endpoint responds, and (b) falling back to `AGENT_VERSION` when it doesn't. Since the assignment lives inside a broad `except Exception: pass`, a unit test on the settings payload is the only thing that catches this whole class of regression (an unbound name / broken helper would otherwise ship green again).

Once the import lands and the test proves `agent_version` is actually set, this should be straightforward to re-review.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
Thanks @webtecnica — I rebased this onto current master for review (the channel-badge block your original also added has since landed via another PR, so I dropped that now-duplicate half; the net change is just the `agent_version` wiring). An adversarial gate then found a **CORE latency regression** plus a silent-drop bug, so this needs a rework before it can land.

### 1. [CORE] Synchronous gateway network I/O in the `/api/settings` request path — `api/routes.py`
`settings["agent_version"] = _detect_agent_version_from_gateway_health(timeout=2.0) or AGENT_VERSION` runs a live gateway probe **synchronously inside the settings GET handler**. Verified problems:
- The helper probes **two** endpoints, so `timeout=2.0` is a *per-path* budget → **~4s total** worst case, and an unbounded slow-trickled response body can exceed even that.
- `/api/settings` is on the page-boot / Settings-open / profile-switch / version-poll hot paths, so a slow or down gateway stalls all of them.

**Fix:** don't do live network I/O in the synchronous settings path. Serve an immediate value from a **single-flight TTL cache** (return the cached `agent_version`, or `AGENT_VERSION` if cold) and refresh gateway health **outside** the request thread. Also cap the response body size and enforce one overall probe deadline (not per-endpoint).

### 2. [SILENT] Some probe errors silently drop `agent_version` — `api/routes.py` + `api/updates.py:563`
`_detect_agent_version_from_gateway_health` doesn't catch every error (e.g. `ValueError`, `http.client.IncompleteRead`). The route's `except` still returns HTTP 200, but the failed assignment leaves `agent_version` **absent** from the payload → the badge blanks (a regression vs master, which always set it).

**Fix:** assign `settings["agent_version"] = AGENT_VERSION` **before** probing, then overwrite it only when the probe returns a valid truthy value — so every error path retains the working fallback.

Everything else checks out: `webui_version` stays the channel-neutral `WEBUI_VERSION`, the channel-badge block exists exactly once, and the focused version/settings tests + full suite pass. Once the probe is off the synchronous settings path (TTL cache + off-thread refresh) and the fallback is pre-assigned, I'll re-gate. 🙏

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Changes requested: the TTL cache does not gate refreshes, and a thread-start failure wedges it

I re-gated exact head `80683015c50b248fc5778df8dcf0daf8366d0cde`. The earlier missing-import/blank-`agent_version` regression remains fixed: `/api/settings` preassigns `AGENT_VERSION`, then overrides it only with a fresh cached value.

The new single-flight/TTL implementation has three objective lifecycle defects:

1. **The 60-second TTL does not suppress refreshes.** `api/routes.py` calls `_schedule_agent_version_refresh()` on every settings request, but `api/updates.py::_schedule_agent_version_refresh()` checks only `_agent_version_refresh_in_progress`. After one worker finishes, the next sequential request starts another gateway probe even when `expires_at` is still fresh. The TTL controls reads, not refresh scheduling.
2. **Failures are not negative-cached.** The worker stores `value=None` with a future expiry, but `get_cached_agent_version()` treats `None` as a miss and the scheduler ignores the expiry. During an outage, every post-settlement settings request can launch another probe.
3. **`Thread.start()` failure permanently leaks ownership.** `_agent_version_refresh_in_progress` is set before thread construction/start, with no rollback if `start()` raises. The route swallows that exception, leaving the flag true for the process lifetime and blocking every later refresh.

The enforced sandbox gate was CLEAN and the submitted targeted slice passed, **18 passed, 0 failed**. The current tests do not exercise fresh-cache scheduling, negative-cache/backoff behavior, or thread-start rollback, so green tests do not cover these defects.

### Required fix

In `api/updates.py::_schedule_agent_version_refresh()`:

- Make cache freshness and in-progress ownership one coherent scheduling decision under a shared state lock. Return without starting a worker while either a positive or negative result is still fresh.
- Represent cache validity independently from value truthiness so `None` can carry a retry/backoff expiry while `/api/settings` continues serving `AGENT_VERSION`.
- Wrap thread construction/start. If it fails, clear the exact claimed ownership under the lock so a later request can retry.
- Publish `{value, expires_at}` and clear ownership in a `finally`-safe worker settlement path.
- Preserve the current `/api/settings` fallback preassignment so the earlier regression stays closed.

Please add tests that prove: fresh positive and fresh negative entries start no worker before expiry and exactly one after expiry; `Thread.start()` failure clears ownership and permits a later retry; concurrent cold/expired callers still launch one probe and settle to clean state.

payload.author: nesquena-hermes
payload.body:
## Changes requested: gateway version refresh ignores supported gateway URLs

Thanks for the rework. I re-gated exact head `4e9c90bd7437420483ef571411a42c9d12353b83` against the August 8 review.

The four named cache-lifecycle blockers are fixed: positive and negative TTL entries suppress refreshes, freshness and single-flight ownership share one lock, and `Thread.start()` failure rolls ownership back. The submitted cache target passed **17/17** in the mandatory networkless sandbox.

One deterministic blocker remains in the cumulative change:

- `api/updates.py::_gateway_health_base_url()` reads only `GATEWAY_HEALTH_URL` and `HERMES_GATEWAY_HEALTH_URL`, then defaults to `http://hermes-agent:8642`.
- WebUI also documents and uses `HERMES_API_URL` and `HERMES_WEBUI_GATEWAY_BASE_URL` as supported remote-gateway locations (`api/agent_health.py::_remote_gateway_base_url()`, `docs/docker.md`).
- In a custom two-container or remote-gateway deployment, the background agent-version refresh therefore probes the wrong host and `/api/settings` keeps returning the stale import-time fallback.

payload.body:
Addressed all three review points in `_schedule_agent_version_refresh` / `get_cached_agent_version` (`api/updates.py`).

**Fixes**

1. **Coherent cache/ownership scheduling under one shared lock** — cache freshness and the single-flight in-progress claim are now ONE atomic scheduling decision guarded by a single `_agent_version_lock`. The scheduler returns without starting a worker while a fresh **positive OR negative** result is still valid; it only claims ownership (and starts exactly one worker) once the cached entry has expired.

2. **`None` carries its own backoff expiry, independent of truthiness** — `get_cached_agent_version()` now judges freshness solely by `expires_at`, so a failed probe publishes `{'value': None, 'expires_at': now + 15s}` (new `_AGENT_VERSION_FAILURE_BACKOFF_SECONDS`) instead of being treated as an unconditional miss. `/api/settings` keeps serving the pre-assigned `AGENT_VERSION` fallback, and during an outage requests within the backoff window no longer launch a probe each.

3. **`Thread.start()` failure no longer leaks ownership** — thread construction/start is wrapped; on failure the ownership *we* claimed is rolled back under the lock (then the exception is re-raised), so a later request can retry instead of the flag staying `True` for the process lifetime. Settlement publishes `{value, expires_at}` and clears ownership in a `finally`-safe path.

**New tests** (`tests/test_6150_agent_version_ttl_cache.py`)

- `test_fresh_positive_and_negative_suppress_worker_until_expiry` — fresh positive and fresh `None` entries do not start a worker before expiry; exactly one worker starts after expiry.
- `test_thread_start_failure_clears_ownership_and_allows_retry` — `Thread.start()` failure clears ownership and a subsequent call retries and re-claims it.
- `test_concurrent_cold_callers_single_probe_and_clean_settle` — concurrent cold/expired callers launch exactly one probe and settle with `{value, expires_at}` published and ownership released.
- (bonus) `test_failed_probe_publishes_none_with_backoff_expiry` — failed probe settles `None` with backoff expiry, and the fresh negative suppresses further workers.

**Verification**: `pytest tests/test_6150_agent_version_ttl_cache.py` → 17 passed; related updates/version tests (`test_updates.py`, `test_version_badge.py`, `test_static_asset_resolver.py`, etc.) → 305 passed.

## 🔬 Gate certification — RED ⛔

**Certified head:** `sha:b8d91ad39650` · **PR:** #6156 · _webtecnica, “fix(settings): prefer live gateway health for agent_version in Docker (#6150)”_

**Verdict:** RED. The latest re-push closes the prior whitespace-precedence blocker and the earlier cache/ownership fixes remain intact, but exact-head gating independently reproduced two remaining correctness/resource blockers: cache identity is not bound to the gateway URL, and the claimed absolute probe deadline does not bound response-body reads.

### Tested mapping

- contributor head: `b8d91ad39650571463853c674fd3566343ae1ca9`
- frozen `origin/master`: `192df903c8bdd7235b23d336f40aa1ef97864d9f`
- rebased synthetic head: `9e29086ca50711392c6ee724d7a80f021cfd636e`
- stable cumulative patch ID before/after rebase: `c6aa48b4f19284e3797f0cc821b65f7965f93357`

The five-commit rebase was conflict-free and patch-identical.

### Gate evidence

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| Threat scan | CLEAN, score 0; contributor code executed only in the no-network/no-secrets sandbox |
| Codex advisor on explicit rebased worktree | **SHIP ONLY WITH FIXES**; reviewer independently reproduced both findings below |
| Opus 4.8 senior review | **APPROVE**; confirmed prior cache, request-latency, deadline-sharing, and resolver fixes, but did not test the two discriminators below |
| Focused sandbox suite | **197 passed**, including the 51-file cache/resolver suite and neighboring gateway/update tests |
| Reviewer runtime smoke | 40 concurrent cold schedulers produced one probe; positive settlement and negative-cache backoff passed |
| Full serial suite, candidate | 14,148 passed; 8 failed, 2 errors, 88 skipped, 1 xfailed, 2 xpassed, 34 subtests |
| Same-box frozen-master control | 14,097 passed with the **identical 8 failing + 2 error node set**; candidate adds the expected 51 passing tests and no PR-footprint failure |
| Diff checks | Codex diff-scoped Ruff and `git diff --check` clean |

The shared suite failures are the already-controlled sandbox baseline and are not attributed to this PR. The RED comes from the reviewer-owned production probes below.

### Reproduced findings

1. **CORE — global cache ownership is not bound to gateway identity.** I started a refresh against gateway A, changed `GATEWAY_HEALTH_URL` to gateway B while A's probe was in flight, then released A. The worker published version `A` into the global fresh cache after B was already canonical. A follow-up schedule was suppressed by the 60-second TTL and B received zero requests. This can occur when profile/runtime environment projection changes gateway variables. The result is a stable wrong Agent badge after switching gateway context.

2. **SILENT/RESOURCE — the overall deadline does not cover response-body reading.** `_detect_agent_version_from_gateway_health(timeout=.05)` with a response whose `read()` took 0.20 seconds returned a successful late version after 0.20 seconds. `urlopen(timeout=remaining)` is a socket idle timeout, not an absolute wall-clock bound around `resp.read()`. A slow trickle can therefore exceed the claimed deadline indefinitely while `_agent_version_refresh_in_progress` remains true and suppresses every later refresh.

### Precise fix-spec

1. Resolve and capture the normalized gateway base before claiming/scheduling. Key cache freshness and in-flight ownership by that base URL (or equivalent identity), pass the captured base directly into the probe, and discard a worker publication if the currently resolved gateway identity no longer matches. Add an A→B mid-flight test proving A cannot populate/suppress B's cache.
2. Make body collection honor the absolute deadline rather than doing one blocking `read(MAX+1)`. Use bounded incremental reads with remaining-time enforcement (or another mechanism that genuinely caps wall time), preserve the 64 KiB limit,

## Watch re-gate — changes requested on `3b91d73df881`

Thanks for the substantive rework. Two prior blockers are fixed at this head:

- The healthy settings path now has a coherent default-ON contract across the backend default, load merge, boot hydration, Settings checkbox, save payload, and runtime opt-out gate.
- The `hide_empty_state_panel` failure fallback and `applyEmptyStatePanelPref()` call are restored.

One certified blocker remains, and the edited test now positively requires the broken behavior.

### 1. Settings failure still overrides an unavailable saved opt-out

`static/boot.js` wraps the settings request and later hydration work in one broad `try`. Its catch unconditionally runs:

```js
window._virtualizeTranscript=true;
```

That means an `/api/settings` failure, or an unrelated later hydration exception, enables the long-transcript renderer when the user's saved preference cannot be recovered. An explicit saved `false` opt-out is therefore not fail-safe. This is the same failure-path issue named in the prior review.

`tests/test_issue4325_virtualization_toggle.py::test_boot_applies_saved_virtualize_preference_default_on` currently asserts that catch-path `true`, so its green result locks in rather than catches the regression.

The English copy changed, but Japanese, French, Czech, and Vietnamese still describe virtualization as experimental/off by default. The current test checks only that 15 keys exist, so contradictory copy passes.

**Required fix:** update both virtualization label/description strings in `ja`, `fr`, `cs`, and `vi` to describe default-ON with opt-out/full-render behavior. Add semantic assertions for the known old phrases, not only key counts.

The PR removes `virtualize_transcript_optin` from defaults and boolean handling, but does not add it to `_SETTINGS_LEGACY_DROP_KEYS`. `load_settings()` therefore retains an existing marker as an extra key, GET `/api/settings` can expose it, and a later save can persist it again. Greptile Summary

 Re-enables DOM virtualization as the default for long transcripts (>80 renderable rows) by flipping the `virtualize_transcript` default from `False` to `True` and removing the `#4343` force-off migration and opt-in marker, now that the `#4346` Phase B footer-jitter fix is in place. - **`api/config.py`**: Default changed to `True`, `load_settings()` migration block removed, `virtualize_transcript_optin` dropped from `_SETTINGS_DEFAULTS` and `_SETTINGS_BOOL_KEYS`. - **`static/boot.js` / `static/panels.js`**: Assignment semantics changed from `===true` (opt-in) to `!==false` (opt-out); catch-block fallback changed to `true`; optin marker removed from the save payload. - **`static/i18n.js` / `static/index.html`**: Settings UI strings updated in all 15 locales to drop "experimental" and describe the feature as on-by-default.

Confidence Score: 4/5

 Safe to merge with awareness that most existing users who saved settings under the prior default-off regime will continue to have virtualization off until they explicitly re-enable it. The JS and HTML changes are mechanical and correct. The main concern lives in api/config.py: because _preferencesPayloadFromUi() writes every boolean checkbox value on every settings save, any user who saved any setting while the #4343 default-off was active has virtualize_transcript: False stored. load_settings() merges that stored False over the new True default, so those users stay off even though they never deliberately disabled the feature. A show_cli_sessions-style guard on key absence from stored would close this gap. Additionally, virtualize_transcript_optin is missing from _SETTINGS_LEGACY_DROP_KEYS, causing the stale key to be re-written to disk on every settings save for affected users. **Files Needing Attention:** api/config.py — the migration gap and the missing _SETTINGS_LEGACY_DROP_KEYS entry both live here.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | api/config.py | Default flipped from False to True, force-off migration removed, optin marker dropped from _SETTINGS_BOOL_KEYS/_SETTINGS_DEFAULTS — but virtualize_transcript_optin is missing from _SETTINGS_LEGACY_DROP_KEYS (stale key persists on save), and the migration gap means most existing users with any saved settings keep virtualization off. | | static/boot.js | Default-on semantics (!==false) applied correctly in both the normal settings path and the catch-block fallback; all other catch-block globals remain intact. | | static/panels.js | Removed optin marker from save payload; checkbox hydration updated to !==false — consistent with boot.js semantics. | | static/i18n.js | Strings updated in all 15 locales to remove 'experimental' label and reflect the new default-on wording. | | static/index.html | Static fallback text and data-i18n attributes updated consistently; checkbox still carries no checked attribute (JS hydration handles it). | | tests/test_issue4325_virtualization_toggle.py | Tests correctly updated to verify the new default-ON contract and absence of the optin marker; coverage reflects the intended behaviour but cannot catch the migration gap for existing users with stored False. |

Flowchart

## Análise da cobertura #4343

Analisei o mecanismo `vscroll-measuring` (#4346) no master atual:

1. **_compensateScrollForMeasurementDelta()** (ui.js:1197) — adiciona a classe `vscroll-measuring` antes do render, permitindo que a medição de altura aconteça sem flicker visual

**A cobertura parece correta para o caso do #4343** — linhas de tool call altas medidas via `vscroll-measuring` sem flicker, e o scroll mantido via `sessionIdx` mesmo quando o nó original sai da janela.

O @rh-id mencionou testar com sessão longa + tool calls pesadas. Se alguém puder confirmar esse teste antes do merge, seria ótimo — mas a análise de código sugere que o fix cobre o caso.

- Adicionar o toggle `virtualize_transcript` nas Settings UI (não só JSON) — concordo que é um bom follow-up
